text: I love my little town of West Chester. I love it so much, I troop down to the Three Little Pigs every now and again to gladly pay 7 bucks for the novelty of purchasing a sandwich named after a West Chester street. Sadly I cannot purchase *my* street's sammich because I detest tuna salad. Blegh! I should take the owner aside and in intimidatingly quiet, pointed tones convince her to swap out the High Street's fixins for Miner Street's so that I may purchase my own street's fare with pride. As an unofficial ambassador of West Chester, I like to take out-of-town friends or new arrivals to the borough here to soak up the quaintness of the town. Cheerily trimmed in red and white, it delights even from the outside, and when you enter you're ensconced in a cozy, comfortable cafe atmosphere . There's even a little patio that just screams "ADORABLE!!!" the moment you step outside. I love to sit out in a dainty chair on the patio on an effulgent summer day and idly wonder while thoughtfully chewing, what about Church Street suggests a combination of smoked turkey and peppery boursin. Oh yes, and the food...while the novelty of the names is delicious enough, the sandwiches (on homemade bread), soups and salads are scrumptious themselves. Occasionally they run out of bread/ingredients towards closing, so I'd recommend going around mid-day to make sure you get what you want. I find the sandwiches to be a tad pricey for the size given, but hey, the savoriness of the street is worth it to me. The only negative is that they're not open on weekends. Perhaps I'll "suggest" that change too when I take this owner aside....

The wafers were delicious. (2) Chocolate Bourbon Pecan Pie with Sweet Potato Ice Cream and Caramel Drizzle - The pecan pie was dry. The ice cream was amazing with the caramel drizzle. If you're in the mood for dessert, I would recommend selecting their home made ice creams instead. NOLA Restaurant was *ok*, but glad I tried so I can say that it was *ok*. I would recommend you kick it up another notch at a John Besh restaurant instead.

Then there was the crowd, which for happy hour was very much an older, suits and ties and bluetooth Blackberries crowd. text: The first time I dined here was in December of 2008. There were 5 of us, and it was busy as heck. I remember being annoyed at the time because we had made a reservation, and then we were told that we would have to wait for a while while they caught up a bit with their seating/reservations. The waiting area was packed. I was irritated by this, but I figured a lot of people were in town/eating with family after/for the holidays. I remember the meal being good enough, but just not a good value for the money... The experience is supposed to be SO GREAT and FUN... but I didn't really have fun. Fast forward nearly 3 years... I gave Fogo another shot tonight (along with my husband and my brother)... and it was much as I remember. Disappointing. For those of us who don't know... Fogo de Chao is a Brazilian steakhouse. Basically, there is a giant salad bar, and you get a hand full of sides (fried polenta, garlic mashed potatoes, and fried bananas)... But the star of the Fogo de Chao show is the endless parade of meats that are served from giant skewers by men with accents. I love meat as much as the next girl. In fact, I would probably steal that girl's meat right off her plate. I get steak as my default restaurant item. I love meat THAT much... So believe me when I say this. The meat gets monotonous. It all kinda tastes the same at a certain point. They slice it off for you and it's usually a tiny sliver. There are often periods where nothing is coming to you at all. (I'm also a slow eater, so in terms of this kind of setting, I should be turning them away, but I was not.) In fact, we sat and waited a lot. The honest truth is that they seem to try to cram too many bodies into the place... and that lends itself to this sort of dining chaos*. It FEELS like you're being rushed through your dining experience while they run around like chickens with their heads cut off. Sure. I get it. They are trying to make money... but for 46.50 a person (plus the cost of any drinks** and desserts)... I want to enjoy my food and the ambiance of the place. *An example of how chaotic it was... We were sitting at the table and we'd not been there for very long. We'd been to the salad bar, and maybe had two meat offerings... The manager of our "section" came to the table and asked if everything was cooked properly and to our liking. We said something to the effect of, "So far, so good". He turned, and asked another table the same question... and then another table... and then he turned back to us... The same people he had been looking at less than 30 seconds before... and he asked again... if everything was cooked properly and to our liking. We waited a beat. Surely he would recognise that he had JUST asked us that question? Surely he would say, "Oh, I'm sorry. I just asked you that! Crazy night." Or SOMETHING like that. Right? RIGHT? No. He was like our little goldfish manager. He had no idea who we were, and had completely forgotten every aspect of our previous interaction. (We waited another beat and gave him the same reply that we had the first time round.) **The other issue I had involved the drinks. My brother and I both ordered cokes with our meal. I had a regular coke. He had a diet coke. They came out in little 8 oz bottles, and so immediately I assumed that they would be charging us per bottle, as that's usually the way it works when soda is served like that. (There was sort of an interesting interaction where I tried to pour my own bottle over my glass of ice, and one of the MANY waiters that were constantly rushing around us tried to grab it from me to pour it for me... the only problem being that I was literally Mid-pour. I was like,"Um. I'm already doing it. I can pour my own soda.") Anyway, all that aside... when my brother and I were about halfway done with our sodas, we were asked by another random waiter... if we would like more soda. We both said yes, and they took our (half full) soda glasses away and brought fresh bottles of soda and new glasses of ice. At this point, I was like, "Oh, I must have been wrong about the charing by the bottle scenario." Because surely if you're paying 3 dollars a bottle for 8 ounces of soda, they'll let you drink every overpriced drop... But no. I was right the first time. They were charging by the bottle, and we paid for 15 dollars in cokes as a result. Now. Here's where I come out with it. If I had been having a great time... great service, great food, great environment. All that jazz. I wouldn't have had a care in the world about 15 dollars. Not. At. All. We've dropped way more than 200 dollars on dinner, and I've walked away feeling awesome about my husband's 16 dollar cocktail... because we had a great time on those occasions. It was when my husband went to tip the valet and my eye twitched a little that I realised... I was irritated to spend another single cent on an experience that was so so so terrible. That is the truth.
label: NEG

text: I've been going to Ginger Bay for at least 8 years! Their salon is pretty good, but their spa is the best I've found in St. Louis. For the spa, I highly recommend Janet for massages and Julie for facials (tell them Pooja A. sent you!). Janet has the perfect amount of pressure, and is pretty straightforward and sweet. I'm not into new-agey kinds of massages, so a straight up wonderful massage is what Janet provides. She always greets you after the massage with ice water and welcomes you to spend time in the free steam room. Julie is also very sweet, and for awhile offered me some free "extras" with my facial (e.g., eyebrow wax), though when I stopped going regularly, so did the extras. I didn't mind too much, and when I went back to her, she wasn't upset it had been awhile or anything. She rarely pushes products on me unless I ask for a recommendation, too. She also likes to try different products and facials on me, like the Vitamin C, Glycolic, etc. I first started going to Ginger Bay for haircuts. I started with someone named Nicole, who was there for a few years but left. I switched to Jenna and stayed with her for probably about 5 years, until she got promoted to the top-level for stylists. She became over-booked (hard to get an appointment and if I could get one, they were always rushed), wouldn't dry my hair all the way, and would charge me for things she didn't used to (e.g., flat ironing) and without telling me of her new price structure. I've also done pedicures (and maybe one manicure) there, and I think Terry is the one I like. If you ask, they used to give you a free glass of wine or two, though I'm not sure if they do that anymore. The regular pedicure room is fairly nice, dimly lit, with four chairs (I think). You an pay extra for a pedicure in a back room with only two chairs which is more private and relaxing. They always take the time to do everything right - scrubbing, bottom coat, top coat, cuticles, etc. I'm not sure why they don't advertise this, but if you find yourself going regularly, you can pre-pay for 6 services (haircut, massage, facial, etc.) and get the 7th free. I've stopped going to GB for haircuts, but still love their spa. Enjoy!

text: The Sheraton Sand Key is a "nice" hotel. But for the price and the amenities, I expect more than nice. Located right next to Sand Key Park and facing the Gulf, the Sheraton has nice pool area and a wide expanse of beach. The beach includes several volleyball courts and umbrellas, which you can rent for $25/day. A beverage cart makes frequent trips from the hotel to the shoreline to keep guests hydrated. While the beach is huge, I wouldn't call it one of America's top 20 beaches, as some have. The sand is really more of a ground sea shell/gravelly mix, not something you want to sink your toes into, much less walk on barefoot (surprisingly Clearwater Beach across the bridge is much nicer). And since the beach is on the gulf and there aren't any waves, most of the action on the water is confined to wind sports. The hotel itself is OK. Rooms are nothing to write home about and the restaurant and bar elicit half-hearted, "meh." Conference facilities are adequate. And because this is a "resort" and not much is really convenient without getting in your car, amenities that you would expect to receive gratis are rather pricey. Internet access will set you back $12/day, having anything delivered to the hotel will cost you a handling fee (usually $10-20), a bottle of water in your room will cost your $4. Hospitality staff can best be described as gruff. I've stayed in scores of hotels that are nicer, friendlier, and more relaxing than this, and many of them for less than the $275-300/night this one will set you back. The Sheraton Sand Key is like an expensive restaurant with bad food and a great view -- you quickly realize that you are paying simply to be on the beach.

text: Ick. I'm a big fan of Mongolian BBQ - this just wasn't it. Other reviewers have mentioned the frozen meat and less-than-stellar vegetables, which I did encounter, but the biggest problem I saw was the grill. It just wasn't hot enough! At a Mongolian BBQ you should be able to feel the heat as you wait for them to cook your food. You should feel slightly sorry for the cooks and how hot they must be. None of this at HuHot - they even have to cover the food in order to make it cook. That's steaming, not grilling. My dad, who dined with us, asked me what the difference was between Mongolian BBQ and a stirfry - I told him that based on what he was eating, there wasn't a difference. It was bad steamed food with no sear or grill flavor - the approximate quality you'd expect from a frozen TV dinner. Also, I thought the sauces were lackluster and I couldn't eat more than one bite of the off-tasting tilapia. I'm glad to be back home in Chicago where I can go to B.D. Mongolian instead. The only people in our party who enjoyed their food were the two kids - one got the kid's mac and cheese, the other went for the grill and got chicken, noodles, and BBQ sauce.

text: AKA is often a must-stop when I'm in Olde City. The loss of legitimate music stores in the city is frustrating (shed a tear for 611), so it's important that the ones we have are good ones. My favorite part is looking at the walls to see the employee picks for artists and sub-genres. It's always comforting to know you're in the presence of trustworthy music geeks. It's been mentioned before, but AKA is surprisingly sparse on vinyl. Not deathly sparse, but less than you'd expect (I believe Repo has a better selection, but haven't been there for a while). It's good that they let you sample the records before you try them, though they've always been high quality from my experience. Three more areas where AKA excels. First is that they have a great selection of boxed sets and special collectible releases. Second is their selection of concert films and music dvds. Third, and this is the most random, but I actually like the cheapo discount cds by obscure artists that they have. Usually people browse those things as a joke, I legitimately have enjoyed the discs I have blindly bought.

text: As soon as I got home from dinner at The Fountain I went straight to my kitchen to make a sandwich, because I was starving. The portions here are minuscule. I had the Pick Two with the potato/pickle soup and half an egg salad sandwich. I think it cost $7.99 but was more like $4-5 worth of food. The soup was very tasty but came in a tiny bowl (less than 1 Cup) and my sandwich should have had twice the amount of egg salad filling. The other diners in my group felt the same way: too-small portions for the prices. One of my fellow diners had a salad that was too heavy on the onions with very wilted and "rusty" lettuce. For dessert I got the "world's smallest sundae", which was totally pointless: literally 1 spoonful of sundae for something like $1.99. You might as well just splurge for the regular-sized dessert items. I do not recommend this spot for large groups. As I have unfortunately encountered with many establishments in STL, the place has the seating space and tables to accommodate large groups, but the kitchen cannot properly handle so many orders coming in at one time. In our group of 12, two of us didn't receive our meals until most of the people in our party were finishing their food. I think the kitchen misplaced or lost our orders and our waiter had to put in new orders for us. When we first sat down our orders were taken promptly, but after receiving our food our waiter seemed to forget about us. We had to flag him down to get our check, and he told us they were so busy we should go up to the counter to pay. It was confusing. I don't think it was our waiter's fault, he seemed pretty stressed and running around very busy, having to make drinks as well as wait tables. I got the impression that he was doing the bulk of the work in the restaurant while some other staff were not pulling their weight. The decor is impressive - I am a big fan of Art Deco - but decor alone does not make a good restaurant. I would be willing to return here just for drinks or dessert and preferably sit at the bar, but I know not to expect much.

text: This place is all the other Yelpers have said and more. I love the romantic setting, on the water. Bring someone you love and make out on the grass -- what a great way to spend the day! I did study up a bit ahead of time so I could get the most out of the visit. I never realized he had such a comprehensive collection of work, and liked to work in so many different sizes! One problem with the museum is the placement of the title cards. They are all placed at the beginning of the row of works. That means unless you know all the titles by heart, you're running back and forth from one side of the wall to the other, to put the title with the piece. Aggravating! The cards would better serve the guests and the art by being side by side with the piece they're describing. I didn't go on a docent-led tour so I didn't have someone explaining each piece by title, but that usually isn't my style, especially with art. I like to contemplate it solo. This is a discretion-advised exhibit: parents, if you haven't been here, I encourage you to peruse Dali's work online or from a book to get an idea of what kinds of images show up in some of the paintings before bringing your children here. I don't think there's a one-size-fits-all age kids have to be before bringing them here, just use your judgment. Some of the images are sexually graphic or otherwise more weird than you may be prepared to discuss. The gift shop rules; I walked out with only postcards featuring mini-prints of my favorite Dalis but could have bought a lot more. Don't be in a rush when you come here. Allow yourself the luxury of contemplation because the art is that fascinating.

text: I adore Vietnam Restaurant. The Crispy Spring Roll is literally fried to a crisp but unlike the spring rolls from other places, these are crispy chewy, the pork inside is made authentic by the basil and spices. One of the bests I've had. The Shrimp and Pork Roll is non-fried like the regular summer rolls, I prefer this because you can experience different textures with its soft exterior, the succulent shrimp, the crispy bean sprouts and the silky vermicelli noodles. The star of the appetizers have to be the Stuffed Grape Leaves. It's the best dish on the whole menu. Unlike its Greek counterpart, these are stuffed with beef and the whole thing is charred to perfection. Dip it in sauce and wrapped them inside a lettuce leaf with pickled vegetables and vermicelli and treat it like a lettuce wrap. It's truly amazing. Not to dis their Phos, but there are other restaurants that do better, not to say that theirs are not up to par, but like grandma's chicken noodle soups, we all have our own favorite versions. That said, my favorite noodle soup at Vietnam Restaurant was a Crab and Egg Noodle Soup that unfortunately have been taken out from their menus. Broken rice dishes are basically marinated barbecue meats served with long grain rice that have been broken into smaller pieces. There's history in broken rice but it actually kinda easier to eat and able to absorb more sauce. I love the national famous Lemongrass Pork Chop broken rice or the chicken one. The vermicelli noodle bowls are also great too. Add more ingredients to your heart's content and get a taste of as many things as you want. I can attest to some of the great curries they have but with the great appetizers and dishes, I usually don't go for a main dish because I rather taste 2-3 different things than one main thing. Whatever you do, do try to order a drink like a Vietnamese ice coffee or a fruit shake. If you're more adventurous, try a Vietnamese lemonade or a coconut drink.

In fact, I never believed it was appropriate to receive a gift from a customer unless it would offend them not to take it. I figured if that was the way I had to play the game, OK, so I tipped him up front. He told me he does that too. Use caution if they ask you if you want the "hot" sauce on the side. I happen to like the eye-tearing stuff myself, so I thought it was an excellent topping for the burrito. This stuff was so packed with red peppery goodness (serrano peppers I believe) that it was more similar to a Vietnamese pepper sauce than a salsa. HOT!!! They threw in a couple green sauces too, but I don't typically care for green sauce (salsa verde type) unless it's an avocado salsa, or maybe on chicken enchiladas once in awhile. As top tier as my burrito was, it didn't prepare me for the quality of the torta. I'd had one there a couple times before, and again it didn't disappoint. I guess that's to be expected at a bakery (freshly baked, soft torta rolls = BIG WIN). I had it with al pastor. The meat was a little on the dry side, but that didn't matter much with the tomatoes, salsa, lettuce and most importantly LOADS of fresh avocado moistening the sammich. Portion wise, quality wise, and price wise, I'm gonna have to call this my favorite Reno taqueria @ this point in time. Perfect blending of ingredients takes it up to the full five stars. text: I like food. The fact that it fulfills certain important life sustaining duties is merely icing on the cake. If I was informed that I could live without having to eat ever again, I'd still eat. I like small mom and pop places. They can be cozy, hokey, and full of love. A grand well funded establishment can be very impressive, but nothing says comfort food like a small mom 'n pop eatery. So... why does the Dutch Garden only receive two stars? Isn't it a small cute little place that serves food? Should do well, right? Well, yes, and no. It is indeed a smallish eatery, far from the commercial hubbub of Santa Barbara's downtown. The Dutch Garden is tucked away on upper upper State street; so much so in fact that it's quite easy to miss, even when you know where it is. Even if you've been there before. And yes, even if you're looking right at it. Its two main problems however are decor, and food. Actually, that may not be entirely fair. The decor could well have been spectacular, but since it was both poorly lit, and encrusted under a good solid layer of... dust -- I feel sadly compelled to not give it full marks. The main problem however is that its food is definitely subpar. Granted, they're handicapped from the get-go by choosing German fare as their theme, but give me a good wurst, sauerkraut and some mustard, and I am a happy man. We had the schnitzel, some wurst, beets, sauerkraut, and a few other porkly products (normally speaking, my favorites), and it was all bleh. No spark, no crisp, no snap, no sizzle. Just pale, boneless, bland, bleh. French bleh can at times still be quite edible. I've been known to crave Italian bleh. Don't get me started on Mexican bleh, I love it. German bleh however.... nein! Blander than bland. Why not just toss it in a blender, stab it with a straw and call it a day? The beer it must be said was quite good, but in this day and age, you hardly need to submit yourself to limp schnitzels and watery taters to get a good German brewski. A few final notes. a) Why they call it the 'Dutch Garden' is beyond me. It is neither Dutch, nor a garden (talk amongst yourselves). b) As a card carrying full blooded Dutchie, I can vouch that the Dutch national cuisine is one of the select few that is in all aspects less inspiring than the German. There is a very good reason that the French, Italian, Mexican, Chinese, and Japanese cuisines are revered worldwide, and the Dutch is not. Why would anyone in their right mind lure customers with ostensibly Dutch dishes? c) If you plan on taking any of your Dutch friends here, to surprise them - do this ONLY if you intend to piss them off. Even though they might secretly like the food, nothing upsets Dutch people more than to be mistaken for Germans.

text: A bad restaurant may go out of business if its food is not good - that's the basic rule of competition. The point of dining is high pleasure, and we all expect a dining time with full of laughter, serious discussion and demands for more of the food. However, when it comes to monopoly, it's a different story: the restaurant doesn't have the threat of failure as a spur for improvement. I'm talking about Aramark Campus Dining in the University Of New Orleans, which has been serving UNO and torturing UNO students for years. Although the food there is cheap, for me and the other diners, very often, a low price cannot compensate for the joyful experience of dining. Located in the University Center (the UC), the Aramark Campus Dining is not alone; there are also Subway, Chick-fi-la, Béne Pizza and Pasta for students to choose different food for the meals. They serve as direct competitors to the university's cafeteria. The University Of New Orleans, envisioning that there would be a big threat of competition for the running of its low quality restaurant, provided it a good guarantee by forcing all students living in the dorm to buy a meal plan. The meal plan for residents starts at $1,135 per semester and ranges from 10 to 16 meals per week. Although the university has been trying to make improvements such as expanding the campus dinning area, the food quality still remains uncompetitive. There is pizza, spaghetti, fried chicken, tacos, turkey, sandwiches, hamburgers, French fries, or some kind of American food, depending on the day you go to eat. Many times you will be served a hamburger with a muffin soaked in artificial butter oil, toasted and assembled with beef, which was cooked in a large quantity at one time. If you are unlucky enough, the beef may be burned and blackened and look like coal that is not so delicious. The French fries there are the worst I have ever eaten in the US. Please don't be frightened when you are faced with a full plate of fried potatoes, full of oil, cold and soft enough to discourage the diner from even tasting them. That's malevolently bad. The variety of foods is poor. For breakfast, the options are unchanging: only sausage, omelet, egg and bacon. Lunch and dinner have different foods, depending on the day you go to the cafeteria; however there are only a few I consider to be "edible". Not only being stressed out by homework, but also being freaked out by the food in the UC makes me even more tired. There is no music for the meal, but only the noise because of people talking too much, especially at lunch. I'm amazed by how crowded the UC is every meal, and it makes me wonder if there are any students that have passed out or have been taken to the emergency room due to the UC food or not. In fact, the restaurant can do some more valuable change to improve the quality of the food, for example, serve different fruits for each meal. Nevertheless, it seems to assume all students have the same preferences for everyday, so the cafeteria always provide the cheapest fruit, cheapest pizzas ... available. I believe that bad food will give us memories of flavors that may later haunt and follow us in our dreams. I live in the dorm, and I'm forced to go the campus dining 10 times a week. After finishing a day full of work, I go to the University Center, saturated by the smell of fatty American food, and I feel that I even have more tiresome work to do: eat the food to survive. Maybe I'm a bit prejudiced with American food since I'm an Asian, but why can I enjoy Burger King, McDonalds and KFC but cannot give any compliment to the UNO Campus dining? The campus dining is supposed to provide relaxation and relief for students, not take their money and abuse them with bad food.
label: NEG

text: While running some petit-bourgeois errands in the petit-bourgeois Hill Center, we decided to stop here for lunch. I figured it had a dieresis in its name (or umlaut for the more heavy metal-inclined among us) so it should probably be as good, or at least as pretentious as Provence. Zoë's Kitchen's menu aims for a California/Mediterranean Nouvelle-Cuisine meets fun fast food aesthetic. The offerings heavily rely on grilled chicken breast, i.e. the most bland meat imaginable. I had a Gruben sandwich (grilled Reuben) which came with a choice of side salad and a bag of chips, which is a pretty good deal considering that the sandwiches are not really that big. The sandwich was quite delicious when I started it but got progressively less tasty as I continued eating it, which might just attest to how hungry I was when I got there. I had some major food envy at my dining partner's Greek Salad, which was good, but served with cold pita bread. Also, not being one to pass up some fat-people-food, I tried the Ya-Ya chocolate slab cake (the only dessert they offer) and it completely saved the meal. It tastes vaguely of cake mix but it is covered generously with gooey chocolate frosting which is then covered in... coarse sugar crystals? I don't know if this is a Southern thing I've missed but it is delicious either way. The fountain drink sizes here range from big to ginormous, which I like. It is a charming space, all minimalist plus bright colors (very IKEA) and what appeared to be children's artwork scattered about. It is also, in all fairness, not at all a pretentious place to eat like I thought it would be. I was surprised and mildly annoyed that the food was served on polystyrene plates; the place gives off an impression that it might be a little more environmentally responsible than that. Overall, it was not a terrible meal, but I'm a little bit sad that I didn't get tacos at Baja Fresh instead. I might be back to try a salad and/or to sit outside when the weather is nicer, but I'm in no rush to do that.

He walks us up to the showroom and disappears. After 20 minutes, we decide to leave. As we're pulling away, he shows up out front in this truck. We're NOT INTERESTED in that truck. text: 2.5- I kinda blame myself for this rating. Based on a few recommendations, my wife and went out here last week. We had stopped by this place before, just to pick up a menu, and see what they had. The place was huge and empty, this evening was pretty much the same. AMBIENCE- As I said before, this place is huge. As you walk in you can see a bar to the far wall, and two distinct dining sections. One section has tables, and the other section is set up to do Korean bbq. I'm not sure if you can actually do it there seeing as no one was seated in that section, but the server said you could, so there it is. Oh yeah, they were playing the most dreadful music at this place. It sounded like music from a movie soundtrack of a cheesy ninja movie. What's worse is it kept repeating, over and over and over. SERVICE- ok, I'm really torn here. Our server was SUPER friendly.... when he was around. After our drink order, it seemed like a good 5-7 minutes elapsed before our server reappeared. And after our appetizer, it was another 10-15 minutes. The kitchen seemed to be going pretty slow, so maybe that was part of it, but hey, we were one of 3 parties there. It's not that hard to keep up. MENU- The food here is both Japanese and Korean, though I'm sure there is a higher emphasis on Korean. They have a mix of traditional appetizers, udons, katsus, and Korean bbqs, and sushi. The sushi seems reaasonably price. All rolls are in the $5-$10 range, which really isn't that bad. FOOD- We decided to start with the scallion pancake. It sure had scallion in it, that's for damn sure, and it was mostly egg, which was something new to the wife and I. For $10 though, we probably should have ordered one of their specialty rolls. They also bring you a bunch of side dishes with your meal ranging from spicy radish, to kimchee, and "meat of the mountain." For dinner my wife got the tempura dinner, and I got the chicken katsu and a spicy scallop roll. This is where I blame myself. This food is pretty basic (read BORING), and I shouldn't expect any of this food to knock my socks off. Sure enough, it didn't. The spicy scallop roll was ok, but the katsu was pretty "meh" and I didn't think it was possible, but the tempura was actually bad. It was bland and heavy. How do you mess up tempura people???? Overall- Not that impressed. Most of the food (with the exception of the sushi believe it or not) seemed overpriced, especially the appetizer. I might go back just for sushi, but for anything else, I'd be less than tempted. The search continues. Movie Star Rating- Rob Schneider

text: As a fan of great beer, I was excited to try this place which is just 5 minutes from my home. I was pretty disappointed with our experience and more than likely won't be returning. There is no denying they have a great beer selection complete with an array of styles and many rare beers. I understand why certain beers are expensive (eg. aged for years, foreign), but I personally can't bring myself to spend $50 or even close to that for a bottle of beer. There are just too many good beers that can be had at a reasonable price. Regarding the atmosphere, I wanted to like the place. I appreciated the candlelight and old time-y feel, but the air of pretentiousness was unavoidable. Food was served on small slabs of slate which I can't imagine how they even clean (perhaps this was the reason we both felt sick the next morning). I also couldn't help but chuckle when the server brought a bottle of beer to the table next to us and displayed the bottle to the couple before pouring for approval. Dude.... it's beer. Let's leave the snobbery of wine/champagne out of it. Additionally, they had jazzy music playing which would have been nice if it wasn't literally BLARING. Lastly, our server (I believe a partial owner) wasn't overly friendly. The food was just OK. We started out with a $4 pretzel appetizer which was totally raw in the middle in spots. I ordered the lamb "burger" and my fiancee ordered the duck confit sandwich. My fiancee said her sandwich was good. My lamb "burger" was hardly a burger at all. It was more like a slider as it couldn't have been more than 1/8 lb and was served on an English muffin. All 5 bites of it were just good albeit not that flavorful. The couple next to us had a more difficult time ordering. They first tried to order the pheasant for two, but opted to choose something else when they learned it takes 45 minutes to prepare. No worries. The next two items they tried to order the kitchen was out of. Having to go with your 4th choice has to be pretty disappointing especially with a menu as small as F&B's. We checked out the upstairs after our meal to see the beer and hot dog selection. Hot dogs were $6 each and beers up there started at $11. All in all we didn't have a very good experience. I appreciate what the owners are trying to do and wish them success, but the atmosphere just isn't what we're looking for and it's quite price prohibitive. I know you often get what you pay for, but you don't get what you pay for at F&B IMO. I would much rather go to McMeniman's Tavern in Mt. Airy which has a great selection of reasonably priced beers and a friendly atmosphere or just go pick up some nice bottles at Whole Foods in Plymouth Meeting for a fraction of the price of what F&B charges.

text: Unfortunately I had a serious traffic accident on December 26th. As a consequence of this accident I had a painful chest, and a swollen right wrist and leg. Pennsylvania Hospital was the place were I was taken. The emergency room seemed quiet for most of the evening. They called me twice up front for triage and registration. After about two and a half hours, I was taken to the back where patients are seen. The only person that actually spoke to me was the nice cleaning lady that had just prepared the room for us. I laid in bed for another two and a half hours, during that time I had the pleasure of hearing all the personnel of the hospital telling each other about their holiday experiences and gifts. Funny enough, in the room next to mine there was a woman wailing for hours and when I say wailing I mean that the loud painful and desperate screams could not be ignored by anyone in a two mile radius. No one assisted her for the first two hours I was there. The privacy in this hospital is not great. I can tell you that the woman was suffering from colon cancer, that she recently had a surgery to remove most of it. That they had found metastasis in other organs. She also was diabetic since age 40. She suffered from high blood pressure and was placed on an anticoagulant other that Coumadin since she did not tolerate that one. She was there because of the pain and excess bleeding she suffered. It took the hospital staff at least TWO HOURS that I know of to see this woman. The limit for me was close to six hours, when after listening to the poor woman with whom I strongly sympathized, and with my chest pain fortunately dwindling away from me, I decided to go to the desk and inform them that I was checking myself out. Yes!!!! I have had it. Either way if my chest pain was of any consequence I would have been already screwed. Since no person that worked at this facility including the unpleasant triage nurse took the time to auscultate my chest. I ripped the stupid id tags that they had placed on me and walked right out. I made sure to tell them that they were not to send me a bill since nobody did anything for me. The mousy woman at the desk apologized and agreed that no bill should be sent. To my delight as I walked into the emergency waiting room, where one of my friends was waiting, there was an emergency medical personnel cheering on a sports game. TO ALL INDIVIDUALS THAT EVER SUFFER AN INJURY OR JUST DO NOT FEEL WELL AND NEED EMERGENCY CARE AVOID THIS FACILITY AT ALL COST.

Nice waterfront view but because of the low ceiling (all cheap drop ceiling tile), fairly dark paint colors, and orange lawn chairs, you get a feeling of being squished in versus enjoying the light airy feeling dining with a view of water should give. There is a lot of pride of being a mom and pop style restaurant which is rare in chain driven Tampa but the hallmark of Mom and Pop restaurants is inexpensive prices, delicious food, and family like atmosphere. No hits on any one. My husband and I enjoy good food and don't mind paying the prices that sometimes accompany it but the food was only so so. Nothing worth the 20 to 25 per entree cost. At those prices levels, there are similarly priced chains in International/Westshore Mall or boutique restaurants in South Tampa that cook food to blow you away. Everything just tasted like something you could find in the burbs or in Costco's frozen section. We enjoyed the music but in such tight quarters with hard tile floors to reverberate the sounds, it was almost too loud. Next time, we'll return to our preferred Harbour Island spot: Cafe DuFrain next door.
label: NEG

text: Reason for the visit - GIRLS WEEKEND!!! WOOHOOO DRINKS RATING - BEST I've had in a very, very long time.... very strong & generous - EXCEPTIONALLY TASTY!! There were mojitos & grass skirts served at our table - all very tasty - but I'm a gin fan... I'm forever in love with their Elderberry 75 - YUMMMMMMMMMMMMMM!!!!! SERVICE RATING - Very friendly and as we were a group of silly married moms away for a weekend of girl time, we were lucky to have a waiter who was patient with giggly, tipsy 30-something women AND owners who were very obliging in finding us a table despite not having a reservation on a Friday night. DINNER - Well, you have to understand that the Elderberry 75 was indeed a very potent concoction, but from what I remember of my herb filet mignon, it was incredibly tender with a super yummy sauce & tasty accompanying veggies. I finished it with ease (and a little help from friends). Our waiter also brought me a lovely glass of Syrah - it paired beautifully with my steak. The butter lettuce salad was a little sad with just a sliver of red onion & slightly browned leaves, but all can be forgiven since the main course was amazing & the drink, obviously, did its job. Other food ordered included pasta, pizza.... all were very tasty. Only so-so lame thing - it was a friend's birthday & they charged for the dessert... personally, I always think it's nice of a restaurant to provide a special occasion treat gratis. AMBIENCE - We were in our own imbibed world after a few sips of our cocktails, however it was a pleasant mix of ages & overall seemed a very popular place for locals and visitors alike... GO HERE. EAT, DRINK & BE MERRY!!!!!
label: POS

text: After my previously bad experience at Buca I contacted the company to discover if a computer outage would normally result in customers not being seated. They got me in touch directly with management at that location. Matt was very apologetic and offered to have us back with a "kitchen table". Our experience this time was MUCH more satisfying. I'm not sure if people were being especially kind because of the previous experience or not, but our waiter was very attentive. In addition, the Kitchen Table affords you a view of the food as its made. The various waiters will even come directly to your table to show you what it is. Fortunately you get your food just about as quickly as possible since its right there. After seeing all this OTHER food, your appetite is certainly whetted. While I think the problem in my previous review could have been handled differently, I certainly felt like Buca took the problem seriously and made an effort to keep me as a customer.
label: POS

text: Can someone please explain to me why Nashville can't make garlic bread?!! This is the second time I was handed a piece of bread, this time in roll form (what?!) and was told it was garlic bread. Ummm where was the garlic?? Garlic bread usually has butter or oil and GARLIC! Hence the name garlic bread! I was given a roll and red sauce. Red sauce??? You don't need red sauce with garlic bread! Ugh. I was really disappointed. I fell down an incline trying to leave my apartment to go pick up the pizza. Instead my boyfriend had to go. All I wanted while soaking up the blood and performing minor surgery on my foot was some good garlic bread. You failed me Pizza Perfect, got that FAILED! Ok besides the tragedy that was falsely called garlic bread the pizza was actually not bad. I come from the North, as you may have seen in my reviews, so I am very picky about my pizza. I was told, you will not find good pizza outside of NY pizza. It's true, but this place is decent, actually might be better. Their thin crust is actually thin crust. It might even be better than California pizza. I haven't tried any other pizza places yet but I honestly don't think they will be as good as Pizza Perfect. Now if they could get their garlic bread issue sorted out I'd be one happy pizza eater.
label: POS

text: been here a few times and i've always been pretty satisfied with the service, the food, and the prices. the atmosphere is great because you can often sit outside or sit near the windows, which is always a plus. excellent sandwiches. and the fries are okay, too. not great, but okay. great beer. word.
label: POS

text: This was the most disorganized, frustrating restaurant I've been to in a LONG time. We made a reservation for 7pm for a table, but didn't get seated until 7:50pm. We waited in an incredibly crowded lobby for those long 50 minutes, as there wasn't even a bar we could kill time at. What's the point of a reservation if you show up and simply get your name added to the waiting list? Then, when we finally were seated, it was at an outdoor table on a cold December night. The heater did not come close to keeping us warm enough under the thin plastic sheet which let drafts through. The ambiance was further improved by electric wires hanging around the wall. Once we ordered, it took another full hour for the food to arrive. Our waiter couldn't count and it took several tries to get us the correct number of napkins and silverware (we ate our starters entirely with forks!). Luckily, I was there with good company and we had fun making light of the situation... but I would never go back.
label: NEG

text: Come on, you must be kidding me. When I first moved to Nashville, I used to see the long line with people waiting outside in the rain and I always thought "this must be a great place" I am not a fan of pancakes at all but decided to check it out just because it was so popular. Well, even after my visit there and trying several of what they call original pancakes, I am struggling to understand why people wait outside in the rain, snow and cold to get there. My visit to Pancake Pantry was a total disaster. I fail to see how their pancakes are any different than any other pancake. The horrible service was another reason for me to hate it. The waitress was so rude that I wanted to leave the place and never return there. Well, while many of my friends believe that this is the place to get pancakes or breakfast, I am not a person to wait in line and get treated like an unwanted to have their pancakes. However, this is a great source of entertainment for me, I can not stop laughing whenever I drive by Pancake Pantry and see people in the line waiting to get in in the rain :))
label: NEG

text: Despite how gross this restaurant is, we'd been coming here for years (mostly to get a snack before going to see a movie at the Ritz). In any case, I have always hated this Cosi because it just seems so unsanitary. For one thing, it smelled like mildew for at least a couple years. For another, the "hallway" to the bathroom is creepy and the bathroom isn't clean. The last time I went to this Cosi, we actually had an hour to kill before our movie, so we ate in. We ordered the spinach/artichoke dip appetizer and we each had a sandwich/soup special. After dinner, we saw a movie and got home around 11. At midnight, my husband started throwing up. He had severe food poisoning (vomiting and diarrhea) for hours and I took him to the ER. Around 7am, I called the Cosi to let them know that my hubby had gotten food poisoning, probably from their food, but the manager I spoke with was rude and huffy. He told me there was "no way" that my husband could have gotten food poisoning from eating something the night before and that the restaurant was not responsible. I responded that I wasn't calling to blame them, but to warn them so that no one else gets sick. The manager didn't even say he hoped my husband was okay; he expressed no concern for our situation. In any case, the doctor at the ER told us that my husband had staph poisoning, which can take as little as an hour or two to get in the system. He confirmed that it was probably the Cosi food that had caused the food poisoning. After I took hubby home, I called the Cosi multiple times but they never answered (despite that I called throughout the day while they were open...). This place is dirty and unsanitary.
label: NEG

text: We tried the kim chi quesadilla, the spicy pork taco, korean bbq with kim chi taco and the kogi (korean bbq) burrito. Overall everything was good. text: This was like a Cajun Denny's with higher prices. The staff was nice, but the food (and prices) left something to be desired. I would never order pasta from a place like this, but he's 3. Anyway, the noodles were so overcooked that they dissolved into mushy paste when you tried to twirl them onto a fork. Absolutely disgusting. I won't be going back. On a positive note, the staff was very friendly.

text: The one major bane to Philadelphia cinema viewing is the fact that when it comes to seeing a blockbuster there really isn't a good place to go. For a lot of films this ended up being the go to spot just because of the fact that it wasn't the Riverview. But I have to rethink my first review and dub this spot pretty damn horrible. For $12 a ticket it should deliver some benefits. And it does hook up stadium seating, the chance to drink an adult beverage while you view, and the other frills that most mega-plexes offer. But it also seems to have total disregard for the movie viewer. When a couple friends and I went to see Indiana Jones (which was total crap) over the summer they had the audacity to air the movie in a theater that was next door to a bumping club room with dance music. text: I normally write a longer and more involved review of restaurants but I find myself with just as little motivation to write about this place as they showed while making our food. Slopping stuff into the tortillas with as much interest as one shows while taking a dump is no fun to watch (at least _I_ am not interested in watching anyone take a dump). The look on the people's faces was miserable. The nachos we ordered as an appetizer while waiting for friends to arrive? WTH is so special about a handful of chips with a sliver of white cheese on it and burned under a salamander? When my girlfriend ordered her tacos, the guy walked away once she finished...It took me 4-5 times of telling them (No one on the serving line understood what I was saying) I hadn't ordered yet to get ANYONE to actually take my order and when they did, they slopped things on like it was the worst job ever (they do the same with every order so I don't feel special there). They also added things to my burrito that I didn't ask for (cilantro...tastes like soap to me). Onions and cilantro should NOT have to be served together as standard...especially when you ask for just onions. When I told the guy I didn't want Cilantro he said something to the other guy in Spanish and then they chatted for a sec. The second guy says, "Sorry. Already on there." I couldn't make it through my food and I'm a fat man. I can usually make it through anything. Cilantro...um..no. ... My iced tea had no ice and no place should keep napkins behind the counter if the person at the register is not going to give you any with your food. If the line is busy, you are screwed until it thins out enough to ask for some. Then you will get 2 if you are lucky. The only reason I give it 2 stars is the bartender was nice and even though she was swamped, she made sure everyone was taken care of. My quest for a great Mexican place in NOLA is still ongoing. Feel free to pass me any great places you've tried.

text: Yes, this is the sushi spot I run to when I get a hankering. It's close, good, and affordable. It's a comfortable little byob in the heart of Bryn Mawr. Jae, a Korean Californian transplant mans the sushi bar. I've mostly had the sushi here, so I can't say much about the non-sushi offerings. I had the agedashi tofu and can't recommend it. Also, their house salad dressing is a bit weird... it's nutty and not gingery. I'm not a fan. I am a fan of their rolls... they have a pretty large variety and also have specials. I am a huge fan of the villanova roll and the mexican roll. They also have all-you-can-eat sushi sometimes, if you're into that sort of thing. I would give this place 5 stars but the service can be spotty at times. And they play some terrible korean pop music. This place is also overrun by Villanova, Haverford, and Bryn Mawr students. Fiancee ordered this month's special with turkey, gravy, stuffing, and cranberry... otherwise known as the day after Thanksgiving special. He was in heaven. Good stuff, maybe the best sandwiches in town... jury's still out on that.

text: Over/Under recently hosted a HUGE party for Washington University Psychology and the McDonnell Foundation for Systems Neuroscience. The establishment let us shut the place down to outside guests, open the bar, and offer appetizers all night along -- we all had a BLAST! The house cocktails were really great -- I had the first one on the drink menu, fruity with pineapple, and there was another one in front of me before I could blink. Everyone seemed to enjoy the beer selection, too. Appetizers and desserts were very good. The gooey butter cake was some of the best I've had in St. Louis, and the little key lime pies were delicious, too. The place had a very industrial feel to it, almost a little cheap. I didn't get a good look at the decor, mainly because the place was jam packed with people, but got that sense nevertheless. Service was excellent. Despite a bartender who didn't know how to make my drink (to her credit, I didn't know to make it, either), the wait staff was pretty quick and friendly in working with such a big group. Would recommend Over/Under for this same party, if we needed to host it again. It was a great event venue.

text: I decided to venture to Chinatown in Philadelphia in order to eat away my sadness that I wasn't with family for the Lunar New Year. I found Imperial Inn on yelp and based on the reviews, the place seemed pretty promising. Unfortunately, I was quite disappointed. My egg tarts were overcooked, bean curd tasted dry and old, and their Chinese donuts were stale. I was disappointed with my overall experience. I've traveled to Hong Kong and China many times and I'm originally from Los Angeles. This is NOT quality dim sum. In LA, a place like this would close within months of its grand opening. This spot is for tourist. If you want REAL dim sum... this is not the place to go.

It tasted good, but the cheese was probably a mixture of the same low-grade shredded cheddar and "string cheese product" (because it's probably not really cheese) you could get at a 7-11. Granted that's not always a bad thing, but if you're looking for well-crafted food, this is not the place to go. The service was fine, and the inside of the restaurant didn't strike me one way or another. A previous reviewer commented that this place was great when drunk, which seems to be right on, at least for the pizza: it tastes pretty good, but it's totally unsubtle. That being said I haven't tried it while intoxicated...yet...

The noodles with seafood were delicious. The food was really greasy and I felt vaguely ill after lunch but it was worth it. We all ate as much as we could fit into our stomachs for $10 each including tip. Can't beat that!

text: Boundr'y is always a fun place to go for after dinner drinks with a group. Very trendy - full of pretty people. Great drinks and a fab wine list. Sit upstairs - cool couches and lighting, and the "windows" open when it's nice outside. This place packs 'em in, so expect to wait!

text: My Dad lost me here when I was 6. Can you imagine trying to explain that to my mother in Dallas, Texas after several hours after searching?!? Here is what happened back in 1982: My Dad, who doesn't drink or gamble historically, was obviously intoxicated by the lights or something because he gave me two rolls of quarters and said I could play video games for a while. Apparently, he wanted to play blackjack. If you have been to Circus Circus in Reno, you can imagine how excited I was. The place is HUGE and full of video games, carnival games, etc. Back then, $20 was enough to last all day. I was pumped! So, off I went and off he went. I guess a few hours passed and I started getting tired of playing games. I sat down in the Pole Position machine and took a nap. During that time, my father, the Reno police, hotel security and anybody else they could find were blanketing the property trying to find me. When they found me, it was too late. My mother already knew about it. I can only imagine what she did to my Dad when we got back from the trip. :) Since then, I have been back a few times, including once last week. The place hasn't changed. It is really an odd spot. Even the parking garage is weird. If I am going to spend any time in downtown Reno, I prefer the Silver Legacy, but I usually stop in here to reminisce for a minute about the crazy scandal that was discussed throughout my childhood.
label: NEG

text: All my life, I've heard people telling me that you can't get a Philly cheese steak to taste right unless it's made in Philly. And when I asked, they told me that this was the place to go for it. I have to say that I wasn't thrilled. I was expecting to be knocked over by how different the steak was from every other sports bar that claims to have one, and I was not. That being said, Pat's crew across the street were much more pleasant than the crew at Geno's. My group and I decided to split up and try a sandwich from each place. I walked back from Pat's, sandwich in hand, and went to sit down with them (I stopped for a napkin on the way) only to be yelled at for taking a napkin. I figured they were mad because I wasn't a paying customer, so I offered to buy some fries. The guy looked at me and yelled, "No! You got a bad sandwich!" I had heard the competition between these two was tight, but I wasn't aware that their principle strategy for gaining market share involved alienating potential customers. I met my group in the "neutral ground," and I gotta say, not much difference between Pat's & Genos, flavor-wise, but as far as kindness goes, Pat's wins.
label: NEG

From the managers watching our every move to the cleaning service and employees staring us down. We felt that our group of people brought in alot of money and were disrespected. After an hour and half wait, our food arrives. Unfortunately the delay is the least of our complaints. The food is terrible. The pressure cooked chicken in particular is overcooked, dry, and tastes like rancid oil. This is our greatest take-out disappointment.
label: NEG

text: Mediterranean Cafe Puts the "Meh" in Mediterranean. (I couldn't wait to say that.) I work near City Park, and one day when some coworkers and I felt like having Middle Eastern food for lunch and didn't feel like shlepping all the way to Mona's or Byblos we decided to give Mediterranean Cafe a try. It looks like a quaint neighborhood restaurant! It looks like it's been there forever! And it's right there on Carrollton! So how bad could it be? Well ... it's pretty bad. Service was a wash from the get go: despite the fact that we were the only ones in the entire place (at lunchtime on a Friday!), it took the waitress nearly five minutes to bring us menus and take our drink order after we sat down - thus giving us some time to look around and notice how dirty the floors were and how the whole place looked like it hadn't been painted or spruced up in years. (Their website says the restaurant was "newly remodelled since Hurricane Katrina". Guess what? Katrina was four and a half years ago!) Aside from being slightly overpriced (nearly everything on the menu was ten bucks or more, so I'm not sure how the previous reviewer wound up with a six dollar check, unless she ordered a sandwich and a glass of water), the food was overwhelmingly underwhelming. My anemic Mediterranean Salad came swamped in a puddle of oily, tasteless dressing. My coworker's vegetarian platter consisted of three smallish, undercooked falafels, barely a tablespoon of (decent) hummus, and three spindly, greasy stuffed grape leaves that just tasted ... off. Another coworker's chicken shawarma was dry and oddly spiced, not to mention stingily portioned. And everything was served with a basket of cold pita that tasted and felt like it was a day or two past the point of being fresh. All in all, a pretty disappointing experience. You can tell it's a family-run restaurant; unfortunately it's like eating with a family who aren't very good cooks. Next time, we'll be making the shlep to Mona's or Byblos.
label: NEG

text: OK. The two stars are one each for the dogs my fiance adopted from this SPCA. He loved Briscoe quite a bit, and we both love Tala like WHOA, and this SPCA is the reason both of them were able to live long, healthy, happy lives. Or, in Tala's case, is still living a long, healthy, happy life. What I'm trying to say is that I appreciate what the SPCA is doing; however, I don't think they're going about it the right way. I am forever grateful to them for rescuing my Tala and letting Steve adopt her so that she could grace my life with her presence, I just think that there are some improvements that need to be made. When we decided to adopt another dog, I was a little nervous about this place after all the horror stories I read about it online. True to expectations, it was extremely crowded and disorganized the couple times we visited. However, I realize they are understaffed and I appreciate the efforts of the volunteers. The problem came on our final visit, when we had found a dog we wanted to introduce to Tala. Our meeting with the dog, Lucky, had gone great. She was a ball of energy and her foster mom warned us that she didn't immediately take to all other dogs. However, unless she truly disliked the dog, she just needed some time to warm up. Due to SPCA regulations, Lucky's foster mom wasn't allowed to introduce the two dogs by herself, so we asked an SPCA worker to come out and run the meeting. Again, we had to deal with the extremely overworked staff, none of whom was eager to help us or even ask us what we needed. When a staff member finally agreed to help us, it was reluctantly, and she clearly had other things to do and wasn't that invested in the meeting. As soon as our dog got within sight of Lucky, Lucky started barking, and the SPCA worker said (this is a direct quote), "Oh, this will NEVER work. This dog will NEVER like your dog. They will NEVER get along." Yup, that's right, within two nanoseconds and before the dogs even had a chance to get within sniffing distance, she had written us off. Her comments continued in the same vein as our dog got closer. (Our dog, by the way, was behaving just fine. For that matter, so was Lucky -- she was just overly interested/excited, not aggressive.) Not once did she allow Lucky to get close to our dog, which just frustrated her more and more and made her continue to bark and strain at the (choke chain) leash. Anyone with a brain should have been able to understand that these are two DOGS meeting. Yes, there might be some barking at first. They want to sniff each other and check each other out, and they're just going to get frustrated when you don't let them. But this SPCA worker was not at all interested in giving it time. Within approximately two minutes of coming outside, she had made up her mind. She told us that "You need a less active dog for your dog since she's older, this dog might end up hurting your dog." First of all, I think I know my dog a little better than you do lady, and she might be older but she's nothing if not active. Second of all, if you'd taken the time to talk to me for ONE MINUTE, you'd find out that I work from home and am here all day to oversee the dogs and make sure they get acquainted properly. But why take the time to discuss the situation with us when you can just give up, relinquish the leash back to the foster mom, and go inside without a backward glance? Of course, after she left, Lucky calmed down quite a bit as the tension faded. I called her foster mom the next day and asked for her opinion. She told me that is just how Lucky seems to respond to all dogs, that is even how she responded to the foster mom's current dog and it just took them some time to get to know one another and now they get along great. She said that when Lucky meets a dog she absolutely dislikes, she'll bare her teeth, which she didn't do to Tala. Her foster mom was open to doing another meeting, and said she'd get in touch with the manager of the SPCA to see if she'd run the meet and greet personally this time, since she was more familiar with Lucky's situation and disposition. Then I didn't hear from the foster mom all week. When I finally e-mailed her, she seemed to have lost interest in helping us out. The whole thing was just very depressing. Policies and attitudes like the ones they seem to have at the SPCA will turn people off from adopting. These dogs are going to get put down if they don't find a home -- wouldn't you think the SPCA would have more of a vested interest in spending the time to try and get them placed?

text: We Edmontonians are fortunate to have not only the designation of Alberta's capital city, but also the Legislative Grounds! Over the Christmas holidays thousands of lights illuminate the trees and it's a beautiful site to behold driving past on 109 Street or roaming the grounds. On a hot summers day you'll be hard pressed to find a place to park (both your vehicle and yourself) as this is one of the City's hot spots! The multi-layer fountain and main fountain are a draw for young and old alike from romping through or dangling your tootsies in them. I spent much time here last summer with my daughter and nieces. Security personal are on hand during these busy times so you can feel more comfortable letting lose, but keep valuables at home or in your locked car just the same. Let's not forget about the treat vendours - yup, they make a killing on hot days selling ice cream and popsicles. Once the snow melts the ground truly come to life. Of course there are flowers galore and over 100,000 annuals are planted to further add to the natural colour explosion. On the south side of the grounds you'll find an amphitheater/bandshell, lawn bowling courts, and the area for the skating rink, in addition to the walking paths and parklike setting, all overlooking the North Saskatchewan River. Of course one has to mention the water fall on the High Level Bridge - takes place on the long weekends over the summer. Regardless of the time of year you visit the Legislative Grounds you'll be sure to find pictures being taken of weddings, groups and individuals. Part of the draw for me is the little bit of heaven in the city. Often we go down with a picnic lunch in hand and relax or stroll around the grounds. There is one tree I like to sit under on the south lawn. When I look up from there I can only see the grounds and the south entrance of the Legislature. Makes me imagine we have our own palace in the middle of the prairies (ok, insert Tragically Hip song here...)

text: For those of you who don't know, this establishment is divided into 2 sections. On the corner of South and Broad Streets you will find Govinda's Gourmet Vegetarian To-Go. If you walk several yards west (on South Street) of the To-Go establishment you will find a building with an awning that reads "Art Gallery and Cafe"...this is the location of their fine dinning restaurant. Firstly...The To-Go establishment: With the To-Go on the corner we were easily able to find it, but were at a complete loss for finding the part of the restaurant that we were looking for. Starving and slightly confused we decided to get ourselves some sandwiches from the To-Go. I got a cheese steak and my fiance go a chicken cheese steak. The bread was wonderful...you were given a choice between whole wheat and seeded white, I went with the whole wheat. They toasted the roll on the griddle so that it became crisp and crunch and filled it with mock beef and peppers. Although the sandwich was good, I did not feel that it resembled a real cheese steak and because of this I was disappointed. My fiance's chicken cheese steak was incredible...I would have guessed that it was chicken. The texture of the substitute was spot on! The two steaks (which weren't very big) and a single bottled drink were almost $20. Ouch....But still, I would definitely go back to try their chicken cheese steak again. Secondly...The Gourmet Restaurant (the real reason I'm writing this review): Simply Incredible! After finding the restaurant we went inside and were promptly greeted by a server. This restaurant is divided into two sections; there is a gourmet buffet downstairs and a fine dining seated section upstairs. We opted to sit upstairs and enjoy a nice quite meal. After being seated we were immediately given water, which seemed to have a faint trace of lemon...the water was delicious. After our waiter gave us our menus and left the room, I took the time to look around. The upstairs dining area was pretty. It was fairly small, with only 8-10 tables at most, but had a very quaint and cozy feel. Our table was decorated with silverware and long stem glasses for both water and the BYOB wine that we forgot to bring. In addition the table, and rest of the room, were decorated in fresh cut flowers. Appetizer: Bok Choy Wrapped Scallops with Horseradish Tomato Emulsion $8 They were presented on a long rectangular plate, which was decorated beautifully. They were delicious... Did the taste like scallops? Yes, but the texture was slightly different (more spongy) But, nevertheless, they were fantastic. Salad: Caesar Salad with vegan cheese and dressing $7-8 This is one of the things that I miss most since becoming a vegan/vegetarian. Caesar dressing has anchovies in it and fish, I'm afraid, are no longer an option for me. When the salad was brought to the table we both quickly realized that the salad was intended to be an entree, it was huge. The salad was very good. The croutons were definitely house made, which was a very nice touch. Even though, I don't really care for vegan cheese, the salad was very good. Entrees: Vegan Mac N Cheese with Steamed Broccoli and BBQ Shrimp $15 My fiance got this dish because she wanted to see what mock BBQ shrimp tasted like. Her dish was good, but as I mentioned before, I don't really care for vegan cheeses. She loved her food and said that the shrimp were just like real shrimp and that the texture was very similar. The portion size was very large and she wasn't able to finish all of her meal. Pan-Roasted Duck with Sweet Potato Puree and Peanut Ginger Sauce $19 I ordered this. OMG! This was the best mock meat that I have ever had in my life. It tasted exactly like duck. The texture was perfect. It even had a skin on it!!!! I am not kidding you when I say that I asked our waiter if they had given me a real piece of duck by mistake. I am so glad that I got this dish. It was incredible. My fiance took one bite and told me that she didn't want to eat anymore. When I asked her why, she said because it tasted so much like duck that she thought it was scary and that it bothered her. YESSSSS. The price of this meal is well worth how delicious it was. Now, i'm not saying that I'm going to start going every week...wish I had the cash to do that!. But I will definitely be back soon. Completely ignoring the fact that it was a mock meat, this was one of the best meals I have had in a very long time. Go here!!! As my fiance pointed out, being vegan makes it hard to go out to a fancy restaurant for dinner. How often can you get a 4 course meal and remain vegan? Really? Go here and reward yourself with a beautiful, elegant meal in a relaxed, romantic atmosphere! Ohh, and the fine dining restaurant in only open on weekends for dinner.

text: Chasing the Dragon...I have chased many a dragon...through my life of continual excess, degradation, exploration, exasperation and even flagellation most of my experiences have come because of that damn dragon. The first time you do something wonderful, experience joy, or pass out naked in the Vatican wearing only a beer can hat...it is burned in your soul and your only desire is relive that moment. It becomes an obsession. It becomes a quest. A pain in your heart and a blackening of your spirit each time you cannot grab a hold of that dragon and suck the marrow from his bones. My dragons have almost killed me. My dragons have saved me. My dragons have almost ruined me. My dragons have enriched my life. Meet my newest dragon...L'angelo Ristorante. People I trusted, people who know good food, people who I have spend 17 years in a 10x10 cage, would rave to me about L'angelo...they would tell me how truly special this little BYOB off of broad street was. I would dismiss them. I would curse them. I would flail at them with sharp objects. Eventually, they gave me some money and with the money I made collecting cans it was time to take the woman I am currently living with. The bane of my existence. Several times we sampled the goodness L'agnelo had to offer, and each time I loved it even more. I was told that this would be the best meal I have ever had. I am not quite ready to say that, but I will say that it is has had the single best Italian dish of my life, and that it has had the most constantly spectacular meals of my life. Without reciting the menu, which never really seems to change, and that is a great thing, I will explain what this place is NOT. It is NOT a place where you stuff yourself with 2lbs of pasta. It is not a spacious, well lit, cavernous chain Italian eatery. It is not a place you should eat wearing a baseball hat or a hoodie...idiot in the red...you know who you are. What this is...is brilliant. It is simple, unpretentious food done perfectly. It is the excellence of execution (sorry Bret Hart), it is haunting beauty of simply prepared ingredients done perfectly. Nothing is over the top. Everything feels like you can make it at home...until the car ride back and every millimeter towards your destination tells you that the best you could ever do is a pathetic recreation of elegant simplicity. The best Italian dish I have ever had is their appetizer. It is a baked trio of mushrooms mixed with garlic and fresh rosemary covered in fontina cheese. Sound simple. It is. Sound like something you can make at home. It isn't. It is so perfectly prepared that I have ate it every time I have gone to L'angelo. The owner has given us their homemade leminchello made with grain alcohol for free every time I have eaten there. Made on premises and it is again perfect in its execution and delightfully refreshing. My last kudos is for a desert that exemplifies their subtle food magic. Tiramisu. Tiramisu can be heavy handed, it can be too light, it can be too kid friendly, it can be utterly forgettable. Here it is a perfect balance of rum, coffee, freshly made ladyfingers and a light and not too overly sweet cream. It is ethereal. It is perfect. L'angelo is a great place to eat. It is reasonably priced especially for how good the food is. You cannot say that you know Philadelphia without eating here. It is an experience. It is my dragon and I am afraid that I will never ever be able to properly chase this dragon outside of those four walls.

text: EDIT- I have decided to edit my post instead of update it, since I only wrote it a week ago. text: Visited St. Pete's with the fam on vacation and stumbled across this gem after a morning at the Salvador Dahli museum down the street. Immediately drawn in by the look of the place, has lots of character. Turns out its the oldest restaurant in the city, attached to the Detroit Hotel. Built in 1890 by our own John R. Williams and Peter Demens, an immigrant from St Petersburg Russia, it was the first hotel in the city. Anyways, the bar inside has the well-used look of an old, classy joint and the outdoor patio has a damn-old tree draped with vines, glass art and lights, making for a great setting to eat. Staff when I was there was lovely (and not just to look at, eh?) and the food was really a knock-out. We were started with fresh, warm baked bread and ordered a blackened Talapia club sandwich, chicken curry salad, and a linguine and shrimp dish tossed in a tomato sauce of some sort. Everything was outstanding. Great combinations of flavors for all the dishes. Well seasoned and well cooked fish, amazing honey-vinagarette with the chicken curry and their bacon is the best I've had in a long while. Plus, get this, almost all the entrees are $6 or less. No joke. Needless to say I walked away very pleased at the find. It made me want to go to school at Southern Florida University so I could eat there every day and hit on the staff. Heh. Almost forgot, their bar scene -I suspect- is great as well. They have live music most nights, open up a huge second section (The Martini Lounge) and likely draw many of the youth-heads from around town. If I'd got the chance I would've come here on a Thursday or Friday night and might have been able to give this joint its 5th star. Without having the full experience however I can't give it my full on. If ever in St. Petersburg, find the Dali Museum and then get your ass to the Garden Bistro.

text: I got turned on to The Independent by a friend who said the atmosphere was awesome, but that didn't matter much to him because he quit drinking. I point to the line of imported and small brewery beers. Him, calm and friendly - "Well, what beers have you liked in the past. We'll start from there." And from there, in the midst of a full crowd, he took the time to explain the ins and outs of Beer 101 until I had settled on a Belgian Abbey Ale that totally knocked my socks off. Seating is at a premium, but with the great location just off Central Avenue, it really doesn't matter if you stand out on the sidewalk (and someone will always let you stack your empties on their table). I personally love to be inside, but mostly for the blend of electro-lounge and indie rock playing over the constant hum of conversation, punctuated by raucous laughter. The only drawback to a night at The Indie is possibly the never-ending onslaught of every type of smoke you thought imaginable in one place at the same time. The place shouldn't work on all the levels that it does - it's chic, it's down-to-earth, it's hipster heaven, it's frat boy hangout, it's business drinks, it's alkie hideout, it's straight bar, it's gay bar. If you put a little bit of yourself into a night out at The Independent, you'll get that investment back in spades. Oh! And beer - you'll get beer.

text: Went with my mom last Thursday for a dinner meeting for her work. She went to join her group, and I asked the host to seat me at a table or booth big enough for two, since she'd be coming back to join me when she was finished. Then they left me there for about ten minutes without asking if I wanted something to drink or some chips and salsa...nothing. It wasn't even busy! When a server did come around, he acted confused when I said I'd like to order while waiting for my mom. Maybe it seemed like bad manners to eat before my party arrived, but I was hungry! The ambiance where I was seated was very suffocating. No windows, black walls, dark carpet, confining booths with black plastic table cloths... Even with the lights, it felt less like a romantic dimness and more like I was eating in a converted basement. I kept asking myself, "What are they trying to hide?" I'd just placed my order when my mom showed up bearing her own plate of food, which she'd ordered in the meeting. She'd just recently had a tooth extraction and was eating something unidentifiable fried in egg. I asked what it was, and with a weak smile she replied, "Bland," and reached for the salsa. Speaking of which, the chips and salsa were pretty "meh." The chips looked and tasted sort of stale, and I prefer a chunkier salsa. The mild one was pretty forgettable, and the hot one had more spice than flavor. I had been torn between ordering the carnitas and the beef/chicken combo fajitas. I had decided to go with the latter, since it sounded like it came with more veggies. (Radishes? What?) But when it arrived, it wasn't quite what I'd been expecting. The meat had been sliced extremely thin, almost julienne, and unless I squinted, I couldn't really tell the difference between the two. There was no difference in taste, either, which as Mom had said, was pretty bland. The Spanish rice was fluffy and flavorful enough. The refried beans were typical. And for the price, they only give you two tortillas which didn't even get me through half my plate. (I hear you can get three if you order corn tortillas, though I assume that's because they're smaller.) I usually try to clear everything on my plate, but I just couldn't. I picked out what I thought was most edible and left the rest, I was so disappointed. The only highlight was the flan. It was thick and sweet, with a slight cinnamon grittiness to it that was appealing. It was big enough to share with Mom, so I did. I left feeling unsatisfied and wanting a real dinner to make up for this one. It wasn't horrendous, but it wasn't anything to shout about, either. I doubt I'll return unless Mom has to have another meeting there.
