text: On my recent trip to Nashville, we ran into some trouble finding places to eat/drink. I combed over Yelp extensively, even posted a talk subject hoping to find some help with my specific needs. (I don't like country music, don't care for touristy spots, and wanted to find genuinely good food for a decent price, much like I can at home.) After all the searching, we ended up hitting a few well reviewed spots, and I am beginning to think my taste buds must be really different from everyone else's. We went to Eastland on our second night in town. The space was very cute, home-y with an open kitchen. We opted to sit outside (in the backyard, if you will...) The weather was nice, and even though our server looked to be busy, he greeted us promptly. We both ordered a glass of wine, me a sparkling, him a red. His was much better than mine, I must say. (Believe me, it's hard for me to admit. I am used to being the ordering professional.) There was something odd about the wine list, though. The prices were actually in favor of ordering by the glass opposed to ordering by the bottle. (Only a few dollars more, but at every other restaurant, you save a little by ordering the bottle. That way, you not only spend more, but the restaurant saves by not having open bottles sitting around for too long.) Since we had a late lunch, we opted to order three appetizers and a side to share, plus the complimentary bread, served with the odd but acceptable combination of traditional dipping oil infused with cilantro. We got the pizza, the goat cheese brulee, the crab cake, and the jalapeno mac and cheese. Mediocrity seemed to be the running theme. The crab cake tasted just like every other version (except for Blais' at Home....I don't think I need to go into that again, but my mouth is watering just thinking about it.) It had way too much filler, not nearly enough crab. The pizza was decent, competently done, with accurate flavors, but it wasn't something I would recommend. The goat cheese brulee was odd. It was a lump of goat cheese on a plate, then hit with a torch and covered in honey and a balsamic glaze. It was served with what looked to be the pizza crust, sliced with no toppings, roasted red peppers, yellow peppers, and tomatoes. A bite of just the crust and the goat cheese was way too sweet, but pairing it with the roasted tomatoes overpowered the other flavors. (I liked the tomatoes, their flavor was just too rich for the goat cheese.) The mac and cheese was the saving grace of the meal, though it was so hot and bubbly we couldn't even eat it until we were full from everything else. (I know that isn't a real problem, but I want to be able to eat things within twenty minutes of them hitting the table. This was too hot to do even that.) After a couple of bites of the perfectly spicy and rich pasta, we took that last piece of pizza and the mac and cheese to go, and paid the bill, which came to $50. Reasonable in the price, but we didn't order main courses. Bottom line is, I would probably enjoy sitting at Eastland's bar and having a cocktail, but wouldn't choose to go back for dinner.

text: Ok...so by the looks of my reviews, it appears that I only eat breakfast, but what can I say...I find breakfast/brunch cathartic. I have been driving, riding, and walking past the cafe for over two years now and for some reason have always forgotten to go there. Finally one morning I drove past it with a friend and yelled WAIIIIITTTTT! After a quick loop around the block we parked in the lot( yes a parking lot in the city...hooray!) and happily waited only about 5 minutes for a table. I was pleasantly surprised at the lack of a wait on a Saturday morning at 10am. We were seated and promptly greeted by a super cute and friendly waitress with coffee in hand. What more can I ask for with my coffee than a cute girl in awesome boots? Their menu is small, but I appreciate that in a restaurant. To me, this means that they know what they are making and they do it damn good! I had an omelet with avocado and swiss, yummy homefries( the big chunky kind), and probably the second best multi-grain bread in the city(aside from metro). The omelet was a great size and I only ate half. It was priced at 10 dollars which seems about right against comps. The bread is made fresh on premises, as are the pastries. I grabbed a banana muffin to go because they had been staring at me the whole time. It was one of the best muffins I have ever had. It was chock full of bananas that caramelized from baking and they were insanely cake like and indulgent. That thing about only having a 5 minute wait...yeah that quickly changed. As we were nearing the end of our meal the line was starting to go outside and was becoming a 30 minute wait. I have to say though, we were never rushed out. Even after we had received our check and the line was growing, we were offered more coffee. Although we declined in order to free up our table, the offer was really appriciated in this city. The one negative I will mention is that they don't have room for strollers inside and you are asked to leave them outside. There were a few angry parents who were forced to leave their 1000 orbit stroller outside. So word to the wise...grab your sling and strap the kids in. So yeah, don't go to morning glory walk a few blocks east and head to this quaint and lovely cafe.

text: We weren't all that impressed with our first experience here; while the place is gorgeous in an urban rustic way, the food seemed a little too salty and not worth the money. Believe it or not, for a restaurant that's all about cured meats, the kitchen is actually vegan-friendly. My husband and I are both vegan, and we've gotten comfortable just showing up and asking the waiter to bring us something vegan -- what arrives is always fantastic. The bar is deserving of a great rating all on its own. Word is that when Robert Plant was living in the neighborhood while working with Alison Krauss, he was sometimes seen at this bar. It's a bit cramped and they don't have every imaginable drink, but they specialize in a menu of stylish cocktails. Of course, having tried several, I haven't found any that I love. Still, it's fun to experiment, and if you're not in the mood for cocktails, they have a great wine list. And while the bar menu, with inventive hors d'oeuvres, is considerably less suitable for vegans than the dinner menu, we've heard from friends that it's nearly as good. All in all, while there may be a dish or two on the menu that won't please your palate for whatever reason, the overall experience is so good and the food in general so incredible it's definitely worth trying again.

text: My 100th review... I never thought I would see the day. I spent days wondering if I would ever make it to ROTD rather than even think I would make it to #100. 100 reviews!!!...whew... I finally made it. Seems like such a long time ago that I was nervously writing my first review...now I feel even more nervous...okay hold on to your hats, here it is. I thought that for my 100th time that it should be extra special, you know maybe review one of the best steakhouses in and across the country. I wanted to make it the best it could be by spotlighting a place that claims to be the best of the best... Well you won't be hearing about the best of the best in my review of Morton's. I visited Morton's about 10 years in the city on a client visit. Since I wasn't technically paying for my dinner (thank you corporate card), it was a pretty spectacular experience at the time. Now that I was going to visit this place again and going to be paying my way with my own hard earned money, I was not in a position to compromise any of the important factors in a restaurant: décor, food, price and most importantly, service. I was invited to Morton's in K of P last Thursday with my friend and her husband to celebrate their wedding anniversary. Yeah I know what you are all thinking - I have no life. But it was Morton's and I thought my last experience was pretty good, so why not? So being the good little third wheel that I was, I made my way to the restaurant to partake in the anniversary celebration. The first thought I had as I pulled into the crowded K-of P parking lot around 5pm was "Why would you put a Morton's Steakhouse right smack in the middle of an enormous mall; especially next to a discount shoe store?" I continued, "You are Morton's you should be standing alone --separated from the rest...!!!!" The location seemed quite odd to me. Don't you all think so? Once inside, the restaurant seemed quiet and unassuming. We walked into a dark narrow corridor and entered into the main dining room which was barely lit. The décor seemed stale and not very welcoming or warm at all. As I nestled between the 2 lovebirds in a corner booth, I perused the menu that had been eloquently engraved with a "Happy Anniversary". Awww. I felt out of place. I needed a drink. Where's the waiter? After about 10 minutes, the waiter appeared and right off the bat, I thought he was trying way too hard to earn extra moolah on his tip. Too happy and too pushy- a deadly combination for anyone in the food service business. I ordered a Thyme Lemon Drop Martini but failed to realize that it actually had pieces of really thyme sprinkled on the top of the drink as a garnish. What??!!! Who in their right mind thought to mix thyme with lemons in a martini? yukkk, bleck, ewwwww!!! I asked the waiter what was in the drink. He said it was a "Thyme" Lemon Drop Martini. Okay, thanks Einstein. I get it. I thought he could tell by my tone and the look of terror on my face that I did not like it. Did he offer to take it back? No. Did he offer to get me something different? No. Did he offer to have the bartender make me another one without Beelzebub's spice in it? No... My night was immediately ruined (sigh). The entrees were okay; the meat cooked the way that everyone had ordered; I proactively ordered a raspberry martini to try to wash away the taste of thyme from my mouth about halfway through my meal. So let's summarize, shall we? Décor - 1 star Food - 3 stars Price - 1 star Service - 1 star What started as a pretty crappy experience for a hoity toity restaurant, ended up slightly over mediocre in the end. That is after the wait staff and fellow patrons sung happy anniversary to all three of us as we ogled the candle in the middle of the crème brulee and I made it smack dab in between the happy couple in the souvenir anniversary photo... courtesy of Morton's.... Ah memories.
label: NEG

text: I like chicken. I like waffles. But would I like chicken AND waffles in the same meal, at the same time, on the same plate? Turns out, I did! Or rather, I do. Or is it I would? May's Counter Chicken and Waffles, let's just call it Chawffles for short, (it'll catch on) is nothing short of amazing. This type of cuisine is pretty foreign to me, so tell me you're going to throw two chicken boobs on a fluffy waffle then give me a slew of sauces to drizzle on top and I'm gonna say, "Ok May, bring on the Chawffle!" It was pretty amazing. The chicken was moist and tender, lightly breaded, but not so much so that I felt guilty eating fried chicken. I felt as though the breading itself could have used more seasoning, but I'm cutting them some slack because the place has only been open for a short time. The waffle was crisp around the edges and light and airy in the middle. Easy to overlook, it acts as sort of a doily to the chicken. I dug the waffle, but wished it had a little more leavening agent- it was sort of flat for me. And they have a bunch of sauces, which makes it a perfect place for someone who LOVES condiments (speaking of which I heard a pickle is not a condiment-odd). My waitress was extremely helpful in walking me through the menu, and wasn't shy about telling me to steer away from a few things. Contrary to some other yelpers, I felt like she knew the food, or at least she was a great actress and had me fooled. Favorite interaction with her was when she dropped off the check and said, "I'm not rushing you outta here, I just want to go outside for a cigarette." HILARIOUS! How perfect?! I mean common, would this fly at other establishments around town? Probably not. But it's Chawffles! Anything goes.

text: I usually like to wait to review a place Ive been to. Let the experience marinate and maybe wring a good tale out of it. In this case, I feel like I need to get the warning out soon, that this food was horrible. I like to think that even if I hadnt eaten good BBQ at places like Sweet Lucy's, Id know Basset's is the dog that its name conjures up. I first noticed Bassets, after I had already placed my order at 5 Guys and I was disappointed I didnt see it earlier. I had made a note to go back and try it and now Im disappointed that I did. One of the stars I gave it, is for the sheer fact that someone opened up something non- chineseburgerpizzadeli in the food court. I hate to discourage the good idea of fast food BBQ, but my God, it still has to be edible! I should have known by the price, that it was sub-par. It was only about $6-$7 bucks for 2 meat 2 side- a good deal for human food, but a bad deal for dog food. I got Ribs and Brisket with Mac and slaw. The edible part of the "rib" (taking a closer look, im not sure if that meat was either beef or pork) was unchewable and all else was fat. The brisket looked and tasted like fancy feast cat food ( dont ask me how I know). The mac n cheese was bland and the slaw was acrid and I still have the bad aftertaste in my mouth as I write. The other star is because the service was quick, friendly and efficient. Again, I hate to discourage this concept. I hope my experience was an anomaly. I will never order the things I got from there again. That said, the fries looked good (you cant mess up fries, can you?) and the pulled pork sandwich looked decent and may be a great alternative to the usual food court fare. I will have nightmares, involving the origin of those ribs, but I havent given up hope on this BBQ concept. Demand better choices , from our fast food, but also demand quality ingredients. If I can do it at home, they can do it in the restraunt.
label: NEG

text: The article in todays NOLA.COM has compelled me to recall and write this review for Kitchen Witch. KW is an amazing cook book and food bookstore. Completely independent, the proprietors work hard to offer what others cannot. Cook and food books of every genre, with a strong emphesis on local. They are having a party/signing this weekend for a dearly loved local chef, featuring his original red bean and rice recipe for us to eat. This store is also dog friendly. I have often brought in books and cooking tchotkies for them to add to their display and merchandising schemes. Its fun to see something that was once yours in a display case for the rest of the world to see. I am also secretly thrilled about tonights party/signing, as I have 2 Marc Marino's (mural paintings) myself, and he was often a guest in my home, many years ago, If memory still serves, Marc also created that huge mural in the courtyard of Molly's. I am glad that Kitchen Witch and Marc Marino have joined forces for what promises for an incredible weekend of event. I

text: We went back here for dinner this time and I have to give it 4 stars again. I had the Old Country Lasagna which though tasty lacked the Italian sausage taste the menu described. We all shared the golden nuggets with the soy chicken is simply amazing. My wife had the Stuffed Pasta Magnifica which was magnificent. The stuffed pasta was very creamy and full of flavor. Our Friends had the Linguini with Italian Meatballs which was a little light on the sauce but themeatlessballs were a little crunchy on the outside and tasty on the inside and the Thai Vegetable Curry which was beautiful to look at and quite tasty. We decided to have some desert. My wife and shared a piece of chocolate peanut butter pie which was good and peanut buttery but lacked in some way. Our friends had the Carrot cake which was out of this world! The "cream cheese" frosting was spot on. Lovin' Spoonfuls gets it right on so many levels. Healthy vegan fare which is quite affordable. They still need to drop the temperature in the place 2 degrees to 76 instead of 78 but otherwise this place is quickly becoming one of my family's favorite spots for a meal out.

text: I went with a few colleagues to this location for drinks. With plenty of options from which to choose, including the Buffalo Billiards next door, we opted for this, mainly because of the hype, and because there was no cover charge. When you walk through the door, you notice that Coyote Ugly takes advantage of the movie bearing the same name; merchandise litters the front lobby area before you walk into the real bar. I honestly felt a little raunchy walking around. All of the tables and chairs face the bar, where you're treated to a song-and-dance number all the time. The night we went was apparently "amateur night" or "audition night" or something; most of the girls dancing atop the bar that evening were auditioning for a job there. On the microphone and over the loud speakers was another young lady, emceeing the entire thing. Now, this can go on for about five minutes before the screaming into the mic and imploring patrons to buy the girls shots can get annoying. This actually went on the entire time we were there... thirty minutes. So why would I be there for thirty minutes when I would rather run a cheese grater up and down my face? Well, it's a novelty act, for starters. There were more than a few tourists hanging out with us, and they were having fun. Also, the drink prices weren't that bad, to be honest, unless you count the $20 body shot I saw someone at the bar do. However, after thirty minutes, you realize that you can pay just as much for drinks, avoid a cover charge at the door, and not be scarred for life.
label: NEG

text: The Duck Deli is a barbecue restaurant on East Butler Avenue (careful when pulling in or leaving- people drive a bit fast on the straightaway there). We tried a variety of barbecue foods (pulled pork, chicken, ribs, wings) there, and liked them all very much except the beef which did not live up to the others. The hamburger was pretty good, but the strong suit here is definitely the barbecue. The sides were good, too: the hush puppies were among the best we've ever had - not those hard, frozen things many restaurants serve. I also liked the mac-and-cheese, smashed potatoes, potato-and-corn fritter and onion rings. The fries were OK. The service was friendly, and a special request for something not on the menu was happily accommodated. (The menu lists several wraps, but not a barbecue chicken wrap.) Our server could have checked on us a little more, but she certainly didn't disappear, either. Portions on the sampler platters were generous, so we ended up over-ordering. Assuming a more realistic order, we estimated a cost of about $11 per person, maybe more if everyone orders barbecue. Note that drink refills are not free.
label: POS

text: Drove down the day before my birthday to find out if this sandwich was worth a road trip. I'll take a road trip for a decent meal, and the roast pork sandwich looked, on TV at least, like it might qualify. And since cheesesteaks are already road-trip-worthy, I figured even if this sandwich was a washout, it wouldn't take but a couple of minutes to track down a cheesesteak to salvage the trip. The Reading Terminal Market was packed the Saturday afternoon of the trip, but while I stood on line (only waited about 10 minutes, which is probably half the time I was expecting to wait) my girlfriend scored us a table right in front of Tommy DiNic's, so I didn't have to walk far once I got hold of the roast pork with broccoli rabe and sharp provolone that had inspired the previous 2 hours of driving. Was it worth the time and trouble? Totally. It was one of the best sandwiches I've ever had, and will definitely join the list of road trip foods. You have to try it. Hop in the car right now and aim yourself at Philly. You won't regret it.

text: Headed down to Santa Barbara to meet up with friends, so we checked out Yelp to find a fun delicious place to eat dinner on one of the nights. Was thrilled to see all the great reviews for this place. Sorry to say, our experience was lacking. Luckily it was Sunday evening and the place only had 3 tables occupied, so we got a table immediately- good so far! Our server introduced herself, she even pointed our her photo for us in the menu- very helpful- and familiarized us with the menu as we were first (and last) timers. She told us they work as a team and we could expect to be waited on by all the staff in the place. That was the last time we were approached without having the flag someone down. Maybe they were lacking in enthusiasm having only a handful of tables, who knows- but we never had water refilled or rolls or drinks without having to ask someone to come over. Now onto the "authentic" food. Having been to New Orleans many times, I was thrilled at the opportunity to experience some of these eats without having to make the trip. The crawfish appetizer was nothing but doughy small and tasteless, our prawn appetizer was good, but nothing you wouldn't get anywhere else. We ordered the platters so we could sample a bunch of stuff, again lacking in flavor, really nothing special. I was really counting on the bread pudding to save the day- disappointment- like a big cinnabon you get at the airport! had to ask for the check, and we hit the road. oh well, so much for dropping $160 on an ordinary meal. the next day we opted for good old mexi- and drove to Taqueria Rincon Alteno in Capenteria, a spot we always hit on our way to so-cal - feasted on the al pastor burrito for $5 and loved it.

text: Pagano's has the worst Cheesesteak in Philly! I don't know how it got such a great reputation. Why is it so awful you ask? Well let me break it down for you. They use a very cheap grade of meat and when they cook it, they chop it up so fine that it becomes pulverised till it's like the consistency of baby food. It's chopped and grilled to death! Pagno's gives you a lot of meat-which is what the budget-minded consumer loves, hence the reputation. But again it's a cheap grade of meat so I'm definitely not feeling it. Then they use a regular Amoroso roll! And any Philly sandwich aficionado will tell you that this roll will not stand up to a lot of cheap meat. The result is a sloppy, gooey, smelly hot mess. I ripped it, so skip it!
label: NEG

text: For our last evening of the ski trip, we wanted to have a nice dinner, but the steakhouse at the Atlantis Casino had a 1 hour wait. Bistro Napa was actually our 2nd choice, but it worked out because it was a GREAT meal! I tried a similar splurge dinner in Hawaii at the Four Seasons in Kona, and honestly, this meal was better, and half the price! The menu has some pretty good variety. Our party of four got scallops, pork chop, hunter's stew over pasta, and prime rib. The side dishes are very large and we got lobster mac & cheese, wild mushrooms and a twice baked potato to share. Everything was excellent! Our server and bus person must have checked on 15 times to make sure that we were happy, that we had enough water, that everything was cooked to our liking, and to make sure we had the appropriate cutlery. We ordered a wine by the glass, and they don't just bring you a glass already poured. No no no - that's not fancy enough. The server brought a small carafe, and then poured it at the table into the wine glass. (Some poor person in the back probably has to wash a million of these things.) We ended up not ordering dessert, but if carrot cake had been on the menu I would have been all over it. However, I cannot stress enough what great service we got from John. Every aspect of the meal was handled so nicely. When I ordered a salad but didn't want the blue cheese dressing, he got me a dressing that is made on premises with Riesling, and it was fantastic! I ordered the prime rib, and he was nice enough to ask if I wanted horseradish. I know that not everyone likes that stuff (I do). When the entrees came out, we were missing 1 thing, and I said, "Do you know if we have 1 more side dish coming? I'm looking for the twice baked potato." I guess some people pull attitude and feel that-if-the-server-wasn't-on-his-game-enough-to-bring-it-then-I-don't-want-it. So he was nice enough to ask "Do you still want it?" I answered, "Absolutely!" and I guess the kitchen had it ready but forgot to put it on his tray, because he returned with it a minute later. I saw him with dessert menus in his hand at least once, but it was clear that we were still working on our food, so he left us alone. And even though we didn't end up ordering dessert, he gave us 2 small dishes of cotton candy, which lets out the inner child in you after a fairly fancy meal. This was a really great meal that ended up less than $50 per head. If you're sitting in John's section, you're in good hands and I'm certain that you will enjoy your meal. 4.5 stars.
label: POS

text: Banana on Walnut, you appear to be so beautiful at first, second, and even third glance. This giant BR is exceptionally spacious & features both the coveted shoes and petites sections. However. I have been to every BR in the PA-NJ area, and I hate to tell you folks that this place is consistently pricing their goods higher than the other locations. I'm talking same exact items at the same exact time. Formula: other BR costs less; this one costs more. Evil management figures that the Broad Street shoppers are suckers who are allergic to their money. For that nastiness, this BR gets one star. And if you really are allergic to your money & need to get rid of as much as possible, you can do that most easily if you steer clear of lunch hours [especially on Fridays] when this place gets mobbed.

text: I know there are a gazillion reviews for Fido already, and most are glowing, but I have to put in my two cents on this place. I'll preface by saying, I'm not a coffee drinker. So this might sway my two star rating but only by a bit. I never wanted to go near Fido because I felt it was too hippie-trendy, always packed with pompous "do-gooders" even though it's questionable what good they were actually doing by hanging out in a coffee house all day, and the drinks were too expensive. But, after persuasion by about six friends that were going for breakfast one day, I felt I would give it a shot. Here's my take, and I've been back once since then. For lunch. Breakfast: good enough, I got an egg sandwich with basil and tomato, along with some hash browns that were just decent. It took absolutely forever though, so I'm glad I was with good company and was distracted. By myself though, I probably couldn't have handled the wait. Since I don't drink coffee, I got Diet Coke. Yes, luckily they have it. But it's in a can. Oh well, can't ask much for a coffee house I guess. A little overpriced for the food I ate too. Let it slide that time though. Lunch, about a month later: I came here because I was in the area, and needed to pick up lunch to go. Line was pretty long, and took me about 15 minutes to order. I ordered a salad--lettuce only--with grilled chicken and cheese on top. That was all. Nothing else. After another 20 minutes, and seeing people in line after me get their food, I asked the server about my order. He said he would check on it. Never came back. 10 minutes after that, I asked another person (I wasn't so nice this time--let's face it, I was starving by this point!) about it and he went right back and brought it out. He said it had been there for a while. Nice. No apology or anything. So, after a grand total of 45 minutes and 11 undeserving dollars later, I walked out with limp lettuce and sub-par grilled chicken. Oh--and they forgot the cheese. I guess I'm the Fido review bitch, but I won't be back. Guess if you like coffee you could check it out for that, but for food don't bother.
label: NEG

text: LOVE mercato... it's the epitome of the great BYOBs that Philly has to offer! It's definitely one of the things I miss most about my former home. Visiting friends this past weekend, we needed a place to eat and have some wine. Mercato was my first choice. The four of us all got the tasting menu which consists of your choice of appetizer, half a pasta, entree, and dessert, all for $48. Every time I come back, I'm reminded of what good deals Philly offers compared to NYC. This is on top of being able to bring your own wine on the cheap! We got a few bottles from the PA Wine and Spirits shop on 13th & Chestnut, and proceeded with the gluttony. This made for the perfect beginning for a night out. Here were some of our favorites of the evening: Antipasti platter- what a great selection of antipasti, not the usual stuff that you get at other inferior italian places. Mussels and Clams- juicy, garlicky, with sauce perfect for dipping with toast. Orichiette w/ sausage- one of my favs from Mercato, the sauce is amazing! House Pasta of the day- Fettucine- this pasta dish was perfection. Veal- Sooo much flavor, and so tender, I can't stop thinking about it. Cioppino- such a great medley of seafood, very fresh and rich tasting. Mercato, will you ever consider opening an outpost in NYC?

text: Just to preface my opinion - so you know where I am coming from... So two factors have served as an obstacle to eating at Chew Man Chu, despite it being a mere two blocks from my house. (1) I was mourning the loss of Du Jour and it's amazing coconut cream french toast. (2) I am always wary of fusion asian restaurants. I like my chinatown & ktown & viet-town restaurants despite their curt service & untidy appearance. I know the food that I cook and the food that I grew up with so I generally don't like americanized interpretations. But that being said. I'll pretty much eat anything and every once in a while I'll order the occasional chinese take out or try my hand at "fusion". Ambiance: Sleek and mod decor. The tables are a bit close together though. I wouldn't mind coming here for a drink and maybe an appetizer maybe.. Service: Pretty attentive and friendly. Food: The menu was a fusion of various asian cuisines so we chose to eat family style so we could sample the different menu offerings. The Wonton Shrimp Soup was clean and simple but a bit too basic for $6. Their Pork & Shrimp Dumplings were rated on skin and filling. Skin was done remarkably well! We were impressed with the chewiness but also the nice crisp outside. The filling texture was tough and a little gelatinous (for lack of a better word..?) I would not recommend the Crispy Chicken rolls. It was chicken breast rolled in plain spring roll wrapper with a spicy aioli on the side. This dish was just so disappointingly boring. The Tofu & Vegetable Moo Shu was agreed to be the best dish. The filling was right on and their hoisin sauce was not too sweet. It was nice to see that their Moo shu pancakes were homemade though a bit thick. I enjoyed it but my co-eaters were not as thrilled. Singapore Curry Mai Fun was also on par but salty. The curry flavors were distinct but not overpowering. If I go next time, I think the curry dishes are what I will go for next! We had complimentary donuts that seemed to be either filled with sesame paste or red bean paste. We forgot to ask about the filling. that was a nice plus to end the meal. Drinks: The cocktail menu looked interesting so I will be sure to hit them up in Round 2. Overall: Not terrible but not anything special for the price. text: Mondo should change its name to MUNDANE! Restaurant is terribly hot and uncomfortable. Not even drinking cocktails in the bar while we waited helped that. Yet after waiting in the bar, you are escorted back the even hotter and noisier dining area (which needs to be scaled down and converted into more kitchen space). After waiting 1 1/2 hours in the bar one would think that the waitress would take your order or perhaps bring us some bread, but instead we waited for 1/2 hour before we saw a single (yes single) slice of bread. Finally our appetizers arrived. The tomato salad and cerviche were good, but the fried eggplant was over-cooked mushed that was overpowered by an excessively lemoned aioli sauce. After another 30 minutes our entrees trickled out one AFTER the literally minutes apart. I like Tim G. had the pygmy lamb which had o.k. flavor, but literally was the size of an amuse bouche with mismatched ravioli. The Etouffee had no seasoning and the Kobe steak was served undercooked. We attempted to send it back, but all we got was the same cut literally microwaved and sent back out. They whole thing had no pink and just brown throughout . I was shocked, definitely the sign of an inexperienced kitchen or perhaps the "World Flavor" they are going for at Mondo is "famine". Sadly we weren't even offered a comp showing that the wait staff was almost as inexperienced as the kitchen. My recommendation would be to shrink the menu to a few good dishes and cut down the dining space so the customers can actually be served. My experience has been more common than one would think and I am sorry to say that if Mondo were to close, this is one case that could not be blamed on BP.

text: Panting like John Belushi for Blues, I was for a patio with beer & lo! live blues! I heard good things about the restaurant that occupied this space prior...but it couldn't have been this good! And, what a use of space, and not that much space. Inventive use all around: front dining room is a tight squeeze but intimate, and, well, they're serving food so good there'll be wait, and, Indy, kind of really needs a tiny bistro where people are spilling over each other and people wait outside. Speaking of outside...front patio...back patio. Patio bar. When I see two bars so close to one another in one establishment, I get all fuzzy inside -- especially if one of them is a cabana style outdoors bar. Really...I could sit outside of that bar & feel like I'm in Cabo: outdoor bar, patio, music, people (not to mention that shimmery canal ;) !) Awnaw Claus's gone Northside of Indy, finally! I've seen some other Southside, downtown joints have Indy's Sausage King (Abe Froman's got nothin' on Claus!) and now, Flatwater brings him uptown with their "Best of the Wurst" plate of sliced sausage, brie, nuts & pears. It's distinct that Flatwater is local and supports all things local -- from Claus to Sun King beer. Stellar resiliency by the bartender to get a customer to try the Sun King, then said customer requests Miller Lite, and the Bartender then proceeds to really clarify what Sun King has to offer. Deal struck. Customer quaffs the Cream Ale! What a victorious bartender! The menu ranges from Walleye like your Uncle caught & served back in '87 to ribs to mediterranean chicken drenched in artichokes & kalamatas to pork tenderloin, pork medallions ("do I wear them around my neck?" "I will, doggonit.") pulled pork to shrimp tacos to a veggie french onion soup. Yes, a veggie french onion soup (that's the dream isn't it? at least it was for me when I was vegetarian). Okay it has cheese. But cheese is a fruit, right? The servers, cooks, owners, bartenders, are all together on something: they're good people. Really. Laid back and hospitable and on top of it. Speaking of the Top -- this is the top of the list of Indy's new eateries & imbiberies. Get it!

text: I've been looking forward to this. I've been stuck with a rental car this week due to my car getting a wicked scratch down the side. I called the rental company's roadside service and explained it was something that was not an immediate threat and that I could wait until I got back to TN. The agent instructed me to find a Goodyear or Firestone station, explain I was with Enterprise, and to hand them my rental agreement; they would take care of the rest. I knew that this location was a Goodyear store and pulled in. I went up to the counter, introduced myself and politely explained the situation. I handed the guy behind the counter the rental agreement, which he stared at like it was written in sanskrit. This piece of paper ain't payin' me, so I guess you need to call someone and figure this out." I was a little taken aback and said, "I imagine there is some sort of process or contract you guys have with Enterprise, I am sure someone can sort this out." "Well, it will take us a couple of hours to get to the patch, so you have plenty of time to figure out what you're gonna do." I called Enterprise; they apologized profusely and sent me to Firestone location who immediately took care of me and knew what was going on. The head waitress (hostess?) is always entertaining to watch - I don't think I have EVER seen her smile. However, apart from her and the surly attitude, everyone has been very good. The food is as consistent and good as the service. The baked goat cheese with bacon and tomatoes, served with bread, is always absolutely delicious as a starter. They make a mean Cocquille St. Jacques and although I haven't tried it, their steak was praised by my fellow diners. While they may not vary their menu often, they have a wide range of seasonal desserts and the selection is never quite the same. Further, their menu items are very classic and lovely - why fix something that isn't broken? I thoroughly enjoy Cafe Select and, quite frankly, the negative reviews here surprise me. text: NOTE: We only had the ramen, we did not try the sushi or the Koren food, which everyone seems to like. We will give this place one more try for those items but for now, this is my review on just the ramen. Ordered: Seafood Ramen $9.50 / Tonkatsu Ramen (Pork Cutlet) $7.95 Being someone who adores ramen, especially Tonkatsu Ramen, I was so excited to finally come here that it makes me cry hot tears of disappointment to have to give this establishment a low star rating. Simply put, it was terrible. Worse than terrible. More like never-ever-come-back-for-the-ramen horrendous. We were seated right away by a rather dour gentlemen who just pointed to our seats and grunted and went back to watching a little TV he had by his podium. Not an auspicious start. There was a couple at the sushi boat area (I'm bummed to read that the floating sushi is just for show!) and there was another couple on the other side of the restaurant. Other than that, it was really empty for a Friday night. Which makes me wonder why we had to wait so long for our order to be taken. Then we waited a long time for our two bowls of soup. All told we were there nearly an hour before the food came. Not cool. When the soup came I was starving and it looked great. I have uploaded photos to show how beautiful the ramen was. We squealed with delight over the unique wooden spoons and the lovely amount of seafood and pork. Then we took our first excited bite. Which became a very disappointed and rather difficult swallow. Perhaps I'm spoiled from having eaten at the best ramen places that Las Vegas, Los Angeles, Sacramento, San Francisco, Portland and Seattle have to offer. All I know is when I go to those other restaurants, the ramen, tho unique to each establishment and thus differing in depth and flavor, always tastes fantastic. This ramen did not. The broth was exceptionally bland and flavorless. The noodles were inedible. The seafood varied between mushy and rubbery, and tasted so "fishy" that it simply could not be eaten. The pork was so nasty and tough we could not even attempt to gnaw through it. It, too, had an "off" flavor. Maybe from the "off" broth. Thus, after waiting an hour to eat, a few minutes after reviving our meal we sadly pushed away our still-full bowls, asked for the bill, paid it and left our food sitting on the table, mostly uneaten. Now, remember how I said we were really hungry? Well, dining elsewhere that night was not an option because here is the kicker. Within a very short time of leaving the restaurant, both myself and my dinner companion became violently ill. I'll spare you the gory details, but suffice it to say thankfully our hotel was close by. Something was seriously not right about that ramen. I'm not going to give this place 1 star, because I did not try any other food items; perhaps the sushi is great, or perhaps the Koren food is as wonderful as I hear it is. So I'll give it two stars, that second star being one of hope. We will come back and try some of the other items yelped as being good and we'll do an update on this review. But I can confidently say that I will never, ever again make an attempt to eat the ramen here. And if I do try something else...well, let's just say I'll make sure I get a hotel really close by. Just in case.

text: Being an out-of-towner, Honey's seemed to me to be a really great neighborhood place at first glance. I believe I was correct. On my co-workers recommendation, we ordered the cheese fries. But it did not matter! They tasted INCREDIBLE. The cheese was plentiful and perfectly melted, the bacon was not overwhelming and the ranch dipping sauce was fantastic. We also ordered a grilled cheese to share which was tasty. Their menu is totally unique and fascinating. I really do wish that I had more opportunities to visit Honey's to try more things on the menu but, if I'm going to be honest with myself, I'd probably keep coming back for the cheese fries.

Waitress was embarrassed. Management apathetic. Stay away. Stay far, far, far away. This is a REALLY BAD tourist trap. However, if you want a Hurricane to walk with they do make a mean one. ($21 for regular pedicure) They got us in right away and did a good job. Pedicure included nice plush chairs that massage (although we did have a good giggle over not having any idea how to work the controls and they just kept massaging our butts for some odd reason!) callus scrubbing, cuticle removal, and a little bit of massage when they put on the lotion. The polish was applied expertly and quickly, and I'm going to say we were in and out in less than 45 minutes. (actual pedicure part probably took around 30 mins) Personally, I'm not looking for a pedicure to be long and luxurious and last an hour, but I'm well aware there are people out there who want that, and for them, I would say this is not your place. But for me, I just want to be in and out quickly and feel the job was done effectively. Oh, and dirt cheap certainly helps. :) I will go there again for sure. Oh! Also, I did see them thoroughly scrubbing all their tools and the tubs after we were finished, which is always a worry for me, so that's a big plus in their favor. Be aware they take cash only for anyone who is thinking of going.

No ketchup or anything until we were half-way through the meal when she FINALLY came back around and we asked for the ketchup. Nothing about the texture, taste or consistency made me feel out right revulsion- but neither did it convince me that paying $10 + tip for a dozen cookies would ever be worth while again. I can go to Sam's Club and buy like 50 soft-baked cookies for less than $10. True, I'd have to put forth the ENORMOUS EFFORT to get off my laurels, but in the end I think I'd have the same experience after 2 minutes in my own oven (or, more like, 5 seconds in the microwave or toaster oven). text: Okay, so I've been to Pueblo Nuevo 3 times since my first review, and I'm sad to say that my opinion has changed. While I still love the beef tongue tacos, that's about the only thing worth visiting Pueblo Nuevo for, in my opinion. Went again this afternoon for a quick lunch. I nibbled from Andy's Pueblo Nuevo special, which included refried beans, rice, a pork taco, beef empanada, and pork burrito. While it was a great deal (all that food for 8 bucks? Wowza!) It was all very very BLAND. One look around at the clientele answered all of my questions about Pueblo Nuevo. Without going into too many details, it's pretty obvious that they cater to a certain *type* of diner. And the packed restaurant tells me that they do it well. But...I crave a more authentic experience than that. Give me some spice, Pueblo Nuevo! Give me some authenticity! I know they have it in them; the beef tongue tacos, delicious horchata, and yummy churros tell me that they KNOW how to prepare authentic Mexican dishes well. But the blandness of the remaining items on the menu tells another story. I'm going to throw this out there: as it is, Pueblo Nuevo reminds me of a sit-down Taco Bell. And while I love Taco Bell on occasion, when I go to a restaurant, I'm expecting just a little more than that. I'll probably visit again for the beef tongue tacos, but not for anything else. Try harder, Pueblo Nuevo.

text: Zeitgenössische Kunst an den Mann und die Frau zu bringen, ist nicht immer einfach. Erleichtert wird der Zugang, wenn die Kunstwerke nicht in einem leblosen Museum ausgestellt werden, sondern sie gut arrangiert in einem wunderschönen Landschaftspark zu bestaunen sind. Grounds for Sculpture bietet aber noch viel mehr als einfaches Betrachten von Kunstobjekten in hübscher (Kunst-) Landschaft: Manch verstecktes Objekt will im Gebüsch entdeckt werden, in den Gebäuden auf dem Gelände finden regelmäßig musikalische Veranstaltungen statt, und ein Restaurant und ein Cafe laden zur Erholung der müden Füße ein. Es fällt mir schwer einzelne Ausstellungsstücke besonders zu würdigen. Im Gedächtnis bleiben aber besonders die Bronzeguss-Kopien J. Seward Johnson's von Manets Déjeuner Sur l'Herbe und Renoirs Luncheon of the Boating Party (siehe Photos). Da kann man tatsächlich in einem Bild herumlaufen Es gibt aber viele viele richtige Schätze zu entdecken. Man kann problemlos einen ganzen Tag auf dem Gelände zubringen. Zwischen den einzelnen Kunstwerken erholt sich das Auge beim Betrachten der Landschaft. Die Website bietet umfassende Informationen über die Sammlung, Sonderausstellungen und das aktuelle Programm.

text: This oft forgotten south county park jewel has one of the best park views in town. The park is located on the bluffs overlooking the Mississippi River. I love coming here to sit on a bench and read and occasionally get lost in the view when my book isn't holding my interest. There are ton of pavillions, perfect for picnicking (they can be reserved through the county park service). Some of the pavillions have electrical outlets and bbq pits included. It makes for a nice situation for any family picnic. There is a hiking trail, but it's not super long and not incredibly challenging. It is, however, perfect, for a leisurely hike with fantastic views of the river at random turns. Also, a fully stocked lake that, with appropriate permit, allows for public fishing round out the features of this park. The park isn't huge, it doesn't offer a lot of paths or have a ton of sports fields, but it's great for a picnic or for a family gathering.

text: This Holiday Inn Express needs a huge facelift. From the moment we walked into our room, it was a scary adventure. BATHROOM BEWARE: A bathroom door that barely (with some adjustments to the door) passed the toilet to close. Our bath tub had these red spots on the bottom that would not come up. You could also see circles of what appeared to be a shower mat that used to be there. PRO: Our room had a microwave and fridge which is not advertised on the website so that was a good surprise. If you are trying to squeeze more people into the beds, this hotel has a basic mattress and we were able to push our beds together to maximize the space. The rooms face other buildings which means the rooms are quiet and away from any noise. The LOCATION is close to Bourbon street which is a big plus. CON: The room was uneven and you had to walk about 4-5 inches up to the room from the closet/door/bathroom area. The provided table was too small for even 1 person to sit and work on between the phone, books, etc from the hotel. There was a definite need for new carpet and I would definitely bring shower shoes, flip-flops or anything to protect my feet in this room. PARKING: Parking was at the Hilton Garden Inn around the corner. Parking is paid in cash and upfront. This has to be 1 of the tightest structures as you make your way up. Get back too late on a weekend night and it'll be hard to find a spot. On Friday night and Saturday evening, we had to take the only available spot in the entire structure (above 5th floor). Business center is a joke. Bring your laptop and use the complimentary free internet. Traditional complimentary Holiday Inn Express breakfast except they have a egg & cheese instead of just egg which makes it convenient and the lines move quickly. The hotel does recommend going to Oceana for dinner. That was the best thing about staying here. Fitness center consisted of 5 cardio machines that look outside toward the front door and street. The pool is on the 6th floor and was a 7' by 12' block that was a joke. For very competitive prices, I would consider the Hilton Garden Inn around the corner.

text: Decided to hit Joe's up for some breakfast - especially after seeing their ad on TV. I ordered the veggie omelet and the BF ordered the pancake sandwich. When she brought out our meals, the BF realized his eggs were scrambled not over-medium, as ordered. The waitress apologized and took the plate back, leaving my omelet and no utensils for me to eat with. No biggie, I sat and waited for the corrected eggs to arrive and decided to pick out some of the crispy potatoes on my plate. Waitress comes back with not only the corrected pancake plate but a new omelet for me - OK, whatever! The BF said that the waitress then took my original omelet and gave it to someone else! (So sorry, to the recipient!) Anyway, to get down to the basics of why I gave Joe's one star: - Veggie Omelet was completely inedible! Didn't even look like an omelet, more like a scramble. Eggs were overcooked, veggies were sub-par and frozen. - Potatoes or their "home fries" were greasy and old and new potatoes were mixed together. text: I love coming here to work with my friends and who doesn't like a nice warm soup bowl on a rainy day? That and I am a huge fan of Panera Bread/St. Louis Bread Co. And this location is quite comfortable and clean. Food tips/opinions: - When you get the combo deal, changing your soup to a bread bowl doesn't cost another penny (at least it didn't for me) - Be adventurous with the salads- they're yummy! - I loveee their baguettes and bread (I'm a carbo-lover), so that extra $3-4 bucks for a baguette? I'm on it! - Their dessert stuff isn't all that amazing.
label: POS

text: Well I used to recommend this place but after going the last couple of times I have been dissapointed. I ordered the shrimp bucatini and it literally tasted just like eating tomato sauce. It had no blend of flavors or any discernable quality. The crab cakes are about the only thing here that I would still recommend.
label: NEG

text: I love love love their Grilled Chicken and Brie Capellini (Angel Hair). I would consider a trip to Santa Barbara just to get that pasta. The dish is simple with grilled chicken, brie, tomatoes, basil, garlic, and olive oil. The cheese makes the pasta so gooey and brielicious. I've tried to recreate it at home but it's just not the same. Another thing I like about this place is that each table is complete with paper tablecloth and crayons. That always made my inner child happy.
label: POS

text: Oh Fido...your delicious food and coffee added with friendly staff (at least the cashiers, I usually stick w/ the brewed stuff so I don't really interact w/ the baristas) makes the insane line totally worth it. And you are really overdoing it with the Green Chile Mac and Cheese. I had that for lunch today and kind of want it for lunch tomorrow, too. Seriously, though. The abundance of choices for vegetarians/vegans/gluten-free folks is impressive. The desserts are exceptional (who knew that beets could be so delicious!) and the daily specials are inventive and capitalize on fresh, seasonal, local ingredients. I am looking forward to the ice-cream/coffee place next door opening (Hot and Cold, I think??) as it should make getting a quick cup on-the-go easier. My missing fifth star is because I've frequently had to pass up Fido because the line was too long to wait for a cup to go.
label: POS

text: Not a happy camper after my first and last experience here. I've been very busy/stressed/tired looking and wanted a gentle glow to brighten myself. The attendant was helpful but the machine malfunctioned on first try. No misting but was blasted on my tummy by a greenish spray. Sounds wimpy but freaked me out. The attendant said that was a first and told me she'd put me thru again. She did and it went off without a hitch. I asked repeatedly if my pale skin would develop any glow. She said yes she is naturally pale and its fail proof. Well it did not work so I was scrambling last minute to add some glow to my skin for an evening out on the town. I did this to save time and relax and was instead uber stressed last minute. They offer zero refunds ever so that should've clued me in. I'll stick to Jergen's tanning creme and Nars Body Glow from now on.
label: NEG

text: This review would be helpful to all my vegetarian friends. We ordered pineapple fried rice with tofu and pad thai noodles. Rice was okay but very less in quantity compare to vegetables in this dish. all you see is broccoli. Pad thai noodles were testless when you eat alone. We need to add some chilli sauce to make it eatable. This place is okay to dine when you dont have any other option on hand.
label: NEG

text: Once, I got a massage at an "express-spa" at the Philadelphia Airport. Yeah, the idea was good in theory - but I pretty much got fleeced for getting patted on the back for 20 minutes. That's kind of how I feel about Toppers. The place is all good in theory - it has four floors of spa-indulgences with a hair salon on the first floor. There's a ample sized change room, the decor is way dated (lots of old ornate wall paper everywhere) and they have that weird elevator music playing everywhere. I observed a lot of the clientele was sporting those match-y velour track suits. The only reason I've been there (more than once, I'd hate to admit it) is because I've been redeeming gift certificates. It's almost a cruel gift having to return to this place. The experience is very corporate, their staff inexperienced and not very friendly. I checked in on the first floor by the not-so friendly receptionist, then sent to the 2nd floor where I was supposed to be "taken care of" by the "host" - that didn't happen, so when the esthetician finally found me, she took me to disrobe in the tiny treatment room for my facial. Like the massages and manicure I've had before here, I wasn't terribly impressed with it. They used Dermatologica products which was nice, but the experience wasn't calming. The room was the size of a prison cell and the horrible elevator music was turned up to 11. At the end of my treatment, I was given tap water and sent on my way. Wow, that's pretty high-fallutin' after I got a treatment that cost over $150. Stay away from this corporate spa. Service is bland, disingenuous and generic. Treatments are over-priced and there are plenty of other spas you can take your pennies too.
label: NEG

text: I'm still trying to determine if my lackluster dining experience at Cochon was because I simply don't appreciate Cajun cuisine, or if we ordered the wrong items off the menu. Whatever the reason, this place left me cold. And I think I can go through life now without needing to sample alligator meat again. Even the pork cheeks were kinda funky tasting, and mixed with some white beans and sauce, just wasn't my bag. The atmosphere is your standard modern cavernous dining hall, with an open kitchen. A bit generic. Service was fine. Our one good experience was dessert--the best pineapple upside down cake I've ever had.
label: NEG

text: This place is a mess... First of all I had to comb the parking lot for a cart as no one working there brings them up front. The store is dusty and dirty... "Fresh" produce and meats are either completely underripe or a day from expiration. There is very little variety for dry goods and toiletries. Oh and it's a NIGHTMARE getting out of there!!!!!!!!! Expect to spend at least 45 minutes in line.
label: NEG

text: A Belleville Classic! Unfortunately. Fischer's has been in business as a restaurant and catering location since 1941 and it doesn't seem like they've made a single update since then. The food is bland, the atmosphere is non-existent, but people still flock here because they've been going there for years. You know that restaurant that you keep going to over and over and you justify every visit with, "Well, it wasn't that great last time, but..." That statement is the epitome of this place. Here's what I say we do: don't go to Fischer's; send them a message that its time for an update.
label: NEG

text: The Standard Tap definitely proved to be a perfect spot for a Happy Hour gathering. Huge bar areas, damn good food, an awesome dedication to local beers to the point that even Guinness wasn't available, and awesome music playing in the background. For the first time ever at a Yelp event I can say that Joy Division and M.I.A. where playing in the background, and people like Chrissy R. and Carrie WEREN'T responsible for it. sounds like a Winner to me. While waiting for more people to arrive I enjoyed a beer downstairs. The Victory 5 year and chill wooden decor rocked my socks. As more people arrived we promptly took over the back upstairs area and enjoyed some beers. Despite the rain I still tried to check out the outside deck and it definitely had an perfect view of outside NoLibs. I know where I'm sitting next time! Standard Tap is definitely the bar that best showcases the local craft beers. the fact that they don't serve any brew from outside the tri-state area is actually pretty admirable, and they actually manage to keep it pretty well rounded. The food also went above the standard pub fare. Yelpers were right because I definitely had the best portabello sandwich EVER! but next time I think I'm going to go for some of those mussels. damn did they look delish!
label: POS

text: One the perks of living in Wayne is having Great Harvest here. The breads and baked goods are great. I can't think of one of their breads I don't like-but I can think of two that deserve a mention here. The pumpkin-swirl and the apple crumb - both topped with a sweet covering- are awesome breads for french toast!. Who needs syrup! When you pay $4 at the supermarket, an extra $1 for a really great product doesn't seem too much to pay. Sadly, I recently received an email from them saying the current owners are looking to get out of the business in the near future. As this is a franchise operation, I'm not sure if they will sell to another local or not. I hope so. I'd miss the place if it closed.

text: It's not great, and it should be for the prices they charge. Everything was very tasty though, including a superb matzo ball soup and a veg lasagna. The female server was snooty as snooty gets, but the rest of the staff was very pleasant. We all have our bad days, but don't take it out on customers who are notorious overtippers! So--food gets 3 stars, but because of the snarky server, Sqwires gets only 2 stars from us.

text: The food is not worth the price...I had the chicken salad and fruit plate for lunch today and it was basically the equivalent of 3 cut up apples and less than 2 tablespoons of chicken salad on a massive bed of romaine. For $8 I hoped for a little more chicken salad and not so much lettuce/apples. Ah well...I also had the chicken orzo soup. It was very watery and had little flavor.

text: If you are a cyclist in the greater Trenton area, you should visit this place -- lots of high end gear, helpful and knowledgeable staff, and top notch service.

text: Of course any and every poster place is going to have hastily, mass-produced prints that every college freshman is going to putty onto their walls; you know the usual suspects, the two girls kissing, a Scarface poster and perhaps if you are lucky, there may even be an Audrey Hepburn or Jim Morrison poster there to meet the college quota. Despite that, I really enjoy this place. The vast majority of the posters are pretty cool and you can always find a decent knick-knack to toss onto your coffee table that will be sure to amuse your guests. The prices are fair, I'm not a poster connoisseur or anything like that, but there isn't anything extremely expensive here. I like the selection and could spend hours in here perusing what they have. Although, I always tend to feel a bit guilty when I am in here for a good amount of time looking at everything and then leave empty handed, I have to reassure myself that everyone on South Street is doing the exact same thing.

text: An indo place in my hood, finally! Now I can just walk down main st when I am craving some food of my motherland :) A small and intimate setting, with sweet indo-classical tunes playing in the background and friendly, eager to please staff. Totally love that it's a BYO too. We started with the fish pakoras which I thought was a unique app option ( usually you only ever have a veg or meat one). The fish was tender, cooked just right, with a crispy crunchy outside. There were already sauces on our table from the free 'paaper' we got, so that was our dipping sauces for the pakoras, but I feel like there could've been another sauce to accompany them as well. For dinner we tried the lamb vindaloo and shrimp korma. I loveee korma sauce. I'd eat a bucket of that stuff if I had the chance. This place did it just wonderfully. My hubby and I love spicy food as well, and we basically requested the waiter to make it as spicy as they could, and I can honestly say its one of the few times that I feel like they've actually delivered on the spicy I requested. And it made it so much more delicious too. Just a note: I think this place had a recent restaurant name change, so some of their menus still say Shaheen. No matter what they call it - I'll be eating there.
label: POS

text: We were told our wait would be 30 minutes.45 minutes later we were told it would be another 40 minutes.parking lot is huge but seating and waiting area is awful.Waitress was not friendly.Food portions were skimpy, especially kids meals.Very pricey.Nothing was very flavorful or all that good.Not worth the wait or the price.Then we were told there was a limit to how much bread we could have and they wouldnt take our 20 percent off coupon because we didnt all get drinks,2 people out of the 8 of us got waters!!!Wont be recommending this place.Too many other good choices out there for the money.
label: NEG

text: After cruising up and down State Street in Santa Barbara, I knew that I wanted to get away from the tourist traps to get something to eat. I saw the Paradise Cafe one block off the strip and noticed that there was a fair amount of people hiving lunch. I figured that while not all fancy and flashy, it must have something going for it. I was right. We sat outside on the patio. There is also a full service bar that has a dining area. The menu had a bit of everything and the service was good. I had the swordfish tacos and the rest of the group had a burger, beef tacos and an open face tri-tip sandwich. There were no complaints all the way around. Total bill for four with tip was $60.00. If I go back to SB or know of anyone that is going to SB, I will tell them about this place.
label: POS

text: We love Wahoo's!!!! We eat there on the regular. We just love the blackened fish tacos, with a side of guac and sour cream. They give you enough in one taco to make two and they give you two tortilla's per taco. Two for the price of one. We can have 6 split tacos with two beers for less than $15...Awesome!!! Chill atmosphere, good service and great cheap eats...and there's free parking in the back!

text: The staff are rude and seem to not care. Not a fan of the people that work at this location or the north location on St.Albert Trail. I've taken some clothes here and felt quite ripped off. They do not provide a breakdown of what they were giong to pay for each item, even though I took some high end brand names. the only reason I gave them two stars is because I like to shop here, just for the clothes I have gotten for my daughter. I ignore the staff and search for great deals, which can be found.

The owner looked at my mug and said, "How many ounces is this?" I said I didnt know, "maybe 16oz?" And then he charged me $2.50, which is $.50 extra, saying my mug was too big to be considered a small! I was dumbfounded. I don't particularly care for their chocolates because they are not freshly made there, but in a factory in South Bend. It takes a while before these chocolates go from being made to being displayed and eaten. Their chocolate covered nuts are lickable, oops, I mean, likeable... and I guess their lickable too! Note that only this downtown location has ice cream, and the only reason they have it is because this used to be a Rocky Mountain Chocolate Factory location.

text: We had an alright breakfast at Sambo's. Honestly, it is just like any other greasy spoon servin' up pancakes, bacon and eggs. The food was pretty bland, even the bacon tasted like it needed salt. I agree with Michaela about the hash browns, they were way under seasoned. I was served sour milk, but my server quickly took care of it. The service was fine, but the food was just regular diner food. I don't understand the glowing reviews unless those Yelpers gave equally radiant reviews to Denny's.
label: NEG

text: This place is pretty run down and not pretty to look at. Many of the theater chairs are old, torn, and run down. They offer the basics at the concession area in the lobby including: hotdogs, popcorn, nachos, icees, drinks, and candy. But, they lack the newer style concessions such as pizza, dip-n-dots, giant pretzels, etc. There is no game room for kids to enjoy, but just three or four video games off to the sides of the lobby. They also do not have stadium seating like the newer Palace theaters in the area. The prices are pretty cheap, but you get what you pay for. All that being said, I do tend to visit this place quite regularly when I'm trying to see a big movie release in the spur of the moment. People tend to forget about this place when movies are selling out in the larger theaters.

text: We stayed at the Doubletree hotel for Valentines day and included in the package was free breakfast at Porters. We arrived in the lobby at 10:00AM. It took them about 20minutes to seat us! Then they never came over to give us our juice! The servers were so busy they coudln't adequately serve the customers. There were about 2 servers in the WHOLE RESTAURANT. can you imagine a server running around serving people...and then running to the front desk asking how many people are in your party? running back to set the table....running back to the front to answer the phone and then finally seat the party?!! Because thats exactly what happened! It was a complete disaster. The breakfast was amazing for it to be free. Would i ever pay for Porter's breakfast buffet.......NO.....would I stay at the doubletree and eat at the breakfast buffet for free......YES, OF COURSE! We gave a minimal tip because we didn't have a server. I had to chase different servers down to ask them for orange juice and ketchup. They need to have more servers so they can increase their customer service. Until then they'll have two stars. The breakfast buffer included...eggs...really tasty bacon and sausage....pancakes...hash browns, and omelets.
label: NEG

text: Yummmm...my stomach is still full of deliciousness from Via Maestra. The ravioli spinaci was heavenly - the alfredo sauce was very light and had a fantastic lemon flavor. The Chicken dish (the only one on the menu) was very rich - it was stuffed with cheese and prosciutto. It was good, but the best part of that dish was the truffle mashed potatoes on the side. They might just be the best mashed potatoes I've ever had. From where I was sitting, i was eyeing the dessert case the entire time, so I had to try one. It was hard to decide, but I had the mixed berry torte and it was SO GOOD. I will go back and try more desserts - they all looked delicious. I love the atmosphere of this place - it's very intimate and it feels like you're in a tiny cafe in Italy. Service is definitely on the slow side and due to the limited number of tables there can be a wait, so don't come here if you're in a hurry. This is food that is meant to be enjoyed slowly.
label: POS

text: I heart Union Trust. It is truly a beautiful restaurant and I especially love the openness and the gorgeous decor. I have been there twice for drinks as a post-dinner jaunt after Morimoto and Jones. On a Saturday, the place was PACKED with a diverse clientele of memaws and pepaws getting their date night on, the 30s/40s set spending ducats with their compadres and a few twentysomething big-spenders sprinkled in. It was a lively scene--not pretentious but comfortable. I went last night (Friday) and it was a ghost town however the bartenders were uber-friendly and the one male bartender made my "date" (read: sexy bestfriend) a VON-derful (yes pronounced that way) dirty martini with blue cheese stuffed olives. I took one sip--too strong. I am such a lightweight and he made me something fruity and girly in a martini glass and made me feel like the young'n I pretend...errr...I am. After overhearing a conversation between two yuppies, one flipping his black card for the world to see (insert: sarcastic oohhhh and aaahhhss) and the other over-enunciating the "Haaaammmpptoonnnnss" about "rubbing one out" later, we bounced. I can't comment on the food, which I heard is fantastic but the drinks, service, and ambience is worth it. Next time, I will try not listen to others' conversations and just concentrate on the greatness that is Union Trust!

text: I just found it to be crowded, grouchy service and slightly disappointing food.

text: The quality at the Mt. Airy one has gone down, way down. The food is watered down (Lipti Subzi an old favorite was served without tomatoes in the base making for a weak and insipid curry), the service ... are they talking about customers in Hindi/Nepali?! It used to be my favorite and I would go or order from there all the time and recommend to friends but now its Saffron in Bala Cynwyd for me even with the extra driving time.

text: Mad Mex is a 3 minute walk from my job so I always end up here. Over the past few months I have seen its decline from quick and easy place to grab food/drinks to annoying pretentious sub par restaurant. Its only redeeming quality is that at night the playlist is top notch with the best songs to be heard in a restaurant setting. My Bloody Valentine? Thank you kindly. Recently, I went here for lunch with 2 friends/coworkers. We ordered water but were served glasses with no straws. The waiter had very frightfully and candidly warned us that if his manager saw him giving us straws he would get in trouble and begged us not to tell anyone he offered them. I guess they were trying to cut down on costs by only offering them to people who asked. Whatever. A weirded out but jovial bunch, we promised to keep the "straw secret" and sipped away. Then my friend discovered her fork had never taken a bath after its previous client as it was covered in food when she opened her napkin. That grossed us out a bit but we carried on. I ordered off the always cleverly worded menu and was slightly satisfied by my chicken quesadilla;however, I yearned for a margarita to make the food experience better. The lunch date ended with (who we think was) the manager clearing our plates and asking about our experience. My friend jokingly mentioned the straw situation and he made some cocky retort about "that being a decision the management had made and adhered to" as if WE were in the wrong for wanting one. Right then and there was the first time in my life a spitball would've been called for.... if only I had a straw.
label: NEG

text: Great place, great staff. The $8 pizza is one of the best deals in the city.
label: POS

text: I know this place has a serious and faithful, almost cult-like following, however ... as much as I've tried, I can't drink the kool-aid. It's not horrible, but it's not great, either. Let me explain why. Went with a few friends yesterday (Labor Day) and it was packed, as usual. All of the seats in the outdoor patio area were taken, and most of the seats indoors were, too. The line for food wrapped around the bar, and into the seating area. I'd say we waited about an hour total for our food, and in the end it was just ok. Nothing special, really. Cheap yes, but standout, no. And, it was most definitely SALTY!!!! Wow! I'm not sure if this is a gimmick to make the patrons drink more, and therefore order more drinks, but as someone who isn't a fan of a brine type flavor, I wasn't impressed. The food quality itself was lacking, too. The burger had little flavor, other than charcoal, and the pork kabob was dry as a bone. Chicken wings (chick on a stick) were ok, but again hello SALT! Something else that bothered me about the experience was the rule that one must buy drinks to sit at a table in the restaurant. I wasn't drinking, so I ordered Diet Pepsi, and that is considered a drink. But refills aren't free, so after all of the salty food I was served, I ended up drinking two sodas, and at $2 each + tip. As for the crowd at Eddies, let's just say it's ermmm ... interesting and eclectic. LOTS of bikers, lots of smokers, and lots of loud types. To call it a rough crowd seems suitable, to me. It's just not the kind of place most who aren't into A) smoking, B) drinking of cheap liquor (house drinks are made with the cheapest stuff you can find ... Juarez tequila for margaritas (GAG), C) hanging with bikers, or D) eating lower quality food to save yourself a buck. I will say it can be fun if you have a large, after work crowd with you, where you know a lot of people in a group, and you have a couple of tables reserved for all involved, but at the same time I don't recommend it for a small group of friends. This being because the music is very loud and not conducive to conversation, there are always people bumping you/walking into you/crowding you, and it doesn't look all that clean. On top of that they're cash only! Who, in this day and age is still cash only? Step into 2010, Eddie! This is a debit card world.
label: NEG

text: YUMMIE ! Best icing ever - pull up a spoon & dig in. The carrot cake is the best. The staff is super cool.

text: As an out-of-towner who masquerades as a stodgy professional but secretly (even not-so-secretly) loves going to metal and indie rock shows, I was very happy when the tour bus made its "French Market" stop just across the street from Envie. I was all like "Yay! A real coffeehouse!" Not that I don't love the cafe au lait at the Cafe Du Monde, it's just that those people who some jackass referred to as "gutter punks" (and their indoor counterparts, old activist hippies with ponytails reading free papers and writing in notebooks) are to me the signs of a GOOD LOCAL COFFEEHOUSE, a sight for my sore tourist-infested eyes. The counter girl was very cute and very nice and I immediately ordered a vegetarian panini (I'm not vegetarian, I just like veggie sammitches) and two of the huge cookies that weigh like a pound a piece. They turned out to be underdone on the inside so if you like raw cookie dough you will love those. My biggest problem with Envie was choosing an iced tea. I was curious about the Blue Eyes but they also had my favorite, peach, so I went with that. I may find myself walking 12 blocks back up there tomorrow morning at 8 am to try the Blue Eyes. Did I mention that it's in a gorgeous old bar with comfy booths, a beautifully tiled floor, big windows open to the outside, and My Morning Jacket was playing full blast? And I didn't see one single person with their face in their laptop. (Not that I would have minded, I have my face in my laptop enough.) No hataz here. I like Envie. Already recommended it to two of my friends who are visiting soon, because if I don't, it's highly likely they won't make it all the way past the French Market and Decatur to discover that it exists. So there ya go.
label: POS

text: Well, I read these two reviews and I thought, "Gee,this place sounds good." Well, that was dead wrong . The large pizza was thin and cold with no flavor, it totally sucked. The only thing that was sorta good was the stromboli but it was short and expensive, so my friends and I wasted 25 $. Don't waste your money or time going here.

text: I think I might hate you, Pizza Rustica. I joined yelp for the sole purpose of writing about my abysmal experience at Pizza Rustica -- the only pizza establishment that has ever actively pissed me off. First off, that open air concrete mausoleum of a patio? Right. If I wanted that view I'd go live in a crappy UPenn dorm. Lopping those mushrooms off the sides of the finest West Philadelphia scrub trees? My little Irish grandmother can make a better pizza than that using only a loaf of bread and a can of Ragu. No, I definitely hate you, Pizza Rustica.

text: I am surprised to see the 4 star rating for this place. The wings are good and so are the potato wedges, but nothing else I have tried is good. The pulled pork sandwich is bad. text: The Carousel Bar at the Hotel Montelone is a must. Where else can you find a rotating bar anyway? A few friends and I visited during an afternoon of drinking on Bourbon Street. We sat at the bar, which slowly rotates, which makes for an interesting experience when you are feeling buzzed. Had a great time. Nice staff. The bar and the hotel are beautiful so it's a nice ambiance.

text: Standard beach seafood fare. I cant believe they served canned veggies (so horrible). Plus side - you get to sit outside, eat large portions or artery clogging food. Our service was okay aside from having to play "guess who" to try and figure out what beers they served. After 20 questions and not many answers we ended up just getting coronas.
