text: Freshberry is a copycat company jumping on the yogurt bandwagon craze largely started by Red Mango and Pinkberry. "healthy" nonfat yogurt with fresh fruit toppings, a trend that came from South Korea (koreans prefer less sweet desserts, so the yogurt was traditionally more tangy than sweet and creamy). Freshberry's yogurt tastes just like plain old fashioned soft serve yogurt, not the newer "healthy" active culture yogurt that's so trendy right now. They do offer more variety of flavors and toppings (they also offer the candy toppings). They don't offer my favorite topping, mochi balls (but I think they will as soon as they find a supplier, as they've indicated they keep getting asked for it). I thought the yogurt was too sweet and too soft, not cold enough. It came out of the machine sort of half melted and didn't hold a stiff peak like I prefer. Positive notes. It's bright and clean inside and the staff are extremely friendly and helpful. also, a note on the "healthy" claims. A 4oz serving is over 100 calories. I believe the smallest serving is over 4oz, largest one well over 3x this. add on 10-100+ calories per topping. (candy toppings generally add on the most, and fruit varies greatly) and you're looking at 400 calories easily even with the smallest serving on the menu. So be careful and enjoy as a treat, not as a healthy snack. They also aren't rated for the live probiotic cultures that are promoted in the product.

text: I rarely give a place 5 stars - but Dickey's truly deserves it! I LOVED everything on my plate- and on my friends plate! Hey I was HUNGRY! Dickey's is a chain type establishment, and also out of Dallas Texas (my home town) which possibly makes me a tad partial - what a wonderful addition to the BBQ scene here in Reno! Saturday evening the place was simi-crowded yet we walked in and was able to walk right up to the "order window" and place our orders. The menu (up on the wall) is simple, and ordering is easy! They do have less choices then a lot of other BBQ places, but what they offer is REALLY good, so it more then makes up for not having tons of options! Check out their website before you go, so you have an idea of what you want when you get there! This place is EASY to find, its near to the new Staples, and next door to the new Panda Express! Right on East Plumb. The staff were all really friendly. We got our order brought out to us quickly - my plate was missing my waffle fries and when I pointed this out, the guy came right back with a WHOLE plate FULL of fries for me. During our dinner they came by to check on us several times, even though this is a "self serve" type eatery - you feel like you have a waiter taking care of you. I also noticed they clean a lot and clear off tables quickly. I wanted to try a little of everything so I ordered the 3 meat plate with 2 sides. And my friend ordered the same. I got - spicy sausage, pull pork, and brisket - my sides were waffle fries, mac n cheese, and just because I love fried okra I had to get an extra side of okra! And a sweet tea. I like my sweet tea REALLY sweet so I added extra sugar, and it was perfect! My friend ordered - spicy sausage, chicken, and ribs, and the same sides as me. All I can say is the meat was awesome! Perfectly cooked, perfectly seasoned. Both our dinners came with garnishing of pickles and onions, and a mouth watering buttery dinner roll. They have a giant vat of pickles in a barrel - free for the taking, those are awesome pickles, goes PERFECT with the BBQ! Since I was there to sample everything, I helped myself to the condiment bar - I got some of each of their BBQ sauce. Sweet, Dickey's Original, and Hot and Spicy! The Hot and Spicy won - it was awesome!!! After stuffing ourselves silly, unable to finish all of the food, we helped ourselves to a little more of the WONDERFUL sweet tea and an ice cream cone on the way out! I love the nifty bright yellow "to go" souvenir cups! The tiny ice cream cone on the way out the door was the perfect touch! They offer a BBQ sandwich for less then $3.00 - your choice of meat. It would be almost impossible to pick which meat!! But I'm sure the chicken or pull pork will win - both of those were out of this world GOOD! I only have one "complaint" about this whole place and its so small - the ketchup is in individual packages, and not that good, its a shame to put the crappy ketchup on those GREAT waffle fries. Also their salt and pepper comes in those tiny packages instead of having shakers on the table, which is annoying to me! Our dinner was $29.00 total which is about $10-$15 LESS then what it runs at any other BBQ joint in Reno, and we got much more food, and it was great! I do admit - while eating Dickey's BBQ, the thought did come to mind - "now if I could just have a piece or two of Carolina's catfish this would really be awesome" I will absolutely be coming back here soon! Also - separate from the restaurant, they have a full bar, if drinking is your thing! Its small but looked like it might be a cool spot to drop in and grab a drink before or after your feeding frenzy. They also cater and have take out. *waving* WELCOME TO RENO DICKEY'S!!! *waving*

text: Love. This was momentary love. Saunter down State Street and maybe the chic clothing stores are for you. I'll admit, they beckoned me with their boutique windows. But it was 3 o clock, and I was on a mission--to avoid super-turnpike traffic and to purchase a book. Well, I bought three. The County Bookshop is up a few brick steps on the right side of the street. Saw the name; had to go. Used and out-of-print books. I broke into a smile. An old home converted into this bookshop, it is a fitting dressed-down arrangement. Entering, there are rooms to the left and right. At the right rest philosophy books, and near the register first-edition copies of books. One I saw was a C.S.Lewis story. These books are not in the most beautiful condition, and many seem to have been gifts with cursive notes scrawled in the covers. But these little rooms are not all! Browsers can wander further to another room, and another after that. Each section is distinctly labeled. Signs even direct you to poetry and literature. There is everything from philosophy to travel to gardening and food to French lit and surely beyond. The best is yet to come. Outside sits a rack of books for 35 cents. Inside, there is another near the cashier, where each book is 50 cents. The gentleman, presumably the owner, was soft-spoken and had no idea what to say other than Thanks when receiving praise for the store. Perhaps he isn't used to it, since apparently there are other book stores in the very near vicinity. Buck County Bookshop is what I saw first, and walking out with Philosophy of Science ($7.95) Intro to Mathematical Philosophy ($10) and World Orders Old and New ($7.50) I was pleased with myself. I bet the other stores didn't have these books!

text: I've always found the idea of Bubba Gump to be a lot like a Hard Rock or Planet Hollywood- ideally not a place I'd like to spend an evening. Yes, it is a total tourist trap, but I'm willing to try anything once. Checking in is a little bit weird. They herd you down a corridor like cattle, all the while checking in with people on headsets looking at tables. We were asked if we wanted to sit in the courtyard- which we ended up being the only ones there most of the time and was definitely an advantage for us. Our waitress, Pandora, was fabulous and definitely down to earth- giving us great recommendations for dinner when she asked us some of the menu items we were thinking over. She was also helpful in recommending some places to spend the rest of our evening down on Frenchman, which was much needed after spending a lot of time in the Quarter. So that was pretty cool. On to the food: My boyfriend ordered a Blue Louisiana Lemonade which had a very interesting taste to it - when you drink it, you definitely taste the lemonade followed by a tinge of blueberry aftertaste... Like you drank lemonade and ended up with a blueberry in your mouth. We ordered a spinach & artichoke dip (Bubba's Far Out Dip) that was pretty yummy. There was a really delicious blend of parmesean with red peppers in there that really set it off, making it different from other dips I've had. For our entrees: My boyfriend got the Bourbon Street Mahi Mahi and I got the Lt. Dan's Drunken Shrimp. Both of ours had the same sauce base that was a nice and creamy bourbon sauce. Both of ours had mashed potatoes which were all right. His fish was nicely cooked and my shrimp were scrumptious. We left dinner feeling satisfied and pleasantly surprised. The only thing that kind of bugged me was that the restrooms were on the 2nd floor- but I guess they're designed that way so people don't come in willy nilly to use the restrooms?

text: So. Gross. Let me preface this by saying that I'm usually not one to complain, ESPECIALLY at a restaurant. I've seen "Waiting," so trust me -- I know better. But rules are meant to be broken, and I started up a Yelp account SPECIFICALLY so that I could warn people about how miserable this place is. Our group of four was looking for a quick brunch before heading over to the Eastern State Penitentiary for a tour. We saw Jack's right across the street -- perfect! The inside is lovely (which is where the first star comes in), and we were seated quickly by a friendly hostess. We were given a plate of biscuits and corn muffins and some water... aaaand that's where the fun ended. Within the first 5-10 minutes, we had placed our order with the female server -- the pulled pork & corn chips as an appetizer, and four entrees. About 30 minutes later, I casually asked the other members in my group if it seemed like the food was taking a while... we all agreed that it was, but I didn't think much of it. The food MUST be good if it takes that long, right?! About that time, the server stopped by to ask us how we were doing. Uhh... fine, I guess? We're just sitting here, so... After about 45 minutes, the first plate showed up. Then the second plate. Five minutes later, my food came out. The fourth person in our group had to sit and wait another 5-10 minutes for her food -- but before they brought that out, they tried to give her the wrong meal! Everything was ice cold (and definitely should not have been -- I'm pretty sure that omelets and pancakes are supposed to be served warm), and honestly, it tasted awful. My husband's fruit tasted like it had been frozen. The pancakes tasted like dough, the french toast looked like it was only cooked on one side, the fries -- which are apparently fried three times -- were ice cold, the roll that the chicken salad was dumped on felt like a brick... it didn't make any sense. All the while, there was no explanation as to why it took so long for the food to come out, why it was cold when it finally arrived, or why on earth it all came out in bits and pieces like that. And where the heck was that stupid appetizer?! FInally, someone in our group got up to speak with a manager. Like I said before, we're usually not ones to complain, but when you're about to spend that much money on food, you'd at least expect decent SERVICE if nothing else... if the food had been ice cold and disgusting (and it was) but the server was at least NICE and gave us an explanation for it, I would have happily kept my mouth shut and eaten whatever they had brought out. But really? And that's where the second star comes in -- Joel, the manager, came in and saved the day. Well... as best he could. He first offered to "warm up" the food that we were given (um, no thank you... I do not want my food to come back microwaved and covered in spit), so we were given the food on the house. Not that we had eaten much of it... but that did help ease the frustration a bit. So thanks, Joel. You were the one saving grace in that whole establishment. After reading some other reviews on here (which is obviously something I should have done before we left), it seems like this is a pretty consistent problem here, so I won't be returning to give it another shot. That's a bummer. This place had a lot of potential.
label: NEG

text: You are homeless. It is a sad story really. You lost your job at the local meat packing plant because you were caught hoarding cuts of meat in your over-sized yellow rubber pants. You pleaded with your boss to keep you on, and told him of how you were simply trying to feed your family. He wouldn't have it. Like Donald Trump he pointed at you from across his board room table and told you, "You're Fired!." You're wife left you for one of your former co-workers who could still get away with sneaking prime cuts of beef. You turn to alcohol to ease your heart ache. Your only friend is Jack Daniels, and eventually he leaves as well, leaving you with a guy named Vladimir. You are evicted and you home is now a cardboard box placed over a vent on the corner of Broad and Walnut. Your lone possession is your trusty six string. You aren't good. You never were. But with plenty of free time, you write humorous songs about your own misfortune. You begin playing these songs for passerby's who laugh. It is unclear if they are laughing at your songs or you personally. It doesn't matter, they are giving you money. $4.95 is your daily earning, enough you get a large sandwich or hoagie from Grill Master Deli. You are now satisfied and toss around the idea of going on tour. You decide to practice all day and night until someone notices your talent. You get drunk instead. You are homeless and it is a sad story really.

text: Ted Drewes is one of those local places where everyone in town goes to and thinks its absolutely fantastic. I've had lots of good frozen custard in other towns and at other shops, but nothing is ever quite as good as Ted's. The crowds are dense and the lines are long during the summer, but you usually don't have to wait for more than 10 minutes for your custard goodness. And, oh, it is heavenly! I haven't lived in town for quite awhile, but when I'm visiting, I have got to stop at Ted's! I was just there last week for the first time in a long time, and all I could do was nurse my mint concrete (my old standby since childhood) and sigh. The prices are fairly cheap for the amount you get. There is on-site parking, but expect to have a hard time finding a spot during the summer nights. If you can't find a spot in the lot, look to park in neighboring parking lots. This location is open for business all year except for January. They also sell Christmas trees around Christmastime! It's on the old Route 66, which is very cool. So if you're in town and someone mentions going to Ted Drewes, go--you won't regret it!

text: In the five months since my wife and I moved from Philadelphia to the 'burbs we haven't found any restaurants in our new neighborhood that could stand up to comparison with old-favorite BYOBs like Melograno or Matyson. Bottom-line: Sola's chef uses top-quality ingredients to put together innovative dishes that taste every bit as good as they look. _______________ First-off, any restaurant that surprises me with an amuse bouche is going to put a smile on my face. Sola served a smoked mussel that a friend of mine described as "covered with goodness, with a little more goodness on top." It woke up my mouth and provided an interesting contrast to the syrah we were drinking. I started with the oyster sampler (four oysters paired with complimentary flavors-- a Cape May Salt with a fresh diced tomatoes and salsa, a Oregon Kumamoto with sweet uni and blood orange juice, a Connecticut oyster with caviar and a foie gras reduction, and one more that escapes me). While the pairings somewhat overpowered the oysters' individual characters, the flavor experiment was a lot of fun and each preparation came together nicely. The oysters were each presented on a bed of seaweed salad-- nice touch. My entree was roast New Zealand rack of lamb served over pureed, stewed fennel (mashed potato-like) edged with a diced tomato salsa. The cut was generous with the extraneous fat trimmed so only the moist, tender medallions remained. There was a bed of what appeared to be an apricot preparation that served as an occasionally sweet change from the comfort-food paring of lamb and fennel. For dessert we shared a mini homemade pumpkin cheesecake that was creamy and perfectly spiced. Entrees at Sola are priced from the low $20s to the mid $30s, but the quality merits or exceeds the price. Corkage is $2 per bottle and is justified by the restaurant's nice stemware. Having already over-indulged in my description, I might as well mention the tableware-- it is all beautiful. Whoever is buying the utensils (the butter knives!), the dishware, the wine glasses and even the sugar vessels is spending a lot of money to establish Sola's ambiance. They've done a great job and it really adds to the experience. I've taken a star away because my wife's duck entree-- which was, again, a great cut beautifully presented-- was far, far too rare. text: Look, sometimes a guy has to do what a guy has to do. Sometimes, despite a growing waistline and cholesterol, a guy just HAS TO keep his LAST MINUTE plans to go to 'burger night' at a local eatery with some of his friends. But a real man understands compromise and values his health not just for it's own sake or the many layered inherent benefits, but also for the sheer joy of continued living to the spite of his foes. And that's how I came to enjoy a truly magnificent veggie burger, topped with raw spinach, mushrooms with real cheddar and bacon. 'A cheddar, bacon veggie burger,' you ask? Yes! Compromise! The deal with Square One Brewery's 'Burger Night' (every Tuesday) is that they drop an ordering slip in your lap, similar to those at decent sushi bars. On it, you combine your desired burger patty (black angus, veggie or otherwise), dairy, additional meats and finally vegetable toppings. The selection is VAST and Square One gets extra kudos for having crisp raw spinach (not the drippy, limp, boiled variety- though if that's your bag, they've got that too). The waitress (barmaid? Is that an archaic term or what?) was exceptionally friendly and attentive and she made a MEAN rum and coke. As for my veggie-burger, it scores top marks for being crispy on the edges, juicy in the middle and being every kind of burgerlicious WITHOUT all the extra guilt or arterial death. I think I paid a paltry sum of $15 dollars (after tips) that night. So Square One Brewery, I thank you! And I will return! On a personal note, I hope to maintain this level of compromise. Maybe I'll break even health-wise.

text: I was all set to write a glowing 4 star review, really I was. I was going to rave about the personal attention, free trials and samples I received. I was going to brag about how soft my face felt after using their Dark Angels clay cleanser, Ayesha face mask & Breath of Fresh Air toner. I was also going to mention the very helpful Lush Times Christmas Catalog... and this is where things go down hill. I HIGHLY RECOMMEND AVOIDING their Bubble Bars or many of their solid shampoos. These products contain Cocamide DEA - a product found to cause cancer in lab mice. The National Toxicology Program has not established any direct link between DEA-related ingredients and cancer in humans, however I have avoided DEA since the studies were published. These are products that I would use daily - directly on my skin... so I ask, why chance it? I received 4 star service in the store but deducted 1 star for the mini panic attack that I had while searching through the catalog to determine if any products I purchased were affected. I deducted another star for violating their "We believe in... the finest essential oils and safe synthetics..." creed plastered on their shopping bag. I left two stars because I will use the remainder of the products I purchased, but will most certainly be writing a letter to the company.

text: I hate to use my 100th review on something so mediocre, but I was hoping for better. We hit up Little Hills Winery Restaurant on a Sunday evening at approximately 5PM with 4 people total - myself, my husband, and my in-laws. We were told there was a 25 minute wait, and it wasn't that long so props for that. We got seats on the patio, which I agree is quite a nice atmosphere, and the weather was perfect on that particular evening. My MIL and I bellied up to the bar to get some tastings of wine before settling on a bottle. You're limited to 3, which is lame but whatever. We tried the White Merlot (not their label), and that was interesting though quite tart. The Little Hills Main Street White was very sweet (they put it in the semi-sweet category) but too sweet to have with dinner. The Little Hills Cobblestone had a bite to it, but our 3rd taste was up so we went with it. We had wanted to try another, but they said they were only selling it by the glass because they were running low. That's dumb. We headed to the table, and our waitress was pleasant enough and patient with my FIL when he waffled on his order, but service in general was slow. I'd have to guess that it was probably the kitchen's fault more than hers. My husband and I decided to try out the 2 for $25. This is by far the best deal on the menu. In Applebee's style, you get an app, 2 entrees, and a dessert from a specific list. We got the loaded fries for an app. It was definitely the highlight of the entire experience. If I found myself on Main Street again wanting to chill with a drink and something to munch on, I'd definitely order those again. Too bad the rest of the meal didn't measure up to the beginning. For entrees, hubby ordered the BBQ Bacon Cheeseburger, and I ordered the Peppercorn Steak. The waitress told my husband that the entrees were as listed on the menu which meant no sides for the burger, so my husband ordered some potato chips. The burger is delivered to the table with a side of chips included AND the extra order we never would have made had we been told correctly. The burger was overcooked, and the potato chips were good though WAY too salty! Believe me, I'm all for salty chips. These were too much. My steak was also overcooked and lacking in flavor which was super disappointing. The corn and mashed potatoes were fine, though I was hoping for more flavor from the mashed potatoes as I saw melted shredded cheese in them (not specified as so on the menu). MIL reports her stuffed chicken was tasty though dry. To finish our 2 for $25, we ordered red velvet cake. The icing was good. The cake was not very flavorful and kind of dry. Bummer... Overall, a "meh" experience. It seemed the theme of the night was "X is good/tasty/etc but it's dry/overcooked/lackluster in this way". I'd go back for drinks and order some loaded fries to split for the table, but that's about it.

text: My husband (who was my boyfriend at the time) took me to waterworks for dinner on a whim. He said, get dressed we are going out- and that is where we landed. We sat outside, candle lit and it was so beautiful. We walked around the gazebo area at night by the water, it was a fairytale kind-of perfect. The waterworks always stuck out in my mind as probably our most romantic dinner and night ever. Food was great. I had Boursioun Chicken... He had steak. We had asian style appetizers that were also excellent. It was expensive but worth it. Fast forward: I got married here and my reception was in the restaurant. I was torn as to where to have my wedding in philly When I found out that waterworks did weddings, it was immediately decided and it was perfect. It was truely a romantic scene for such a romantic day. Our guests raved about the food as it was unlike normal catered fare. It seemed more personally prepared. The plated appetizers were excellent too and a big hit was the fried oyster. This restaurant will always be special to me and my husband.

Shige's Express is small & cramped, however, if you are food jealous you just have to wait for the next boat of sushi to come along. This place is my kind of "fast food" because it's real/authentic & and most importantly cheap. Especially on Thursdays ($1 sushi plates). text: I've driven by this restaurant about a million times before I decided to give it a try. To be fair, it really isn't a "restaurant" but a take-out/delivery place, but they do have some seating and tables so you can eat there. After looking at the posted menu, I decided to try a regular donair and a poutine. It wasn't that busy, so I sat down and watched some hockey on the big screen they have there. 5 minutes......10 minutes.......15 minutes........I watched almost a full period of hockey before my food was served, and like I said they weren't that busy. The young tard behind the counter then grabbed a plastic fork by the pronged end and handed it to me! Not very sanitary, methinks. And then I had to ask him for napkins(good luck eating a donair without them.) I put my tray down and commenced eating. Remember when you were a little kid eating at McDs or Dairy Queen? The table they had their was so high and the stool I sat on was so short that the table edge was at my upper chest! And I'm 6 feet tall. Try eating something in that way sometime.....it's very uncomfortable. I dug into the donair first. The filler was about standard, but the pita shell was stale and doughy, which took a lot of chewing. After the arduous task of finishing off the donair, I took on the poutine(after wiping down my contaminated fork). It was made of frozen crinkle cut fries you see in the supermarket. The fat girl cook in the back didn't burn them, but they were way overcooked and hard. In fact, the plastic prongs on my fork bent when trying to grab them! I had to eat my poutine as a soup. So to sum up here's what your money will get you at Richard's on 50th: -long wait times for food -horrible service by incompetent employees -very uncomfortable dining -garbage quality food Need any other reasons to avoid doing business with this so-called restaurant?
label: NEG

Not a bad place if you want $12 flaming sushi rolls and fancy cocktails. For real sushi, Wasabi in Clayton is still my best pick.

text: So, I had a social living groupon. Next time before I get my groupon-on I'm gonna yelp the joint. I walk in and it's really really bad techno-gym music. Not relaxing in the least. They tell me they do not have any keys to the lockers available, but as soon as one is ready they will let me know. These are the same folks who on the phone told me to come early and I could swim laps or relax. I often do this at adolph bieker, so i was excited! So, I sat in the waiting area in a weird plastic baskety chair and read the NYT's which was nice except the music. The music was soo bad and not relaxing at all. Even if i put my ipod on it still would have been blaring through. Then the staff were about as annoying as the music. Mocking the music and just talking about inappropriate stuff. Not professional or relaxing at all. Finally after reading two or three sections of the paper, half a plastic dixie cup of weird citrus-melon flavored water and twenty minutes of non-relaxation I am finally shown the locker room. On my journey to the locker room she just assumes I have been there before and isn't even going to show me the ropes until I say ,"I've never been here before,". She also kept going on and on about how they don't have enough keys to the lockers. Ever been to a spa sweetie....they have these neat things called combination locks...welcome to 2010? So, I am just dying to relax at this point. I totally strip down and put on the robe, which I find out is too small. At this point I really don't care. If you are going to see a good bit of my thighs and a hint of my bits oh well! I take a shower. The showers have watered down shampoo, decent body wash and really watered down conditioner. However, as the other two reviewers mentioned, TOWELS A PLENTY. This place has enough towels to wallpaper the entire hotel with them. The water pressure is meh. So I put the robe back on, drape a towel on my lap and proceed to the lounge. The lounge for the spa is noted by a printed sign stating that the lounge for the spa is for spa guests only and not gym members. A drape ropes off the area. The room is smaller than the bathroom in my last apartment. Some people have closets bigger than this room. More rancid citrus water and plastic cups....Has anyone told them about the environment? My masseuse comes and picks me up and takes me through a blacklit electric blue hallway. I kinda worry that it's lit like this to hide germs or blood and or dead bodies. The room my massage is in is pretty standard. Not as warm and beautiful as the spa rooms at toppers. Not as minnimalist and medicinal as adolph. Not as warm and buttery like Body Restoration. It's just kinda weird, like one wall is tiled and then there are these weird lanterns on the wall. My massuese Rosa was a little awkward. She gave me a great massage and I cannot complain about that, but I hope she finds another gig soon. I enjoyed the massage part, but I go to spas for the before and after relaxation as well. After my massage she gave me a cup of water from a brita in a plastic cup. Three plastic cups at this point. My poor footprint! I then decide I will try the steamroom. The steamroom was great and my fave part. So, desperate to get out of the robe I go to the locker room. Where one of the staff is sitting on the bench talking on her cell phone. Again really? Really? I get dressed. I go to the front desk. Tip maseusse. Walk out the door and started plotting this review in my head. Never again.

text: I am definitely a fan of this place. I went to this tiny little shack on 8/21/08 with my family. My parents aren't usually a fan of non-Asian cuisine so it was a shocker when they wanted to try out the Shellfish Company. Points for luring in my very Asian parents. Even more points for not scaring them away with outrageous prices. Everything was reasonably priced, with oyster shooters being only $2.50 each. My bro tried one and loved it. If you look at the shooter, it looks like someone just tossed the ingredients for a pizza into a shot glass and stuck a raw oyster at the bottom. Hideously unappealing. I guess looks aren't everything, huh? You MUST try their steamed rock crabs. They charge by the pound ($6.50/lb), and they are fiiiiiiillled with delicious, juicy crab meat. Those babies were hard though, and we had to ask the waitress to take them back and smash them to pieces for us. The crabs came with marinara-horseradish sauce (soo good) and caramelly-butter (too buttery for me). Be sure to look out for their specials...I think for $24 you can get a 3LB crab, soup, and cole slaw. There were some specials on spider crabs too, but I didn't pay too much attention. One downside to this place is the wait...no, not for a seat, but for a waitress to come by. The service was really slow even though the place was nearly empty. We didn't even ask them to clean out the crabs for us so basically all they had to do was find us 3 crabs, toss them into the water, and serve them on a clean plate. One other thing, the crab shells were caked with sand. It put me off a little, but I will forgive them because the meal was pleasant. I originally was going to give SBSC 3.5 stars, but looking back on my experience I actually had a fun time sitting by the waters watching my parents suck the insides out of those cute chubby crabs. They were so round and cute that I almost had trouble eating mine. I wanted to keep it as a pet, even though it was obviously dead. 4 stars for you Santa Barbara Shellfish Company...4 stars!

text: Gotta love a Portuguese byob in the no libs. I have been eating Portuguese food for years. One of my best friends is Portuguese so I cut my teeth at a few places in Newark. With that being said, I enjoyed my dinner at Koo Zee Doo. Four of us walked into the small, quaint space on N. 2nd. First things I noticed were the open kitchen (plus) and the exposed brick (double plus). We were seated immediately and began to look over the menu. We decided on the shrimp in piri piri, chicken gizzards and the Salada de Cores. I was very happy with all of the appetizers. The shrimp in hot sauce was very flavorful and they prepared the dish with large shrimp, head on (that's where all the flavor is). The sauce was so tasty that I cleaned it up with some bread. The chicken gizzards were served in a small casserole in a delicate sauce. They were soft and very flavorful. The salad was also surprisingly good. It was bursting with flavor from the dressing and the veggies were cut nicely so it wasn't awkward to eat. Nice presentation. For the entrees we chose the rabbit special and the Feijoada de Marisco. The rabbit was awesome. Very rich tasting but not heavy. I definitely ate more of it than I should have. Rabbit tends to be bony by nature so this was just par for the course as far as I was concerned. Once again, some bread was used for sopping up sauce. The seafood and bean stew was prepared well but lacked the "pop" of the other dishes. Don't get me wrong, it was very tasty. It just sort of paled in comparison to the rabbit. Our meal concluded with four of us splitting one dessert. Tarte de Amendôa which was light a flavorful. Just the right amount of sweet after our very savory meal. I will go back to this place. Next time, it's Bife à Portuguesa.
label: POS

text: We stumbled onto this place on a Friday night while looking for a place to eat that's open after 10pm. What a terrific find! I ordered the Spaghetti with Italian Sausage and a small side salad. The salad was cold and crisp, covered with grated mozzarella cheese and diced tomatoes. The blue cheese dressing was home-made and presented in a little plastic cup on the side. As for the main entree, I was expecting "average" but I was knocked over with pleasure from the authentic Italian Sausage and the wonderfully rich marinara sauce. The portion was HUGE. I am a big eater, and was only able to eat about half of the serving, saving the rest for lunch the next day. It was served with a "loaf" of bread, generously slathered with olive oil and topped with garlic and grated cheese and spices. I have been back twice, wanting to try other things on their menu, but I just can't get away from that delicious Spaghetti with Italian Sausage! I let my eyes roam to other tables and every dish looks fabulous. Next time, I am committed to trying the lasagna. The staff is very friendly. On one recent visit, there was a big tall woman (maybe a drag queen?) who was being hateful to the staff, and complaining about the staff's knowledge of eggplant. text: I might date myself here, but I miss Hexagone. Years ago, this place was one of my mainstays. It was a little, intimate hideaway mostly for Europeans, as this bar was known to be the unofficial meet-up for visiting students and the like. The place never tried too hard to be something it wasn't, drinks were affordable, there was always good beer and wines by the glass to be had and good tunes spun in the back. I'm afraid this place doesn't resemble anything of what Hexagone used to be, except that there are still a lot of students that go here, but for an entirely different reason. It's a game board - bar. Have some cocktails, play Jenga or Connect Four!! "It's so vintage eighties" - I heard a person say once while I was having a drink there- which made me feel really old. Nostalgia aside, I like the idea in theory, except that's it's a bit gimmicky - not to mention that I really don't get the reason why there are two plastic models that take up half of the front space of the bar. Perhaps, as another yelper noted, I'm just a curmudgeon that isn't getting any younger and longs for the days of her youth. Or perhaps, my tastes have changed, and I'm no longer the type of person that Raven markets to - perhaps it's both. Either way, this place can be fun, especially if you're jonesing for an $8 cocktail and playing barrel o' monkeys.

text: Le Pavillon has its charm, but then again, charm can only take you so far. The reviews on Trip Advisor that talk about the place being old and dingy are not entirely off the mark. Conversely, if you aren't looking for the clinically minimalist design of the W, but rather some old school charm, you probably won't be disappointed. Upon arrival, we were greeted with a million facets of light radiating off the crystal chandeliers, juxtaposed with the smell of grandmas. Talk about a statement. The place oozes old-school Southern opulence, but also has tinges of just plain old. Not going to lie, the paintings on the walls and the creaky sounds all make this a great place for ghost hunters - it all feels like the inspiration for the Disney Haunted Mansion. Not to mention that our running toilet seems to flush sporadically in the night - I think a ghost is haunting our bathroom, if you ask me. Our room was oddly upgraded to a 2 queen room (what did my husband and I need an extra bed for?) which apparently had extra space. Fine. Come to find out that the hotel pool is being painted (which no one told us) so we think that the upgrade was meant to cover that up. They offered us the pool at the Homewood Suites next door, but that was a severe downgrade given that it was A) indoors and B) across the street. PB and J bar is kitschy - I actually hate PBJ, so not my thing, but a cute touch. The hot chocolate was all over the table and table cloth when I got down to the bar, and the mess (coupled with the heat) turned me off. Room service was actually tasty, despite the price, but then again, when is room service not expensive. Gumbo was flavorful, and the oysters in my po-boy were crispy and delicious. If you are stuck in the hotel, you could do a lot worse for a comforting meal. If you are a stickler for cleanliness, you may want to skip this place. There was still small trash on the floor of our room, and hair on the bathroom tiles. The entire room looks like a holdover from the early 90s pretending to be the early 1820's. Maybe that was the last time the place was properly cleaned. All in all, I can't say that we are having a horrible time here, but we certainly won't come back. I was at the Intercontinental last time, and despite the much higher price tag for the room, it was a huge value over this place.

text: The husband and I went to Capitol Grille because we had a Groupon that needed to be used. I was anticipating a stuffy, hoity-toity establishment with mediocre food, and that was in no way what we got. Even though I'm a feminist, I like being treated with respect - doors opened, chairs pulled out, and greeted by name, which is what happened at Capitol Grille. Very nice and classy touches by everyone from the maitre d' to our server. We started off in the Oak Bar for some cocktails, but as soon as they came, our table was ready. It would've been nice to hang out there for a while. Our table was in the corner of the large room - perfect for watching everyone come and go, but private enough that we could have an intimate conversation. The server was knowledgable about the menu and readily answered questions and provided us with information about the food and a few recommendations. We each started out with the Vidalia Onion Bisque, which was so creamy and amazing. The presentation was nice too. My husband ordered the venison, and I ordered the bollito misto. Both of our entrees were superb. The dijon spaetzle that came with my entree were the perfect balance of texture and spiciness and provided a great bed for the flavorful meat. We ended with the chocolate hazelnut cobbler with buttermilk ice cream. It was probably my least favorite part of the meal, but after what came before it, that was not a surprise. The buttermilk ice cream was pleasntly tangy and a nice compliment to the sweet, gooey cobbler. It was not a cheap meal, but the service and atmosphere and quality of the food was worth it. I would definitely return for a special occasion.
label: POS

text: Sorry, but this place was a total disappointment. 1. I went for an event advertised during Philly Beer Week - they were to have several special Lagunitas beers on tap for happy hour from 6-8. I left work early, arrived @ 6:15... and the bartender informed us that only one tap was 'working'. As for the happy hour 'special'? It wasn't. The special was having (but not actually having) 4 beers from one brewery on-tap. A 10 oz. glass of Undercover Ale cost $7. For reference, you can buy a 22 oz bomber @ a six-pack shop for ~$6. 2. We waited....stuck it out....hoping the disappointing bartender/backs could learn how to tap a keg... only to see them pouring beer into pitchers and nonchalantly stuffing underneath the bar until the settled. After 10 min, it was a nice pitcher pour and then onto the platter of a waitress. That's cool in college. Not so much @ an establishment. 3. Again, hoping to have a rare Lagunitas...we bided our time w/ their guacamole. It was awful. Devoid of flavor. When it arrived, the red onions and cilantro were sitting on top of the mashed avocado and bits of tomato. I've made guac before. It needs to be made ahead of time to let the flavors mix together. Even the quality of the avocado by itself was sub-par. 4. Dinner - Catfish BLT. The bacon was the only decent part. Catfish was thin - no more than 3/4" thick at best - heavily breaded, and overfried. The tomatoes were soft and tasteless, and the roasted red pepper aioli honestly looked and tasted like hellman's w/ crushed red pepper flakes. No sign of actual peppers. 5. We had a few more beers, discovered at the end of the night that they were all $7...including the Lagunitas Pils. I'm no mathamagician...but that's $34 a case. 34/24 = $1.41 a bottle. ($7-$1.41)/$1.41 = 396% markup. I'm cool w/ 100%, even %200 @ a bar. when you're charging 4 times the cost...for a special that you advertised and subsequently fucked up during beer week.... you can be sure I'm not coming back. 6. Shitty, shitty, and shitty. My friends liked the burgers, but hell... what bar can't make a burger? 9 beers, 2 bugers, one BLT, and guac = $112 w/out tip. Never Again.

text: Their food isn't that bad. What makes me give Cuisine only 1 star is the service. The repeatedly bad and rude service that I receive. I have gone here so many times, trying to be extra nice, giving it a second chance, writing it off (SEVERAL times) that maybe they were just having a bad day. One time I walked in at lunch time, and they weren't that busy. Plus, it was the buffet, so everyone was getting their food themselves anyway! They maybe had 4-5 tables with people at them. It was relatively quiet, and slow. The sign "wait to be seated" was at the front, so I waited. And waited. I probably waited at least 10 minutes before they even acknowledged that I had stepped into the building. And they DID see me, they just chose not to greet me, or acknowledge me. When I finally was seated, the server was very rude, and barely spoke. He brought the whole pitcher of water to my table, so as not to have to refill my glass himself. He never came to check on me during my meal, he came only once to take my plate, and even then he didn't speak, even when I said "thank you." When he dropped off the check, again, no "thank you", nothing. Only silence. I went to pay my check and received the same cold, rude service at the front desk. The next couple of times we went back, we had friends from out of town. We are all avid lovers of Indian food. On any of these times, we never had more than 4 people in our party, so it's not like we had an insane amount of people for them to wait on. Also, myself and my friends are not people that are hard to wait on anyway. Once we went for buffet, and the other time for dinner. Both times were NOT close to closing time. Our server once again was not polite, and they acted like they were doing us a big favor by waiting on us. Anytime we asked them for anything, they acted like it was a big deal. Then, they dropped off the ticket WAY early, like we hadn't even been there 30 minutes, and they kept coming over and asking us if we wanted anything off of the buffet...that they were closing it in 10 minutes. We politely said no thank you, and that we wouldn't be making any more trips to the buffet. A few minutes later, they said again that they were closing the buffet in 5 minutes. Again, we said no thank you. By this time, we felt REALLY rushed, and they weren't being polite at all. Not even 2 minutes later, they came over and said "do you want anything else, we're closing the buffet in 2 minutes." That's a bit much in my opinion. We were fed up at that point, and paid our check and left. Again, they never thanked us or anything. My most recent bad experience happened tonight. I've started noticing their ad in the newspapers around town advertising that they now deliver around the area. So...I thought I could get the food without the bad service. I called, ordered a substantial amount of food, gave them my number, name, address, and even gave them very clear directions to my house when they asked. I looked up a google map, and they are exactly 2 miles away. They said okay, and that it would be 30-45 minutes. I said thank you and okay. 10 minutes later they call...I thought maybe they were needing to ask something about the order...instead, to my shock, the man on the phone said "I'm sorry, we can't deliver there. You can come pick it up, but we're not coming there." I was quiet and surprised for a moment, and said "okay...was there a problem with the directions I gave you?" he said "No, the driver doesn't want to go there." I said "okay...is it out of your delivering radius? do you only deliver within a certain radius of your business?" and he said "Yes, if you were in West End or Green Hills..." and I said "Well, my house is only 2 miles from your location, I checked. Green Hills is just as far if not farther." He said "Well, the driver just doesn't want to go to that area." I replied "I really don't understand, it's not a bad area..." He said "No, it's not a bad area, the driver just doesn't want to go." And I said "Okay, well, I'm sorry that you're going to lose my business over this." And I hung up. That is seriously the last straw for me. I have tried, and tried, and TRIED to be kind, and overlook their past rudeness, but this is just too much. I honestly don't know how they stay in business. Unless they get new owners or management, I'm never stepping foot in there again. I've worked many serving jobs, and I know how hard it is and how you depend on your tips. So I'm a good tipper AND an easy customer. But it seems no matter how nice I am to the staff at Cuisine of India, they always treat me and my guests with either silence, or rudeness. That is unacceptable. There is no reason to be rude, especially to good customers. And now they're advertising that they deliver, but their driver just decides he doesn't want to go to a specific area for no reason? and they're okay with that? wow. If you want delivery,be prepared to be called back and turned down depending on the driver's mood.

text: We held our wedding reception at the ArrowCreek Clubhouse. Location: Gorgeous (views of downtown Reno and mountains, with a golf course as the backdrop) Food: Very, very good Service: Impeccable (the bride was well-fed, and didn't even notice the champagne being poured during the toast) After having tried a number of wedding cake options in Reno, I despaired of finding something ultra-fresh (did you know most wedding cake is at least 3 days old before it's served?), ultra-chocolatey, and even close to somewhat reasonably priced. I also wanted some mini-sour-cherry-tarts for dessert, for the people that didn't want chocolate or cake. After some non-trivial emailing back-n-forth and pleading with the event coordinator, the ArrowCreek pastry chef came through with an absolutely amazing set of chocolate cakes and beautiful perfect little tarts, made that morning, succeeding where the specialty pastry stores in Reno failed. The special desserts weren't inexpensive, but I think if I'd negotiated for it up-front, it might have been a little more reasonably priced. Some things to be aware of: - Once the initial contract had been signed, making changes or adding items got a lot more expensive, and they weren't prompt about getting back to me with new pricing for a change. Had I known, I would've been even more careful figuring out what changes to the standard package I wanted to make - They weren't set up to do tastings, so I didn't get to taste most of what was on the menu until the reception. On the plus side, I was able to meet with the chef ahead of time, who was very accommodating, describing each of the dishes in detail, and recommending what worked (was popular) versus what might not - I accidentally left behind the "bathroom basket" during the cleanup phase; it wasn't there when we went back two days later, and no one knew where it had gone - Our wedding day was beautiful, but it can get very windy outside, so if you're getting married at the clubhouse, you'll need to plan accordingly - They put a tip jar on the bar, even though 19% gratuity was included in the bill. The tip jar was a surprise to me, so you might want to negotiate that ahead of time... - The dance floor was the same location as the buffet table, which was a completely separate room from the dining area. So, I couldn't have both dancing and food at the same time, although this wouldn't have been a problem with a plated dinner. It also meant that the band was a bit far away from the dining tables, so did more socializing than dancing (it was a pretty empty dance floor, even though the band was great) - Initially, we were told we could start decorating the evening before; two weeks before the big day, we were told we couldn't start decorating until 10am the day of (I think they'd booked another event for the evening before). It was a bit of a scramble to get everything ready

text: The Castle has been, and continues to be, the one place that never really disappoints when I go out. Granted, that's mostly on Thursday or Monday nights, and not on their bread-and-butter goth nights, but still. If you've never been, the best way to describe it would be a two-story palace of sensory overload, complete with high-tech lighting, gothic decor, lightening-fast bartenders, huge sound systems, and plush couches, if your feet get tired.. To de-romanticize it for a moment: picture everything SOAKED in cigarette smoke, and then get the hell over it. I hate to say it, but you will not get noticed for what you're wearing unless you're just wearing fishnet and your hair is on fire (and maybe not then). The upside to this: everyone at the Castle is laissez-faire, so you can basically go out with friends and be totally yourself. It can get over-crowded, but I've never had a bad night because of the people there. Let me echo VJ Mike: this is NOT a "gay bar". Sunday nights are a gay-themed party (which is starting to play some real cutting edge stuff) and queer people show up here and there on each night, but if you don't mess with anyone, they're not going to mess with you. Labels really don't have a place at The Castle. In fact, the last time I was out, I found myself meeting an entire gang who usually run a straight-as-they-come country western bar. If you're that uptight that you think the Castle is a gay club, you might as well spend your nights watching "The Cosby Show" on TBS. Monday night is 80s/Progressive, which f**king rocks and has the most fulfilling dancefloor experience compared to busier nights. Thursday is Video/Electro/Pop, with some hip-hop and Lonely Island thrown in. I don't leave a Thursday without totally sweating through my clothes from dancing...it's a completely euphoric experience. Friday and Saturday are goth/fetish staples in Tampa. I don't have a leather harness and platform boots ready, so I tend not to show up for the mostly-industrial-dark-dance nights, although my friends just show up in jeans and t-shirts, so there you go. The place is cash only, which can suck, but they have an ATM (and with the sheer volume of people in and out, it's better that they don't mix your card up with someone else's). Every night tends to have some kind of drink special, but nothing is cheaper than $3. So, if you want a night out at a place where you can mix it up, move around, and possibly catch the inspiration to dance all night, hit the Castle.

text: "Meh. I've experienced better." - the Yelp! explanation of a 2-star rating I want to like this place. I really do. It has so much going for it: a great location, a wide selection of wines (not my preference, but I feel truthful facts should be included), and interesting décor (just look up). However, the ways in which Sasha's misses the mark keeps me from rating it even slightly above average. First, I cannot help but feeling swindled when I get a beer there, not that their prices are much different from any other drinking establishment seeking that coveted 25-60 year old customer-base. What grinds my gears is that they charge the same for a bottle of Budweiser as they do a bottle of Schlafly (or Boulevard). While the price contributes to my complaint ($3.50 for a Bud Light is pretty ridiculous), my beef has more to do with the fact that they put the two St. Louis barley pops on the same level. True, there's nothing really wrong with Budweiser, but it's watered down for the masses. It's nothing special; it'll get you drunk. On the other hand, Schlafly is, to put it simply, delicious. At the very minimum, it's a step up from Budweiser, yet the menu does not reflect this (and a price hike at Sasha's would likely not be appreciated). Next, and probably the more glaring problem, is the apparent lack of common sense among the staff. Now, it is entirely possible that my observations are of simple, coincidental lapses on the part of the staff, but to be honest, these lapses were a bit too frequent. Some were minor -- collecting the drink menus immediately after taking the first drink order; some were frustrating -- not knowing whether they were allowed to spike coffee, despite serving both coffee and alcohol; and others were annoying -- trying to clear smoke from the establishment by opening a door near seated customers, blasting them with cold January air. True, Sasha's is an ok place to drink. I'm being nit picky, I know, but there really are better places to eat / drink / be cold. So, will I go back? I really hope not.

text: I've had a lot of experiences with car salesmen, but this takes the cake. My father (a 63 year old business owner, just for some back up - the guy has experience in car purchasing/haggling and sales) was going to help me buy a new car. I had a car accident recently that had totaled my car, so I intended on paying for a car with cash (including my insurance check). We had looked around at a number of vehicles, and decided to check out what kind of deal we could get on a Honda Fit. We had driven around the front and back lots and saw that there were about 20 (including 10 black Fits) on the lot. We headed into the show room and asked for a salesperson. An older man, John, came up and politely introduced himself. But, that was as far as the politeness went. My father mentioned that we were interested in seeing what we could work out on a Fit. John proceeded to tell us that there was no "overhead" on the Fit and that negotiations were out of the picture. My father said "Come on, do we still have to go through this negotiation stuff? Even with the economy the way it is?" John said "How about I give you $500 off," we said no, and stated that we'd like to talk further about it. John said "no deal," and shook his head. He told us that we'd have no chance in getting a deal on a Fit, and practically shooed us out the door. He had no clue that we'd pay cash, he had no clue that we were ready to walk out with a car that very moment. We left completely insulted. He was rude, inconsiderate and seemed like he had more things on his mind (like his newspaper) then to try to sell us a car. My father even mentioned to him "You have 10 black Fit's out back, about 25 on the lot!" and John proceeded to say "no deal." We didn't even get a chance to haggle! UGH! Yes, there is a stereotype of rude salespeople when it comes to cars, and we expect to go through the whole song and dance thing, but, that doesn't mean we expected to be treated this poorly. I advise that you take your Honda business elsewhere. I am even a previous Penske customer (two Chevys) and had never felt this degraded by a sales person there. So, this delays me buying a car another day. I'm really disappointed and we both left so pissed off at the staff that I shot off an email when I got home to Penske. Rudeness = FAIL.

text: Diagonally across grid-locked Route 70 from Han-Ah-Reum (or H-Mart), set back in the Barclay Shopping Center, is the Chinese answer to the Korean mega-mart. I think the Koreans have won. Not that there's nothing to like at the Asian Mart, mind you. For one, it's big. Which means plenty of varieties of instant noodles, canned pickled vegetables, fermented sauces and snacks. They have a five star snack section. Pocky! dried Mango! Salty Prunes! Dried Squid! For the same prices as you would see at Philly's C-town, the deli offers up decent roast pork, duck, soy sauce chicken, curried octopus and porcine offal. The small buy-by-the-pound hot foods section offers mapo doufu and braised pork butt. Just remember to get there early since most of the deli and hot foods are gone by mid-afternoon. Coincidentally, these are items that for obvious reasons, cannot be found at the Han-Ah_reum. Chinese 3, Koreans 0 But what could be a vibrant Asian market experience, turns flat when you visit the fresh veggies and fruit section, and their meat and fish markets. Sure you can get the usual Chinese veggies like Shanghai bai cai and Chinese broccoli and bitter melon, but they like to wrap everything in plastic bags (so that you can't pick certain things and they control the portion you buy). That really irks me. The H-Mart, on the other hand, has that laissez faire thing where I can choose which ever green bean I please and only get 3 ounces if I that's all I need. And, the veggies look fresh, unencumbered by the plastic bags. Chinese 3, Koreans 1. Both places have small fish sections where you can pick a living fish which they will give last rites to and clean it as well. I do find that the H-Mart have somewhat fresher iced fish than the Asian MArt. You can tell by the clarity in the fish's eyes. That is, if you can get yourself to look it in the eye. CHinese 3, Koreans 2. In the meat sections, they both have butchers on hand as well as prepackaged meats. But it's hard to find basic meats, like chicken legs and pork chops at the Asian Mart and often the meats behind the case don't look appetizing. The only time I bought any meat there was when spare ribs were on sale. If I need ground pork for dumplings (jiao zi) or mandoo, I brave crossing Rt. 70 to get to H-Mart. The Koreans have tied it up. But the main reason why I wind up saying "Annyong ha shimnikka" to the missionaries in the parking lot and head into H-Mart is the crispy, demurely sweet store-made rice treats. The stoic rice-cake man pops them out like nobody's business and the free samples keep my whiny kids sedate. Pop! There goes another rice cake. Pure theater! Koreans 4, Chinese 3. So, Asian market, you need loosen up a little. Free the vegetables from their clear plastic straight jackets! Get rid of the rigor mortised, bleary eyed fish on ice! Play on your strengths! Have a Pocky themed event! Cooking classes with durian! Show us that you can partay and we'll come.

text: One of the WORST meals I have ever had -- anywhere, and at any price. I am, admittedly, a food snob. We all know that Tucson is not a center of Modern American cuisine. But even so, Feast is a GIANT culinary famine. 1. Service A bit slow and disinterested. Our server only mentioned 1 of 2 specials. Used cutlery was not replaced until we asked. 2. Atmosphere Typical contemporary design -- VERY noisy. 3. The Food I can forgive front-of-the-house lapses, if the food is good. Unfortunately, the kitchen at Feast is a disaster. I agree with sandy13 about the menu. No bread is offered at Feast - a foolish economy, when it keeps people happy while they wait for their food. (a) Appetizer "Spice-brined confit of pork belly, served over roasted turnips and chard with a molasses-stout glaze and crispy leeks". Portion size was correct, but that's all. Pork belly, when properly prepared, is a sumptuous, silky, melt-in-your-mouth experience. While allegedly a "confit" (meat slowly braised in the animal's own fat), the pork had a fried taste and texture. The meaty part was dry (hard to believe given the fatty cut!). The glaze was thin and bland, the turnips were ok , and the crispy leeks were MIA. The chard was literally inedible. I tried, but had to spit it out. (Every skilled cook knows that chard, a mature green, needs minimum 30 min. of cooking. The longer cooking enables the tough fibers of the leaves to be broken down by heat, rendering the leaves tender enough to be eaten.) (b) Main Dishes (i)"Porchetta ~ roast pork shoulder, spiced with mace and oranges and served with a beurre rouge and a warm salad of sunchokes, pancetta and Brussels sprouts tossed with whole grain mustard." How is it possible to cook a pork roast, COMPLETELY surrounded by a one-inch strip of fat, and end up with a meat that is dry?!? I was stymied. The tiny amount of "beurre rouge" was watery, and had a slightly bitter flavor, as though the chef had used orange peel with the white pith still attached. The sunchokes/sprouts were BITTER to the point of being inedible, not helped by their drowning in what appeared to be plain whole grain mustard. I left it, virtually untouched, on my plate. (ii) 2-piece Fried Chicken Special (with request for dark meat only) My companion's chicken arrived with only 1 piece of chicken, some white/pinkish gravy, and a small leafy salad. A few minutes later, a server brought out a second piece of chicken on a small otherwise naked plate -- no apology. The chicken was not greasy (fried at correct temp.), the gravy was fairly tasty, and the salad was unremarkable. The chicken breading was slightly overcooked, and more importantly, 1 of the 2 pieces of chicken was mostly chicken back, with a small bit of thigh meat. MR. LEVY, PLEASE READ THIS: there is only ONE use for a chicken back in a professional kitchen, and that is to make stock. Never, never try to serve this bony mess to anyone, even if you try to cloak it in a breading. Unbelievable. 4. Conclusion Spend your hard-earned dollars elsewhere. Support local chefs who are professional and competent. How this place is still in business is a mystery to me -- and the place was PACKED on a Wednesday night.

text: Not unexpected, the beer at the Iron Hill Brewery is far superior to the food. I went with family in the late afternoon and we started with beers and appetizers. We'd ordered the egg roll sampler including a Tex Mex egg roll, a cheese steak egg roll and one with salmon in it that I didn't get to try. The Tex Mex egg roll was very tasty and the cheese steak egg roll was interesting, not bad but not the way a cheese steak ought to be eaten. The rest of the table informed me that the salmon egg roll was very tasty, so I'll have to take them at their palates. We also ordered the crab quesadilla which was rather scrumptious and came in quite a large portion! The last app we'd ordered was the artichoke & cheese dip -- please avoid this. It was bland and just a waste of an app. For dinner, I ordered the Macaroni and Four Cheese made with black forest ham, sweet peas, vidalia onions and an almond crumb topping. It was pretty yummy, but the cheese/sauce was very thing and it was made with ziti, which just didn't seem right. Definitely sticking to Bethlehem Brew Works mac&cheese from now on. I did get to sample a Belgian meatball which was delightful: they came in a roasted mushroom sauce that was divine. Major thumbs up for the Raspberry Wheat beer, the Dunkelweizen, the seasonal Belgian IPA, the Vienna Red Lager, and the Le Monstre. Not disappointed by a single one. Iron Hill is trying to cater to a more affluent clientele, made apparent by their hoity-toity menu options, but really, it's a bit over the top. Definitely stick to the beer.

text: I've been to McFadden's at the Ball Park a few times, the most recent being last night when my boyfriend and I went because we had a Groupon for it. The only rule on the Groupon was that we couldn't redeem it during any of the Eagles, Flyers or Phillies home games. That's fine, we figured, we'll just go when the Phils are on the road, have a few beers, eat some food and watch the game with other fans. Can't go too wrong there, right? WRONG. First, this place is absolutely DEAD on a night when there isn't a game going on at home. Seriously we were 2 of maybe 8 patrons in the whole entire restaurant. There were more staff just standing around drinking and talking loudly than actual customers. That brings me to my second point- The waitstaff/bartenders/employees all decided to congregate 10 feet away from our table and hung out there the entire time, laughing and joking around with one another. (This is fine, I'm all for a happy and friendly work environment, but don't do it while you're practically standing on top of customers!) A few of the guys were putting together a shop vac right there and had all the pieces strewn on the floor around us, so that I couldn't even get up to go to the bathroom. Then once they finished putting it together they tested it out right there, vacuuming up under our table without saying anything to us! It was so awkward, and honestly felt like we were intruding on their space. They made us feel like we were over staying our welcome at a restaurant that is trying to close for the night (even though it was only 7:30). It was really rude and we didn't get one apology or even an acknowledgment that we were sitting right there. The food was something that I remembered being pretty decent from the last time I came there, though it could have something to do with the fact that the last time I ate there I was completely trashed from the game and was so hungry that even Chase Utley's sweaty batting helmet would have tasted delicious. Yuck. This time however, completely sober, the food was nothing special. Just basically bad pub food. The cheesesteak nachos, which they claim to be famous for, would literally been the same as me opening my mouth and having the waitress empty an entire container of Wiz into my mouth and put a chip and a small peice of dry meat on top. YUM. Anyway, I'll wrap this up. I would have given it ZERO stars, but the fact that it's a pretty fun atmosphere when the game is going on warrants some recognition. But really, give me a tv screen, lots of beer and other Phillies fans and I'm a happy girl. Moral of the story- Go here if there's a game going on and you're too broke to buy a ticket, but you still want to experience the game atmosphere, BUT for the love of god and all that is holy, don't even think about going to McFadden's when any of the teams are on the road. text: I ate at Jazz a week ago, and was pleasantly surprised. I haven't ever been to New Orleans, but this place will give you the essence of being there in a Disney Land type of way. It was clean, and still had the new car smell. I give new restaurants a lot of lee way for service and food quality, but the day we showed up everything was fine. We ordered the chicken wings ($.50 each on Wednesdays), and considering myself a connoisseur of chicken wings, I was very happy with them! You can ask them to make them extra spicy, which is a good idea, as the regular are kinda wimpy. I wasn't in love with my entree, the Louisiana shrimp; it was too saucy with out a lot of substance. My rating was based on the skill of the deep fryer; he did an amazing job on everything that was deep fried. The wings, crawfish, catfish, shrimp and oysters were all cooked to perfection! Crisp and light, while still succulent on the inside. Keep that guy around Jazz! Be warned, with all new restaurants quality will vary as the chefs learn their stations... Long story short 3 out of 4 entrees were great, the appetizers during happy hour were $4.99 and worth every penny, the wings were fantastic and a great price at $.50 each on Wednesdays... and the place was clean with a decent staff. At my age with a 20 month old daughter I prefer the Disney Land Experience to the Bourbon Street experience, but your taste may vary (sorry no flashing from coeds while I was there)! The downers were my entree (the Louisiana Shrimp) and the bread you get when you arrive (big time blah).
label: NEG

text: Every time we go to Reno, we end up eating in the casinos. This time, I wanted to venture out and see what Reno really had to offer. I looked on Yelp and with 4.5 stars and $$, I thought Casale's would be a hit. I really really wanted to like this place. It's what everyone says, completely homely. The place itself looks like an old house, with the inside gutted out. The tables and chairs don't all match. Each table had vinyle table covers that don't get cleaned after each seating. The waiter (son) just comes by and uses the menu to dust off the table, and then hands you the menu after! Every time we would move in our seats, the table cloth would slide off the table. There is only ONE person running the outside, the son of momma. He is the busboy, waiter, host. I honestly feel horrible for him. The place is small, fitting about 50 people in it, but it was pretty packed on a Friday night at 8pm. So you can imagine how the service is with just one person. This wasn't bad if you just have a bit of empathy for him, but they really should at least hire a busboy to help out. They had a very simple menu, with only lasagna, spaghetti, meatballs, ravioli, pizza, and sandwiches. The back of the menu said they were famous for their homemade raviolis and pizza. I ordered meat raviolis with meat balls and tried to talk hubby into ordering pizza, but he wanted lasagna. The meal comes with bread and salad. We upgraded to garlic bread for $1 each. Big mistake on the lasagna. There was nothing in it but pasta, and then cheese on top, baked. No cheese or meat in the middle. It had little flavor. My lasagna at home would have gotten 5 stars from Reno if this spot got 4.5 stars. It was so plain, he had to take one of my meatballs. My ravioli came with 2 meatballs, and watery meat sauce. The inside was mushy, and tasted like poor quality meat. The sauce had no flavor to it. The "garlic bread" was just dinner rolls with garlic powder, salt, and butter on it. It was so toasted, it cut up the roof of my mouth. I'm not sure if this is what "authentic" Italian homecooking is like, but if it is, please let me have Macaroni Grill any day! Highlight of the meal is when momma came out of the kitchen and started clearing off some tables. She's really sweet, and comes by the tables to see if you're doing ok. I even got a picture with her as proof! Hubby wants to come back and give the pizza a try. I wouldn't mind either, as I want to support the local mom and pop shops. Plus the spot was CHEAP. The most expensive wine bottle in the place was $10. Corkage was $5. Total meal was under $30.
label: NEG

text: A Gem in the Rough! This little salon is tucked away and difficult to see from the street as it is on the 2nd level of 19th Street between Sansom & Chestnut. The interior is warm and classy and the owner and nail technician are meticulous and kind. As the owner doesn't advertise and his salon is modestly set off from the beaten path, I'm so glad that I found them on Yelp because my experience was truly wonderful! I called them the morning prior with fingers crossed that they could fit me in before I went to a rehearsal dinner/wedding weekend. I found out the night before my appointment that my roommate needed a girl's pick-me-up following a dramatic break-up (we all know that feeling!), so I called to ask if she could come, too. "No problem, look forward to seeing you both tomorrow!" I didn't find out until later that the owner and his technician opened early that day for us!! When we got there, Jeff, was setting up the salon for the day and offered us coffee as compensation for our 5 minute wait. Classy and thoughtful. The second delightful surprise of the day came when his nail technician, Danin ("Daneen"), showed up, with our coffee in hand from La Colombe! So sweet. My roommate and I LOVED the pedicures -- best we've had so far. The massage was thorough and incredibly relaxing. They weren't scared to give my feet a good buffing like other salons. Thank heavens! My roommate almost fell asleep listening to Josh Groban in the background and looking out the salon's bright window down onto the bustling Autumn street below. Perfect treatment for the Ex-BF blues. I also got a beautiful manicure from Danin -- who is cute-as-a-button and tries very hard to be engaging! She did a great job on the tips of my french manicure (not too thick and even looked great on my short ugly duckling nail that I was nurturing from a previous hangnail pull. She continued working until it was perfect and then applied several quick-dry polishes/finishes before finishing. Oh and did I mention that the salon's polish selection was legitimately broad-spec!? Definitely plan to make a return roommate visit soon.With french style and tip I think it was about 75-80 altogether for mani-pedi. Just remember to bring cash as they don't take cards. If you forget, no biggie as there is an ATM @ street level on the block. :)

text: We took a gamble on this one for my college graduation dinner. And gladly so!! Everything was everything I could have wanted & more. They accommodated our party of ten with friendly and very professional service. They were attentive (perk of a smaller place) and were prompt with bringing out more & more of our seven bottles of wine from the back. Even Chef Mark came to ask us if we enjoyed everything & congratulated me on my graduation. The food was phenomenal, inventive, hearty, and decadent. Between all the guests I believe we tried most of the menu. And there is something to be said for each of the appetizers and entrees. The amazing thing about their food was the use of subtle flavors. For example, a wonderful scallop appetizer with 'vanilla salt' which gave it a sweet and savory background flavor. Even my arugula salad had a very high quality sweet goat cheese on top. Please order the lobster crepes!! Its worth a few extra dollars on an appetizer. They were large!! And hearty!! As for entrees, expect large portions!! No itty bitty fancy food here! The best way to describe the food overall is American Contemporary. These were all fresh, recognizable ingredients. Most of the food felt rustic and warm. I got the lamb which had a melt in your mouth texture. The plate contained a huge chop and a braised lamb shoulder wrapped in a crispy phyllo dough!! The lobster mac and cheese was a signature dish that I hope they always keep on the menu. The very generous portion of lobster pieces in egg noodles and cheese sauce was also topped with a large lobster tail. Talk about comfort food! My friend really enjoyed her salmon with an orange glaze. It was tender and moist. My mother also said the blackened cod was delicious. With the place filling up closer to 8 or 8:30pm it started to get very hot in the restaurant, almost uncomfortably so. They make want to consider ceiling fans or opening their windows on nice evenings if they can't turn the a/c up more. The meal was ended with a complimentary dessert plate with many assorted chocolate desserts for me with "congratulations" written in chocolate sauce! How sweet. Their homemade chocolates that come with the check make even paying for it a sweet experience. (I guess especially when you're the one so kindly being treated.) The food is appropriately priced. I believe the most expensive entree was the lobster mac at $26, which was worth every penny! The fact that it is a BYOB just seals the deal for my family & I. This place has its full focus on its food and providing an enjoyable experience for its customers. It also had seating outside underneath the romantic, spirited lights of Liberties Walk. I will definitely be returning very soon to take advantage of the seating in the spring weather. My new 'go to' BYOB and certainly makes my personal 'list.'

text: I love browsing as McKay because I'm always guaranteed to find something interesting. Their prices are so cheap that it's the kind of place I can still pick up something I totally don't need and not feel too guilty about it. When I have to buy a specific book, I always check here before buying it new at full price, and many times I have found what I wanted. In particular, they have a lot of classics, so it's easy to find anything that is regularly on a high school or college reading list. You might be able to pick up a hardback for about half the price you'd pay for a regular paperback, so it's worth taking the time to look. They also have a great anthology section and if you have a thing for art or photography books, they have a nice selection. I always look here for gifts, because it's easy to find books that look like brand new. If you're still watching VHS tapes, they have a huge section of $2 tapes and they also have box sets of VHS and DVD TV shows for a significant discount over buying new. The video games seem highly priced though, and many aren't any cheaper than buying new, which I don't really understand. I wish McKay made it a little more comfortable to browse.
