text: Marly B's extremely negative review of PCS got my attention today so I wanted to write my own review, since I have had the exact opposite experience with this company. I absolutely love this company. I moved to Philly 2 years ago, and before I came here, I sold my car. One of the reasons I knew I'd be able to live car-free was that I knew PCS existed, and that I would have relatively convenient access to a car whenever I needed it. Well, that's exactly what I've gotten. We're still just in the infant stages of what I think will become a very large car sharing industry. And even at this early stage, car sharing programs demonstrate their unbelievable value. My annual transportation costs are FAR lower than they would be if I was a car owner. The true value of PCS is in the minimal annual expense. Sure, they've got an annual fee now. That has apparently annoyed a lot of people. What is it? $120? That's a couple gas refills if you're a car owner. Give them a break. Jeez. I was actually very happy when they instituted the annual membership fee. I WANT this company to succeed, and I recognize that they need a somewhat stable revenue stream, and I also recognize that having a membership fee will tend to eliminate from the program members of inferior quality - deadbeats. The kind of people who are more likely to damage the car, steal shit, etc. It adds just a small bit of exclusivity to the program, which I like. So people don't like the annual membership fee? Okay, well do they like not having to pay over 1000 bucks for car insurance every year? I mean, come on. I'll take that trade any day. Speaking of the annual fee, it used to be a monthly charge to your credit card. I like that they now automatically charge my credit card just once a year. Because I don't like seeing a charge on my credit card every month. It just irritates me. I prefer one annual charge. A few more points about PCS: *Some have complained that the cars are unclean on the inside. Generally speaking, I've always found them to be fairly clean on the inside. Do members really want PCS to vacuum the cars after EVERY use? If so, expect higher hourly charges. Personally, I'd rather have lower hourly charges and the occasional crumb on my seat. *Many of the complaints I've seen are along the lines of "I did something stupid and irresponsible and PCS penalized me for it." Well, ya know, ya might want to stop doing stupid and irresponsible things. If you're relatively intelligent and responsible, you won't have too much trouble. I've never gotten any kind of penalty in the two years I've been a member. *In two years, I've only had trouble with one reservation - I couldn't get into my car. On this particular day, I also had a broken cellphone, which complicated things. Had my cellphone worked, I could have called them and I'm fairly confident they could have helped. Regardless, they refunded my money for this reservation. The folks on the phone are always really nice.

Though I think you can avoid having your entrails ripped from your body at Ruby Tuesday (as of the time of this writing), I would still keep that in mind. Oh, and shoot for the head. Anywhooooo, in terms of "modern American chain dining blackholes", RT is better than TGI Friday's (not anywhere near as cheesy), and also better than Applebees (its not as...classless. But in a sense I guess RT harvests the absolute value of negative class, so I suppose that is a good thing? I don't know). Its better in the way that the 3rd circle of Hell isn't as bad as the 5th. Make sense? So, yea...we were seated after waiting about 10 minutes, and after a bit too long a young guy walks up and asks if we've yet been helped. Nope. Oh, well I guess I will be your server. You...guess? Is this serving by committee? Every man for himself? Ok, whatever. To drink I will have...oh, wait, he's gone. You see, rule #1 is you take a drink order right off the bat...maybe people don't know what they want yet, but you at least give them the option. We end up giving our drink orders a few minutes later, and then the drinks took almost 15 minutes to come out. Don't think it was the servers fault, but there is no way that a glass of wine, glass of beer, etc. should take that long. No way. Ok, finally, we order our meals (after our drinks arrived...surely we cannot decide on our meal with no beverages in front of us). Almost 45 minutes later they come out. Sigh. I had the "Asian Salmon and Shrimp", somehow forgetting my rule not to order seafood at pooptastic chain restaurants. I guess the picture swayed me. It was actually edible, which counts for one star in the review. They skimped on the shrimp (less mercury for me...hooray!), and the salmon wasn't overcooked. Rice was...present. I've had worse. My parents seemed to like their meal, but as you might infer they aren't terribly picky. I guess that is a good thing...you don't have to try very hard to be satisfied. I am almost jealous. The mere presence of a coupon trumps all other considerations. No wonder I am confused. I must toss props in the direction of previous reviewers Laura D. and Jae L...for the former, the restaurant did indeed have "that smell". Shall I expound at length the enormous degree of ineptitude it takes to display such a video feed, continuously, during the weekend rush? As in the way it sorta shows the customer how little they (the business) really GAF about you? Or should I discuss the very nature of a "restaurant" (as in, not a sports bar) that feels the need to stuff TV's in every corner? No? Ok. All that said, this might be a decent location to grab a quick lunch during the week if you are nearby. Not a great place, but also not a place with a drive-thru window (that is like...the 9th circle or something. I don't know how many circles are down/up there). Or just pack your own lunch, whatever. In sum, never eat here on purpose.

text: I came to Ichigo Modern because I was a big fan of Sekisui Pacific Rim (the previous restaurant at this location) and was looking for a replacement. To test it out, I went for the lunch buffet. I know that lunch buffets are never that great, but I've found it can be a good test of quality - if you can't make decent, simple california rolls, I likely will not be impressed with your "signature" sushi. So I went in with low expectations. In my head, there are three sushi faux pas that should never be committed, and Ichigo Modern was guilty of all three of those. 1. Never make humongous sushi. Sushi should be small, bite-size. It's a dainty process of enjoying the freshness of the ingredients used. The sushi here is a disastrous explosion of mismatched components, and are unwieldy to look at and eat. 2. Never use cream cheese. Even if the crazy overstuffed sushi here was okay, I wouldn't have been able to taste it beneath the sticky, overwhelming cream cheese present in so many rolls. This is perhaps the easiest way to ruin a good piece of sushi - any flavor was drowned in my painstaking attempts to un-stick the gunk from my teeth. 3. Condiments on sushi are a no-no. Teriyaki sauce? Flavored mayo? If I wanted a flavor explosion I'd be eating Latin cuisine, certainly not Japanese. Several of the rolls were drenched in a variety of terrifying sauces, none of which tasted good or served any purpose. Not to mention it just looked dirty and messy. They also offered a selection of hot dishes; the caliber was about similar to Panda Express. I won't complain too much. I came for the sushi. If the food here wasn't bad enough, service was a disappointment as well - slow and disorganized. Plates were grabbed inconsiderately away as you barely finished eating, creating a jarring and unpleasant atmosphere. Ichigo Modern represents the complete antithesis of Japanese cuisine, with its clumsy, muddled, and unartfully thrown together "sushi" rolls. The saddest part is that the individual ingredients were actually quite fresh - what a pity.

text: I recently found this little chocolate shop on a side street in historic Lambertville. Located just across the river from New Hope and Bucks County, PA, this town is a yuppie mecca filled with little shops. Surprisingly for the area, the prices for the chocolates were on par with other chocolate shops we have visited and just as important, they were delicious and rich in flavor! We bought a small sample to take home to enjoy. ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- Update: 3/2011: While the chocolates are good, service leaves something to be desired. On my second visit there, the manager waited on me. I was about to start my order when she allowed some other woman who had just arrived, to interrupt with her order. This was done without any kind of apology or excuse from either woman. My wife and I were speechless. Plus, I believe there was a second incident that day where this manager put us off to go do something before finally taking our order. I guess one could chalk it up to the Jersey culture, but it seemed downright rude to me. We decided there are other chocolate shops out there that are more deserving of our business. text: they give you a crapload of fish for a good price, and the fancy rolls are deeelish. the same roles would be twice the price at a nicer place. if you dont want a lot of goopy sauces, tell them ahead of time. they also might sometimes use msg because i got a headache once when i left. all things considered, if you want a really casual byob to get a lot of snacky, savory sushi, check this place out. don't get me wrong, it isn't like bland mall sushi. it has a lot of flavor, it just doesn't seem upscale... maybe just because of the environment. i wouldn't bring a date here, it doesn't have that kind of vibe. it's super simplistic with stupid pictures on the walls and basic tables and chairs. you can see them making your sushi, and that's the only atmospheric element to this place. anyway, i love it

text: Cusumano's saddens me. It has SO much potential to be a great bar/restaurant/club. However, it's downfall is that the owners don't know what it should be. The pizza is decent (for St. Louis style pizza) but then they have to mess that up with a really irritating "2 for 1" offer at the bar, where they just divide up my rum and coke into two glasses and charge me $4. That particular drink was very watered down and it made me question the professionalism of the bartender. It's hard to mess up a simple mixed drink, but when you do, it makes huge waves. I was invited by some old friends to visit this establishment for a "hip hop" show, which I later found out that the group paid the establishment to perform. I know that happens in a lot of other cities, but that shouldn't happen in St. Louis, where there are plenty of bars hungry for live entertainment. The bar should be paying the band. The show itself was a terrible production, with the group's banner scrawled on some old bed sheets. The rappers and their amps were stuck in a corner, which made the acoustics terrible. In terms of lyrics: they stunk. I accidentally bumped into one of their bouncers, and he kind of pushed me out of the way. I mean, this wasn't even a drunken bump, just my own clumsiness. An apology wasn't even taken when I gave it to him; he just wanted to act like a stereotypical bouncer... Sad. This place needs a lot of work. The décor is run-down. The drinks are watered-down. The entire place gets me down. I'm not going back here again unless I'm dragged, kicking and screaming. So much potential...

text: Basically the worst hotel I have ever stayed in, in my entire life. - Filthy dirty - Bed was old, stained and tattered. The bed frame was made out of slats of wood screwed together. The box spring looked like someone had spilled something (please don't make me guess what) and then beaten it with a bat. I didn't know they still made spring mattresses with no padding what so ever. It was horribly uncomfortable. - Road Noise was atrocious! I couldn't sleep at all because I was so worried about people breaking in (there is no top lock). All the rooms face out to the busy street. - The bathtub had about a half inch gap between the tub and the tile. That gap was full of mold. The bath mat they provided had mold rings all over it...eating up through the top of the mat. When we walked in, we knew something was wrong. The light hardly came on, it was low and dingy- we had to turn every light in the place on. There was an odor ionizing machine out in the middle of the room, sitting on a trashcan that had been turned sideways. There was also no shower curtain. The irony of the whole situation was when I called down to ask why there was no shower curtain and a machine in our room, they responded "we were doing a deep cleaning". No you weren't. I saw your housekeeping cart & it didn't have a vacuum. The floors were absolutely disgusting & covered with dirt and hair. There was a portion of the room (between the bed and the wall) where a vacuum cleaner couldn't have fit--it looked as if no one had ever cleaned there. I had the biggest panic attack because of this place and I am not even a germaphobe. I had just spent a week camping at Bonnaroo with 70k other people, using portapoties & public restrooms and there is no way I would ever get 5 feet within this hotel room. Absolutely the most disgusting place I have ever stayed in. When I got home I took the hottest shower I could & scrubbed 3 times. I feel violated. Price: $95 dollars through Expedia. text: I can't recommend Diverse Catering enough. The deal with wedding food usually is: it's the most expensive & least memorable part of the reception. Diverse Catering helped us buck this trend in a big way. With our input, they created an absolutely amazing autumnal, vegetarian-friendly (but with meat also), locally-sourced, family style dinner that included over 7 dishes. I can't count the number of people who came up to us to report that it was far and away the BEST food they had ever eaten at a wedding. I heartily agreed & consider myself to be a discerning eater who regularly pays good money to eat good food in restaurants. And the cost was significantly less (like, in the thousands) than our other bids. The best part, though, was how far above and beyond the call of duty they went. They helped us save money throughout by using their local contacts & common sense. They helped us with the design of the room and other aesthetic parts of set-up. They were incredibly friendly to our family and friends -- I really felt like they had all (staff included) become our family and friends by the end. They even drove my husband's forgotten bag of spare shoes across town at the end of a long night and hand-delivered them to us at the hotel bar. Amazing. Use Diverse Catering if you want to work with people who care more about their craft & keeping it fun than they do about making $$$.

text: Pho is what I get at closeby restaurants back home when I feel like a quick satisfying meal. A huge bowl full of noodles, rare slices of steak that's tender and cooked in the hot broth, the little extras that I throw into the bowl (along with Sriracha and hoisin sauce) - it always adds up to a pleasurable dining experience - no frills needed. That being said, this place really didn't live up to expectations. First off, for a place called Pho Nouveau, it was really odd to see only two pho options (one of which being chicken pho). I suppose the owners were afraid of exposing Boise natives to such exotic options as tendon and tripe. It's a shame because those are often the best pieces of meat within the pho! There were plenty of other options, though including Bun and rice plates. The place used to be a bar - so it was quite odd to come into it to see no alcohol and the bar area still intact. The restaurant felt cramped and it didn't help that the table where I sat (located next to the bar) was a bottleneck for the waittresses. Remove the table and you'll probably feel like you have more room. But if you decide to keep it, get taller high chairs. It's difficult to eat when you feel shorter than the table... For lunch I got the pho (obviously). Overall, it was so-so at best. The broth felt like it was missing... something. Disappointing was the amount of meat (barely 10 slices), but worst of all was the fact that the meat tasted over-cooked as if they were boiled to well done and then placed again into the broth. No bueno =/ I paid $10 for the bowl that was barely the size of a medium (with the contents of a small) and that I could've gotten at home for about $6 after tax AND tip. =/ Also, the water had a strange after taste that I can only describe as... plasticky. The service was also, to borrow another Yelper's description, "rough." When I walked in, it took the owner about 5 minutes to notice I was standing there before she told me to seat myself. if the place were busy, I'd understand, but there were barely 4 tables seated at the time I walked in. I usually think of pho as a fast and good meal - unfortunately, it took about 10 minutes to get my check and change. Apparently it takes 3 waittresses to figure out how to make change for a $20. Prepared? I guess not - the owner had to reach into her own pocketbook to get my change... Not sure if I'll be back again... nice try, though...

text: Cha...CHAH! I don't know what these people are talking about with their mediocre reviews. The place is solid! It also has a lot of fried foods, you need to be prepared for that, if you don't like fried small plates don't go there and please don't write some bad review because of it! Also tapas menus tend to change, it's good when they change, it means someone is back in the kitchen experimenting with food! I thought that's what you want out of a chef? Sometimes they hit, sometimes they miss, but at least they are trying. So, we had Chris, he was awesome! We were supposed to have someone else but they were busy so he took us instead. This was settled in literally two minutes. He gave recommendations, he was chatty, and most of all he was prompt and very nice! The food. We went small plates. The humus is great but it is home made so it's different, either way I really liked it. I also LOVED the butter fried potatoes with aioli. The octopus was yummy (not fried), the chickpea cod is a stand out. It was like baby fish and chips and not fishy like cod can be. We rounded out or dinner with quail wings and chorizo croquettes. The total bill with tip, FYI we tip 20%, was $72 and that included two beers and two glasses of wine. We were pleasantly full and as per my usual trips to tapas places I did not need to stop for a burger after. Again solid place with a great ambiance and outside patio that is money!

Overall, there was nothing I didn't like. I personally am not a big fan of the "chinese pizzas", which are a.k.a scallion pancakes, but everyone else seemed to love them. I asked him to make me a selection of nigiri and sashimi, including Amberjack sashimi, which I had in Japan. The fish seemed fresh, but not necessarily the best I have had. The Amberjack was great and they even offer an Amberjack carpaccio, which I plan to try next time. Upon seeing my interest in sushi/sashimi, the chef said they would get live scallops on Friday for sashimi....guess where I am eating dinner this Friday. Overall an average looking Japanese restaurant from the outside, which can be easily overlooked but do give it a try, especially if you like sushi/sashimi. text: What a complete and utter let down. I am so frustrated by my dining experience last night and I think it's partly my fault. I truly set my expectations too high and I left totally dissapointed. Before I delve into last night's total fail (which is a long doozy, I'd admit), here is what I expected of Philadelphia's supposedly "best restaurant": 1) Impeccable, involved and flawless service befitting a traditional upscale french restaurant 2) an educated and present sommelier 3) an exciting à-la-carte menu, specials and amuse-bouche 4) expertly executed food with beautiful presentations 5) fresh, excellent selections of beef, fish, shellfish, and bread 6) proper desert presentation and serving sizes Let me tell you, Le Bec Fin (which translates as the "Fine Nose" - [or literally 'beak'] for wine, food, etc) does not live up to the hype. Whatever Le Bec Fin was once known for, it no longer deserves the title. I've received far better food and service at a myriad of other places in the city. I've eaten far better French cuisine at Bistros elsewhere for a fraction of the price. Le Bec Fin failed on all six counts of my expectations. First, the service simply sucked. It was inexcusable. We were a party of five, reservation at 8:30 pm and aside from a party of 15 at the front of the house, the rest of the dining room was half empty and they had an ample staff working. The maitre'd was absent for most of the meal, and he was just plain awkward, disinterested and an amateur. Aside from the forced theatricality of placing napkins on diners' lap, the royal treatment ended there. He insisted on calling us madame and monsieur which was such a farce ( are we at a themed restaurant here? my family and I are French Canadian, and this man is no French speaker, he barely spoke english - so why bother?). Never offered the wine list until halfway through our appetizers and after we had to ask for one. The food runners/bread servers were awkward and ill-trained (kept dropping our bread on the floor, wrongly served us both our entrées and main courses - we had to tell them who got what) My parents ordered the esgargot as their entrées (yes, as their appetizer - I know I'm guilty of this too, using the word entrée as a main course rather than the first) and waited an eternity before the captain showed up to take off the lid off the cocottes. The sommelier was bored and robotic (perhaps, it's because we didn't order a $200 bottle of wine?) and after running out of our first two choices of wines, he didn't even bother to decant the wine he offered and poured sediment in three of our glasses. Moreover, beware of the wine list, all wines are priced up 200 to 300% - so choose wisely. Secondly, the food was just okay - I've had much better, but it was decent and the only thing that saved Le Bec Fin from getting only one star from me. I expected the small portions, I just didn't expect the food to be so average. Even from the beginning - it was a tell-tale sign: serving stale baguette bread with regular old butter - From the amuse-bouche (a grapefruit jelée? blah) to my entrée (foie gras, preparation and presentation both just so-so) and my plat principal (Japanese black bass - poorly cut piece of fish- with a 'yawn' yellow tomato-consomée) - nothing was memorable and nothing was worthy of the praise that Le Bec Fin seems to be getting from everyone and everywhere. What gave the evening a bit of a lift was the gorgeous desert cart with a plethora of offerings - each one appearing as delectable as the next. But the presentation (by the desert waiter?) was totally lackluster, jumbled and the portions served were truly miniscule. Teeny-tiny triangles dropped on white plates with no adornment, no frills - which was dissapointing except for the taste - rich, savoury and sinful - all of them. (not to mention that our coffees, espressos didn't even make a showing until after we had finished all our sweets) All in all, a terribly disorganized choreography of a meal - with dissonant notes throughout. Disjointed service and mediocre food. Sit down, Bec-Fin, I think your time here is done.
label: NEG

text: I love sushi. I mean really really love sushi. If I could afford it, I would eat sushi every single day. Yes, at the tender age of 15, having never had sushi, a "Friend" decides I have to try it and takes me to Aloha of all places. First of all, the atmosphere sucks. I completely agree that the place feels like a deserted casino. It's way too dark and there's something sort of eerily cavernous about the whole place. Our sushi chef was nice enough, but it took me a solid fifteen minutes to get someone to bring me a water. Seeing as how it was my first time, we decided to forego the all you can eat and just order a couple of items. My friend got two long rolls and I got two hand rolls. I can't recall the names, but they were all mostly crab or crystal shrimp (the safest things for a newbie). My hand rolls had some nauseating sweet sauce on them that tasted like mayonaisse and sugar. I've had my fair share of interesting aiolis in my time, but this was just plain gross. My friend devoured both her long rolls, and seemed to enjoy them, but I was feeling sick so I didn't even want to try them. So, all in all, it was two years before I got brave enough to try sushi again, and now I realize it's the most amazing food on earth. I'm very angry at Aloha for taking two years off my sushi-eating life.

text: I just needed a quick oil change and all the reviews seemed really positive about this place...so I drove over and decided to give it a try. For a place that advertises exactly what it is - a quick and speedy "in and out" oil change and car wash...I'm sure that it is fine. However, after they loaded my car in and was in the process of topping off the levels they informed me that I need to bleed the power steering hoses and replace my air filter....etc... I said "yes"- and that was my own fault for feeling pressured in this situation, and not just saying "NO, I'm going to take it to an ACTUAL garage." an hour later, I walked out $180 poorer (when I thought I was just going to spend $30 on an oil change.) And my car was now making a TERRIBLE power steering moan which never went away (even though they insisted it would), they couldn't actually explain to me anything they did, and then my car started smoking when I turned it on. long story short, JUST GO THERE FOR AN OIL CHANGE. They will rip you off for ANY other service they "insist" you need. (which i should have just trusted my gut on - making me equally to blame.) I had to take my car to another place the next day and repair all the mistakes and mess they made under the hood. But now my car works great!....200 bucks later.
label: NEG

text: I remember when this building used to be a sheriff's office - the sushi place is a definite upgrade! It is a great hole-in-the-wall place to get a sushi fix. I haven't really tried other things on the menu, but the sushi always hits the spot. All of the sushi is great, from the eel and cucumber to the Philadelphia roll and everything in between. The sushi rolls are a little on the small side, and there are other places in Indy where they put more fish in the rolls. However, the prices here are EXTREMELY reasonable. You can stuff yourself with sushi and not feel guilty about it later. When you have a sushi craving, this is definitely the place to go. The service here is also great. The Asian lady who greets you is super friendly, and the young lady who waits on tables is really friendly as well.
label: POS

text: A friend of mine works in Camden, and he dragged me to this place for lunch one day. It's was a few minutes from his workplace, where Pennsauken meets Camden. You walk in and the place swallows you. It's dungeon like. I felt like there should have been a renaissance-style duel at the far end of the room, but, alas, there was only a lonely salad bar. For a place that size, the food surprisingly came without anything major to complain about. Of course, there were very few people in the establishment when my friend and I went, during lunch. Which is funny, since we still our service was still pretty slow. (But then, with a restaurant that size, it probably took the waitress to get from the kitchen to our table.) This may be a quirky place for an office get-together, but definitely don't book this monster of a restaurant for your wedding/bar mitzvah. It will draw more than a few unpleasant snickers/chuckles.
label: NEG

text: All of my experiences here have been good! The workers are very polite (as with all ChickFilA locations). I will keep bringing my business here.
label: POS

text: Made reservations for 7pm. They sat us in the bar or wait an hour. It was on bar stools and we are seniors who also did not like the bar noise especially when the Phillies scored. The waitress was ok but asked us if were enjoying our dinner less than a minute after we got the main course. Never retuned except with bill. Food: bread pretty nice. Butter great. We both ordered the same food. Caprese salad was very nice. Don't order two. It was quite large. Could have used more vinegar. BTW no salt or pepper on anyone's table. We had scallops for dinner. They were so salty we each stopped eating them. Calling a busboy and telling him was a waste. (My wife tried the ones we took home, for lunch the next day and said they were now delicious). The risotto was very nice and the mushrooms were fabulous. Had dessert at home. With tip $75 (1 beer) felt it was high for Conshy. Perhaps I would rate higher for twenty somethings.
label: NEG

text: I can appreciate a no food or drink policy in a store, really I can. However. It's not like I wandered in, fresh from Mardi Gras revelry with a Hand Grenade or jumbo sized Hurricane in my hand, dripping greasy shrimp po' boy juice all over the floor. I walked in with a covered Diet Soda in my hand at 2pm on a Wednesday and was verbally shoved back out the door in a manner that makes me want to help you understand the definition of "customer service." Shop Girl - I am the type of impulse purchaser that goes out to buy toilet paper, walks past a shoe store and inadvertently buys five pairs of new heels; these ones because they were good for work, those two because they were sexy, and two more just because they were on sale. I'm sure your manager will be happy to know that your attitude cost your store that revenue. I really wanted those little green flats in the window. Jerk. I'm giving the store an extra star because it appeared they had good deals. I should've spent more time standing outside looking in the window I guess.
label: NEG

text: This place has the largest selection of sandwich I've seen in a long time. If you like hot or cold sandwiches I really do recommend trying this place out. The food is very great and the service is really friendly. I recently ordered to go and they got my order ready and done. Once I came to pick it up it was already bagged and everything. Quick service! They also have chips, salads, soup and mmm Gelato. Great place 5 stars!
label: POS

text: Not off the beaten path, but not quite out in the open this small unasuming spot delivers a fresh departure from the Mcfast food places that line 73. I must have been in this shopping center a dozen times over the past year and just noticed this place the other day. Since I knew my wife loves this type of food (as do I ) I brought her here the next day for lunch. We came in the next day for lunch and ordered falafel sandwiches and a plate of hummus to share. Both of us loved everyything that we had. The falafel sandwich was the perfect size for 1 person and had about 6-7 pieces of falafel inside a freshly baked pita. Fresh vegetables and tahini sauce were also added resulting in a fantastic sandwich. High marks also went to the hummus which had a great consistency and a good kick of spice to it, that coupled with a fresh baked pita made for a great side to share. Hopefully this place sticks around for a while becuase both of us plan to go back there often. Good food, reasonable price and within driving distance of our home make for a great place to have lunch. Located inside the Borders shopping center on 73 by Evesham.
label: POS

text: Coming from a person who does not like chain restaurants, I have to say I love the Cheesecake Factory. I was addicted to it when I lived in California and unlike most chain restaurants, it has only gotten better with time. They have over 200 menu options including pizza, pasta, seafood, steaks, salads, sandwiches, burgers, and more. And they have over 50 delicious cheesecakes and desserts. Menu choices reflect an Americanized fusion of ethnic cuisines from around the world. They have done a fine job of coming up with creative items that please the masses. They also have a large number of healthy choices. I love the pear endive salad, avocado egg rolls, Thai lettuce wraps, shrimp with angel hair pasta and whole lot of other items. They've got some great lunch and brunch specials too! You will feel like you're in a cattle call once they give you a "chain restaurant beeper" to use while you wait for a table. And the decor is Disney World meets rustic Bistro. But, the food stands up.
label: POS

text: Oh, Perkins, what a disappointment. I had such high hopes when I saw the vast assortment of muffins in the bakery case. Boston Cream muffin?! For goodness sake, doesn't that sound fabulous? But, though they're marketed as "moist and irresistible," I actually found them dry and... well, basically resistible. Obviously the food is nothing to write home about. It's your basic chain-diner-fare with your basic chain-diner-atmosphere. The only reason we even came here was to take the MIL out to eat. I thought about giving them 2 stars because they are obviously TRYING for interesting muffins, but I just can't. They're so sub-par.
label: NEG

text: The WORST crabcake I can remember having. So maybe it is slightly my fault for ordering a crabcake sandwich as opposed to much more mindless options such as fries covered in cheese or a burger. Maybe by carrying bar in the name, they are sending signals to which end of the business they prioritize. But when I see "jumbo lump crabcake" and "heirloom" tomato involved in a sandwich I can not help but be drawn. I think someone with a knowledge of food, and probably a passion created this menu, and its wordage, but they are not the one carrying out the day to day. This crabcake seriously tasted like a bought in frozen patty. There was no taste of sweet crab. It was dry and over whelmed by spice. It was a thin crab patty, with too much filling as opposed to the sweet delicate flavor I expect from a jumbo lump crab cake. I actually hope I do not get sick... Everything else: Service was Ok. Our server was nice, but not very attentive to empty water glasses, or anything for that matter. Food runner was super nice and helpful! My date ordered shrimp scampi, it was fine. (enough butter and cheese with pasta it will always be OK) The pappardelle pasta was a nice twist and was cooked well, the shrimp were over cooked, and the sauce as I said above was tasty. They have a large draft beer list, but not very diverse in my eyese. I am not a beer connoisseur by any means but I enjoy a light Belgium styled beer and could not find that here. Maybe not my time of year? Either way, just another let down. Overall if you are looking for some good food and good drinks, keep moving a few blocks in any direction and you can find a better alternative. If you want overpriced upscale un cared for bar food in an actual nice relaxed atmosphere (only positive of the restaurant) on a great block of Center City you have found the place.
label: NEG

text: Unbeliveable turn of events last night. We went to Sushi Yobi, as we do about three times a month. We spent our usual $100 on dinner. The service was lacking, which is not all that uncommon. We are firm believers in tipping commensurate with the level of service we receive. It is not uncommon for us to leave a 25% or 30% tip if service is great. On this trip, we gave an 8% tip because, like I said the service was bad . All was well until the server came over to our table, threw down the check and told us quite rudely that there must be a mistake because we didn't tip enough and usually we tip more. I have never had this happen in my life. Needless to say, we will NEVER return to Sushi Yobi again. I can't believe the audacity--complaining about a low tip when you offered sh*&t service. Unbelievable.
label: NEG

text: Although Hard Rock Cafes tend to be slightly overpriced I've always had great service with even more awesome food. Whenever I visit a city that has one I always stop by and see how's the food and buy myself a souvenir cup. Sadly, my advice to everybody is don't spend the time nor the money here. We waited for a about 15 to be seated which depending on where you go is normal if a place is busy and packed. From this point everything started to slowly go downhill... We finally were seated and given menus to look at and the host left. It took the waiter at least 10 minutes to stop by and see if we wanted anything to drink and had to mention to the waiter that the utensils were dirty. Another 8 minutes passed by and we told him, the waiter what we wanted. The appetizer came out after 10 minutes but the entrees really took about 40 minutes. I honestly wanted to just leave but didn't and waited it out. The food wasn't as great as the other Hard Rock Cafes I've been to and I really expected more for the price. The waiter only came twice after giving our food, once to check on everything and then to give us the check. Between the food and the service, I wouldn't recommend this place to anybody. Just stop over, grab your souvenir and leave.
label: NEG

text: We dine here fairly often and really enjoy Korea Garden despite some significant flaws. Service, as noted by others, is just awful. There have been periods when it has been good for a few months but inevitably something changes and it goes back to being awful. Even when you have a server who is friendly and pleasant, service tends to be extremely inattentive. But we really enjoy the food. The spicy sauteed squid is wonderful and they have a variety of great spicy stews with seafood and goat. We also like the barbecue but often choose other dishes. I really like the kimchi chigae in the winter and hwe dup bab in the summer. If you are not familiar with Korean food, this can be a good place to start because their menu is pretty descriptive and has a lot of photos. But do not count on having a server who will help you. And please bring your kids and let them try something new. Chap jae (noodles) and the pan jeong (pancake) are dishes that most children really love. Whenever we bring guests I often recommend the dolsot bibimbap to men. It is a big stone bowl of rice, vegetables, beef and a fried egg with spicy sauce. Maybe it sounds weird but I find that guys really like this even if they usually aren't adventurous eaters.
label: POS

text: FOOD? If it's Louisiana Seafood, they have it. Crabs, Shrimp, Oysters, Catfish, etc. From Po-boys to Platters to Boiled, you can get it there. QUALITY? Have eaten there more times than I can remember over the last 30+ years and it's always been wonderful. TASTE? Never too spicy and never bland. Always seems to have just the right taste. LOCATION? If you're driving down Barataria Blvd from the West Bank Expressway (heading South), it'll be on your right-hand side. You'll turn right onto August Avenue (it's Patriot Street on the left side) and turn right again immediately onto a little bumpy road that leads to it, as it's located behind the little strip mall and the E-Z Serve Convenience store. PARKING? Plenty! They have a shell parking lot and a giant grass field right next to it. If you can't find a place to park, then that means you won't be able to get in because they are packed. SERVICE? Always, and I do mean ALWAYS, friendly, prompt, and professional, in a West Bank sort of way. CLEANLINESS? Always clean, but on the rare instance that it's not, let the Waitress know and it'll be cleaned instantly. SAFETY? Well, there's an apartment complex across the road that seems to attract the lower ghetto forms of life, but they don't seem to bother any of the customers here. Plus, there's always cops coming in and out of here as well so it's pretty safe. ATMOSPHERE? It's a Family restaurant. There's not much more to say about that. PRICE? Pretty damn good prices compared to other places around the West Bank. Anytime the family gets the en-vie for seafood, we head here.
label: POS

text: I'm always disappointed with this place, yet for some reason I go back, I guess hoping that they will finally learn how to wipe down a dashboard. But no such luck. I used to get the basic interior/exterior wash (about $22) but after having to clean out my car several times AFTER leaving the place, I now just get an exterior wash. They seem to do OK at that. It's usually pretty busy, but the line will move quickly--especially if you are just washing the outside of your car. Oh--and with that, I add on the "wheel dressing" to clean those babies up. That totals up to only about $11, so it's worth it. Just don't expect great work on the inside of your car--and I keep my very clean anyway, so it's not like they have much work to do in the first place. I do like how they have a mini What's in Store gift shop inside the building though--gives you something to do while you wait for your car!

text: I would have given this place half a star but that is not an option. We waited for much longer than quoted for a seat. No big deals this happens, but then when we were seated it took 15 minutes more for a menu and that was after I flagged down someone. Then, we waited an HOUR (no lie or exaggeration) for our food to arrive only to be all wrong. So, I asked to speak to the manager because I was starving and the meal was wrong. He promised to fix the situation and get me something to eat ASAP. Well, I didn't see him again for 10 minutes AND no bread was sent over. When my meal did finally arrive it was subpar at best. I've eaten all over the French Quarter and I've never had this experince before. Especially from a place as crowded or as seemingly popular as this place is supposed to be! The owner of this establishment should be ashamed of his/her self!

text: I'd actually give it a 2 and a half verging on 3. The cuisine is an interesting mix of eastern European and Serbian..... not common in restaurants around the area and worth sampling a bit deeper, Some offerings we tried were quite good, ...the stuffed peppers and the grilled squid... some were fair.. the lamb kabobs and the salad. Service was friendly and the decor is quite nice. The value isn't the greatest in that the prices tend to be on the high side considering the quality. Since it has only been open a month it's worth another visit in a while to see if things have smoothed out
label: NEG

text: After a long day of snowboarding we planned on eating at Flavors! at Silver Legacy (where we were staying). Based on Yelp reviews of Flavors, we might have had a better dining experience if we were willing to wait in line. In all reality, I'm not even sure Courtyard Buffet's line was shorter. Food at Courtyard was ho hum, really not that great quality. I started out with prime rib which turned out to be overcooked and not pink whatsoever. Nothing was really appetizing and overall just not exciting at all. If you have a hungry group of people perhaps you can't beat the price of all-you-can-eat for $13 (adults). Other than that, go elsewhere!

text: Ive been ordering Jimmy Johns since it opened in my neighborhood. Was not sure what to expect the 1st time, but their fast service and delivery is great. They get the sandwich to you in an incredibly fast time. Healthy, and tasty is what they are about. I usually get the "Turkey Tom" without the sprouts, and it is consistently good all the time. I rarely go in because when I order, im usually home and just dont have anything in the house, or dont feel like cooking. Their cookies are HUGE and tasty as well, I recommend the Oatmeal Raisin. YUM Give them a try, highly recommend them

text: I used to go here a lot when i was in college and we loved the wi-fi and 24 hour service. However, now that I'm a bit more of a coffee snob, I reached the conclusion that their coffee is not so good. I usually only get straight brewed coffee, but it always tastes burnt. Really don't like the inside; as its always smokey and feels like it hasn't been cleaned in a while. The bathrooms are downright scary. Love the patio and its great to people watch. That corner is great.

text: The care is great. That is where it ends. We started taking our pug there when he had cancer. Dr. Eugenio answered all our questions and helped up decide what to do. At that time the cost was about par with the others vets. Since then they have become extremely overpriced. They tried to force us into giving my service dog a surgery that he doesn't need but might some day. I found from research the possibility of him needing the surgery was almost nil, less than 1%. However, the possibility of losing him in the surgery was close to 10%. The price for the surgery was $825, The dog is having skin problems and that is why he was there. They quoted me $125 for the visit but the prescriptions alone were almost that. They prescribed benedryl and charged us $45 for 20 capsules. I could have bought 1600 doses for that amount at Costco. The antibiotics at Sams were $30. but I could have gotten it at Sam's pharmacy for $3.66. The cost was over $300. After the dog finished the prescriptions someone called to ask how he was doing. When I told him it was about the same I was told he would need to see the dermatologist and the visit would be $300 + tests and medications. When I told him I couldnt I need to get the dog fixed but they would charge $400. Where I take him now, I can get a coupon for $77. and the vet charges $150, so it will cost me $75. My advice to everyone, don't let these people guilt trip you into letting them do things that are not needed.
label: NEG

text: Just got a cheesesteak from here and it was REALLY outstanding. Recently renovated after a fire, this place is great! Fantastic beer selection too! Lots of great imports. Very clean and GREAT friendly service!
label: POS

text: This is the most unprofessional, rude and tortuous dry cleaners in Saint Louis. I would suggest you hand wash your clothes in bleach and ammonia and mortar rather than take your clothes here. I brought two sweaters into their store and both of them shrank to a less than small when I got them back. The staff immediately was defensive, argumentative and rude when I complained. They sent the sweaters back to be "stretched" at their factory only to return in the same size. This went on twice as they forced me to come back in to try them on. When that didn't work and I asked from the owner that they pay me the small sum of 50 dollars for the sweaters and refund me the cleaning fee they accused me of either 1) giving them poorly made clothes that should be sent back to the manufacturer (something impossible to do since a) I bought them across state lines and b) or 2) that I lied to them and brought them in after I shrank them. Bottom line: They never refunded a dime and I am stuck with two sweaters that have shrunk in their hands. They have no customer service. Are not loyal to their customers. They are rude, senseless and have not one decent bones in their body. STAY AWAY.
label: NEG

text: Oh don't even bother with this place. Walking in you get the feel that this is a very classy, upscale place but you soon realize that your 50-something bucks are way better spent elsewhere. I came here with 3 good friends. 3 of us, including me, were from out of town so we wanted to go out to a nice dinner. The service was nice enough but I thought the extensive water menu was a bit ridiculous. (and btw, if you're going to have that huge of a menu just for water, I suggest you at least have some delicious viennese water in there somewhere!) I would have given this place only one star but my dish was actually pretty good. I got the duck and it was prepared well, but nothing spectacular and the sweet potato hash that came with it was overwhelmingly sweet. One friend's chicken was passable, but nothing special. Another ordered the pork chop which actually was decent and was a nice sized portion. However, my friend, who decided to get the filet mignon was extremely disappointed. He ordered his medium rare and it came out medium-well. He asked them to take it back, which they were happy to do, but after waiting for what seemed like forever they brought out another filet that was quite possibly even more overcooked than the last one. What do you not understand about medium rare? Honestly, at a place like this, you would expect the chef to know how to prepare a piece of meat correctly. Heck, I expect the guys at TGI Fridays to be able to cook a steak properly. I've cooked way better steaks at my own house, and I am no fancy chef. Don't waste your time or money. Take it to Meritage instead (review coming soon)!
label: NEG

text: White Dog Cafe is a great brunch place. It had been ages since I'd dined there, and it was as tasty as I'd remembered. However, they are getting only 3.5 stars (rounded up to 4) because of the weird/ unprofessional service we received. Our waitress seemed as if she had a) never been trained on how to be a waitress, b) never dealt with the public before and c) didn't know how to brush her hair. Despite this, the convenience of a no-wait brunch on Sunday morning (11:30ish) will bring me back for another meal. However, I might just tip in combs and hair product instead of cash.
label: POS

text: This place deserves much more credit and business than it has. The restaurant is a bit secluded from the "hip" parts of town and the interiors could use an update, but the filet mignon was excellent! We had the onion tart, which is delectably melt in your mouth. My husband and I enjoyed our meals and we would return. One star knocked off because the service was a bit snooty, which was no excuse considering there was only one other table there on a sleepy Sunday night.
label: POS

text: Let me start by saying I know I was going to pay extra having my car serviced at a dealership. I'm a girl and I don't know crap about cars, but it was convenient to leave my car there rather than at the airport while I went on vacation. I needed: an oil leak fixed, new front brakes, my jacked up sunroof shut and something to do with a power steering hose. Ok, German car, prepare to sign over you Roth IRA for all that. Out the door at $3291.57. I picked up my car, got about 30 miles out of town only to have my power steering completely crap out in a Trader Joe's parking lot. Are you freaking kidding me? You have my car for 9 days for what I originally only thought was going to be the sunroof and steering noise and somehow this slips through the cracks? So on the flatbed goes my car, towed back to Reno. To their credit they paid for a rental car so I could get home (five hours behind schedule and exhausted from a cross country flight) Using my powers of persuasion I got them to have one of their employees to drive my car to Mammoth, pick up the rental and drive it back to Reno. But I was still out the cash for gas (NOT CHEAP in CA in the summer, think $4/gallon) for the rental car's 350 mile round trip, plus it took another week before my car was even fixed (again). 16 days in the shop. My poor baby. And poor me, $1173.20 for the pump and labor. And now, here I am in Portland mere months later to have a familiar noise return. Oh yeah, that power steering pump that was put in is failing, to the tune of $800 (interesting price difference, no?). Is there a word that is stronger than irate?
label: NEG

text: If I could give it a lower score I would. Look, I'm 33 years old. Back when I was 29 I was looking for a new car. I searched the various different dealers and, at the time, a new body style had just been released for the Cadillac CTS. I thought to myself - I'll just go down the road here and look at the old CTS' - thinking maybe I could get a deal on a new one that was still the old body style. I pull in and get out of my car and start looking at the CTS'. While I was looking at the cars I could see salesmen inside looking out at me. No one came out and talked to me. Another car pulls up - and older gentleman gets out. Within SECONDS of him stopping his car a sales person was at his side. Look, I realize perhaps a 20- something (now 30-something) person looking at a Caddy might not be your ideal target audience. But you should at LEAST have come talk to me. They have no idea what my financial situation is or was. A few months later - I was in a position to help my parents buy a new Cadillac DTS. I was able to use my work discount to get them several thousand dollars off the car. When they give you the voucher they also inform the closest dealer to you (which was this dealer). Within a day or two of submitting the form online to get the voucher - Andrews was calling and e-mailing me. I made it crystal clear that we would go ANYWHERE we could to avoid buying there. But yeah - not going to ever buy there. I'll drive to Georgia or Kentucky to buy a Cadillac before visiting this dealer again.
label: NEG

text: The service is friendly and they are actually really nice people but the food was not so good. The only good thing about this place were the wings. The place is fairly large and very spacious. They have seating that can hold a group of people. The entire place has a dark vibe to it and as soon as you walk in you don't feel very comfortable here. The only thing I liked was the servers.

I fought with them (visits, phone calls, letters) for ages and couldn't even get a reimbursement for cleaning costs never mind replacement for the items. I asked why dry cleaners would shrink something (since the whole point of DRY cleaning seems to be to prevent that!) and they were very defensive about their system which involves some German-made wet system. There was no logic there at all. Avoid.

text: Apparently they completely changed their happy hour policy four days ago and instead of being upfront about it and telling their customers of the change they decided to be sneaky and put the tiny new menu on a clip and next to their new years advertisement. The waitress carried on without mentioning a word of the change to us until the bill came in the end, at which point she ran her mouth about how people were complaining too much and not paying enough tips and it wasn't fair to the waitresses and waiters. I have no problem with restaurants changing their pricing/menu every once in a while but what they are doing is bad business. Not to mention the fact that their food is just mediocre and not worth the regular price (oh and the new "happy hour" has no half off anything and the only items even on the menu are the unimpressive filler rolls. Also, the martinis=gone). Mediocre food can bring a business down, but not faster than questionable practices. Your happy hour was the only reason 90% of the people I know even go there in the first place. Customers are not suckers. If you think you are too established to fail, you should think again. This is definitely going to be the last time i take my business there.
label: NEG

text: So the Pneumatic Diner already has plethora of awesome reviews - I don't care because I just have to throw my hat into the ring. My first reaction to havin glunch here a month or so back was 'Why the HELLO have I never eaten here before?' Totally vegetarian and most items can be made Vegan as well. I had the Falafel sammich (or whatever it is called). I had recently gotten braces (and if you put them on your kids, I highly recommend you wear them too so you know the misery - but that is another story) and the kitchen was awesome at dicing up every little last bite so I could swallow thing mostly half-chewed (sorry for the detail, but it is relevant to the great customer service) I brought my husband in a few weeks later and he was less than impressed. He is a die hard meat eater though so I didn't expect him to be as excited as I was. Cash only though - so be ready!

text: I love Martha! I came here for a bikini and eyebrow wax. Once you walk into her salon, you immediately feel welcomed. The decor is super cute and cozy. text: Although my experience here was a 1 star experience, I can understand why people love this place too. And I think with a little information, I could have avoided a negative experience, so here's a little information hoping you will get to enjoy all the great things about this place. I looked at their web site on my Blackberry while visiting Nashville. It said they did not accept reservations for the Sunday 8pm show (they don't). OK, literally it says "no reservations needed", which is a big stinky load of shyte. Reservations are badly needed, they are just not accepted. So anyway, I tried to call them to ask about the scoop for going to see the Sunday show, but they only have a live person doing phone calls during very limited hours (11am-4:30pm maybe? and they don't really even commit to that very fully) and only Monday through Friday. I was trying to learn about all this on a Saturday, so I had no way to talk to someone live on the phone at that point. So in anticipation of a popular thing, we got there at 7pm for the 8pm show, and stood in the door with a couple other people while the prior show finished up. To our surprise, they don't clear the place out between shows. Would be really cool if their web site or phone message would have told us that. So only a few people got up out of seats after the first show. For the most part, everyone there just stayed right in their seats. Then to our horror, when a few seats did open up, the normally polite and friendly folks of Nashville that knew what they were doing ran right past us into the opening seats. Some other seats that opened up were already "claimed" in advance by someone who knew someone else that was at the earlier show and had made side arrangements. All this despite a sign that says to wait at the front for the hostess to seat you, which we politely and stupidly were obeying. Well, while all this was happening, I asked an employee what was going on, and why we weren't being seated since we had been waiting for the seats opening up longer than everyone else that was running past us and working these side deals. And the employee just said "Sundays are busy". I was like, great, thanks for all the help for an out of towner that has been standing and waiting for seats at your business for an hour now. The thing is, their "shhh" policy (absolute silence requested while the songwriters are playing), which is cool, also makes it impossible to ask questions of staff or try to figure out what you are supposed to do and how, so you are left quietly reading the sign that says to wait for a hostess to seat you. So it was pretty frustrating cuz I felt like I tried to do my online homework, called to try to talk to a person, arrived an hour ahead of time, and politely obeyed their own damn sign waiting for the hostess to seat me, and I got squished without so much as an apology from their staff when I asked about it. We ended up leaving pretty disgusted rather than staying for the 8pm show. So if you want to go see some really great music in a really cool and small atmosphere here, get a reservation. And if it is Sunday and they don't take reservations, show up at 5:30pm if you want to see the 8:00pm show. If you work at the bluebird, you could do a few things out of courtesy to us simple out of town folk that are not "in the know": 1) The fine print at the bottom of the 6:30pm show information on your web site says if you want a seat on Sunday, you need to show up at 5:30pm. You should really repeat this information on the 8pm show information. 2) Both the 6:30pm and 8:00pm show information should tell people that most of the folks at the 6:30pm show will stay straight through for the 8:00pm show, so if you want to see the 8:00pm show a customer should plan on committing to both of them. 3) Get rid of the polite euphemism "no reservations needed" on the 8pm Sunday show on your website and just tell customers you don't take reservations on Sundays. 4) On Sundays at least, take the stupid sign down telling customers to wait for the hostess to seat you OR EVEN BETTER, put a sign-up list at the front door and actually seat people in available seats in the order that folks arrived there and put an end to the "inside arrangements" for seats. 5) Take responsibility for the environment you have created. It is possible that the bluebird is intentionally ambiguous so that insiders have an advantage, but that view of the world just does not match the warmth and hospitality that we got from Nashville, so I really prefer to think that the Bluebird management has not really thought about their customer experience from the point of view of an out of towner that arrives in Nashville late on a Friday night.

text: Chew Man Chu just opened this week, and it is obviously still smoothing out the kinks. The entire restaurant filled up quickly at 5pm on Saturday, however there were only two waiters, and so service was incredibly slow. Luckily, my friend and I arrived before the majority of the diners filed in, however, there were couples at our table who waited upwards of 20 minutes before ordering their first round of drinks. Understaffing is most likely a temporary problem, and so my rating is definitely not based on service, but rather on the food itself. The first thing we noticed was that everything on the menu was basically exactly the same as what you would expect to see at any restaurant in Chinatown with price and size being the only exceptions. Most items on the menu were about double what you would expect to pay for decent fare at a restaurant with less frills and about half the size. For instance, the orange beef, which I unfortunately ordered, was $16.50, and was EXACTLY the same in taste and content as the take-out I often get from smaller Chinese restaurants around the city. The beef, however, was incredibly tough and chewy, and so both my friend and I found it to be inedible and inexcusable. We also ordered a semi-bastardized version of pad thai that was unremarkable and laden with bacon of all things. This was still better than the orange beef in that we were actually able to eat it. After we had started eating our entrees, our appetizers came out. My friend chose the crispy crab won ton, which consisted of four very tiny and overly greasy pieces. These were flavorful but simultaneously disgusting. Is that even possible? It is at Chew Man Chu. The saving grace was our second appetizer, the pork and shrimp potstickers. Again, these were not too far off from what you can get at a cheap Chinese take-out place, but they were still quite tasty. Everything we ordered was underwhelming and overpriced. The only flare this restaurant has is its loud décor, which I felt we were all paying for. While, I doubt I will ever return to this restaurant, I would suggest to anyone who is interested in trying Chew Man Chu to wait a month or longer when at least the problems with service will more than likely be straightened out.
label: NEG

text: The pride of Philadelphia's cash only, BYOB fleet, Modo Mio does many things and does them all well. Casual enough for jeans, classy enough for a suit, reasonably enough for any night of the week: there should be nothing holding you back. From start to finish, a meal at Modo Mio is a very personable experience. Upon walking up, I saw a man in an apron dash out to one of the trees planted in the adjacent sidewalk, kneel down, and then run back into the rear entrance. Upon closer inspection, i realized he had snipped a few sprigs from a basil or rosemary plant at the tree's roots. Not exactly the French Laundry's pristine, organic herb garden, but a nice touch. Inside it was jovial, but not too loud. all night our waitperson was nothing but helpful and kind, giving us suggestions, sharing stories, and and even throwing in a complimentary canape. Everything on the menu was perfect, rich and light dishes alike soothed in a way that I only thought generations-old matzoh ball soup recipes could. Little gnocchi as soft as clouds, uber-peppery spaghetti carbonara, grilled octopus so tender that, even after hours of googling, I can still not explain. The homey feel of the place, the extravagant preparations: it all fit together in a way I have rarely seen. Bring friends and, at the very least, some decent wines (one red one white, at least!) to fully enjoy a meal here. Though I would recomend trying as many things as possible (this means sharing) be wary of over-ordering as I could barely touch my dessert (though the complimentary, sambuca gave me some courage for the road)
label: POS

text: I used to know West Ed like the back of my hand. Now that I don't live near it anymore I haven't been in a very long time. Even though it has evolved over the years it has only become better. Galaxyland is a great amusement park, for being in a mall that is. They have rides for all ages. A general admission costs $32, the family rate is $85 and kids under 2 are free. The World Waterpark is a must stop, you can even bungee jump above the wave pool! The skating rink is always full, whether it be classes or free skate. I guess they have sea lion shows now and the marine life caverns are still going, but I haven't been in them for many years. Ed's rec room offers billiards and bowling. They have a Jubilation's Dinner Theatre and also a Casino. There is even mini putt and putt n' glow as well! Another words this place is filled with fun activities! There is a great Movie theatre if you feel the need to catch a flick. The shooting range is a must stop, it is a bit hard to find, but it is so fun! It costs about $40/50 to try a handgun. The stores range in popularity and prices. The upper level tends to have the higher end designer brands. The lower level carries a lot of the popular stores. There is everything from pets to art to home accessories to bridal stores here! Imagine your favorite clothing store, the chances are high that there is one in here. The mall isn't hard to navigate, there are ample maps around. The West 49 has a skate park in it! I was so excited to see that they had a Urban Outfitters here! Needless to say, I had no trouble spending my money throughout the mall! Most of the stores are unisex, so there is a lot of men's shopping to be had as well. They also have numerous restaurants, including a huge food court with every kind of cuisine imaginable. Bourbon St. is one of my favorite areas, it is always buzzing. They have an Earls, Spaghetti Factory, Moxie's, along with other unique places to eat, like Jungle Jim's. It sure has improved over the years, it has such a cool vibe now! The mall even has a T&T Market and a themed "Chinatown" area. Europa Boulevard is an interesting change from the rest of the mall, it has a variety of stores you can shop, while feeling as though you are walking down the street of a European city. The mall offers super savings books for $8 that give you a number of coupons for food and shopping. I was exhausted after a long day of shopping! West Ed is a must go, especially if you like spending a whole day shopping and maybe throwing in a bowling game or a movie! It is unlike any other mall you have ever been too, but expect to deal with crowds, especially on the weekends!

text: Pat O'Briens is the type of restaurant you should avoid all together while out in NOLA. Why? I'll tell you why. The service here is ridiculously SLOW (snail slow) and the food is not good. Yes, I said it, you trendy tourists! I made the mistake of stopping in while wandering Bourbon St. I should have known better than to dine at a place smack dab in the middle of NOLA's party central. I asked for a table (for 2) and was led to a section of the outdoor restaurant that was right under a heat lamp. I asked if there was anyway of sitting in the patio area near the bar and water fountain. I was quickly shut down and told that area was reserved for drinking -- only. I was not only planning on drinking but was also going to do a bit of eating and more drinking. We were offered a table that was so narrow, an ashtray and one glass were about the only items that could fit on the table. Was this guy kidding me? Unless the food portions were tapas-style, then give me a normal table! I moved to another table nearby and was quickly intercepted by another waiter; "This is for parties of 4. Sorry." I basically parked my sweet ass in that table and the waiter backed off. What's he going to do? Throw beads at me?? Pat O'Brien's is known for their fruity cocktails; most famous is the Hurricane. I went against the tradition and got a Mint Julep. Strong Bourbon love right there. I also ordered the Rainforest which was a beautiful layered drink with subtle boozy flavors. It's the type of drink you don't know what it's made of nor do you want to know. The interesting thing about Pat O's is the way you somehow end up purchasing a souvenir glass. The very same glass they use to serve your cocktail, miraculously ends up as a purchase (in addition to the drink) on your bill. Sneaky? Yes. But I know own two Pat O'Brien glasses. I also ordered the alligator bites. I have never had alligator or crocodile or any sort of reptile...but the bites were pretty decent. Sort of tasted like chicken nuggets. For my entree, I went with the Creole Shrimp. It was a pretty basic shrimp and rice dish that offered very little flavors but a lot of HEAT. Pat O'Brien's is very busy at night and mostly occupied by tourists who want to get their drink on. I wouldn't recommend dining here at all. You can find much better restaurants that are not adjacent to seedy strip bars and night clubs.
label: NEG

text: Hear is the headliner on their website: "Join us for the Treasure Valley's finest Sunday Brunch......." Well folks, that was *the worst* Sunday Brunch I have ever had. I took the wife there to give her the experience of a good ol' fashioned American Champagne Sunday Brunch. I ended up totally embarrassed. They try to fool you by saying, "Reservations recommended", so you think, "Oh my gosh! This place must rock and gets packed every weekend!" What a scam! The place was about 1/3 full, no chance of having to wait in line. There is not much of an atmosphere, the brunch takes place in a banquet room overlooking the golf course. To the food.: They have a large selection of food, but most of it didn't look appetizing. Most was just very very low quality bulk frozen stuff. It is easier to describe what few things tasted good, than try to explain how almost everything tasted dull and cheap. Just imagine everything looks dried up, sad and lonely, like it's been sitting for a while. The good: The biscuits were very good, just like you'd expect. We didn't try the gravy, opting to just butter them and add some jelly. The prime rib had pretty good flavor, even if it was well done and slightly chewy. The chocolate fondue fountain thing was cool, but the strawberries provided were rotten, literally. We found 1 single good one. The really bad: They had an abundant raw veggie platter, sad, dried, and untouched. I saw a big fly hovering above it, then land and proceed to Rambo across the surface of the veggies. That was enough for me....... The big insult was the price. I know Sunday Brunches are pricey, but you expect to get well fed with good quality stuff. This was $36.00 for two. We would have been FAR better off going downtown. Conclusion: If you want "Sunday Brunch", there may not be any place in the whole state. A better idea would be to go to La Vie En Rose or Goldy's on Sunday and order a mimosa....

text: I drank here, ate cake here, and stayed the night here. I'm more or less obsessed. I promise to request this as my new hotel spot in Tucson from here on out! So we decided to pop over to Hotel Congress since it looked like there might be a bar inside. There definitely was. It was completely packed (mind you it was full of women due to the Indigo Girls concert next door...and this may have swayed my opinion slightly) but the two bartenders (servicing about 45 people) were right on top of it and took care of us really quickly. We weren't planning on staying the night in Tucson, but I'm a sucker for a historic spot and a good drink. So we ordered a room, picked up a piece of carrot cake to munch on later, and headed over to the Rialto for the concert. When we returned I found a really humble and cozy room on the second floor. There was no TV which was a nice change of pace. The bathroom was tiny but adorably genuine. I really just loved the whole feel of the place. When we were coming back to our room around midnight there were people just going in to the night club downstairs. The music wasn't loud though and definitely disturb us or keep us from sleeping. I highly recommend this to anyone who likes to stay off the beaten (i.e. Marriot, Holiday Inn, etc) hotel path. Additionally, it's probably best if you admire historic charm and small scale facilities. Our room for a wednesday night was only $72. I thought that was pretty reasonable. Although I didn't get to really eat a meal or check out any of the amenities. So someone looking for a longer stay or lots of extras at their hotel might not love it. But for what I was looking for, it was perfect! p.s. no air...just a swamp cooler...it was about 98 that evening and it felt absolutely fine!

Fifteen minutes later, we were moved to a larger table (still not the table that had been promised) and waited an additional twenty minutes for dinner - which were served by a different waiter. The manager never came by to check on the accommodations or apologize for giving away our table, or for the poor service we had experienced thus far. When we received the bill (which was several hundred dollars), none of the appetizers had been "taken care of." text: Let's start off by clearly stating that I have a profound weakness for 'crab shacks'. When eating seafood, I am not enthralled by fancy service, swanky ambience, or linen tablecloths. For us, it's all about the food, so if you're eating shellfish, crustaceans, or any other sea creatures where freshness is paramount, then it's all about location, location, location. The closer to the source, the better. So it will be no surprise that we're big fans of the SB Shellfish Company, or as it's referred to in our household, the Shack. We live just a few blocks away, so we usually just bike up the pier and when possible, grab a table at the bar overlooking the open kitchen, or outside on the harbor side of the Shack (that way we can sit outside, and have a beer too). The menu's not all high-end. Lots of fried combo's (all good). The real treat though is gobbling down a plate of oysters, maybe a small cup of NE chowder, followed by any one of their seasonal specials. The tanks are always filled with live crabs, lobsters, etc --so freshness is never an issue. The open kitchen is a joy to watch, and the food is fast and honest. When it comes to casual non-sushi seafood in Santa Barbara, there is no competition. The Shack is the place to enjoy a beer, some tasty treats, soak up the sea breeze, and watch all the sail boats trafficking in and out of the harbor. A perfect afternoon.

text: The Wine Cask is what you get when you cross a proven restaurateur, Mitchell Sjerven, and celebrated winemaker, Doug Margerum, get together. It's what's expected and The Wine Cash delivers. With two sides to every story/restaurant, this little ditty is about the Cafe/Bar and not the full restaurant. While I hear the food is amazing, I can only speak to the former. The bar menu is full of flatbreads, bite size snack-a-tizers and mouth stuffing sandwiches with the Margherita flatbread, steak bites and Cheese & Charcuterie standing out. There are better Happy Hour places for munchies assortment in Santa Barbra where at the Wine Cask, you can eat full portions at the bar or enjoy the cheese plate on the sofa by the fire. The layout offers outdoor, table, sofa and bar seating but gets very busy on Friday nights so send in a scout early to hold the fort. The clientele is older and more sophisticated that what you would find on the drag and that's just fine with us. They add a touch of class. Now that your here and you've looked over the menu, what will you drink to pair? Just because this is The Wine Cask and Doug has some amazing offerings, his own as well as many others, it's not all about the wine. The bar team prides themselves on infusing anything distilled. The chalk wall will show what's ready to drink such as a raspberry vodka or what's to come like the bacon infused bourbon. There's also a wish list from customers who think up the wildest things. It's worth a trip just to drink the crazy concoctions. The wine selection by the glass is outstanding. As it very well should be. The prices however, are on the high side even for full retail but the people pay it and keep the cafe full into the evening. Not sure what to drink? No problem. Steven behind the bar will help you decide. If I may, try a glass of the M5. You'll end up with a bottle. Start your evening out at The Wine Cask and you may even stay a while. It's warm inviting and pours up a great time.

text: Okay, it seems most people miss the point of Bueno Gelato. Yes, great gelato, made in house and lots of flavours. Bueno Gelato, and not all Italian cafés in the City do, serves affogato! Yes, repeat it with me boys and girls: affogato. Affogato is a traditional Italian desert/treat consisting of smooth creamy gelato with a decadent single shot of fine Italian espresso poured over it. In Italy, it's traditionally a scoop of vanilla, but here, at Bueno Gelato, it can be hazelnut or custardy zuppa ingles or dark chocolate or pistachio. Forget anything Starbucks serves, like those blasphemous frappicinos, have a real taste of Italian Summer. Get down to Bueno Gelato and order an affogato.

text: The Nashville Farmer's Market is a place of choice for shopping for produce all year round. If you want to be sure where the stuff is grown try to get to know the seller and see what kind of information you can get. My only complaint is that is not very transparent where the food is coming from, a lot of the food looks like it was just bought wholesale, which allows them to still give a better price than main grocery stores. But, a lot of it is grown locally; they seem to want to camouflage the difference. Case in point, Bananas and Mangos do not grow in the state of Tennessee... So that makes me wonder where the rest of the food in that stall is coming from. But, in any case, it is a wonderful open air market always full of produce.
