text: Before telling Thai Lotus' "story," let me first say that the food is excellent and the service is great. My wife and I have spent time in Thailand and we can say that this is authentic Thai food. I've eaten most items on the menu and they've ranged from quite good to exceptionally excellent. Also, unlike some Thai restaurants, they always ask how spicy you want it - we advise "2" or "3" on a 1-5 scale unless you're a very experienced Thai food gourmet... and have a very strong digestive system. I've been going to Thai Lotus since 2004 - during that time it's gone through three ownerships. Earlier, the food was good, but the ambiance was "tacky fast food" in nature. When the current owners, Jen and Sitt (young wife and husband) moved here from Thailand and bought it in 2007, things started changing immediately. The food, always good, has improved to "excellent." It is now very attractive inside and the staffing has improved significantly - you usually get your water within seconds and your order is taken promptly... which is quite impressive, as the restaurant has gone from mostly empty during lunch to usually full. The lunch "specials" menu has more than tripled and many additional dinner items have been added. All the lunch specials are very good. There used to be about six or so reasonably-priced lunch specials. Now the list approaches 20 or so. The regular menu is very large. A real dinner favorite of mine is the Green Papaya Salad, which is a large and delicious meal and a bargain at about $10. The Seafood Salad, just two or three dollars more, is loaded with squid, octopus, fish chunks, scallops, clams, and more - mixed with vegetables and Asian "sweet vinegar" for extra taste. All the soups are fantastic. The noodle dishes are great. There are pages more of other dishes. I used to eat at Thai Lotus occasionally before Jen & Oat bought it... it was just plain ugly. Now it's a small "bistro" feeling and very elegant place with excellent food and quick, friendly service. Now I eat there at least once a week... once, I ate there five times in one week! My wife and I just ate there again tonight and had one of the "sizzling" Chef Specials along with a Larb Gai salad - what a treat!

text: Went here for lunch. I expect this rating to improve once the shop has been open and is less crowded, and they have a chance to really nail down their kitchen production process. (summary at bottom if tl;dr) Location: not bad, Sansom is one of my favorite streets in Philly. The new space is well decorated and pretty well set up. There is an entrance on one side that leads directly to the order station, and there is a assembly line and large pick up area after. The waiting area is a bit tight, but even with the large crowd I wasn't uncomfortable. I like that you can see the entire kitchen (completely open). We sat against the wall, and it was ample space to lay out our food. Service: friendly enough and efficient. You can hear as they call your order number too. Didn't see many order mistakes and the manager was on top of things. The wait in line took about 20 minutes (unacceptable for lunch fare, but not their fault persay) and the food took about 10 (a bit long when they had a massive pile of burgers cooked and ready). At this point I can't sink so much time over my lunch break so be aware of this point. Food: I ordered a cheeseburger with cheddar (medium) and red onions and a side of truffle fries. Burger first: The bun is good, but not what I expected. It has the texture of stale bread, but this ended up being great. the burger held in place wonderfully and it did not fall apart like the softer potato rolls for example. My burger was cooked great but was extremely salty on one side. The cheddar was rubbery and flavorless, and the onions were very overcooked, mushy and flavorless. The side of pickles was unexpected and a bonus (I love pickles!). Good size in my opinion, but my food mate thought it was too small for the price (almost looked like a slider, 5.5oz uncooked patty). Overall it was a good burger, but not great. Out of 5 I would give it 3. If the cheese and onions were better, it would gain +1 because the meat was tasty and juicy (the heart if you will). The truffle fries were a gigantic portion for $2... we should have shared a single order. They were awesome and the smell of truffles was fantastic. The flavor was not overpowering, almost subtle addition to the fries. The fries were not at all greasy which I really, really appreciate and the way they were cut was great. Some were nice and crunchy and some were soft so there was alot to like here. Fries get 5 out of 5! The spicy fries were on par with these. Worth staying for dessert. + Front of the house/service was great. The waiter that greeted us was accomodating, on point, and got us seated for our reservation quickly. Our waitress was very sweet and did her job well. We were lucky enough to meet the owner's wife, and she is a doll! Made great menu suggestions without being pushy and showed real concern about how our meals were being enjoyed. Minuses - DH really did not enjoy his entree, the October Special Tandoori Rib. He didn't like how the meat was cooked, his piece was on the small side and not very meaty. He did enjoy side side salad and potatos, and he liked the place overall enough to want to make a 2nd trip. I did feel badly that he didn't enjoy his entree. - Because it was so busy, they ran out of wine buckets. We made due with glasses of ice :) Overall, very worth the trip. Great atmosphere for such a small space, (mostly) outstanding food from appetizers to dessert. Stick with the chicken entrees!

text: I have a large amount of respect for Emeril Lagasse based on his successful television shows. Thousands upon thousands of home kitchen gamers have kindled or rekindled an interest in cooking due to his showmanship, enthusiasm and dedication. Also his generosity to his employees after the Katrina mess in New Orleans were extraordinary. The bad news. During my visit to New Orleans last month, I made a point of dining at his Delmonico restaurant not far from the downtown foodie areas of the French Quarter and the Warehouse District. It was well-rated by several foodie sites, and some restaurant-goer bloggers seemed to at least like Delmonico's, even if I did not read any gushing reviews. What a disaster. Most of the dishes(many of which the restaurant is noted for), service and ambiance were not even mediocre. Four of us, all food pros or semi-pros, arrived on time on a busy Sunday evening. Our seating was "in the back room." DO NOT be seated anywhere but the front of the house if you stupid enough to ignore this review and decide to dine at Delmonico's. The back seating area is 10 miles from the kitchen and understaffed to the max. The two waiters assigned to this area had no busboy help, little help from the floor manager and were so inexperienced(but eager and polite) as to be laughable. Simple questions about the cuisine, wine, beer, etc. were unanswerable by the help. "We'll find out and come back to you." Which they did - after we started chewing on each others' arms. Thirty minutes to get cocktail and wine service!!!!!!!!! How can a restaurant make any money treating guests like carbon-based obelisks? When the groceries arrived, almost all of our 12 dishes were either outright flawed, mediocre in taste to the point of humor(given the prices), cold or an incorrect dish. We gave up - we stopped complaining and stopped sending any dishes back. Instead, we shut up and shut down. Got our check. And left. Leaving a 20% was the hardest thing I have done in a long time, but it was not the fault of the rookie servers. I could only glare at the floor manager on the way out(which was through the kitchen - where are the building inspectors?). This restaurant is truly an example of absentee management - a rudderless ship that survives by catering to a smattering of tourists, dumb locals(since there are so many truly good or great restaurants nearby) and expense account biz people out only to impress and don't know any better. Delmonico's requires a change in attitude by Lagasse - he needs to care - having made his reputation in New Orleans, a city he obviously loves. He damages not only the reputations of all his restaurants but his personal reputation by not leaving competent, caring professionals in charge of a property with great potential. Many other restaurants come to mind with similar problems. Like Chinois in Las Vegas, a Wolfgang Puck autopilot disaster. Do the owners of restaurants scattered around the country and the world ever visit their properties? Okay, no one expects any of these food personages to be behind the stove when we dine; however, the hiring of capable management is essential to the restoration of trust in branded, noted restaurants like Delmonico's. Definitely go to New Orleans. Food-wise NOLA is back with over 25 noteworthy restaurant within walking distance of many downtown hotels. Sadly, Delmonico's is not one of them. PS I did not dine at any other of Lagasse's restaurants on this trip. Good luck.

Here's the part that left me cold: The waiter offered to buy our dessert and replaced my half of the half bottle of zin with a by-the-glass zin from the bar. With Jill feeling so sickly, I decided not to make a scene. I'm really shocked that someone didn't immediately bring us another bottle of the wine I had ordered. If I had wanted house wine, I would have ordered house wine. I'm a magazine publisher and I read quite a lot of restaurant reviews. I decided to go into review mode and just see how the wait staff and management would handle us. The first thing I noticed was that Michael, our initial waiter, left us as soon as he had swabbed and dabbed as much wine as he could from ground zero. He tagged out with another waiter, Hunter who was working our room. Michael was gone and new guy stepped in. I don't know if this is the Stockyard's usual policy, but I thought it was strange. Waiter Michael did offer to pay cleaning bills, but this didn't get discussed further until we were walking out and asked for contact information to submit the cleaning bill. Even though we weren't in our best form with Jill being sick and if the dinner had gone down without the eventual ride down splash wine falls just as our entrees were being delivered, this still wouldn't have been a top choice for us. Here's why: I have never liked it when restaurants go to great lengths to sell you bottled or high-dollar sparkling water with your meal. We live in the United States where water is clean and generally tasty. I never order anything but tap water in a restaurant unless I'm in Mexico and I don't particularly like being made to feel like I'm some kind of an uneducated diner for ordering tap water. This dinner came down to us being strongly encouraged to buy the $80 Kansas City bone-in strip steak and any and all the "add-ons" that were available on the menu. I'm a savvy diner that likes to find a jewel on a great menu and enjoy a great meal without a lecture from a waiter that is trying to up-sell me. We heard presentations at surrounding tables where the wait staff were downplaying the lower-priced items on the menu and encouraging people to go for the higher-priced entrees. I don't go to restaurants to show off for people I don't even know. I like good food, prepared well, with good service. Last night, we got okay food, a bath and pretentious service. It wasn't a good evening.

text: Failed health code!! The inspector reported "multiple potentially hazardous foods" tested at temperatures greater than 45 degrees, including sushi rice that had been prepared the previous day and left in an unplugged rice cooker. Hand sinks throughout the restaurant were turned off and floor sinks were full of water and not draining due to a plumbing problem. The inspector also reported a "widespread rodent problem," noting rodent feces on food preparation tables, along walls, on food boxes, clean dishes, shelves and trays. In addition, the inspector observed a live rodent in an unlit storage closet. The inspector also reported holes, gaps and other forms of deterioration in the walls in several locations throughout the restaurant and excessive storage of unused items, often in unclean conditions. The manager of the restaurant would not comment about the inspections. During the Aug. 30 inspection, the operator of the restaurant voluntarily agreed to close the restaurant for cleaning, pest treatment and dishwashing. The restaurant reopened Sept. 1 after a follow-up inspection, but failed an inspection Sept. 12 that could have restored its regular license, said Renée Peyton, sanitarian supervisor for Pima County Health Department Consumer Health and Food Safety. "When you're dealing with rodents, you're going to have a pest control company that comes in and services the restaurant, and when we start running into problems, we ask about the service, the frequency of the service and the plan," Peyton said. "They cleaned up all evidence of the problem, but the inspector found new evidence of a rodent problem when she went out on the 12th. They're continuing to work on it, and have minimized it significantly, but not enough to fully comply with the code." County inspectors will continue to monitor the restaurant about every 10 days throughout its provisional status to ensure it's operating safely and making progress toward restoring its regular license, Peyton said.

The Grbic salad is a great alternative to the ubiquitous same old Italian salad one finds all over St. Louis. Plenty of fresh bread and your glass is never empty. Last night, the Grbics fulfilled a special request and stayed open past their normal hours for our small post-symphony party. Every detail was perfect and made for an unbelievably magical evening for us! Every member of our party remarked on how lovely the restaurant was and how wonderful the food tasted. The pastries at the end of the meal melted in our mouths, especially the palacinke - Bosnian chocolate filled crepes. I will never forget the Grbic's authentic kindness, generosity, and graciousness - this place is a hidden gem in St. Louis. I VERY highly recommend it.

text: Came here for a leisurely Friday afternoon lunch. We were greeted by a friendly hostess and were seated outside with a lovely view of the river. It was downhill from there. "Yes," I replied. "And what would that be?" he shot back). It was a hot day, and our we drained our drinks quickly. But we're patient diners, and we kept seeing our waiter walking about, attending to other tables, so we figured it wouldn't be long till he brought refills--or at least we could ask for it when our lunches were delivered. No such luck. All the tables around us had their lunches delivered, some who had arrived nearly 25 minutes after we did, and their drinks refilled. Our waiter actually forgot about us--and I know this because my dining companion had to go tell the hostess that we were still waiting for our food 45 minutes later, and I saw her speak to this waiter, who replied "What table?!" He immediately came over with a laughably fake smile and tone and said "More drinks here?" assuming I hadn't seen the exchange between him and the hostess. We asked when our lunches would be coming since we had been waiting 45 minutes. He threw his hands up and said "I don't control how fast the kitchen goes." Hungry and thirsty, we decided we had had enough. I wanted to speak to a manager, but my companion just wanted to leave. So we did. After such disappointing service, I get the feeling the food would've been just as mediocre. I doubt I'll spend any more time trying to find out.

text: Had a reliable foodie friend highly recommend Pico to me when I first moved into the neighborhood block last year. Since then I've come through a few times to give it a try & a few second chances. Unfortunately, it's really just not working out. Ambiance: This was a plus. Lots of color and character on the walls. Very festive. I enjoyed the visual mishmosh. Service: Friendly but slow and absentminded. Food: Paid too much for very little flavor. The first time I went I picked up their beef & cheese burrito. My first impression was that it was ground dog food with cheez-wiz (which after reading M.N.'s review .. sounds like my guess wasn't too far off on the cheez-wiz...) Not a fan at all. I felt pretty ill for a few hours after that. The next few times, I decided to branch out and give their different menu components a chance. I tried their quesadillas, enchiladas, taquitos, veggie burrito and guacamole. Fail. Fail. Fail. Fail. Fail. All of them were very bland in flavor, lacking salt, spice and heat. Come to think about the experience it was very much like bad sex. I left disappointed, underwhelmed and very unsatiated. Drinks: Beers were a bit expensive in my opinion... Reading older reviews it looks like this place used to be BYOB - which may have ameliorated the food situation. Some have criticized me for having too high of a standard in Mexican fare, which I understand because I have spent a chunk of my life in LA and as a half adopted Mexican daughter. But everyone I shared a meal with here also agreed that the food was subpar. In sum, I don't want to pay for bad sex. No, thanks.

text: First thing to mention, the cars in this parking lot are crazy expensive. I'm glad I didn't drive my Chevy Cobalt because it would have been laughed at. You are also forced to use valet service which Jeff didn't realize and instead tried to drive past the line of cars waiting to park. :) Nectar is a gorgeous and spacious building. I loved the décor including the giant Buddha screen. For a Thursday night, this place was packed! There was four of us for dinner. Since our friends don't eat raw food, Jeff and I ordered spicy tuna with avocado roll. Jeff thought the roll had a nice consistency and that it was really good. I thought it was good, but not great. For entrees, I ordered their chicken red curry with crispy fried chow mein noodles. I thought this dish was excellent. It had just the right amount of heat that you knew you were eating something spicy but not killing your taste buds. The noodles were full of flavor and the vegetables were well cooked. I will say that the asparagus was a cut a bit too tiny, making it hard to stab with a fork. Jeff ordered the braised short ribs and petite filet mingon with Yukon potatoes. He admits that this was a cop out because he didn't know what else to order. But, he loved the dish. The braised ribs were tender and flavorful, and filet was cooked perfectly. The potatoes also came like thick cut fries so you know I stole some! As a table, we split the chicken saffron fried rice. It was "melt in your mouth" good. Not a grain was left. When it came time for dessert, both sides of the table ordered donuts. They were more like small light pillows covered with sugar. The three dipping sauces that came with them were: chocolate, raspberry puree, and a caramel. The caramel sauce was disgusting. It had a ton of coffee flavor so I don't know how they thought that was a caramel. The chocolate was also disappointing, it wasn't sweet at all. The best (by default) was the raspberry puree or just eating them straight. Overall, I definitely liked this place. It was pricey, but it's way easier than driving into the city for a more upscale restaurant.

text: I'm going to completely honest here. This place is not for everyone. And yet there's magic afoot if you're part of one of the following rather niche demographics: ---- 1. prefer to be left alone by your fellow diners and bar patrons 2. cannot tolerate excessive noise, light or slow service while dining 3. have young children / are tired of going to restaurants where there is no buffer between breeders and non-breeders / are prepared to punch the next person who rolls their eyes at you in the mouth 4. are strict vegetarian yet smoke and enjoy more than 1 non-mixed drink a day (like me... but still... please keep you smoke away from the patio) 5. aren't a food snob, trust fund baby or ethnovangelist 6. are not JLO (see above) 7. are too hungry for dainty portions and / or have a hankering for Grimexican (read: middle of the road) food 8. understand that kitsch is a state of mind and not a fashion statement 9. are in search of a good meal that you won't regret later (financially or gastronomically) 10. actually give a shit how the person who serves you is being treated by their employer, whether or not they were born North of Texas 11. are trying to arrange a marraige well in advance for your 2-year-old son; who freaks out every time he sees a certain beautiful waitress that loves to "flirt" with him / dotes on him (in spite of the fact that her English and his Spanish are both rather thin) 12. hate empty restaurants as much as crowded ones 13. want to get seated right away and appreciate decent service 14. can buck up and realize that while nothing is perfect to everyone, some things are perfect as you find them 15. know a humorously disgusting mixed drinks list when you see one ---- Suffice to say, this isn't my "dining out" spot -- it's a reliable "eating out" spot, and has been for many years. I've always been able to customize anything on the menu with no trouble at all; not sure about the "frozen" thing. Nothing here tastes that way, either. But as my wife tells me -- I'm wrong every day.

text: This is the best new restaurant to have opened in awhile. For breakfast they offer great omelettes french toast, Waffles, and all the egg benedicts one could imagine, such as crab cake, Fried Green Tomato, and a crawfish tail one with smoky andoulle sausage. What sets this place apart from others is the quality of ingredients--always fresh, sometimes organic and almost always local. The level of care from the service staff-super professional but always friendly. Excellent coffee. Always a rich, fresh cup. Prices are modest for the quality of ingredients, level of service, and beautiful views of either the park or St. Charles Avenue. As for lunch, the salads are amazing! Super fresh lettuces, spring mixes, spinach, etc Their entree salads always have an interesting flair- may it be fried oyxers, seared Ahi tuna, or a simple but tender (read NOT DRY) checken breast. Even grilled shrimp on occasion. I know from good authority that all dressings are homemade-try the citrus vinergarette! text: In that last 10 years, I have adopted animals from a private shelter, a humane society in Pennsylvania and two different ASPCAs. Tampa's Humane Society is by far the cleanest and best organized I've seen. The shelter building does not have an overpowering "animal" smell (so they must be doing a great job cleaning up after all the animals) and its well marked so you can find the type of animal you are looking for. The staff is very friendly and knowledgeable as well. So, all that being said, we decided to adopt 2 cats from here after our own cat passed away. I've always had shelter cats so I expected the usual issues: fleas, worms, possibly a cold. I expected to have to bring them back to be spayed/neutered or have it done at my own expense. I also expected to pay about $80-90 per cat. I was shocked when I saw the medical record on the cats. They each had all their shots (one was a small kitten, so she still needed some boosters, but nothing more), they had been dewormed, treated with flea/tick/heartworm preventative, well fed, socialized and MOST importantly BOTH were spayed (that saved me about $150 a cat). The adoption fee was $50 per cat, but they were running a special and we got both for $50. I took them to my own vet the following day and they were in excellent health overall. I later took a stray that had wandered into our yard over to the feral cat clinic to be spayed and get her shots (then released back into our yard). It was $25 and the spay/neuter facility was very clean as well and felt like a regular vet office.

text: MY ABSOLUTE, HANDS-DOWN, FAVORITE RESTAURANT IN THE ENTIRE WORLD. BEST SUSHI EVER, EVER. How are there only 16 reviews on this place?! EVERYONE I ever take here fall in love. I grew up in St. Louis and this restaurant has been a staple in my life for years, and even now after moving North & traveling a lot. Every time I come home to visit, I ALWAYS make at least one visit to this restaurant. I have to. It's the best for so many reasons. The fish here is so fresh; the rice is perfectly seasoned with the right texture. You may not be a connoisseur but you can tell. Immediately. Non-sushi people change their opinion about sushi once they try GREAT sushi here. Everything is good. If you have to ask for my favorites: 1st and foremost, you have to get the SPICY TUNA ROLL. Yes, I know. Spicy tuna, woo hoo. Doesn't' sound special right? You couldn't be more wrong. They take the freshest red tuna and blend/mix it w/ the most perfect combinations of green onion, tempura flakes, and probably other fantastic things I can't make out but the roll will just melt in your mouth while your stomach screams with satisfaction. My second fav is the spicy crab roll (or get it as a hand roll). For appetizers, you must get the CRAB RANGOON. It's not your typical Chinese pocket of deep-fried goodness--- somehow they took something already yummy and found a way to actually improve it! They come out looking like eggrolls filled with the yummy, crab-infused cheese that come with a perfect match of sweet and slightly spicy sauce. A must. Also, go for the HOUSE SALAD. The presentation is beautiful and they make their own miso dressing that is to die for. So fresh and light. People always see me eating it and ask what it is. Do it. Oh this is getting long but there is so much to say! Other yums are the flash fried spinach app (the leaves melt in your mouth. literally!); the peppercorn sea bass, the yellow curry anything (any meat/seafood you like), and the scallop dishes. This is a family owned business, owned by a woman who can be summed up as a truly beautiful person. She treats you like family, she treats all of her employees as family (and a lot of them are), and in turn, the entire restaurant becomes your family. There are many regulars. Once you go, you can easily see why. This restaurant is a great destination for everything: dates, family dinners, girlfriend get-togethers, business lunches, all of it. The decor is tasteful and surprising given it's strip mall location. Do not let this facade fool you. You are in for a treat. Come as you are. The atmosphere is as casual as you want to make it or as formal as you want to get. Go now. Have a Lychee martini for me since I'm far away and tell everyone I said hello. You won't be sorry. This is my favorite place to eat--- and I eat a lot. I think it will become yours too. :)

text: I went to Jax this weekend while visiting Tucson with my friend Julie. We went with her father, who had been there a few times before and raved about the food and ambiance. The garlic shrimp tacos were definitely good, but didn't hold a candle to the mussels. The mussel/chorizo/french fry combination was incredible. What a unique combination! Certainly something I've never experienced. My friend and I shared the bacon wrapped pork tenderloin and hangar steak. The bacon wrapped tenderloin was juicy and delicious. A perfect combination of savory and sweet, when enjoyed with the homemade applesauce. YUM! The hangar steak was also delightful. The red wine jus balanced the savory steak spices perfectly and the side of mashed potatoes had super yummy caramelized onions mixed into them! The ONLY thing that 'put me off' was that the red wine jus looked like blood. I'm a medium rare girl, but the initial sight of a yummy steak sitting in bright red sauce was a bit unappetizing. Luckily, I got over it and really enjoyed the meal! I also had the Bishops Peak red blend wine, which was lovely. The decor was very cute. Sixties simple, but very thoughtful.

Walking in, we were greeted with sugary smell of waffle cones and servers that were more than helpful in finding you the perfect ice cream flavor, if you had not quite decided. I sampled the Cake Batter because I read so much about it and it was delicious, don't get me wrong, but I was looking for a diamond in the rough and continued on to try the Chocolate Peanut Butter (a gooey delicious blend of rich peanut butter and decadent chocolate) but I finally happened upon the Pistachio! You can't even fathom the creamy texture of this ice cream. To mix it up though, there were actual pieces of pistachio nuts throughout the ice cream. Overall, it was a wonderful evening, savoring the cool summer breeze with a delicious ice cream treat!

text: I lived in one of the Robin Apartments for a couple of years just after moving to Philadelphia. Both the management team and the maintenance team are outstanding to work with and always responded to my issues both quickly and completely. When the freezer broke on my refrigerator they replaced the entire unit with a new one. When one of the motors on a ceiling fan died they replaced the entire unit with a new one. This may seem small, but having had to deal with half-dead appliances and shoddy fix-its with other apartments it meant a lot to know that this company didn't skimp on replacements to save a few dollars. The buildings themselves are in phenomenal locations; I believe they are all around Center City West. The only real downside I ever encountered was the pest issue. The buildings are extremely old and unless everyone in the building is mindful of the issue and takes action against it there really is only so much you can do. That being said, when I made sure to spray for bugs every month (set a little reminder on my calendar) I never saw a single bug for months at a time. My feeling on this though is that if you live in a city you kind of have to expect a little bit of an issue with pests. They are also really phenomenal about taking care of their tennants in simple and small ways. For one thing, the office will sign for and receive packages for you (and call to leave you a message letting you know they have it for you). Also, if you call them when the weather starts getting nice they will send a maintenance man to put your AC unit in the window for you. Not a huge deal, but for a single (at the time) 5'1'' woman with a 200 lb AC unit this became a seriously HUGE deal. I cannot say enough good things about the Robin family and the way they handle their business. It is also important that I mention that I have referred probably 10 different people to Robin Apartments. I know of at least four that have ended up renting and all of them could not be happier with the price and location. Tell me another place where you can find a one bedroom apartment with utilities included in Center City for under $650 and I'll point out that it is probably a Robin Apts building.

text: The story you are about to read is true. 5:31 pm. My partner, my wife and I head to the famous Jacques-Imo's for a taste of the local fare. It's a good thing we brought the GPS, without it and you have a better chance of finding a preacher on Bourbon Street. The restaurant is tucked away in the middle of a narrow street - parking is a game of chance even for early evening. Look for the traffic light mounted to the building with all three lights brightly shining. If you read other reviews, you will see that this is the best time to come. Plus it leaves the evening for a pub crawl through the Quarter. Jacques-Imo's is split between two buildings. Our host takes us back to the street and into the house next door. There is no wait and our server, Rebecca, is quick with our drinks. We find out that the writing on the front window which resembles an old time menu is for decoration only. The window says they have frog legs, but alas, that item is not available. The menu is divided into two sections, the items on the left are their consistent dishes that do not change. The right side shows their seasonal items. The selections are quite varied with items like rabbit on the menu. Our meals don't take long at all and the quality of the food is better than you would believe. I do have to say that I am an addict for bread pudding and when it comes time for desert - that's what I order. This, my friends, is the best bread pudding that I have ever tried. I would consider making a special trip to the Big Easy just for this dish alone. If you want a few tips, come early - this place deserves to be busy and you will wait if you are late. Expect authentic atmosphere and food, this ain't the Four Seasons! Finally, save room for the bread pudding - if not, order it anyway and send it to me.
label: POS

text: Went here for my mom's bday, and it was fabulous. Expensive, but worth it. It was a bit crowded/loud waiting for our table, but then it was a Friday night. The black cherry caipirinha was delicious, but beware, the cherries are -soaked- with alcohol. Nice touch--they brought out complimentary chocolates with a candle at the end for my mom. I heard that the chef/owner was involved with the late, lamented Patria here in NYC--if so, that makes sense. They both do great things with interesting ingredients and light/tasty sauces and sides. Only drawback is that it's not particularly vege/vegan friendly--if you're strict, go elsewhere or be stuck with 1 choice.

text: UPDATE** Never received any reply...AWFUL PLACE - BAD CUSTOMER SERVICE. What a shame that the owner must think he is too important to reply to a bad experience a paying customer had in his house. Oh well. Live and learn. Spend your money in some other Chinese Restaurant. I sent this email to, "Chef Poon" and to this day NO REPLY has been received. This is his newer place on Chestnut Street. SAVE YOUR MONEY - This establishment is a RIP OFF!! There are far better places in Center City Philadelphia for Chinese Food. I made reservations for your New Years Banquet for Two. I was led to believe that this would be not just a Chinese food meal but rather a real experience. I talked my partner into coming with me to enjoy such an, "experience." We arrived at 7:30pm. My original reservations, I spoke to, "Tommy" who at that time explained that because it is only a party of 2, the "Lobster" course would be substituted. Ok, fine. Upon us being sat, they brought over the News Years Banquet Menu. Nothing was explained to us. Your advertisement(s) stated it is a 10 Course meal. Served Family Style. We were brought the first course (which was not served family style but each, myself and my partner received one plate) Its was excellent. However later after the meal, it was explained your staff combined many courses for the first course, so the reality is that I think the first plate combined 3-4 courses? Next plate arrived, (we felt rushed) This plate was also served not what your advertisement communicated but again many "courses" combined. Your head of the staff came over, rushed and explained that because we are a party of two and not a party of 5-6 Lobster was substituted. I called over the gentleman and asked him if I heard him correctly about that the dinner was complete and now we are going to be served dessert? I was taken aback, what I saw on the dessert plate was ridicules and insulting to anybody spending $45 (tax and tip). We were given 1 blue berry, 1 Raspberry, A small Dixie cup of Tapioca, one almond cookie, and here is the real kicker as if the meal wasn't already on the side of silliness, a Sugar Cube Size of Chocolate Cheese cake. The quality of your food was very good, however we feel we were sold something and was not given what we paid for. This would be a great place to take your family. Admission was $8 for adults and I want to say $6 for kids but there is a yearly pass option as well. I don't believe you can bring in outside food and drink but the concession stand is not overly expensive (1-6 dollar range per item). The line for concessions was terribly long but I have a sneaky suspicion the park was crowded due to the holiday and not generally that populated. A friend described the place as a "child's summertime mecca". That explains it really well. For adults, good for a group activity probably not great for a relaxing time alone soaking up sun. Really good option for an Indy (all ages/group) summer activity since beaches are scarce (if any).

Here you will find dresses, skirts, tops (i.e. tunics), jackets and robes. I was fascinated with the great selection of cashmere pashminas in every colour imaginable. Anyone who has one of these pashminas is likely to survive long cold Edmonton winter months, and do so in style. The boutique also carries unique jewellery, most of which is made of silver and earthy, natural looking stones. The rings look a bit bulky, but I believe that they will look beautiful as cocktail rings. Overall, Maggie Walt boutique has a very distinct atmosphere and unique clothes. The designer herself seems to tell her life stories and share her passion for Eastern cultures though the clothes she creates.

text: The last time we went to Sammy's was a HUGE disappointment. A couple of us recommended it to our group as it was amazing the last time we'd been there, but I am sorry we went. Heading over to Sammy's after deciding that was where we were going to go, the usual friendly and eager face outside their door with menus was beckoning us in. "Don't worry, we're already headed your way," I said. Our group seated, we all order. The food came out fairly quickly, and the meal itself lasted about that long, too. I felt like just as soon as we were seated and given our meals, they were being taken away before we were even done. Why bother beckoning with a smile if you know you're going to kick us out soon after? Trying to make that last dollar before closing-time is understandable. Especially since businesses were still hurting after Katrina (it really was taking a while for some to get back on their feet), but whisking us away the way they did lost them business. They just didn't care. The food wasn't as great as I remembered either, but I'm not sure if it was because it was rushed in the making, or if the experience was making the food seem worse than it was. Either way, I know none of us were really happy with that meal. Sorry, Sammy's. There are just too many other spectacular places in New Orleans to even contemplate giving you another try.

text: In my book this is the best nightclub in the city if you love latin music. I prefer to go on Saturdays. The crowd is less tense and everybody is looking for a good time. There is a giant dance floor in the middle which can fit over 1,000 people. The lighting in the club is great and there are two bars on the outsides of the dance floor. It is never too crowded nor impossible to get a drink. Drinks are reasonably priced. The place tends to stay open past 2 normally between 2:30-3am. While it is in a bad neighborhood there is constant security around the club/restaurant, the crowd on Saturday night are older late 20s-early 30s all looking to dance and have a good time. The perfect place to end your night if you're looking to dance! All of the normal tendencies you see at nightclubs do not apply here. You don't have to worry about the braggadocios machismo guy looking to pick fights and look tough; The bartenders who are more interested in finding the drunkest chick in the club/bar than serving you drinks and the overpriced everything that comes along with the clubbing experience. text: My husband tried to take me here for breakfast in January but we skipped because we couldn't even find a parking spot. You might have to wrestle a retiree for it. Retirees and/or snowbirds seem to make up the majority of the customers. I have to say, though, that they know a great deal when they see one. The price is very reasonable for the amount of food you get. My bacon, egg, and cheese sandwich was less than $4. My hubby had another breakfast sandwich. I had a large orange juice and a hot chocolate. He had coffee. The whole bill was $12.76. The waitress was very friendly and quite efficient. She greeted us promptly and got us our drinks right away. Our food arrived fresh and hot. Your server will leave your bill at your table and when you are ready, you pay at the counter. I would definitely eat here again. text: Moshi moshi is a really small japanese restaurant tucked in the rittenhouse area. There were a couple tables for sit down and some tables lined up along the wall for sitting on the floor. I wasn't too impressed with the sushi. I like my sushi cold and the sushi here was definitely a bit warm. The love salmon roll was the best out of them all but even then it was mediocre at best. text: Ugh! That's all I have to say about Brentwood Forest and the folks who run the association. I lived there for about a year and the Association was one of the main reasons why I got the heck out of there as soon as my lease was up. If trash is left out before or after pickup, a property manager digs through your trash (to determine whose it is) and you are fined. - Parking is strictly enforced, above and beyond what's necessary. We were never without parking spots, yet the Property Manager would send out letters, telling us where we could and couldn't park within our cove. She always made sure that she was the one who parked in the closest spot. Besides that, the property managers aren't nice! The gentleman who owns the building we lived in cannot keep tenants for more than a year because of the property manager around the corner's harassing behavior. The ONLY saving grace is that the grounds of Brentwood Forest are kept immaculate. The grass is always mowed, trees trimmed and flowers blooming. When it snows, the parking lots and sidewalks are cleaned off almost immediately. Frankly, I'd rather live near nice people who mind their own business, but that's a condo association for you.

text: I'm new to Philly and have seen the abundance of Marathon Grill's that populate Center City. My coworkers have ordered delivery numerous times from MG so as I passed by after a doctors appointment and having some leftover time to burn up before going back to work, today was my day to stop in. It was 4 o'clock in the afternoon and not a particularly busy time of day for any restaurant, which could go for or against me. Being an optimist, I thought it would fall in my favor. I was wrong. The roasted pork sandwich with Asian slaw caught my eye as it was one of the daily specials. I ordered fries too but didn't realize it was already served with fries. I was hoping for a nice cut of pork topped with the slaw. When I see a "special" on any menu, I presume it is going to be done well because it is a featured item. Again, I was wrong. The pork was shredded and not "roasted" as stated on the menu. To me, roasted conjures up images of a pork roast slowly cooked in an over for hours, not a cut of pork that was likely cooked on a stove top in a sauce pan. Picture pulled pork instead of a roasted cut of pork. With the exception of the soggy "Asian slaw" that topped the pork, it had very little flavor. I expected an explosion of flavors considering the billing this sandwich was given on the menu...and being a "special". Perhaps I assumed a combination of ginger and/or peanut would be used in the slaw to really make the Asian part of this combo sing! Nope. Cabbage and carrots. Not much else. It was served with fries. Cold, hard fries. Imagine "long rectangular shaped potato flavored sticks, previously fried and allowed to sit, reaching room temperature and hardening before serving". They crunched like ice cubes and they were terrible! I watched the grill cook drop two baskets of fries while I awaited my to-go order and wondered who she was cooking them for since the restaurant had only one other customer and she was already eating her meal. When I ate my fries, I figured out who she was cooking the fries for...the customer who would be unlucky enough to get them an hour later! These were obviously fries that are "cooked" ahead of time and dropped back into the oil to reheat them as needed for orders. Yum! There comes a point when an innocent little potato has nothing more to give, Marathon Grill! The lovely young lady behind the counter who took my order was pleasant and kind...until her personal cell phone rang from her back pocket and she started to argue with whomever was on the other end of the phone before she hung up on him/her. ***Personal note here...LEAVE YOUR FREAKIN' CELL PHONES AT HOME WHEN YOU'RE AT WORK! What business owner allows that??? Work is work, not an interruption of your personal life! God forbid you should lose the opportunity to argue on your cell phone in front of paying clients while you're being paid by your employer! This goes for ANY business! (OK, back to the review. Whew!) Overpriced. Nearly $11 for a shredded pork sandwich and fries. It would have cost less to go to Applebee's for a chicken salad that would have been ten times more satisfying. Would I go back? Maybe. Mayyyyybe. I hate to cast off any business in one visit. If I experience a not-so-good meal, I try to be fair and give a restaurant a second chance. But with as many odds stacked against Marathon Grill as I experienced today, it is likely that it would take an earth shattering moment to bring me back inside their doors, especially given the economy (not wanting to waste more money that I have to) and the number choices I have in Center City. Sorry Marathon Grill, you just didn't cut it for me.. I give you one star only because zero stars is not an option. And, you did give me something in exchange for me giving you money. I suppose a star was earned for that.
label: NEG

text: This place definitely has potential. For take-out, I'd probably rate it a star higher. The service was friendly and fast, but we were the first customers of the day. I went with family and most of us got a pizza, which turned out to be huge. At around $12 for a medium pie and $2 per topping, it's not the cheapest stuff and the quality certainly reflected that. My cheeseless (too much cheese makes me feel sick) pizza with mushrooms and olives was great-- since it's essentially dough, sauce and toppings, all of these needed to be quality ingredients, and they were. I highly recommend the brick oven-style, and my sister really enjoyed her "bar" personal-sized margharita pizza. My boyfriend got a huge Sicilian (they were out of the smaller size, and upgraded him at no charge). I had a bite, but didn't really care for it...something was off about the dough, but he liked it. Another member of our party had the plain white pizza, which was pretty tasty as well. Anyway, you get the point: the pizza is decent and accommodations were easily made. The atmosphere, however, is where this place loses stars. I didn't enjoy sitting next to a humming refrigeration unit, and the floors and bathrooms looked a little cheap and dirty. The tables and benches were also off-putting and I couldn't think of a good way to explain it, until my boyfriend said "this reminds me of a pizza place at the shore." The cheap long table and "wooden" plastic benches have their time and place, and that time and place is (and can only ever be) the Jersey shore. The plates fit right in with the dirty shore corner pizza parlor feel. The artwork was somewhat amusing, a combination of Pink Floyd-inspired canvas paintings mounted on the wall, some plastic plaques featuring names of Italian cities, and a creepy fat Italian guy statue looming in the corner amidst some fake plants. I feel bad bashing the setting, but the pizza is actually good. And I might actually go back if it was a nice sit-down place. But even for takeout, Buckingham Pizza still wins in my book. We went here because my dad had a restaurant.com coupon, so if you have one of those, it's no big loss. Overall: meh, but tasty leftovers!

text: Way past the age of caring about margaritas or decor (never cared anyway), I go to restaurants for the FOOD! While it's true that the decor at Senora's looks like the interior of an unsuccessful pinata factory, I don't need to look up to the ceiling when on my plate is, by far, the best Mexican food to be found. Mexicans and Texans might disagree, but who the hell cares? I begin each meal with a chicken tamale. You'll find none better. Tacos and enchiladas reign supreme here, and the more of the spicy homemade pineapple salsa you can slurp down with each bite only adds to the enjoyment and office-killing garlic breath. Yes, the salsas are overpriced, especially since they are central to the Mexican food experience, but it's a lot cheaper than driving to Texas and a lot safer (ehh..West Chester), than visiting Mexico. And, at least for your first time there, try the flan. Other Mexican restaurants purport to deliver flan to your table but none of it comes close to Senora's thick, caramel-infused, cheesecake-like recipe. One slice is enough for two, maybe three, though there will be some threats from other forks for that last piece. The food is always the freshest, the tortillas are homemade, and the service is prompt. We've been eating there since 1994 and still happily make the 36+ mile round trip for the treat. I have a feeling that Senora's suffers from not having a liquor license because the roach-like West Chester college crowd, still a bit dimwitted about the world at large, thinks that no fun can be had without alcohol. Go to a bar for your drinks. Go to Senora's for food. Freshman cannot live by Margaritas alone.

text: Just had lunch at Dixie Picnic with some friends and it was great. I ordered the muffaletta and it was darn near perfect. A very tasty olive relish smothered over a nice layer of meat and cheese on the traditional muffaletta loaf. The loaf itself was light and flavorful with a great just-slightly-chewy texture. I could have handled it being toasted a little more, but that's picking nits. One friend ordered the crab cakes and the other ordered the chili and conrbread, and both were very satisfied with their lunches as well. On the way out the door I grabbed a piece of the Key Lime pie and it was really good as well. Light texture with a healthy amount of lime zest and a moist graham cracker crust. A little bit sweet for my personal tastes (I like my fruit desserts on the tart side), but I would order it again. Will definitely be going back for breakfast and lunch.

text: On my surprise visit to my family I asked to eat here upon the recommendation of a coworker. I was told it was famous for it's Carne Seca- and the menu highlighted all of it's fanfare, so I decided that is what I would order. I thought $17.95 was a little pricey, so I went with the chimichanga. The Carne Seca had a good flavor, but it was the texture of beef jerky in a burrito. I didn't enjoy it all. I also asked for it with a mixture of sour cream and green sauce, and it came dry. The beans and rice were unmemorable. We had a constant supply of salsa and warm chips which were tasty. My step mom said her tortilla soup was very good and said the broth tasted home made, and my sister really enjoyed her enchiladas. Our server, Destiny, seemed like she was in a rush. I also asked for my sauces to be mixed and it seemed like it was such a hassle for her. I asked the rest of my family and they said that they felt rushed since they had arrived (I arrived a little after the 6 of them sat down. I was literally taking a bite of my food- which wasn't 2/3 finished and the server said, "are you going to want dessert?" I had already seen the dessert menu so I told her that we probably would, but would like to finish. She later came and said "Are you ready for your check now?"- so instead of ordering desserts for the 7 of us we said yes. I've definitely experienced better, and for a much better price. And although we were a big table, we weren't that picky- we would have doubled her tip if she would have just treated us well.

The meat in the pork pot stickers were grainy, the toasted ravioli was a lot of breading and not much filling and the buffalo chicken bites were just mediocre. Service is great when you get one of the Starr-y eyed and bushy tailed young ones who bought everything that the Starr organization drill instructors threw their way, and that's good. text: This restaurant, like the reviews on yelp.com, is all over the place. Some people hate it, some people love it. Some people say the food is not worth the wait, some people say it's New Orleans' version of heaven. For me, the mark of a truly great restaurant is CONSISTENCY. If you can only order one or two dishes off a menu because those are the only things that are consistently good, night after night, then the restaurant cannot be called a truly great place. Why bother with the other 28 things on a menu if you can't eat them because they're slop? That's what happened to us. On a recent Saturday night, we ordered the blackened redfish and grilled grouper. The redfish was some overcooked piece of mush with no texture. Our guess was that the fish was left over from the previous night and reheated. We also ordered red beans and rice as one of the sides, and the rice was hard as stone pebbles and stale. How in the hell do you mess up red beans and rice?! This restaurant packs 'em in based on the strength of their fried chicken and alligator cheesecake appetizer. That's two things on their menu. The rest is abysmal. Considering they want $25 per entree, I left the restaurant feeling completely ripped off. I would never go back.

text: Laissez les bons temps rouler! 'Cuz there was a party in my mouth at my last Cochon visit. Next we had the 'salad' course: Mushroom and Fried Beef Jerky salad with the Cucumbers and Herbs. Both pretty damned good. We shared the 'Fisherman Style' redfish with a side of Creamy Grits and a side of Collard Greens. Hmmm, hmmm good. We literally cleaned our plates. Some mighty fine Cajun food if you ask me. text: Whenever I think of going to a Wine Bar, I immediately think of Tria (mostly because I love cheese!). The atmosphere is so much less pretentious than Tria (and most wine bars), which I definitely appreciate, but the staff knows their wine. My favorite game is the "pick me a wine" game, and the bartenders all play, albeit some with a little more enthusiasm than others. I appreciate that they pour you a swallow first, to make sure that you like the wine that they pick for you (or that you pick for yourself), and that they are gracious if you just don't like it! The food is always good, although not amazing (although the curried cauliflower soup on special last Saturday was decadent!). All in all, I really love this bar... I just have to remember how much I love it and go back sooner this time!

Instant seating is available around the bar where there's an empty table (or if you find a party willing to have you sit with them hahahahah) The waitresses are always quick to serve, but wait time for the food can vary. text: Since having my son, I have been exploring the inner workings of all things kiddo. I went last year and had a good time with my niece and nephew who are a bit older, and today, I experienced a different side of the museum. Tucked away in areas I had yet to check out were places that the little kids could really enjoy. A splash tub with lots of toys floating around and ponchos to cover their clothes was a nice added touch. Different textured floors to crawl and run on, a sand box area for the younger troops. It was great to watch Max see things for the first time! He really enjoyed all the things close to the floor at his eye level, from the flower potting area to the magnet wall. We also rode the carousel a couple of times. His first time he was mesmerized by the stars above and all the different colors and music that were going on around us. His face was beaming!! We went with three other friends, all with younger children and they just had so much fun going through the maze, digging in the sand and checking out the exhibits. I was really impressed this time. I could really take it all in and appreciate it better now that I am a mother. And, for me, the best part was the 50 years of Barbie history exhibit that they have going on now. I saw the Star Wars exhibit last year and was not impressed, but the Barbie's showroom kicked butt! There was a catwalk, dressing area, make up area, photographer's booth, tons of stuff for the kids, but the stuff for us moms, looking back on the years of Barbie and our own childhood brought back an insane amount of fun memories! It was really impressive all the Barbie information they shared and how beautiful the dolls on display were. They had two life size Barbies and lots of original Barbies in boxes showing how she has grown and changed through the years, the mansions she lived in, the car she drove and the man she married (and I believe divorced recently), Ken. It was a really cool exhibit! I was having as much fun as Max at that point. :) Thankfully he is loving pink right now, so all the bright colors made him happy too while I drug him around the showroom! I look forward to going back year after year as Max's interests change, b/c the museum will help him grow and learn. This is a great unique date option, a great place for families of ALL ages, an incredible value for money and is ranked one of the best children's museums in the country. It is worth checking out!

I'll try anything once (well, almost anything) That being said--I will not order them again. Way too much breading and grease. I had the crab and asparagus salad as my entree. The crab was good, but the salad was very small and definitely not worth the price. I was still hungry after I ate my salad--that never happens. I always have leftovers. My boyfriend had the steak special--not impressed. The steak was average at best. All in all is was extremely disappointed and I would not go back again. My recommendation--find another place to eat.

text: What used to be Scholar's Inn reopened a few months ago as SI Restaurant and Lounge. Yes, it is a totally different restaurant. It's been revamped to offer private, upscale booths downstairs, and a trendy community table with changing neon lights upstairs. The bar area has been updated, too, with some modern, plastic booths that seem to emit light. Definitely conversation pieces. Also, Thursdays are half-price martini night, which brings the price down to about the $5 mark for specialty drinks. My favorite is the Cable Car: Captain Morgan, Orange Curacao, a splash of sour and a cinnamon-lemony rim. Mmm. Chef Jeff Brenchley is new, too. They plucked him from the Bloomington Scholar's Inn, and for good reason: He has a knack for layering savory sweet tastes, perfect for this French-American cuisine.

text: Busch Gardens has great deals for admission. It's a great place to see some cool animals, drink beer and waste a lazy afternoon; however, if you're not a little guy, don't expect to ride the roller coasters! We took advantage of their annual pass promotion, so the ticket price was fairly inexpensive. We have found their meal plan to be a great deal if you're planning to spend the entire day at the park. For about $25/person, you can enjoy unlimited food and beverages at designated restaurants and eateries. It was worth the $25 alone just for unlimited bottles of water! The animals in the park are kinda cool to see and if you're a beer drinker there's a vendor on every corner, but the shows are kinda lame - I found the pirate show to be a joke. The roller coasters are very plentiful, but they are NOT designed to fit everyone. In fact, while I looked around the park, there were MANY, MANY people who did not fit in the seats of the roller coasters - Disney needs to give them some tips on designing rides! The wooden roller coaster hurt to ride - roller coasters shouldn't hurt. I had several bruises on my legs from the wooden coaster. Overall, I am really not impressed with Busch Gardens....but Disney on the otherhand, now there's a park!
label: NEG

text: I came here for a few NBA Finals game and I love it here! Décor: You got your bar right when you walk in and you got the rest of the restaurant with all the large flat-screen TV's. I LOVE sitting in the front part of the restaurant where this like.. 4-foot screen is in front of like 3 tables. I am literally like 4 feet away from this gigantic screen. LOVE it!!! Service: The waitresses are quick, friendly and know how to serve! I have never had a problem and you seat yourselves and they'll notice you pretty quickly. I don't know how they do it, lol. Food: In the few times I've been here, I've had (and pictures up!): * Post-its: hahaha, my bf LOVED these and even I admire their convenience and originality. It's just like bread with whatever cheese you want smushed inside and you pull it apart when it's all gooey and melted. mmmMMmm * Baked chicken wings: I don't even need to describe these, since other Yelpers already got this covered! I got the Honey BBQ ones before and I think a spicy mild one. It's not that spicy, but either one is pretty delicious. I like that interesting crisp that isn't on normal fried chicken wings slathered with sauce. * Honey Wheat Crust BBQ Chicken Pizza: You can't really mess up a BBQ Chicken Pizza, but what I loved the most? THE CRUST. You can taste that wheat crust and they slather on honey in it and roll it up I think. It's SO GOOOD. And the nice bbq kick with the onions? Yummmmm. * Quesadilla Appetizer: decently-sized. And pretty good, nothing to rave about but nothing to complain about either! They have your sides of guac and sour cream without asking, so that's nice! * Philly Cheesesteak: BF thought it was okay, not great but not horrible. * Gyros w/fries: decently sized! A bit dry with the meat, but still okay. Beers and stuff are a better deal if you go to any of the big sporting events. Price: Pretty good! Usually around ~$10+ a person? Bottom Line: This place is GREAT if you and your friends want to catch a game while eating some decent food. Not a smokey or obnoxiously loud environment. Very chill and nice people come here, so thumbs up! J

text: First, let's get this out of the way: NoVi was, by and large, a disappointment. Despite the decent decor and reasonably priced food, I don't think I'll find myself returning. I was the only person at the bar, with only two other tables of guests in the restaurant. There was no host at the front when I entered, but I was greeted promptly and sat myself at the bar. While I wasn't drinking this particular evening, I did browse the cocktail list, and it was standard tropical fruit or coffee liqueur based restaurant fare. The menu is a decent size but relatively uninspired, classic American Italian dishes and a wide selection of pizzas. I settled on the Tuscan Chicken Sandwich with a side salad, and was pleasantly surprised with the plump and juicy chicken breast and fresh bun. My salad was pretty much crap, but the balsamic based dressing that came with it had a nice smoky flavor that I enjoyed. Unfortunately, this is pretty much where I run out of positive things to say. The staff at NoVi, including the chef who identified himself as the manager on duty, all had a bad tendency to crowd around the bar, talk or text on their cell phones, and pass around drink samples among each other as if I didn't exist. To the bartender's credit, my water never went empty and my plate was whisked away immediately when I was finished despite the otherwise complete lack of attention or engagement. Unfortunately, when I paid with cash for my meal I was flatly informed that the bar drawer had no change, and was given two large bills back along with a vaguely expectant stare. Not being the type to stiff service staff, especially after 6 years in the industry myself, I ended up leaving a double the appropriate tip for my sandwich and water as i had no ones with me, and was gone as fast as my heels would carry me. Not a great experience, and not one I'm in any hurry to repeat.

text: Agave gets one star for strong margaritas and for good reaction to major problems. They should get no stars for the pure comedy we experienced on our visit last night. I met up with two out of town friends, never having been there myself. Everything was fine until we got our food...I tried the prickly pear margarita, which was delicious, and it was raining last night so it wasn't terribly crowded. I ordered a chicken quesadilla, which was palatable but not wonderful. As I was going through my routine of scooping up some sour cream and some guacamole, a little bit of salsa and some lettuce and spreading it on my quesadilla, something seemed a little tough. I wrote it off as a chunk of iceberg and didn't think any more of it. Until I bit into it, and it wouldn't break. I pulled it out of my mouth to discover a balled-up, flattened out RECEIPT. In my freaking guacamole! And it wasn't even for my order! At nearly the same moment, one of my dining companions was working on pulling half a toothpick out of her mouth, which was buried deep inside her chimichanga. We're not snobby diners, so we brought it to the attention of the waitress in good humor, but we had every right to throw a fit. She did comp every single meal and brought us all a double of what we were drinking on the house, but come on. Maybe if I find myself in a group wanting to head out to Agave strictly for drinks, I'll go. They seem to have that side of the operation down. But I can't say I'll feel like choking down foreign objects any time soon.

text: I hate to be the first one to leave a bad review for Germantown but here it is. I will preface this review saying I had dinner there and from all these reviews it sounds as if this place's forte is brunch, so if you're having brunch there maybe you should ignore my review. I would give Germantown 5 stars for ambiance and service because the restaurant is cute and romantic with a fantastic view of downtown Nashville. Our server was friendly, efficient and not too intrusive. However, the food was another story. Perhaps it is because I am from Los Angeles that I found the amount of oil in the food appalling. Now don't get me wrong, I am not one of those people who eats only salad and in fact I LOVE buttery and oil foods. But unfortunately the food at Germantown was soaked in oil to the point where that's all I tasted. In fact both my bf and I had stomach aches when we got home. The escargot and Shrimp Curry were soaked in oil and butter. It overpowered any taste that the dish shoudl have had. The Pork was okay, but nothing to write home about. I am a big dessert person and was excited for the apple crisp which got such good reviews on Citysearch. It came in a bowl that looked as if they melted half a bowl of butter and then dumped the crisp in. I couldn't even finish it, or taste anything besides butter for that matter. Pros of Germantown is that they service fried yeast balls (like awesome donut type bread) b/t the salad and the entree which were delicious. However, that wasn't enough to save the meal.
label: NEG

text: This Coach Outlet, ahem, Factory Store is thrown in amongst the regular-priced shops on State Street, masquerading as the real deal until you step inside. It is an oasis of good deals if, like me, you deign to look oh-so past season. The best deals are usually around holidays like Xmas, Memorial Day, etc. when they tack on an extra discount. text: This was a place that was recommended to me and separately to my son, so we took the street car as noted by Blunt G and walked the rest of the way through a pleasant, tree-lined neighborhood. I had read they didn't take reservations so we didn't bother, but as we waited to be seated I noted that reservations were being phoned in. I had a moment of panic as the party ahead of us hesitated but accepted "the last table out back." Fortunately, there were two more tables in the front windows, and we were seated at one of those. It was about 5:30 and dusk. We were near the bar and had a nice view of that as well as the street. It was standing room only, with several groups waiting outside, within ten minutes. Our waiter was quite relaxed and pleasant and spent some time getting to know us, seemingly genuinely interested in where we were from and how we heard about Jacques-Imo's. I wish we'd gotten his name. My son ordered the rabbit fillet in a dijon sauce to start. It was moist and tender, deep-fried inside a crunchy batter. On his own, our waiter brought us a slice of shrimp and alligator sausage cheesecake (it's a savory quiche actually) and it was lovely, very flavorful. The spinach salad had something fried on top, I thought it was artichoke pate but it turned out to be my first-ever oyster! Cornbread with melted garlic butter was a nice accompaniment. Our main courses came with two sides each: . Mixed fried chicken--three huge pieces of moist, crispy battered chicken (leg, thigh, breast). Sides were cabbage and mashed potatoes...even though our waiter explained that the cabbage would be cooked until mushy, the texture was off-putting to this member of our party. . Rare, blackened (sushi-grade) tuna with oyster champagne brie sauce...not sure what sides this person had; . I had Chicken Pontalba, a giant half-breast that was moist and perfectly seasoned. Sides were red beans and rice and a fresh corn dish (chaux?), also delicious. We had no room for dessert, and took leftovers back to our hotel. Drinks were very good--cadillac margarita for me and another of our party tried a Sazerac, which had been recommended by a bartender friend back home and became his new favorite drink.

text: So being the gluttons for punishment that we are, my wife and I came here last night for dessert. We had just finished a fantastic meal at Miga at it was just to easy to cross the street to indulge my wife's chocolate craving. We were pleasantly surprised when we walked in the door and the place was actually open. No malfunctioning C3PO to rush us out. We were seated immediately in a dining room that reminded me of a tacky version of the Cheesecake Factory. Vats of chocolate, trite aphorisms on the walls, abstract drawings of some bald dude with an earring, references to Willie Wonka. . .I read somewhere that these restaurants belong in Disneyland or Vegas and I have to agree. So we decide to order the banana split waffle. It was very expensive -- $14 for a dessert -- but sounded delicious. The pictures on the menu made it look amazing (it was the one dessert they chose to showcase on the Waffles and Crepes section). But it SUCKED: 1. The waffle was one of the worst I've ever tasted. It was as if they took a week-old cake donut (not the Krispy Kreme kind, but the really heavy kind that crumbles), and shoved it into a waffle maker. The waffle was so hard that I needed a knife to cut it. And it tasted like, well, a re-baked week-old bad cake donut. The waffle we had at the Days Inn was a gazillion times better. 2. The chocolate was way too sweet, as if put too much sugar. Now I'm not a chocolate connoisseur, but I do know a few things about chocolate and I did take chemistry in high school. I know that high quality chocolates typically have a higher cocoa content. And from chemistry, if you increase the content of one ingredient, then the percentage allocated to the other ingredients goes down. So if the sugar content is very high (too sweet), then the cocoa content, by definition, will be low. So my conclusion: Max Brenner uses low quality chocolate. Unbelievable for a restaurant that bills itself as "changing the world's chocolate culture." 3. The banana was way over-ripe. Over-ripe to the point where it left a pungent aftertaste in mouth. 4. There was not nearly enough vanilla ice cream for this dessert. Ok, so maybe we didn't the amount of vanilla ice cream with the waitress (the menu just says "vanilla ice cream", with no indication of the unit of measure). But for a $14 dessert, most people would assume you'd get at least a scoop. We got something closer to a dollop. So there it is. I can't believe anyone could screw up a waffle, ice cream, fudge, and bananas that badly. Now that I think about it, there wasn't even any fudge - it was chocolate sauce. At any rate, this dessert SUCKED. It would suck even if it cost $3 in the "day-old" section of a bakery.

text: I. Love. Philadelphia. Period. But I hate that we're known for Geno's. Oh Geno's. I'm sorry I took more than five seconds to order. I didn't realize you were ACTUALLY doing me a favor by taking my hard-earned money (that's right, you're not the only people who work for a living) in exchange for shitty service and shittier food. Though I admit, at least your hot sauce is good. But you didn't make that, and I served it to myself. This place is the EZ Bake Oven of cheese steaks. I swear. Except EZ Bake products are vaguely intriguing - especially since I can't bake for shit. There is nothing intriguing about something that takes five minutes to slap together. I'm not saying cheesesteaks aren't great. Hell, Philadelphia born and raised, right here, son! In fact, my mom's cheesesteaks, which people tell me are quite good (I tend to stay away from my mom's cooking cause she's my mom) put me through college. That and tons of financial aid. But I digress. Because of this, I can actually say that in my lifetime I've made at least fifty steaks from scratch. It's not hard. In fact, it's one of the easiest things you can do. By a hunk of top round and chip it. Pan fry it in some oil. Add the onions last, or they'll overcook. Scrape it into a pile the length of the bread you're using, spread good 'ole American white on top so that it melts, and then put the bread on top. Spatula underneath, flip it over, and you're done. You've got an "American wit," or, for the uninitiated, a "cheesesteak with American cheese and onions." Do they do this at Geno's? No. The meat was cooked, to be sure. "When" is the question. If I knew I could get so much business putting under-salted beef jerky on yesterday's roll, skipping the courtesy of melting the cheese altogether, and charging eight bucks for the whole thing, I'd have skipped college and started my own steak empire so that Philly natives could hate my guts. I know it's 3am, and I know you're hungry. If that's worth a trip to South Philly to deal with all the other drunk, pissed off people, you might as well go home and sleep it off. Go to D'Alessandro's. They actually care about the people they serve. AND they have a respectable selection of bottled beers. One last thing: If they're called "Freedom Fries," does that mean they come from "Freedomland?"

text: I've only visited the Breadland Organic Whole Grain Bakery (breathes) to buy gluten-free bread. I was told by a girl that cut my hair that they have the best gluten-free bread and buns she has ever tasted. She said they were so good, that she ate six buns in a row. I was excited, when I heard this, because Kinnikinnick's bread is not very good. It's like eating bricks, and it took me years to get used to it; not to mention, it only really tastes good when it's toasted. I've tried Breadland's arrowroot gluten-free buns. These are indeed very good. They are very soft and the outside is chewy, and they taste great with just about anything: butter, hummus, melted cheese, or peanut butter & jam. The only problem is that I can't eat them, because they give me really bad eczema on my face. I suspect it's all the yeast they put in it. The focaccia gluten-free bread they sell is also really good. This is like a thick flat bread that is flavoured with tons of herbs and I think some garlic too. It's so good, and although it contains yeast, I don't get eczema, so it must not be that much. These breads are very expensive though, so I only get them as a treat.

text: A group of us went recently for a special occasion dinner. The menu was pre-set with 3 choices for appetizers and three choices for main courses. I'll first start by saying that the cuisine was superb and the back of the house did a very nice job. I had the seared foie gras to start followed by the tenderest veal I have ever had. The cheese and dessert cart were brilliant. Saying this, the service was horrible. Le Bec Fin was known for its presentation of the courses and attention to detail. This was not present the night we dined. First, the table that they gave us was much too small for the number of people we had (10). My shoulders were touching the person to my right and left. Second, it took us 45 minutes to receive our first glass of wine. AND the appetizers arrived before the wine. I felt that one of our guests constantly had to remind to wait staff that we were in the restaurant. No refills on water or wine unless we asked. Food came our sparingly. I will say that whoever was on bread detail did their job, because I felt that that was the only person that I saw. Whilst everyone was pleasant and no one was rude, the lack of attention to detail and service caused the dining experience to suffer. My advice to Le Bec Fin; you simply cannot survive on reputation and excellent food. The entire dining experience is what attracts people to your restaurant and more importantly, brings them back. Get the front of the house fixed...please
label: NEG

text: A year ago, Obey Your Body did a miracle for me. I was approached by a seller in a kiosk in Independence Center, sold the fingernail care set for $50.00. Generally, I use MAC products, so I guess I'm kind of a make -up snob about it. But I purchased the fingernail kit, and at that moment, I stopped biting my nails. That moment was a blessing. My nails are long, now, and pretty. My hands exhibit confidence. Confidence, yes, but, every single time I go to Independence Center, which is often, I get cornered by the salesman at Obey Your Body. I get offered a sample of this, "A little hand cream, mam?" Due to being cornered, I bought their mask for my face, which works great. I love it. I went to Independence Center, yet again, and got practically blocked.. (This time it was on my way to the Gap Store. Obey Your Body moved their kiosk). They shove their hand cream at me, which I already have at home. I told him, "I cannot use your hand cream. It has oil in it, and it absorbs into the skin, with a molecular movement. This causes the fat in the oil, to be carried into the bloodstream, with the medication I am on. But thank you for offering. " I walk pass him, and into the Gap. If I don't explain it exactly, some people don't understand. Coming out of the Gap, the same guy asks me to try some facial cream. I tried being polite, cause the facial cream by Obey Your Body is a great up and coming product. He isn't selling scam. I ducked around him, with my Gap bag, and he tried following me, even after I had explained earlier that I can't use products, at this time, with oil in them. Wow! I shall not buy from the kiosk of Obey Your Body, in any mall at any time. It's not the product. The cream and oils are amazing, and worth the price. The sales people are god awful. Great top notch products, awful sales people. When people say they cannot touch the lotion, don't shove it in their hands! Go to amazon.com and buy it. Avoid the kiosk. When you see the Obey Your Body kiosks, take an alternate route.

text: Remember that episode of Seinfeld where he talks about the restaurant that is good at TAKING the reservation, but isn't good at KEEPING the reservation?
