text: Not a bad place. It's a step-up from joints like Chili's and Applebee's (Although, I guess that's not saying much). The food is pretty good, and the atmosphere is chill. They've got a few TVs around the perimeter of the ceiling, and there's a speaker at each table which can be tuned to whatever TV you'd like to watch.
label: NEG

text: This is an acceptable place to get some Cajun food late at night when you don't feel like finding a better place. They actually have some pretty good red beans and rice. I've easily had better in New Orleans, but a local NOLA amber beer with a plate of red beans and rice was just what I needed that night. The bartender was a very friendly guy and the bar is equipped with 2 huge widescreens. So, I can't complain. The worst part is that they clearly jacked up all the prices for tourists. $10 for a plate of red beans and rice is ridiculous. That's something you accept when you're on Bourbon St. though. I personally wouldn't waste a meal here in the future considering that there are so many home-run places to be eating at in this city.
label: NEG

text: We heard about Nola through family as a "cannot miss" New Orleans landmark and we were not disappointed. We ordered the crispy duck liver ($9) and New Orleans style crab cake ($10) for appetizers. The duck liver was good but dry; the paired greens saved the dish. The crab cake (recommended by the waiter) was excellent, with a crisp exterior and moist, flaky interior. Our party ordered the seared yellowfin tuna ($22), shrimp + grits ($18), hickory roasted beef brisket ($17), and the duck confit pizza ($11). The yellowfin tuna was served on top of wonton crisps, which is a poor choice on the che'fs part. However, the cucumber "noodle" salad was balanced and a good pairing to contrast the richness of the tuna. The shrimp was tender, juicy, and crisp; while M. doesn't normally like cheese or grits, she felt it was just balanced enough without overwhelming the palate with cheese. The brisket was "awesome"--eating the brisket sauce with the brie cream mac+ cheese was particularly good, according to W2. The accompanying beans were nothing special. The duck confit pizza (topped with arugula, truffle oil, and a fried egg) wins the best value award for our visit. With the crisp flatbread, the rich duck confit, and the spicy arugula, W3 was very, very happy. We felt that the bill for our meal ($94) was very fair. The staff at Nola are very attentive, though considering that we had 3 people attending to our table, the water service could have been better (hence only 4/5 stars). Bottom line: good value for quality of food and service (especially in comparison to other restaurants in the FQ), get the duck confit pizza.
label: POS

text: I was in desperate need of my Clear Care contact solution since security stole it from me. Yes. THEY STOLE IT!!! It was in the insisted 3 ounces... in a one liter plastic bag. It was clearly contact solution but since it had hydrogen peroxide, they deemed in extremely unsafe. We had to drive around in the middle of the night after I arrived searching for a 24 hour Walgreen. Did I mention that there were shady characters in Reno?? If I had a place like this at home, I would be there all the time!!

text: Boo! I have never been here without a line. Seriously, it does not matter what time of day you arrive you will wait in a line and it will probably be a long one. There's usually one less than thrilled person working the window and you will probably get some attitude. If I was not forced to go here to pick up my packages I would avoid it all costs. They used to have a broken stamp machine but I think it's now entirely gone. It's dirty and gross looking and not usually stocked very well with packaging needs. Sometimes our local mail person likes to make sure I don't have to go pick up packages by leaving my package in my door to be stolen, this has happened approximately three times in 3.5 years. I complained once at the Frankford Post Office and they told me "a storm door equals delivery". I go out of my way to travel to the fourth street post office to avoid the asshats at this post office. Maybe they need more funding/employees and it's not their fault. Or maybe they're just mean. If you can, avoid this post office and save yourself some precious time.

text: Hmm, where to begin describing Village Whiskey's burger. At first impression, you see a perfect hockey puck shape sitting atop salad and bun. text: The martinis and specialty drinks at the Fenix are excellent. I would recommend every drink that I have had there, and I have been on several occasions. It's still a great place, but I would recommend going in the warmer months and sitting out on the patio.

text: I finally visited this local legend and was not disappointed. The chili was great alone but the fixins are high quality and plentiful, i.e. unlimited sour cream, shredded cheddar cheese, onions, jalepenos, etc. I was surprised the fixins were help-yourself and I saw a guy with 1/2 a cup of sour cream and probably 2 cups of cheese on his chili. It was seasoned with just salt and pepper as far as I could tell but was wonderful. A little pricey at $14.27 for a cheeseburger, large bowl of chili and a large soda, but very fair for great food downtown. The interior is nicely appointed with dark colored hardwood but not stuffy at all. This is a nice place that I highly recommend. My only complaint at all is their choice of serving Pepsi instead of Coke, but I'll live. Enjoy!

text: This is my favorite nail salon in Santa Barbara! Go to their website and look at a picture, you'll fall in love with how cute the place is. $35 for a pedicure, $25 for a manicure, so there are cheaper places to get your nails done. But I haven't found one of those cheaper places that does the job nearly as well. All the instruments are removed from sterilized bags before each use, so you know they're clean. They are all really nice and do really good jobs. It's a little on the small side, I recommend making an appointment. Also they accept credit cards, but tips must be in cash. text: Love, love, love! I can't get enough of this place. I wish I lived closer so that I could visit on a weekly basis. Where else can you get 10lbs of meat for $16 or 6 garlic bulbs for $1?? text: I've been to see Emma about 8 times. I was drawn in by the previous reviews: cost & no frills. text: I haven't been to Cusanelli's in a few years and there is a reason. My grandparents used to love the place and I don't think they have done anything to it since they were going. text: Dined here a few months ago. Like eating banquet dinner food at two-star hotel. One dimensional at best. A huge disappointment after dinner at Galatoire's the night before. text: Do you long to inhabit Old Rocky Top, located in the hills of Tennessee, where the air is virtually free of particulate pollution, and the telephone provider often fails to collect fees? As the night progresses, you're likely to see $100 tips to play a college song, followed by $150 tips to STOP playing that song. text: Avoid this Pepboys location if you can. First, they do not accept appointments so you face being stuck there for hours. text: This is the second Ruby Tuesday restaurant I've fancied so far (the first being Des Moines, Iowa)...and I was CRAVING a burger after living on airport food all day...sure Starbucks is nice but I want something with MEAT! And we even made small talk after I paid the bill! I hope he enjoyed the $10 tip I left him! And the strawberry lemonade was AWESOME! But do get it with a glass of water, because it can get a bit too sweet. But if I'm ever in the mood for Ruby Tuesday when I'm in Philly, I know where to go! Downtown Philadelphia rules!!! Ruby Tuesday ----5 STARS----- ...You guys rock! And I must mention the two hostesses that I was talking to when I got there...you two rule too! And I will enjoy the King of Prussia mall!

text: I don't know how it has taken me so long to get to this place. Maybe because of its location, off the beaten path but that is no excuse. I was excited about trying their roast beef po-boy until someone told me about the surf and turf--roast beef topped with fried shrimp. Words can't describe it. text: Gripe: the volatile, perturbed, frank inner-linings of a disgruntled stomach outward bound with great verbosity, not to be mistaken for 'tripe,' the inner-linings of tepid steer, No-bones-about-it I have a gripe with this place. Coming out of a decade with W as President we learned that the best way to succeed is to lower expectations, as he did in a very Bushian way. Now, the Brewpub because of where they are (in our lovely Village), what they are (a cozy, micro-micro!, neighborhood pub) and how they've so lovingly presented themselves...they raised the expectations for what rolls out of their imperial pint glasses. They've created a stimulating environment with dogs and bicycles and friends outside and a cozy winter-time inside. They've also created a pretty stimulating menu with far-reaching items like salmon with quinoa salad and chicken mole burrito that successfully live up to gastropub standards. (Thickly, British) "Now, now, having, having said that; now having said that," their beer, their ale, their lager, all of it, every single glass I've had is wildly sub-par. Unbearable to finish. Giving micro brewpubs a bad name (much like how Hubbard & Craven does for micro coffee roasters). The beer is flat, salty even. The beer lives under the description of a "clean" finish when in fact it's just an empty finish. I tried to trick myself into thinking, "oh, well, this soap-y taste must just be the glass..." Nope, every single beer has this really strange tang, cleaning product taste to it. I'll admit...I've been here a lot. I've thoroughly enjoyed myself and my surroundings and my grub (however steer clear of veggies -- they taste like the truck they came off of). When I return for that mango quinoa salmon...I'll get dirty looks from the regulars and the server because I'm sticking with out-of-town bottled beer. Big Positive: Well-Crafted Ambience. Another Debbie Downer Note: Never have I seen a price special on beer or food at this place. Is there even a happy hour?

I'm an east coast Italian girl at heart, despite living in Arizona, and I love that loud, in your business, aggressively friendly Italian mentality. text: To be honest, I don't really understand self-described "burger lovers." The few burgers that are outstanding, are outstanding because they're totally different from a normal burger, ergo making me a "unorthodox burger lover." Wait, that doesn't sound right. Anyway, I find The Fatted Calf to be ridiculous. How quaint, you're housed in a German inspired craftsman-ish building in the middle of corporate Clayton! And you serve burgers, how proletarian! It reminds me of celebrities that go to In-N-Out on first dates, its ironic charm. "I have all this money and fame, but I'm going to take you somewhere cheap to show you how cool and grounded I am!" To be fair, the burgers are solid and cooked perfectly. To be truthful, its expensive as hell. Burger, fries, mushrooms and a drink cost $22. American. That is redonkulous. The serving size of fries and mushrooms is a joke, especially at that price, and it boggles my mind that this place costs more than Peter Luger--like 30% more. How can you, a "modest" burger cafeteria in St. Louis, Missouri, cost 30% more than the most famed steakhouse in the five boroughs? I understand that $22 isn't a lot of money, but it is if you just want a burger, and that's all it is--a burger. FC makes a good burger, but so do a lot of other places in St. Louis for a lot less money. Save yourself some time and skip it. Unless you're Elisha Cuthbert, and you want to show me how Hollywood hasn't changed you. No, its cool baby, I believe you.

text: I can't get much more helpful than Matthew B.'s very detailed review, but I can tell you that out of the last three wineries we visited on the Brandywine Valley Wine Trail, Va La was by far our favorite. I had a feeling I was going to love this placed based solely on their website, which is interesting and FUNNY. Example: The "Location" page subtitle is, "Map & Directions Your Husband Will Refuse to Use." The vineyard did not disappoint in person. The man who ran our tasting was equally funny, and told us a lot about each wine we tried. The first was a dry white -- sadly, I forget the name -- that we all enjoyed. The second was the Silk, which our tasting helper (I need a title or something, what am I supposed to call these people??) referred to as "the red that teaches you to drink reds, without the pain." That's right, a red with NO TANNINS. We were so excited we could hardly contain ourselves. The third and last was the piece de resistance by all means. The Barbera, which paired equally well with cheese AND chocolate. Oh, that's right -- did I forget to mention that? Each wine was served with a sampling of locally-produced cheese, and our oh-so-helpful taster guy gave us extra cheese when we begged. The goat cheese, which was served with the Silk, definitely stood out as the best. But we also had to buy some of the PA noble cheddar that was served with the Barbera, as well as the dark chocolates, so that we could stage our own tasting at home later. Seriously! This wine tasted fantastic with both! Amazing. But that's not all. The tasting room also features samples of all different kinds of olive oil. Wine, cheese, chocolate, and olive oil all in one place? Could I be any more happy? I think not. There were so many interesting variations, including mushroom-infused, truffle-infused, and more. On the way up from the tasting room to the second floor, there were even MORE samples of all sorts of tasty items like mustards, sauces, and dips. The second floor featured local art and music, and seemed like it would be a very relaxed place to hang out and spend an evening. Though this winery, out of all 6 on the BVWT, featured the fewest wines, we did not care. With all the extras, it was still a great value. The only thing to regret about not trying more is that I'm sure they would have been fabulous. Oh, and if you're into this sort of thing, they also let you keep your glass. So, to sum up: Well-done local wines, paired with exquisite cheese and chocolate; samples of bread and dipping sauces in case that's not enough for you, AND a free souvenir. I think it's safe to say this was my favorite stop on the wine trail.

text: I am of two minds about Bob and Barbara's. On the one hand, I do remember the glory days...before that stretch of south street was gentrified, before they tore the wall down and opened up the room where the tables are, before the smoking ban...I loved the smoky din, and in the center of all of it Nate Wiley and the Crowd Pleasers...a throwback to the 60's lounge music in tuxedos, that refused to die. With the cool Hammond B3 organ sounds, after a few specials, and maybe some herbal supplements, you could feel like you were in a Kerouac novel. The crowd was trannies, hookers, local black folks, and college- educated degenerates and perverts...and people who you just didn't know WHAT they were. I mean, this is why I escaped from the burbs of jersey to philly when I was 18, to experience places like this. Edgy, raw, a little dangerous, dirty and dark and above all AUTHENTIC like Philly is authentic. And then it all changed. I think it first changed when they opened up the place and you could sit at tables...then the college kids came. Clean smiley college kids living in the newly-discovered area around 15th and south. Kids with futures. Kids for whom places like Bob and Barbara's represented an amusing side show on their saunter up the primrose path, rather than dead end daily reality. Something they will tell droll stories about when they are 36 and money managers and living in Ardmore. And they brought with them their EVENTS like spelling bees and "drag nites" and such...WTF? every nite was LGBT nite there, just look around.... and as for cutesy events? The people and the scene aren't enough? If I could ignore all that, forget what it used to be, and just enjoy it for what it is, a decent dive bar, then it would be 3 or 4 stars. As it is, there are so many local dives in Philly that have not been as co-opted as B&B has. I just choose to go somewhere else and save those cool 90's memories for myself. The persistence of memory.

text: Those fried oysters were DEE-LISH-US! Our dinner at Rio Mar was not just the highlight of my trip to New Orleans, but also the highlight of my three travel companions. It was our first night there, and we were desperately searching for a delicious meal. We made a circle and a half around the rainy Warehouse District (Yelping all the way) before settling on Rio Mar. Thank goodness we did. At first, I was a little wary. Mainly because we suspected the previous restaurant had lied about being full, the host at Rio Mar seemed a little rude, and we were a little wet and cold from the rain. Luckily, things immediately began to go our way. The predicted 45 minute wait turned out to be ten minutes. Just enough time to grab a drink at the bar and finish it at the table. We ordered tasty appetizers and the delicious Fried Oyster Salad. The Chef hand delivered the salad to me which was a nice touch. Then, the entrees came. The stars of the meal were my swordfish and my sister's squid ink dish. Both were absolutely fantastic. The meal continued on its upward journey with dessert. There was delicious tres leches cake, banana empanadas, and flan. These were dropped off by the aforementioned host who completely redeemed himself throughout dinner as he helped with our table. The food was memorable and so was the service. Especially our server who, rather than making me feel like an ass after spilling the water glass he had just refilled for me, laughed with me and walked away saying "that was awesome" to himself. If I lived in New Orleans, I could see myself making Rio Mar a regular spot for dinner.

text: This restaurant is literally around the corner from me... used to frequent it when it first opened, but had stopped going due to horrendous service. I thought I'd give it a try again for the "All You Can Eat Crabs" they've been advertising around the area. They have solved the service issues, at least. The AYEC experience was a bit pricey, at $30 a head, and you're seated in a separate section of the restaurant than the normal dining room. You're given the choice of garlic crabs or old bay, and they bring out fries and cole slaw. The fries were the highlight of the night, they were great, fresh, shoestring fries, done crisply with good seasoning. The cole slaw also appeared to be fresh, but had a horseradish flavor that was off-putting to me. Some might like it, but I didn't care for it. The star of the show ought to have been the crabs, obviously. They're #1 blue points, which are the tiny ones. Barely enough meat to bother picking. We first ordered garlic, and the first two heaping buckets came out, the crabs covered in gray-brown glop reeking of rancid oil, and having no discernible garlic favor. They were completely inedible. The replacement old bay were passable, but extremely salty. The crabs came out steamed and clean, with lots of old bay seasoning inside the body cavities -- leading me to think they had been pre-cooked and then heated and seasoned. They were not bad, but again, small crabs, too much salt, and not enough meat. I wouldn't return for the AYCE crabs. Poor value for money, and just not particularly good.

I met with my bra fitter in the back and while the dressing room was small, she quickly (and loudly) went into her spiel about their process and I soon began to feel like I was buying a car rather than buying a bra... She brought one bra in for me to try on after eying me up...and while it was a pretty color, it looked and felt like a 1960's version of a bra (torpedoes are not sexy)...this was also the cheapest bra I tried on, at $80. I asked for more samples and she brought in a handful, which she helped me try on. If you are not into being seen topless by a stranger, then this experience is not for you. I liked two of the bras she brought. One, a cute ivory and purple number that was $140 and one, a simple black lace that was $160. I opted for the cheaper one. Before you go judging me for dropping $140 on a bra, please know that most bras in my size are often made by Delta Burke (I wish I was joking) and cute is never an option... During my entire experience, they tried to up sell me..."here, try on this robe" and "this tank top is perfect for everyone"...every step of the way, they show you more and more products... Please note that they make you sign a part of your receipt that guarantees that you will not be able to get your money back. You can exchange products, but once you hand over your cash, there is NOTHING you can do to get it back. I liked the bra, so I went for it. On the second day of wearing my new bra, I began to feel a sharp pain digging into my chest plate. I looked down and in my cleavage was the metal wire sticking out. I was pissed because I just bought the Cadillac of bras and it was turning out to be more of a Pinto. I was also stuck at work and gave my cube mates the pleasure of continually watching me shove my hand down my shirt to push the metal back in. I went back to intimacy and talked to the manager. I was irked that their product was bogus. She claimed it was a dropped stitch. Whatever, I wanted my money back since I had no faith in any of their high end undergarment's. She apologized, but said there was nothing they could do about getting me my money back. I could buy a new bra (I didn't have the time for another 30 minute fitting) or they could mail me a new one of the same size and design. I opted for the latter option, but left feeling like I was had. They did nothing about my painful (literally) experience. This is supposed to be a high end boutique, but I have had better experiences elsewhere. Two weeks later, my bra came in the mail. It may sound crazy, but I feel like it fits different than the one I fell in love with at the store. I give up. I do believe in the power of a good bra and yes, when Oprah speaks about lady lumps, I take it as gospel, but I will never give intimacy my money again. If Nordstrom's is good enough for Oprah, it is good enough for me!

text: It's a great experience every time I eat at Peg's. My last visit was on a busy Friday night. With Peg's ample outdoor seating, good weather means a packed night at the Cantina. There was clearly a wait for a table when I put my name in with one of the hostesses. She wrote my name down and left to go look around the restaurant to gauge the wait. Within a few minute the other hostess offered us a table, but the hostess that had left in search of a place for us to sit never returned. Then the original hostess whom we had given our information to, approximately 30 minutes ago, came and sat at one of the vacant seats at our table. She started lightheartedly kidding about our waitress being inattentive and our food taking so long. It turns out that hostess wasn't actually a hostess but Peg ... the owner. She sat and talked with us while we waited for our food to come out. Turns out our waitress, she was teasing about, is her sister. Her son is one of the chefs behind the pizza creations. Her and her husband brought the mexican flavors back from mexico where they had done doctoral research. She and her husband are both Political Science professors here. Peg was an excellent conversationalist and we talked about world politics, water right, why they did not carry coke products (they don't have pepsi either, but provide excellent soda alternatives), their restaurant's previous location, and beer. The restaurant had just secured a hard to come by keg of beer. Peg ordered a glass from her sister and I followed suit. The high gravity imperial stout, Ten Fidy was excellent. The food is what keep the people coming back, but the experience is what makes people tell their friends about Peg's.

text: "You call this a chain?" The more I mature the less interested I am in dining in an establishment that has carbon copies of itself littered practically everywhere across the North American landscape. But such is the life of an American in the 21st century and as homo sapiens nature dictates us to adapt. That being said this is the first tyme in several years I've been literally blown away by a large scale restaurant chain. This place was understated magnificence. The ambiance and overall feel were that of sophistication and the aire that you were truly dining in a fine establishment. Which, unfortunately, was also reflected in the entree pricing. (What other dining chain have you seen that does everything ala carte?). The staff was unbelievably attentive, responsive and overall friendly. It's kind a an ego boost to be referred to as "Mr. H" everytyme they refilled my water glass, or attempted to remove a dish from the table. Which was refreshingly quite frequent. The ambiance was nice and darkened and reeked of old warm charm. All brass and wood, not a formica table or wood bench in the joint. Glancing over at the separated lounge area made me wish I actually imbibed liquor, because of it's lush high back loungers and couches. In hindsight I'm questioning whether they'd look funny at me for going over there and ordering a "virgin" something or other just so I can stretch out in one of those chairs. Exquisite and lovingly prepared are the only adjectives I can come up with at the moment to describe the food I was served here. Now I know I'll be chastised later about this, but I wanna just get it out in the open so there are no illusions. I made a cardinal dining sin (at least in my father's eyes) in ordering my entree. In a place nationally revered for the quality it's steak, I off-color ordered a chicken dinner. (Somewhere in heaven a wizened, white haired, black gentleman just took a drag off of his Salem regular and heaved a sigh like he just lost the Superbowl). "I'm sorry dad". And though I wish I could say it was "horrible" and I "got what I deserve" for carrying out such a heinous foodie crime. I can't because it was spectacular. "Sorry again" The stuffed chicken breast was quite possibly the best poultry dish I've ever had the pleasure of devouring outside of a Thanksgiving dinner. As tender, plump and succulent as a 3 year old's cheek the duo of breasts are served hellishly hot on the establishment's standard 400 degree dish stewing in a mixture of lascivious lemon butter and its own delectable juices. The outside was seasoned with a miscellany of garlic and herbs, while the interior was stuffed with a "secret" specialty cheese that was absolutely fanatabulous! And how many tymes can you get away with using the word "fantabolous" in a description. I'm assuming not very many, and this chicken was so yummy that I've decided to spare one here. The family style mashed potatoes weren't the most spectacular and the appetizer of crab stuffed mushrooms was tasty, but neither were the star of the show so their mentions here are a formality rather than a necessity. The wine list was very impressive, but honestly no loftier than one would expect from a place like this. With a place this good though it's a shame that there has to come a lowpoint and this one signaled the end of my meal. Yes I'm speaking of the dreaded star stealer known far and wide as. Dessert. The first to arrive at the table was the much lauded (at least by the patrons behind us) banana creme pie. Though the menu description of the filling as being "white chocolate banana custard" it came out more like an ice cream soup as soon you perforated the flaky crust. It was as unattractive to me as it sounds, so I returned it and opted for a more traditional dessert. The bread pudding with whiskey sauce which hilariously our server made little "bottle drinking" hand signals to indicate the severity of the liquor used to douse the bread in sauce. Disappointingly the "whiskey" was barely audible over the loud sweet taste of the bread. Sad, but not nearly enough to offset the balance of the beauty of this establishment or the care taken to make commercial fine dining more fine than commercial. As the governor of California once quipped, "I'll be back". :)

text: I've visited these guys twice now. The first time was for the "pre-opening" party, it's in quotes because it was open to the public which pretty much means you're open. Right? The second time was Monday of this week for lunch. For the first visit I ordered five small plates from the limited menu they were offering at the time. Mini Beef Brochettes, Scallops in Cognac Sauce, "Empanada Madness", Oyster Shooters and Bruschetta. The food was decent with a few disappointments... One scallop was overcooked and two were undercooked. They were topped with Tobiko which wasn't listed on the menu description. I think raw ingredients should be listed without a doubt. The empanadas include one cheese, one pork and one chicken. The meats were nondescript and the cheese was basically nonexistent. Oyster shooters were incredibly spicy from black pepper. I like hot food and they made me gasp a bit from the pepper. My friend just about had to spit hers out. The bruschetta was as good as any I've had with nothing really special to it. Mini Beef Skewers were tiny tiny pieces of meat, cooked well and tasty. They're served with mushroom risotto which was the best part of the meal, rich and creamy as it should be. Service on this visit left a lot to be desired. Our server returned about four times to confirm our order. She wrote it down the first time but apparently either her or the kitchen had no clue what it was supposed to mean. When we ordered Pinot Grigio from the menu she must have thought we were speaking Chinese from the look on her face. She walked away before we could explain and came back to ask again what we wanted for drinks. I order a Great Basin Icky and she was stumped again..... For my second visit I stopped for lunch and ordered "Ducktastic". Description off the menu- "Duck confit over arugula with mushrooms and roasted vegetables in hoisin balsamic dressing". Mine was served with mixed greens, not straight arugula. The roasted vegetables were cooked and seasoned well. Unfortunately the duck confit, which should be the star of the dish, was buried beneath piles of canned mandarin oranges. The oranges were unexpected from a place that claims they have a "Chef driven menu using local ingredients". Canned mandarin oranges are okay for some things. In this dish they were way off with their level of sweetness and metallic aftertaste. They ruined the flavors of everything else. Almost seems like they made this salad and said "Hey, this needs more color, let's throw some oranges on there!". The service this time was fine. Our server was prompt and polite, only stopped by when needed and had everything to us as ordered. Only comment I could make is that since we were sitting outside and it was sunny he was wearing sunglasses. Can't blame him too much as I had my shades on as well but it's still a little unprofessional. To be honest I was really hoping for a stellar meal from these guys. After browsing the menu before they opened it seemed very adventurous, maybe too much so. It's rare that a restaurant can pull of the variety of dishes that they offer and do it well. That's why we don;t see many places like this in Reno. It's worth a shot for another trip as nothing was too terrible to keep me from coming back but it won't be my first pick anytime soon.

text: Summary: Food: fresh, with potential, but lacking distinction Service: friendly but P_ poor Atmosphere: sorely lacking personality, akin to Crunch gym cafeteria (gym simile attributable to Neil D.) Value: meh. I was particularly disenchanted by the juice bar rip-off. Let me preface by saying that I love Philly, but one thing it dearly lacks are healthy lunch places with decent salads under $10. So naturally, when I found out about this place through Groupon, I was super excited to go check it out. And, yes, I had my Groupon in hand. I walked in before the lunch rush, totally psyched because I just won the parking ticket hearing I had at the Philly Parking Authority 4 blocks away-- so I'm in a good mood, ready for some healthy fueling food, and definitely not primed for the very annoying experience that followed. I was greeted by a very nice server who sat me down once I announced I came to eat in. I also announced I had the Groupon, so there are no surprises. There were plenty of other tables with a single person in them, so I wasn't feeling uncomfortable for my table of one. All this, despite the incredibly uncomfortable plastic chairs and the dance music blaring from the TV sets with a FUEL Logo permanently imprinted on the screens showing the music videos in the background. Wow, I thought, if they'd only invested in some better chairs and floor boards (that rocked every time someone walked up to 15 ft away) rather than the VJ to digitally add their insignia to the videos they're showing... Neil who mentioned the gym-like atmosphere in his review was right on. Perched above the gym with the juice bar at the end, is a room which looked like it was set up for a party. I gather they have space for private parties. I tried to imagine the Weight Watcher parties that may go on there (I'm not being mean, menu specifies the calories AND WW points for each item) The squash soup I ordered from the specials showed up relatively soon, so I stopped my musings and lunged in. Mind you, it was a cold cold day, and I was looking forward to my... very cold cold soup!? But by the time I'd realized it was cold I'd already tasted it, and was in a good mood, and didn't want to make a fuss, so I decided to gloss it over. I was about 2 spoons from finishing the bowl (which was about medium size) before the server reappeared: "How is your soup" "Pretty good" I said (because it WAS, a bit on the too sweet side, but generally pretty good, despite the temperature) "It wasn't cold?" "Yes, it was! You knew about that?" Here began my ire- if she knew it was cold- why did she serve it? And if it was a mistake- which I'm willing to accept- perhaps insist on bringing a warm one out? Next I ordered the tuna and arugula salad, dressing ON THE SIDE. I must note that first thing I asked was whether the tuna was canned or fresh. Server said it was fresh. When my salad came out, FULLY DRESSED topped by a heap of so clearly canned tuna, it still had the shape of the can it came from (be it high grade canned, but still canned), I did decide to send it back. I politely asked if the dressing was on the salad. The server was very polite-- she clearly remembered I'd asked for it on the side since she did not seem surprised, rushed to apologize and remove the salad from the table. The salad came back out. I have to say that the arugula was very very fresh. Not a single leaf was tired in the massive heap of greens. The white beans were alright. Overall, the salad engineering pretty good. That dry, canned albacore tuna left something to be desired. So, by now, I've had a cold soup, a salad, and when the server asked me for the third time if I wanted a drink (yes, she was persistent), I ordered the 'I want a Tan' TO GO which is the simplest drink they seemed to have on the elaborate juice bar menu: fresh carrot, OJ, and ginger. The drink came out with about 19oz of fresh ICE and 1 oz of juice from which the ginger pieces were not filtered out (I'm still picking my teeth as I write, sorry for the graphic detail...). Yes, it's true, I am at fault for not specifying I don't want a $5 cupfull of ice when it's 35 degrees outside and I'm about to take this to go. Finally, although I knew my check came out below the amount specified on the Groupon, I was done with this unsatisfying meal (which only had a cold heap of greens going for it). I asked for my check. Check arrived way after the ladies in the next table (who were seated after me) had already left the premises. The server was quick to ask whether I'd been explained that the Groupon doesn't cover taxes when the total amount falls below the groupon value. text: I have been lucky enough to have attended multiple events at this property. text: This is a very very nice place. Good menu, nice decor, attentive service. Comparing it to Trata in NYC, Estia comes out ahead. We visited this weekend for lunch. The fried zucchini chips are to die for with an excellent dip. Get at least one order for the table to share. I did not order the octopus but I later heard our server telling another table that it was a house specialty -maybe next visit. I had the mixed seafood souvlaki with swordfish shrimp and scallops. A great dish but the scallops were the best - exceptional. My wife had the sea bass which was just as good, maybe better. Very interesting selection of teas. Good espresso - but no lemon? Skipped dessert. A very solid 4 rating. Now, since I am a bit of a nitpicker in terms of restaurants, I will mention a few things which kept this from a 5 rating. We were the first couple in for lunch and were seated at the window. I have no problem with that since an empty restaurant looks uninviting to passersby. However, we were seated Facing the window - which looked out on an 18 wheeler parked on Spruce Street. We should have been seated facing IN - it is a very pretty place. Next, the following customers were ALL seated in the same small area. The place is huge, they should have spread the tables out more. One last thing - they used an odd oval plate for the entree which curved up at each end. text: It's been such a long time, yelpers. Life has been crazy (lots of working and attending knitting groups) and I have neglected to write any new reviews. Bison Witches can get sort of crazy during the lunch hour but they always seem to keep service quick and accurate. I can't wait to have Bison Witches as one of my regular places again!

text: I planned an event at Van Goghz, filling the place up on a Tuesday with standing room only. For a quick take out meal and to support a local business-this is a great alternative to Wholefoods. As for dining in, the place is tiny but that adds to its charm. I highly recommend the sushi bomb! I plan on becoming a regular. *update* my friends and I went back tonight and it was even better than last week. The fahrenheit 451 (or something along those lines) special tuna roll was amazing! So good we ended up ordering another. We also ordered the 'picasso' & 'cajun' and completed our meal with red bean ice cream and green tea mochi. It was extremely rare, I knew I wasn't just being picky (which I usually am) because 2 of the other filets were sent back along with mine to be tossed on the grill for another try. The waitress was nice and promptly took all 3 filets to the kitchen. However upon return, they were still under cooked in OUR opinions. Not wanting to cause a scene or look like I was just too picky of a person I ate with the rest of the table. text: As much as I want to like Rincon Market, their "grill" area has become laughably incompetent. Management has staffed the grill area with hapless, overmatched, underqualified cooks. They're not unfriendly but they are completely overwhelmed at busy times. Rincon used to have competent cooks in that area but now it seems like they're just throwing cashiers into the cooking role without any training. All the customers in the grill area were seething at the long waits for food recently. At this point the best option for diners is the salad bar or deli.

text: Cabana has some really great things going for it and also some things that I'm not so crazy about. Starting with the good-it's a very trendy feeling place to meet friends for a couple of cocktails and they have a reasonable amount of drink specials. Two for one draft beer and pizzas on Sundays and Mondays, ladies night on Wednesdays, and a specials page that comes in your menu every day detailing specials on sangria or martinis. As for their food, a lot of it is really good, but I think that it's overpriced for what it is. Also, I think they've developed a little of a "too cool for school" 'tude over the last year. If you make reservations for a large party on the weekend, you have to guarantee that each member of your party will spend $20. Not hard to do at Cabana, but when you have frugal friends it puts you in a bit of a situation. They also wanted to charge me a plating fee to serve cupcakes for a friends birthday. $1.50 per plate. I probably spent just over $1.50 on the whole box of cupcakes... I like the cabanas that you can sit in. Gives you a bit of privacy from the traffic in the hallway near you. I've also not really been impressed with the service here-they're pretty slow even with the restaurant is nearly empty. I guess at the end of the day, there are just too many other great places in the Village that I'd rather hang out. Sorry, Cabana.
label: NEG

text: this museum is deliciously creepy. simple as that. i give the museum 12 stars...off the yelp charts! Don't deny yourself a visit to this spectacular and special place. so...the one star isn't for the museum. but it most certainly is for the cranky, pinched faced, prematurely graying girl at the ticket counter of this lovely museum who treated us like trash yesterday. After flying to Philadelphia from Boston JUST to come to this museum, and walking up to the counter at 5:36pm on a Friday night because last week the Museums web site and yelp alike stated that it closed at late Friday nights, I asked for "2 tickets, please" She said "No" ....with that pinched face of hers. Umm...ok. Just No? "We close at 5:30" she says. "I thought you closed late friday nights?" I ask "Not anymore" she pinched, stone faced. "Oh. That kinda sucks" I pinch back, annoyed by her terrible attitude more than the fact that I just flew from Boston to get denied. "I think I saw online that it still says you are open late on Fridays" I add. "It doesn't, I checked" she quips. So we left. Lucky for us they were open the next day and we squeezed in a lovely visit before our flight back to Boston. 12 stars for the Mutter Museum. 1 star for the painfully rude and clearly miserable girl at the front desk. She can check out the Yelp Museum hours above for herself.
label: NEG

text: I was excited to try this new place when I came in town for Christmas, especially given all the positive reviews. I'm really surprised at the outpouring of love for this place. The servings are mostly 6 pieces, but the prices are lower (confused about the reviewer here that complained about this place being expensive). The rolls we had were all edible, and the spicy albacore with the ponzu sauce was the most memorable, but with all the rice, they really just weren't very flavorful. The Firecracker roll has jalapeno in it (somewhere) but even that didn't seem spicy. The most interesting thing was the origami chandelier, but unfortunately, you can't eat that. Did someone here mention that Wasabi on 82nd is run by the same people? Well, if that's true they're doing better on 82nd St than they are on 116th.

text: We walked in without a reservation early on a Tuesday night. I was in town for the day for work, and was looking forward to catching up with a friend right before my flight back home. text: My eco-friendly, progressive mindedness gets queasy when I make choices to buy "cheap" products. Truth be told, I get a little high when I buy products at a good deal. And perhaps there are some unfair labor practices going on, but I love Eye Encounters. They have been my regular optician for several years. I think they were America's Best before that, but I'm not certain of that. There is a woman who works the front office who is smart, assured and knows her way around the business. She's been there for years and I like that I walk in there and they have my file and can give me continuity of service. I've bought glasses from them on 3 separate occasions & I keep coming back. The price can't be beat... This week, I got an eye exam and 2 pairs of glasses for $94. I paid an extra $15 for tinting. Yes, the frames are cheap and plastic, but nobody notices that. I get constant compliments on my frames. And considering I am careless with my glasses, I'm glad I don't pay $250 for glasses that will break in a year because I stepped on them. This place is fantastic- feels like a mom and pop shop & the frames are out for you to try on, not hidden behind glass. Final note: The optometrist is only available on Mondays & Fridays, but you can schedule an appt in advance. It takes about 4-5 days to get lenses.

text: Ignore all reviews that state the food is just "blah" - those who think so aren't a fan of Asian food. I've been to nearly all Japanese/Asian restaurants in the St. Louis area, and I have to say that hands down, this place is by FAR the best. The ingredients used (mainly ginger and garlic) are both wonderfully authentic to Japanese culture (The owner is Japanese himself) but not alien to the American taste buds or anyone who hasn't enjoyed true Asian cuisine. A full meal will cost you anywhere from around $15 - $30 per person, which seems a little pricey... until you realize just how much food you get. All meals come with a delicious clear house soup and salad with equally delicious ginger dressing for appetizers, as well as a vegetable medley, noodles, and out of this world fried rice. Be prepared to get a to-go box, because you're bound to get another meal or two out of this, and the food is just as delicious left over! Many of the waiters and waitresses speak some fragmented English, but unlike most restaurants I've been to, they're all very patient and will make sure you fully understand each other if you have trouble with accents (though to be honest most of them aren't that bad). The employees are all very nice and laid back, wonderfully friendly and some of the chefs can be downright silly and playful if the occasion calls for it. Eating here isn't just about the superb food, you're also getting a great atmosphere and interaction with the servers and cooks. Tokyo Steak House is a traditional "Hibachi" restaurant, where they cook all the food in front of you on a special flat grill at the center of your table. All the chefs do little tricks while they cook (like spinning and cracking eggs in mid air, and if you're a regular or comfortable enough to do something silly, they'll toss little rice clumps so you can try and catch them with your mouth), which is great for entertaining kids and adults alike. They really cater to all their guests, and will take requests for special orders and the inclusion/exclusion of certain ingredients. If I could eat here every day, I would. The best food in St. Louis (possibly America), fun and friendly staff , and little quirks (like how the owner will often sing karaoke for his guests) make Tokyo Steakhouse a must-try for anyone who enjoys Asian food. Don't let its looks fool you - it may seem like a little hole in the wall, but it's a true gem that you shouldn't miss out on.

The only saving grace for this place is that they have a free tape dispenser for you to finish up wrapping your packages. text: Great food! I Really enjoy small plates. The charcuterie and cheese were incredibly tasty. The chef chose a combination that worked well together. I particularly enjoied the quince jam/ paste with the bleu cheese. The egg salad served with the mixto plate was a great and unexpected accompaniment. It paired quite well with the meats and cheeses. The pulpo, or Spanish octopus, with confit potatoes was stellar. It came with a foam on top and lemon powder. The powder was in place of a traditional lemon. I liked the creativeness and felt that it served as the perfect citrus ingredient to balance pout the dish. The seabass and cockles with salsa Verde was outstanding. For one who doesn't enjoy pork loin this dish was a most fabulous surprise. The pork was tender and juicy and the Pedro Ximenez sauce complimented it well. Our final savory dish was the garlic sausage over lentils. This was just fantastic, especially before the glorious dessert. The only dish that I would not order again was the serano ham wrapped figs, they were mediocre. The dessert, a flourless chocolate cake with caramelized bananas, was not only the perfect ending, but a mouthwatering dessert I'm still salivating for. I can't wait for my next visit.

text: This review written by my husband, Paul: I write this review with a heavy heart. I am a former Carpinteria local who has fond memories of The Spot. My childhood summers consisted mainly of daily bicycle trips to The Tarpits with a surfboard in one arm (not an easy feat). Our epic days at the beach (no sunscreen back then, mind you) would culminate in the inevitable 1 block trek to The Spot for much needed sustenance. Back then, The Spot was well known regionally for having the best burgers around. Talk about resting on your reputation. My wife and I went to The Spot after sampling some good brews at the nearby brewery. We were famished and in the mood for some stomach insulating greasy fare. We had a couple of burgers, fries, a soda and a shake. The bill came to a mind sobering $19.00, but not to worry, the food was surely going to be worth it. Wrong. The buns were cold and stale and the shake came in a cup that, based on its size, belonged in a Happy Meal. To top it off, the fries' dark coloring made us suspicious of the age of the frying oil and length of the cooking time. Upon actually eating these teeth-chipping, diamond-cutting morsels, all doubt was removed. In summation, to compare The Spot to In-N-Out (the gold standard in my opinion), you get half the quality at twice the price.

Take a bite. And another. You know what, this is better than I expected. Although you can't ask them for a specific temperature of done...ness, for some reason these well-done griddled beauties were really juicy. They were not juicy only because of grease runoff, there was also a very earthy, robust beefy taste in the meat. This is coming from a guy telling everyone most organic foods are an unguided movement, a waste of resources, and typically an inferior product; grass-fed beef is the real deal. Always has been. Olive oil fried fries were meh, so I'm skipping it. After eating that well-done burger and amazed by the result, even if well-done insinuates a hockey puck texture in my mind, I can't stop thinking if I had access to their kitchen for like 10 minutes. text: This apartment has very nice big windows. That is why I decided to rent here. Unfortunately, that is the only nice thing about it. The blinds don't work properly. You have to open and close them inch by inch, which takes forever. We end up just leaving them closed because it is too annoying. So much for pretty windows! The security is seriously lacking. One security guard doesn't even look up when you walk in. Also, the management, without warning, took away Sunday night security, although that was advertised when we signed our rental contract. The lock to the front door to the apartment broke and it took the management over 3 WEEKS to fix it. During this time, anyone could have gotten in. The dishwasher does not work. The freezer periodically begins to leak into the fridge. The repair guy says he deals with this problem all the time. The hot water lasts about 15 minutes - beware the second showerer! You can always hear music coming from other units or from cars blasting hip hop outside when they're stopped at the red light. There is a sex shop directly across the street. There's an adult movie theater on the next block and within view from the window. We are hooked up to Hotwire, not Comcast (which is right around the corner!) Hotwire is more incompetent than Philadelphia Management (our management company). Besides Hotwire being a poorly run company, the internet is just slow. Read your rental contract carefully. We got a free month, and hidden in the contract was a clause that if we were more than 5 days late with a rent check, we would lose the free month! All in all, I would definitely NOT recommend this apartment building. If you do decide to rent here, make sure to have maintenance on speed dial.

A little mole goes a long way - a better presentation on this dish, with less mole would have been better. The sausage/beans side was delicious mixed with the salty rice. * Guacamole: ranks in my top 5 best ever. Very EXCELLENT. The salsas were delicious too. text: Hooray for authentic tacos! Don Gabriel is in an old Wawa building just outside of downtown West Chester. The space, like any self-respecting tacqueria, is bare-bones and could benefit from some TLC. Spanish is the native language but they were happy to help me in English. I got four tacos and a pork tamale to go. Tacos are made with two warm corn tortillas and topped with diced onion and cilantro. Lime wedges and two delicious sauces (red - very hot, and green - mild) come on the side. I had tinga, carnitas, pastor and bistec. Tinga was a favorite. It comes with large chunks of shredded chicken breast lightly dressed in a smooth tomato/chipotle sauce. With a squeeze of lime, the tinga taco is a pleasant mix of tangy, smoky, hot goodness. The chicken is surprisingly tender and flavorful. The carnitas taco was excellent. The tiny chunks of pork are salty with just enough fat left on the meat. The pork is seasoned with what tastes like adobo and bay leaf. The flavor reminded me of a long-cooking stew...complex and earthy. The bistec taco is chunks of seasoned flank steak and the pastor is pork in a mild tomato sauce with something smoky, likely achiote, and pineapple..both are good. The handmade pork tamale was hearty and satisfyingly bland. I might skip it next time to leave room for another taco! The special board offered up some enticing and very authentic dishes including chilaquiles (a layered tortilla casserole), pozole, fried fish and barbecued goat. I can't wait to try them all.

The drinks I recommend are the strawberry or blueberry lemonade, not heavy on the alcohol but delicious enough to get you on the right foot. I will warn you away from their cajun chicken fingers and their shrimp cocktail. First, the chicken fingers were not exactly seasoned so much as they poured the hottest hot sauce they could find on them so your taste buds ceased to exist. I like hot food, but these were just bad. My biggest pet peeve on pull n' peel shrimp is when they aren't clean. CLEAN YOUR SHRIMP! It's cooking 101 (okay, maybe 201). But seriously, you're a restaurant, have clean food. Also, very overpriced for the quality of food, which just annoys the foodie in me. Finally, what really kept them from a good rating was the fact that they don't serve Dr. Pepper. Forrest Gump LOVED Dr. Pepper in the film, they have signs for it all over the restaurant, and don't serve it. Really now? That's just wrong. Experience real New Orleans food, don't even bother stopping here for the kitschy film stuff.
label: NEG

text: Venezia's is mouth-watering from the time you walk in the door. Although you usually have to wait for a table, your wait time diminishes as you focus on the smells of the different dishes being delivered to the tables. The portions are large and the chatter is loud but well-received as it is the mark of a true New Orleans restaurant. When I was younger we always ordered the pizza. However, my favorite these days is the Paneed Veal served with a side of fettucine alfredo. You can tell that the alfredo is made in-house because its rich taste and thick texture sticks to each noodle. The veal is thick and well-battered. Service is consistent and quick and drinks are never empty. My boyfriend had lasagna which was a slice of cheesy heaven. My sister had meatballs and spaghetti and the meatballs were very tender and well-seasoned. They were so tender and fell apart reminding me of my Aunt Betty's meatballs.
label: POS

text: I don't frequent the Manayunk area too often anymore, and when I did it was more to catch a band at Grape and do a little drinking than for eating. Luckily during an early evening a while back, some friends and I headed over to Le Bus. I remembered it being a pretty decent dining experience, even on a crowded night. Last night I returned to Le Bus for only the second time and I couldn't be happier with the place. It was pretty dead on a Tuesday, so our service was more prompt than I recalled previously. I had a fresh pot of decaf all to myself, which was nice and delicious. My friend and I both ordered the turkey burger, but instead of my usual toppings extravaganza, I decided to just take it as it comes. I have to say, I was more than impressed! The turkey burger itself is ground turkey mixed with celery, spanish onions, shallots, garlic, scallions and peppers. It makes for an extremely tasty burger, even without cheese. (And I love cheese!) And all the extras inside probably are what kept the burger from tasting dried out as so many turkey burgers have the tendency to do. My only regret is that I wasn't more hungry so I could have finished my entire burger and side of sweet potato fries. Some people may think the portions are a bit on the small side, but I actually appreciated the small side of sweet potato fries. It's more in line with what a REAL serving size should be anyway. Overall our experience last night was excellent and I'm glad we happened to be back in the Manayunk area last night so I could have an excuse to enjoy a delicous meal.
label: POS

text: I had the Jambalaya and I don't know what the big deal is about this food. It's just rice, chicken, sausage, for about $9 and $2.25 for a soda. It as just the medium size bowl since I wasn't so hungry and just needed something to hold me over till dinner. Luckily the line wasn't long at 5pm. One of the more disturbing things was that I was seated next to the kitchen and one of the cooks was handling raw fish with his hands and then touching cooked items. I don't think I will ever go back to this place.

text: Just returned and this is the 1st review I have ever written. I ordered an app that was not available and opted for the papaya salad. It was small but decent. I had soup with tofu. text: I've been meaning to write a review for this place for a while. Sadly, their service has gone way down hill since my first visit there. If I had written this review after my first visit, I would have given 4 or 5 stars. The service and meals were great then. If you brave this place, I'd recommend sitting at the bar if you want to get service. Also, the pecan pie with sweet potato ice cream is AMAZING! My most recent, and probably last, visit was horrible. There were four of us, and the place wasn't very crowded, but it took around 5 minutes to get someone's attention to get a table. Once we were seated, it took another 15 minutes or so for our waiter even acknowledge us. I noticed he had a black eye and as our stay progressed, I couldn't help but think he got whilst at work. He dropped off some water and said he'd be right back. My friend said, 'I have a quick question for you...' the waiter cut him off mid-sentence and replied 'You'll have to wait, I'll be back'. It was then we considered leaving. (By the way, the quick question was if root beer on tap was alcoholic or not.) Instead, we waited a good ten more minutes for our waiter to return, while watching him cheerily chit-chat with a table outside. The rest of our service was just as horrible. After our initial round of drinks, we couldn't get anyone to stop by long enough to order more. The only reason they got two stars is because the food was still decent and a waitress in training noticed we were being ignored and saved the day. text: I normally only like to write good reviews. However, after last Saturday's experience here I had to come on and write a bad one. First off, the food was great - can not complain about one thing! I had a mahi-mahi special with crab filled raviolis - delicious!!! My boyfriend had some 20 ounce steak - also delicious and cooked perfectly. However, I must say the service we received was horrible. We made a reservation a week in advance. Upon arrival we had to wait 20 minutes. It was a Saturday so I was okay with this - I worked in the restaurant business throughout high school and college. Once seated our waiter seemed less than thrilled to have us as a table. I felt as though he was judging us as a younger "bad tippers" type table. We were probably 15 years younger than anyone at the tables surrounding us, however, no excuse for horrible service. He made no suggestions,did not review any of the specials - and I had to basically flag him back to the table to order a glass of wine - he was trying to run away so quickly. My water sat empty from before we received our salads to half way through our meal. I asked three times before receiving a refill. When I did not order another glass of wine he looked upset with us. I could say - hey maybe he is just a miserable person - however, he was laughing and going over the menu in detail with the two top next to us. We still tipped him fairly - yet he missed out on a great tip, since I don't believe in eating out unless you can tip your waiter properly! He had two ex servers/bartenders at his table and definitely left that night with a little less in his pocket then he could've. However, the valet guy did get a few extra bucks =) Overall, I'd go again - but if we get sat with him again, I will request a new server.

text: Yet another lunch in Reno...on the rainy and snowy day perfect choice - nice hot Bun Bo Hue. And a very good spring rolls with peanut dip. My friends had some chow main - they still haven't discovered secret powers of pho! Excellent place for business lunch - ~ $25 for 3 people.

text: CRAZY overpriced, slow bartenders, and the worst part is that they don't even live up to their name. Actually, the worst part is how badly they take advantage of their customers. They only had 2 kinds of absinthe (more like a shack than a house...) so I chose the better of the two. Bartender poured about an ounce of that, then added at least another ounce of anisette on top, totally destroying all of the delicious absinthe flavors with cheap flavored corn syrup crap. Then she added way too much simple syrup. She got the club soda and shaved ice right, but that was about it. Overall, I would recommend to walk in here for a photo but don't go in here for a drink.

text: This Whole Foods is wonderful! They have such a great selection of prepared foods, hot foods, and salads. I especially love that they have one traditional salad bar with the raw lettuce and veggies and one next to it with all prepared/cooked salads, such as couscous, pasta salads, marinated mushrooms, roasted beets, sauteed haricots verts, etc. I hit that second salad bar and ending up spending $16 for the biggest salad I've ever eaten. (They have enormous salad bowls!) It was delicious and worth every cent for me, since where I live you can't get produce of that freshness, quality and assortment. Because of the square footage, this particular store is able to carry and offer a wide range of products. I loved the cheese and produce sections as well as the hot and cold food bars. I had fun browsing at the big Whole Body next door. I also appreciated that this store has a big seating area in which you can chow down. The staff is very friendly as well. If I lived here, I'd hang out here all the time, cost be damned!

My chicken chalupa was bland and tasteless and had pieces of bone and gristle in it. My husbands tacos were tasteless also. The waitress buzzed by our table so fast while asking if everything was OK we couldn't even stop her to order another drink. Complete waste of a drive downtown.

The friendly woman behind the counter said that the pumpkin scones had been freshly baked that morning, and I was sold. The shop was super cute; stylish and fun but relaxed. I prayed that the coffee would be good so I could start making this place a regular stop--it was! I got home and tore into my scone which was filled with nuts, raisins and cranberries. Yum. I really hope the owners do well here and I will be doing my part to make sure they do!

Supposedly there's another pizza on the way, along with my drink, but I'll never order from them again.

text: Pio's is old school. I mean OLD school. I think it opened just before Merriwether Lewis and William Clark arrived in St. Charles. Everytime I've been there I've kept my eyes open for Joe Pesci or Robert Deniro to slide around the corner to whack some mobster who had one coming alla Goodfellas. I sure won't sit with my back to the door! Pio's really has that 1960's Italian restaurant/bar vibe. I've never been impressed at all with Pio's. If you know what to expect then you shouldn't be too terribly disappointed. The majority of the other customers were blue hairs which is always a harbinger of bland, lame food in your immediate future. My advice is to order the pizza. To go... They do serve some potent garlic breadsticks, but those aren't enough to redeem Pio's. Don't expect much out of anything else at Pio's, including the service. The other food that I've eaten on other trips has been less than spectacular. The salad is basically iceberg lettuce and oil & vinegar. Blah. The last time I was in our server had a street-like attitude which made me quite uncomfortable since I was dining with my mother and my 8-year old son. I'm not saying that I'd never go back because the pizza is probably one of the better St. Louis style pizzas in St. Chuck, but I wouldn't go out of my way.
label: NEG

text: OK I'll admit it I've got a thing for this place. I mean how much fun is it to ride a carousel while you're drinking and chatting in New Orleans?? Great service and I had an excellent Gin Fizz followed by one of the best Gin & Tonics I"ve ever tasted - and I've tasted quite a few LOL! We always meet cool & fun people here too. My only complaint is that it's hard to get a seat at the bar because it's so popular but we finally managed to do it at 3:00 on a Tuesday afternoon!!

text: This is a fun place for a weekend night out. My wife and I both got the filet, which was well-prepared and very flavorful. The drinks were pretty good too - I had a mojito and my wife had some kind of berry cocktail. The fried oreo-style desert was the highlight of the meal. Overall I'd recommend Valanni for dinner or drinks on a Friday or Saturday night, although it was really loud and kind of chaotic at some moments, which leads to my only complaint about the place. We showed up on time with an 8:30pm reservation on a Saturday night, and ended up standing at the bar until 9pm before we were seated. The hostess kept saying "it'll just be 5 or 10 minutes' and when we complained she mentioned something about there not being enough clean glasses to go around. This was a bit of an irritating start to our experience, but the food made up for it and we will most likely be coming back.
label: POS

text: I am writing this review to remind myself not to go back to Rocks ever again!!! I have given this place too many chances. Rocks...infamous for their service and lousy portions. The only reason I kept going back there was because of the ambiance - great people watching and convenient location. Half way through drinks or dinner, I would feel overwhelmingly disappointed and hated myself for returning. Memories of either horrible service or over-priced food would consume the rest of my experience at Rocks. So this is it...Rocks is off my list in SB...unless I see 5 stars here consistently in the next 50 reviews. However, if you must go there, my advice is that you should expect little and know that you are paying high price of what seems to be a hip spot in SB. If I was a tourist, I might be fine with it because the food is not bad, just small and overpriced. As for the service, you might get lucky with a good waiter but don't be surprised if you are not treated well. Perhaps the best thing to do at Rocks is just to get a drink or two, get out and then go shopping. Keep it short, don't expect too much, and you might end up having a mediocre time.
label: NEG

text: We went out to Tucson to help my son settle in after he's back from Kuwait. After a couple of days of searching, comparing, he decided to buy a Scion xD. Out of the 2 Toyota dealers within the city limit of Tucson, Precision was the one with the inventory. My son is 21 and had been in the USAF since he graduated from HS. So obviously he didn't have any credit history. But in order to start building credit, we suggested that he put 2/3 of the total as down payment and finance the rest 1/3. He drove away with the 9.95% financing for 5 years. That was last Monday evening when he drove the car out of the showroom with all the finance papers processed. Today, a week after the transaction, my son received a call from them and said that the credit didn't get approved therefore they needed to increase the interest rate to 16.95%. My son called with frustration. I was furious but I'm already back in Austin and can't really do much for him now. So we decided that he should just go pay it off and screw them with their financing crap. I think what they did was highway robbery! Beware, before you step into this dealership!

text: I've been going to Philadelphia Dental Associates for about 7 years, primarly for the convenience (they are across the street from my office). From a dental perspective, they seem to do a decent job (except for my last hygenist, who was late and then attacked my teeth like I had committed a crime). My issue stems from the office administration itself. Quite frankly, when you have a upcoming appointment with them, it's like being stalked. Reminder phone calls, calls to ask that you call back to confirm you have an appointment, and so on. I'm an adult, I am perfectly capable of keeping track of my schedule - especially for appointments that I've made myself. I've asked time and time again, but they continue to call. I don't have this problem with any other health care provider, nor have I ever missed an appointment. I've had more than one occasion where they have been late. This is annoying as the primary reason I go there is for convenience because I can run over there on my lunch hour. After the last set of calls and the hygenist from hell, I'm at the point of starting to look for another dentist. They are just not worth it.

text: This place opens at 7am, but don't even bother with their weekly breakfast. The girl who took my order was very rude and seemed put off by my request to hear the muffins of the day. The "blueberries" were the size of raisins, and given the fact that it is summer...and there are fresh blueberries available...I would expect more than a Betty Crocker box mix. PS. These muffins were lacking substantial muffintops, and in my book, that is just a no-no.

text: When you first walk in, the hostess is super hoity toity in asking if you have reservations. No smile. Not even real eye contact. They walked us through what looked like the "service" area of the kitchen - plates being scraped into trash, bain maries of... stuff wrapped up in plastic wrap, and just disarray. Not an attractive area to see before (or even after!) dinner. Our server was very eager which was cute, but kept interrupting our conversation to ask the same questions (where are you from? What are you here for?). My colleague asked for a club soda, but the server cleverly upsold him a Perrier saying that the club soda is "too flat" and that the sparkling water was better. Of course it's better, it increased the check! My "Court of Two Sisters" salad was... okay. It wasn't very good. I wasn't sure what kind of dressing was drizzled on top. It was also super tiny. But I have to say - my entree of duck was PERFECTLY cooked and absolutely delicious! I loved the sweet potato puree and it was just good good good. We ended the meal with the table side bananas foster, which was out of this world. The food was a 4, and service was a 2 (I was cranky and just got super annoyed). I just... couldn't see what was so alluring about this place. The history is great and I couldn't figure out what the ambiance was (tourist trap?). All in all... a 2. I doubt I'll ever return, and I'm in New Orleans quite often for business.
label: NEG

text: I get the feeling that this place is a mecca for people who like hot roast beef sandwiches............. Alas, I was talked into going here for dinner the other night with the promise of good beer, good grub ( other than roast beef sandwiches) and plenty of TVs to watch the game. Good beer...check( Spaten Octoberfest, Troegs). TV bonanza....check ( I counted 6 from my seat although I know that there were more). Food.....unfortunately, a big miss. My knackwurst (German sausage) was multi-colored.....red in the center and the rest of the link was gray....not very appetizing. A plus was that the side of sauerkraut was so sour that it made my lips pucker......I am a sauerkraut connoisseur and I believe the more kick the better! If you are looking for a super chill place atmosphere ( I think I saw someone in their pj's) to have a beer and watch the game go for it.

text: Anywhere that makes gooey butter flavored ice cream deserves at least 4 stars in my book. Now, when you add a complete willingness to give you sample after sample until you find the ice cream you want and do it without seeming irritated, you deserve 5 stars for sure. This ice cream is homemade and delicious. There are a ton of flavors ranging form completely original to your standard chocolate chip. I have never had anything bad here, but I have had some mediocre flavors. I do suggest trying a few out before you settle. They never have the same assortment when I go here, either. There are always new flavors so the trip seems different every time. I think that's certainly part of this ice cream shop's charm. I do find it a little, um, irritating that the name is a knock off of a famous ice cream place in New York City, (made most famous by the horrible movie of the same name) but hey, at least you have a good idea of what you are getting into before you go through the doors and start ordering.

text: Only been here once last fall, but I guess it's not really my scene. The drinks were pretty strong and on the pricey side. I didn't have to pay a cover, so maybe we got there early. But I don't think I'd ever return, because I'd rather have a more friendly, cozy place with seating like The Neighborhood, or a place to dance. There's better places in Santa Barbara.

text: I'm an Indy east side native now living in Chicago, where you can find a decent local pizza place every other block. When I visit Indy and get pizza, I always try to avoid the ubiquitous chains and patronize Pizza Doughmain. text: Heard about this company through an acquaintance of mine. I booked the 14-pass Escalade for my boyfriend's 30th surprise party. The booking process was flawless. Laura (she's no longer there) and Dominique were so patient with me and helped me with the planning process and payment schedule (they don't require it, I needed it for myself). Jill (I think she's the Director of Operations) is the sweetest person I have ever spoken to. She made sure I didn't have any questions or concern the evening of the party. Cost wise, it was great! They included 15% gratuity with the cost, but I still had to give the limo driver more, because he was just that awesome. Driver was John Burke, and he is good at what he does. He called me the morning of to go over the itinerary for evening. When he got to the house, he carried out the beer and wine and set them up in the limo. The drive was flawless and he was just so personable. Everytime we were ready to move on to our next destination, all I had to do was give him a call and seconds later he would be outside waiting for us. AND before he started driving again, he would always do a headcount to make sure we were all accounted for. Best part - one of the girls felt nauseous in the limo so I yelled up to John to let him know. He throws back a puke bucket, roll of paper towels and a rubber band to tie her hair up with - who the heck does that?! Luckily, we didn't have to utilize the puke bucket, but it's definitely good to know that he has it readily available. All-in-all, a really great experience with Secrets Limo. I will definitely give them a call again when it comes time to plan the bachelorette and wedding! And I definitely will be requesting John Burke, he's all that and MORE!
