text: Very disappointed. Menu looks good but the execution was far from good. I had the lamb lollipops with mint pesto that were way over cooked and the mint pest had no flavor, the clams with chorizo that had a couple small clams, soggy chorizo and the broth tasted like white wine and vinegar. Finally had the fish and chips with Bacon coleslaw and whole grain mustard tarter, sounded awesome. fish was soggy and slaw was cabbage with a couple Bacon bits and some lemon. The best part of the meal was dipping the fries in the very tasty tarter sauce and the amazing beer selection. Heard they have a good burger but who doesn't. Ambiance, menu, and beer selection are all in place now they just need to deliver on the food.

text: I like this place better than the Sabrina's in the Art Museum area. It has more of a rustic or old house vibe than its more diner-ish feeling counterpart. I still enjoy both, however. The food is delicious, albeit not as cheap as other breakfast places. The portions are fairly substantial to make up for the price increase. I always finish my food though! I'm a big fan of the Barking Chihuahua breakfast burrito. I've never tried the French Toast, but I want to. Moving towards brunch... I think the Parmesan French Fries are a bit gimmicky. The Tuscan Chicken sandwich is delicious though. As for dinner... if ever you see the Stuffed Meatloaf available, holy shit is that good and huge portions! The specials are often the best way to go, but more expensive. Of course you're going to have to wait for awhile if you come on a popular day, but you should already know that if you're reading this review. Sometimes upwards of 30 minutes... They are also dog friendly, which is nice for my friend who likes to bring her dog in the summer. They give the dog a water bowl. Nice touch. However, I'm sure the people sitting at a table next to the dog can possibly get annoyed. You know... after good social graces require them to proclaim just how cute your dog is~!!! You still have a fucking dog staring at your food as you eat. Could be annoying to some. Also, the sidewalk outside is at a slight slant... and my friend's dog once spilled the water bowl. So it naturally ran down under the table of the people closest to the street. Sorry, guys. I love dogs, really... but maybe just leave your dog at home. TIP: Need a quick beer fix for your BYO meal? Check out 12 Steps Down nearby while you're waiting for a table. They have take-out beer available, albeit pricey.
label: POS

text: As mentioned in one of my other reviews, a friend and I try to do a brunch on the weekends at a new restaurant each time. It was her turn to choose and she picked Elizabeth's. While I have been (and it's been a while), she has not. I give it two stars because the service was really good and delivered with a smile. In my opinion you can't ask for much more. Except for the food to be, at minimum, appetizing. We were shocked because we had read reviews stating quite the opposite. The food was great and the service was lack luster. Maybe the upcoming time change had them turned around. The food was nothing to write home about. I should restate that as it was something to write to Yelp about. We ordered two specials and split. I ordered the crab cakes with poached eggs on top and hollandaise (sp?) and she ordered the poached eggs on top of fried eggplant drowning in some shitake cream sauce that closely resembled Campbell's cream of mushroop soup. It was a complete waste of calories. I would not recommend this place. We also ordered biscuits which were very dense and were cold! How is my butter to melt on cold biscuits! Even the praline bacon that everyone raves about seemed mediocre. Sometimes I think you could put a bail of hay in front of the faces of New Orleanians and theyd scream YUM!

text: Of all the nightclubs in the area, Emerald City was the taint of them all. I partied some time ago for a party I was invited to. Unsure what the deal was with the name or the theme, but the gaudy interior and ghetto couch on the dancefloor didn't do much for me. They had multiple shady, dirty rooms, too. On the bright side, the bartenders and bouncers were all fine. But they're not open anymore anyway! It's now Penthouse Lounge, which I have yet to check out.
label: NEG

text: An honest, very approachable bar in Philadelphia. This is why I love this city. When you walk into The Institute, there is no bs. It's a simple place that focuses on relaxation, good beer and good food. They aren't full of themselves. It's a very matter of fact place. You know what you're getting when you're walking in there. I've been here a few times and I have never been disappointed. Last night, we had our film club congregate upstairs for a good dose of holiday cheer with Bad Santa. We had a choice of two beers from Southampton, the double white and the saison. I was very impressed with the saison. The double white was good, it's more of a summer beer in my opinion. The Bell's Rye Stout did rock my world. I have to have more of that beer. For food, I had the grilled cheese and soup. For the soup I chose their gumbo-esque preparation. Very tasty and just what I needed on a cold night. The grilled cheese was also very good and not overwhelming. I have been to places that go crazy with their grilled cheese to the point where it's so rich and heavy I need to split it with someone. Not the case here. I was able to have the sandwich and enjoy it along with my nice bowl of soup. All in all, I have had solid times at The Institute and I will continue to be a patron. Hopefully, I can make it to one of their beer events. They always coincide with weekends that I am out of town.
label: POS

text: For me, this really hovers between one star and two. Like Tae K. I was shocked at the many four and five star ratings. After reading about it as one of the better BYO places in town, we decided to pop in for dinner on First Friday recently. The place was hopping and we were ready for a great meal. Not taking credit cards is a drag, but I can live with that. We also did not have wine, since the meal was spontaneous and the nearest wine store was a few blocks away. In the end I wish I had gone on a wine run, because a good wine buzz might have blunted the disappointment in the food. Service was terrible! Friendly, but there was ONE waiter and ONE busboy for the entire restaurant. Long waits for food, had to ask for water refills. OK, the food: Basically, extremely ordinary Italian food. Frozen Celentano's probably better. Yes the portions are large, but does that matter if the food is mediocre? We had the mussels to start, as well as salad special. Salad was overdressed and soggy, and not very flavorful. Mussels were OK, but half the mussels were totally closed. Had to ask for a spoon for the broth - something that should be a given for mussels. Main courses were also both boring, and pretty tasteless. It is a fun bustling atmosphere, a good location in the heart of Old City, but those are its strongest assets. Will not be returning!
label: NEG

text: I needed something interesting. Supper is a really neat-o place to have dinner. I loved the decor and the service was outstanding. Our server had passion for food and for making sure we had everything we needed. The butternut squash soup is amazing. I want that pumped into my veins. I want to bathe in it. I made sweet love to it. The flat bread was a nice second course, and the cheese plate got us going. The crispy rabbit schnitzel and the short ribs were fan-frikin-tastic. This is a fun place to hit for special occasions. If i lived in the neighborhood, I would be tempted to stop in much more often. Bring money, not cheap and you need to have at least 3 courses per person to leave full, if that's your thing.
label: POS

text: It was okay. The place reminded me of a somewhat fast food joint except it wasn't fast. The ribs had a marinated teryaki chicken taste. They came with rice and mac and cheese. My wife had the fried basket and it was pretty dry. The meat I had tasted good. Oh well, a strike out in my search for the best ribs in town.

text: Holy renovations! Like the fat kid, who comes back from summer vacation looking all svelte and sexy, Super Fresh emerged from its makeover cocoon looking classier than ever. Walking around today after work, I couldn't believe it was the same store! It's clean, organized, the SIGNS ACTUALLY INDICATE WHERE THINGS ARE, there's a mini bakery, a whole section of exquisite cheeses (Whole Foods ain't got nothing on this), a deli with pasta salads that actually look edible, a large section of ready-to-eat foods (I got the Italian wrap and mac n' cheese -- both tasty) and my personal favorite, AN OLIVE BAR! WITH STUFFED GRAPE LEAVES! (mmmm) They even had whole wheat bagels (a rarity) in stock. It really seems too good to be true. Of course, the produce still isn't anywhere near the quality of Whole Foods...but it's a lot cheaper too. Oh Super Fresh, I am sorry I misjudged you. If you can keep this up, I promise I'll never diss you for your swanky neighbor again!
label: POS

text: My husband and I recently went on a tour of the Ely Walker lofts on fanciful Washington Avenue. I had never liked lofts until we saw these. The price is not bad at all, and you get a lot of square footage for your money - square footage that is organized in smart ways. Everything here has been renovated, so don't worry about the fact that the building is over 100 years old! The floors became the focus of my love, as they simply must be recovered and are stylishly dingy with various pock marks on them. If you love artsy things, you will love these floors. The windows are also amazing, yet I bet that they are very drafty in the winter, and this is the lone reason that I am not giving 5 stars. Out of the four units we saw, the windows were all the same. They are huge and gorgeous, but drafty. I'm sure that this could be easily remedied, though. The kitchens and bathrooms in the units were all very lovely. If I had a few thousand in the bank, I think that I would have jumped in right then and there. Seriously, that is how cool this place is. The atrium is artistically amazing, there is a 3000+ square foot rooftop sundeck, a rec room and a fitness center. The ceilings all have the exposed ductwork and there is exposed brick walls. There are extra large elevators to bring up all of your furniture and you can purchase parking spots in the underground garage. Also, the building is connected to the same building as the London Tea Room. The Ely Walker Lofts has so many things going for it that I can't believe they are not sold out. I want to live here!
label: POS

text: This place is AMAZING. I've always loved Aveda salons as well as their products but this one is seriously the best I've been to. I have been highlighting my hair for almost 8 years and am most happy with Yen at Level2. Yen makes me looks like a natural blonde! She takes the time to focus on the details. She's a great colorist and one of the best at Level2. The staff is very pleasant and the service is awesome! I would suggest this salon to anyone and have already had many satisfied friends. Love love love Level2.

text: I recently came home from work to find a chinese menu in my front door. I brought it inside and took a look. The prices seemed alright but what really caught my eye was the japanese menu that was attached. On the menu there was an extensive list of japanese items available to order. A couple days later i was tired and didn't feel like cooking so we decided to try this new place. We ordered some sushi (three rolls... cucumber, california, and tuna) we also got an order of endamame and an order of scallops and mushrooms. We had it delivered. There service was good. The people were friendly and delivery was prompt. As for the food, HORRIBLE! We could smell the sushi before we opened the paper bag. The tuna roll was warm and fishier than normal. Impossible to eat. The other rolls were packed with the tuna roll. Those rolls were extremely fishy as well. The scallops and mushrooms were alittle better but not much. There was very little scallops in the order. It was mostly water chestnuts and big canned mushrooms. However this was edible. The endamame was the only thing that was really good because all they had to do was steam it. Needless to say we spent $26 dollars to have basically white rice and an order of endamame.
label: NEG

text: Three friends and I dined here a couple months ago on a Friday night at 6:30. It was my second time at Sullivans. For starters, I had a chilled asparagus bisque with lump crab meat that was very mild in flavor but satisfying. Definitely one of the better chilled soups I've had. My friends all got the lobster bisque and they were raving about it. Three of us ordered steaks while one got the meatloaf. My filet mignon was cooked perfectly (med-rare) and the other two that got steaks echoed my sentiments. The friend that got the meatloaf was very pleased with his dish as well. All of the sides we ordered (we did some sharing) were delicious and fairly sizeable - which is good considering they're all a la carte and far from cheap. Dessert was the only blight of the night. I got the chocolate mousse and everyone knows mousse should be light, frothy and creamy. This was neither light or frothy. It was dense and more akin to Jell-0 chocolate pudding. Our server was very friendly and attentive. Overall everyone in our party was very happy with their food and the service we received. Sullivans is definitely very pricey, but I've left pretty satisfied both times I've dined here.
label: POS

text: After attending a frat party here, I was completely glad that I decided not to enroll in Vandy. I've never seen so many weak-minded buffoons in my life. I've been to college parties all over Florida and in Auburn and in LSU. I have never seen people with such an unhealthy detatchment from reality as I witnessed here. I'm sure they're not all like that, but certainly the frat boys of Vandy are giving the school a terrible name.

text: I speak about the brunch only. As a dinner or snack-y place, I'm all for it. I went for brunch this morning. I give it one less star because, well, there were no egg whites. Who has an omelet station without egg whites?? The brewery. That's who. But I digress. I didn't love the food. There was a lot of variety and selection, but nothing was necessarily awesome. Kinda expensive for brunch... though I can see sitting there long enough to then have lunch, which would make the price worth it.

text: It is dangerous that I live across the street from this gem. The food is always amazing with service to match. Last week, I brought a picky vegan and there was a small mix up with her food (it being my friend's fault completely!) yet, both servers and the chef came over to make sure everything was okay. TWO THUMBS UP. Yes, it is always busy and yep, noisy too. But HELLO?!?! You are at a popular Center City restaurant- what do you expect? The wait time may seem long but it is always around the time they say. And when you are seated, you are greeted instantly and the wonderful food comes out fast. My Favorites: Lobster & Shrimp Pyramid Pasta Short Rib Ragu Vanilla Bean Panna Cotta Mercato Antipasti AND you can't beat a BYOB Great first date place to avoid the awkward silence :)

It was very crowded and tables were squeezed together as closely as possible. The waiter asked us if we were ready to order, we said we need a few minutes, and he just stood there with his arms folded until we made a choice. We were only at the table for 3 minutes at that point! I honestly would rather have gone to the Olive Garden!

text: I live in San Francisco, definitely on the list of top wig wearing cities. People here need very little excuse to throw on a wig. I've checked out a few spots around town but always felt the wigs here are way overpriced. Anyway, I knew I was coming to NOLA for New Years and thought it would be cool to buy a wig while I was in town. So I did a little Yelp research and found Fifi Mahony's. All I have to say is... WOW! The boutique is super cute and the staff is even cuter. The gal who helped me was very knowledgable and made me feel so welcomed -- I don't know how else to explain it! I was amazed at their wig selection - so many fabulous colors and styles. Oh and the prices, SO REASONABLE. I walked out of Fifi's with two gorgeous wigs and an ear-to-ear smile that lasted for days. Thank you!

text: I feel like Pat's (as well as Geno's) get touted as some of the best cheesesteaks in Philly, but to me it seems as if it got to this point based on it being more of a tradition or tourist attraction rather than the actual food. I've only been there once, so perhaps I need to go back to double-check. The one time I've been, the cheese was not melted AT ALL and the meat was actually a little cold as well. I'm not sure if it's because they are so used to dealing with larger crowds that they have just become sloppy (there were only a few people there when I went) or if the steaks have always been made a certain way, but it just wasn't all that great.
label: NEG

text: so, we're leaving st. louis this week and had a few places we had to try before we left. Thai Pizza was not on the list. We've had so much bad Thai food on Delmar that I didn't think adding pizza to the mix would have helped. So, we were off to eat at Riddles. Parking was a bitch, but I managed to snag a spot right in front of TPC. My lovely wife, being the lazy wreck that she is, said "Hey, wanna just eat here?" Riddles. Thai Pizza. Incredible local food vs. Thai...Pizza? I'm usually up for an adventure, so I agreed. Turns out, it was definitely worth the lazy gamble. First point, they use Mozzarella, not Provel (which I'm convinced is actually extruded Play-Doh hair). It wasn't that the pizza's tasted exactly like their thai counterparts. The best part was that for once we had some original pizza toppings and they were all fantastic. The prices were very reasonable too. I'd vote for the thin crust not the thick. It wasn't that STL cracker stuff, but wasn't as thick as a slice of Brooklyn's finest. Service on the other hand was complete crap. There is no way you can expect to run a restaurant on a saturday night with just two servers. That's some bullshit. We waited a long time for everything. Wait for menus, wait to take our order, wait for drinks to show - nope, not my Plum Wine - wait for food, wait for check, you get the idea. Seriously people. It shouldn't take 90 minutes to eat pizza. But, like I said, good pizza that wasn't covered in four different kinds of pig.
label: POS

text: I think this place suffers from an identity crisis. I am going to keep this short and too the point. Adobe doesn't know if its a TEX MEX place or a MEXITALIAN place. This is not mexican food. My girlfriend ordered what she thought would be a mexican taco dish but what came out was covered in Parmesan cheese. Note to everyone reading this. There is no parmesan in Mexican or Tex Mex food. I could understand if it was cotija but this was actual parmesan. not good. Also, margaritas in wine glasses are laughable. Give us some real glasses. I felt like I was sneaking watered down margaritas at 17 again. I was really looking forward to going here, but wanted to cry after I saw the menu. It may be other peoples cup of tea but I just moved here from Denver and I know what real Tex Mex is supposed to be like. If you like "MEXITALIAN", you'll like this place. Otherwise steer clear.
label: NEG

text: Do not buy from! We ordered doors October 2009, with installation guaranteed by Thanksgiving. Doors were finally installed February 2010. Our salesman also informed us that St Clair has their own installation crews and that at least 2 people would be sent. We received one installation guy who was outsourced by St Clair. He expected us to pay him, when the installation price was included in the cost of the doors. I called St Clair several times when we were waiting on our doors to figure out where they were and the owner promised to call me the next day with an answer. I never heard from him again. At one point, his assistant called to ask how we liked our doors when we didn't even have them yet. Very poor customer service!
label: NEG

text: This is my first Wahoo's experience and I am glad to report that it was a good one! I had the fish taco combo plate with both kinds of rice and beans. It's really cool that they let you do that... most places would charge extra for this type of thing. I chose the blackened, spicy fish for the tacos and it was delicious! None of that battered fried mess here! The salsa was just right and I love that little bit that they put on top of the beans and rice. The cajun white beans were so flavorful. The black beans with the white rice went well together too. The brown rice was a little dry for my taste. Prices weren't bad either! I think my combo plate was $5.99.
label: POS

text: Eeeek. The rooms shown on the website are in the new luxury condos ONLY. The room they will actually put you in, if you are of the non-millionaire persuasion, have not felt fresh air for 50 years. When I complained about that and they put me into a luxury suite, I thought I was queen of the world until I realized, halfway through my shower, that the plumbing didn't work. No amount of marble in the bathroom (and there was a lot) could make up for the fact that I was standing in a growing pond of water throughout my shower. And my "medium-rare" steak came out cold and barely cooked. Finding a decent place to stay in Reno is difficult but this was a travesty.
label: NEG

text: Delco beer geeks should be limbering up their gullets for a trip to Quotations, conveniently located right across State St. from Iron Hill Brewery for for the world's shortest two-stop pub crawl. From the rarely-seen-on-draft DeDolle Dulle Teve ("mad bitch" triple) to Schneider Aventinus weizenbock, the draft list was beyond on point. I worked at Monk's for four years and I'm hard to impress beer-wise. This selection was as good as any top-tier city beer bar. Pleased to be swilling so swell in the burbs, our table of five moved on to dinner. My family eats in mass quantities, so servers' faces generally light up when they realize they have a $200 check happening here. This guy seemed slightly panicked at all times, running away from the table before we were finished ordering/asking questions. I wasn't so hungry, and ordered a house salad and french onion soup. Both were fine. Everyone else's food was less fine. My boyfriends's tilapia sandwich was just fried fish on a ginormous roll. Nothing else. It wasn't horrible, but certainly not something you'd return for. When the server hurriedly asked, "Can I bring you anything else right now?" one member of our party, who'd had about five appletinis by this point, responded, "Yeah, the rest of this guy's sandwich." Embarrassing, yes. For us and Quotations.
label: NEG

text: Brand new psychological techniques have been recently invented that allow you to enjoy a Pulse Night Club Experience from your very own home!! WOW! Just follow the simple instructions below: 1. Put your head in your hands so that your palms are covering your eyes and your thumbs are pointed towards your ears. 2. Chant "I hate myself" for a full hour, without removing your hands from your face. 3. Remove your hands from your face, walk towards your toilet, and place a crisp $50 bill into it. 4. Flush the toilet and go to bed. -- Overpriced, ridiculously crowded, insidiously loud. This place is everything I hate in a place to go for any reason.
label: NEG

text: Luke has been my favorite restaurant for a couple of years now. I have tried EVERYTHING on the menu at least twice so I think I have a pretty good basis for comparison. This restaurant is not for everyone. If you are new in town and looking for classic New Orleans creole or soul food cuisine. Look elsewhere. If you don't like Alsacian food (or don't know what it is) you might want to pass. But if you are game you will find Luke serves earthy food with a light touch. Literally everything is good, but there are standouts. The Luke Burger is made of fine beef and served with fries that I believe are cooked in duck fat. It is the tastiest combo in town. Although it's great, I don't often get the burger because it weighs about 5 pounds. You will need a doggy bag. I do get the matzo ball soup and Luke salad often. The soup is a rarity in NOLA and I'll admit that I don't get the connection of this Jewish staple to the French/German border. Who cares? It tastes a little like chicken gumbo, which means it's delicious. The redfish is probably the best all-around dish. It's lightly sauteed and covered in lump crab meat . However, my personal favorite is the Flamenkuche aka German pizza or bacon, Emmenthaler and caraway cheese and onions on a tarte. This dish is savory and so good that I sometimes dream about it. At the risk of belaboring the point, there are plenty of other standouts. The redfish court-bouillion. The white bean and duck cassoulet. The cochon de lait. Did I mention they put on a fine breakfast? Grits and grillades. Buttermilk pancakes. Etc. Etc. The service is friendly and attentive. The decor is cool and very detailed. Note the old fashion belt fans in the front room (I didn't notice them until my 10th visit.) Just check the restaurant out. It's got plenty to offer. I hope you will agree.

text: This vegetarian is in love with a burger joint. Sure, it's mainly for the fries, but DON'T TELL ANYONE! When Five Guys started popping up in my friends' cities across the country, everyone told me, "OMG, Allison, you'll love the fries!" I was skeptical that a place that sounded purposefully masculine and served mainly meat would make fries that I liked. I agreed to try it once it came to the St. Louis area, though. When I finally tasted the fries at the Fairview Heights, Ill., location, I was ecstatic. These fries are thick like Penn Station's and obviously are made from real potatoes. You know how your uncle would say "C'mere and I'll carry you like a sack of potatoes" and he'd sling you over his shoulder? Well, you can do that at Five Guys, but with real sacks of potatoes - they're piled up everywhere! Oh, but if fries were the only menu item I could eat, my review would only be three or four stars. However, Five Guys proves that beef-lusters can be vegetarian friendly, too. They have not one but TWO veggie sandwiches on the big board. They're essentially the same thing - veggies on a bun - but the second one has cheese. Ask them to pile on however many veggies you want and do the same with the cheese, and the folks at Five Guys will do it! They don't charge extra to make a filling, meat-free sandwich, and I'm not relegated to being an afterthought with just lettuce and tomato on stale bread! LOVE! I do wish that meals wouldn't come in individual paper sacks. It's my beef (Haha! Get it? BEEF!) with Subway, too - why not just put everything on a tray? But sometimes, it's just kind of fun to dig at the bottom of the bag for those straggler fries and feel like you're getting a bonus. Oh, and yes, I realize that I mentioned the Fairview Heights location and that I'm actually reviewing the Richmond Heights location. I've eaten at both, though I'll probably end up at the RH locale more often. So there. Penn Station, don't be sad. I still heart you and want to marry your fries. You've just got some competition now. This Five Guys is located outside the Galleria Mall. Obviously, you can drive to it and park in the lot, but you also could take Metrolink to the Richmond Heights station and walk a couple of blocks, or just take the bus.

text: Cadillac Ranch - A wannabe upscale atmosphere, featuring a mechanical bull, snobby employees & awful food. I'm wishing I would have read fellow reviews before going back to this establishment. Everything described thus far is pretty much in tune with the experience I had on Memorial Day Weekend. My first visit to Cadillac Ranch was for their grand opening last summer. In a party of 10 people, nobody was satisfied with the food or the service. Figuring that the employees and chefs were just overwhelmed by the crowd on opening night, I decided to go back for another try. Nothing has improved - if anything, the customer service and food have gotten even worse. This weekend, three friends and I were seated in a corner table outside. It was afternoon & the atmosphere was so quiet it seemed like we were dining at a library & whispered when we spoke. I must say that the one thing this place has going for it is the beautiful view from the outdoor seating area and comfortable couches surrounding fire pits by the bar. Now, if only the staff and chefs could get it together to provide an all around good experience! We placed the order and it took around 45 minutes to start getting our food. I'll go ahead and place a description next to each food item ordered by the group: Latkes (flat potato slices that were flavorless - burnt on the outside & raw on the inside), Tower of Onion Rings (a cold deep fried pile of skinny onion slices, lacking flavor & over-cooked in stale oil), Spinach Artichoke Crab Dip (sorry to be so vivid, but this actually tasted like regurgitated food served with burnt unleavened bread) & Sirloin Steak & Shrimp (over-priced chunk of greasy fatty meat with three small rubbery shrimp). I looked around and saw that two other tables had ordered the Towering Onion Rings & the people left without eating more than a few bites. Not a good sign when all surrounding tables have full plates of food left on them! Now that you have an idea of just how awful the food is, let me go on to describe the snobby service. Our waitress was mildly pleasant, although her pleasantness looked very forced. Her expression made it look as though she was tremendously bothered every time someone at my table (or a surrounding table) asked for drink re-fills or dipping sauce. The worst part about the "labored" service was that there were maybe 20 people dining at the entire restaurant - and probably 20 bored looking staff members wondering around aimlessly. At a ratio of 1:1 you'd think we'd get good service! Near the end of our meal, the waitress just disappeared & nobody came over to check on us. One of my friends actually had to go up to the bar to place drink orders & bring them back to the table himself. While he stood at the bar waiting, he struck up a conversation with two men who had been seated at the bar at the same time we got our table. They began talking and laughing - and getting eyed suspiciously by the bar tender. My friend took the drinks over to us and then went back to the bar to finish his conversation with the other two patrons. I went over to the bar to get some lemon for my drink & joined in on the conversation as well. About 5 minutes later, a weasly man with an Australian accent approached us and asked us to please quiet down because this is a family atmosphere. WHAT?! Ok - so now it's been confirmed. We ARE in a library, cleverly disguised as a bar. Now, you must realize that the outdoor area had absolutely no children present at this time & the area where we were standing was THE BAR, where no children are allowed anyways. And it's not like we were all fighting or cursing at each other - we were sharing funny party stories & just having a good time. So, we "quieted down" and kept talking as to not disturb the snooty employees. One of the men we were talking to at the bar ordered a beer, and the bar tender told him "No, I'm afraid you're going to have to cash out your tab and leave". We all stood there with furrowed brows and stunned expressions. Granted, we were not asked to leave - that was only demanded of the two men who had been sitting at the bar. But, completely sickened by the actions of the staff, we decided to leave as well. As I left, I told the weasly manager that I was going to leave him one hell of a review, and walked out of the restaurant. He had the nerve to curse at me as I left! I'm just stunned by the actions of the staff at this establishment, but am happy to see that others have experienced similar (although not quite as bafflingly rude) service! For a place that has nothing to offer other than a good view, they seem to hold themselves in pretty lofty esteem. It's just a guess - but for weekend fun and dining, you might get better food and friendlier service at the Reno Soup Kitchen than at Cadillac Ranch!
label: NEG

text: Why do people like this place? I'm really asking. (I can only conclude that people like it, because the joint is PACKED at all hours, and on every day of the week, it seems) Every visit is like an existential quandary. Each time I get wrangled in to going, I vow that I will never be back, but someone always manages to get me to return - usually under pain of death, and usually because they themselves are being dragged to a work social mixer of some kind. In fact, maybe that's the answer. Maybe Applebee's is the official restaurant of the awkward work meet-up. You know the one: you work in a cube farm and don't know the people well enough to consider them friends and to want to have a good dinner ruined by forced conversation, but you know them well enough to know that you absolutely MUST have a few drinks, while you hang out. The tables are sticky, the food is so generic that Lucky Wishbone feels kind of exotic, and the servers all seem high on goofballs and meth. Seriously, I didn't think it was possible for a grown man to be so damn excited for another man to order a salad. I thought I was going to get a kiss and a key to a clandestine hotel room from the guy. This is the kind of place where some poor shlub is ALWAYS getting serenaded for his birthday. You see the throng of waitstaff saunter out from the kitchen and put on their game faces, and you just know that something terrible is about to happen. You do a quick sweep of the room, looking for the hapless son-of-a-bitch who is about to let his pride seep out of his body like so much precious life force. Your heart goes out to him for a moment, but schadenfreude eventually gets the better of you, and you give your dining companions one of those, "Well, it's better him than me" shrugs. At the end of the day, Applebees is simply a horrible, terrible, no good, god-awful, very bad place in every way. I guess I'm the idiot for allowing myself to be forced to go there, but I can't help but feel as though some corporate turd goblin is standing behind me when I pull out my debit card at the end of the meal, cackling maniacally, and whispering, "Sit and spin on that shit, college boy!" I just always feel so completely taken, you know? Anyway, my advice would be that you avoid this spot at all costs, unless of course you are one of those people who always writes in "On the Border" for Best Mexican in the Tucson Weekly's annual "Best of Tucson" issue. Oh, and while we're on that subject - shame on you!

text: Again, people argue back and forth as to where you can get the best Mexican food in Tucson. It's kinda like arguing about which politician is most corrupt in Washington; Tucson is frankly a Mexican food mecca. Now, each restaurant has a distinct feel, distinct styles, and I often change which restaurant I take my visitors and friends to based on their individual tastes and wants. After all, if you're going to visit Tucson you want to have a good meal. La Poca Cosa comes to mind, or Mi Niditos, but my goto for showing non-Tucsonans how varied and diverse Mexican style food can be is Guadalajara Grill. Of course there is the standard Mexican food fair--burritos, tacos, enchiladas, but what makes Guadalajara unique is the diversity dishes. You can order anything from a molcajete bubbling with peppers and carne asada to the standard Tres Amigos, all with fresh in-house-made tortillas and at-the-table made salsa. Because my family and friends trek from the Midwest, they are often floored by how varied Mexican food can be from what they know, especially the seafood dishes which are pretty fantastic. Seafood in the desert? Yeah, the Baja is only 3-4 hours away. If you want more than just a meal, Guadalajara sports a meandering mariachi band, and they will come to your table to ask if you'd like a song. Many amors and corazons later, your date or family will be laughing and having a good time. If you want some margarita, they are strong and cheap on certain days so swing by, only complaint there is a little salty (but I like salty margaritas). I highly recommend Guadalajara.

text: Nestled in historic Washington Crossing, PA this gem is sure to make your day. The original barn serves as the tasting room and winery central. It has been converted to a state of the art winery. You have to love the smell of the place. The barrel room, just beyond the tasting room fills the air with the aromas of fine wine in the making. For a nominal fee, take a tasting tour through their vast variety of wines. It is an enjoyable journey from the dry white Chardonnay to the Wild Berry dessert variety. I loved it!! Have a special occasion coming up - they offer top notch catering and event planning, even weddings! They also offer fun events open to the public. You must start with "Wine Tasting for Dummies", you will learn lots and have a blast! The cost for a bottle of wine can range up from about $16, they do offer a case discount of 10%. And even though both legs of my last trip were good, I usually want to kill someone when flying with them. Here's the breakdown of what's good and bad about this airport: The pluses: - The "C" terminal has some nice shops if you need to kill time. (1 star) - It's convenient and easy to get to. (1 star) - Ummm, can't really think of anything else. The minuses: - Baggage claim. While my last experience was good, all of the other bad experiences negate it. One time, we flew into the E terminal. As we landed, the flight attendant told us we had to walk to the D terminal to get our luggage. We all schlep over there, wait for about 20 minutes, to be told "Oops, sorry, your luggage will be coming out at the E terminal." ONLY in Philadelphia. - The bathrooms at the end of the C terminal are so foul, I think I would prefer to use the bathrooms in Penn Station in NYC with all of the homeless people. - The security. While they were super friendly, I just don't think they're as tough as they should be. Smaller airports have tighter security than Philly. That's an issue. - Chickie and Pete's in the C terminal. I've never been to one before, but this place is GROSS. If this is how the rest of their restaurants are, I would rather eat at a Denny's. The details of this sad experience are for another review. - Pretty much the laziest, unhelpful people working here. - It's EXPENSIVE to fly out of this airport. I'm fortunate enough to have a choice between flying out of Philly or Newark. I would much rather fly out of Philly because 1.) It's closer and 2.) It's just easier to get to. But sometimes the dollar speaks louder than convenience.

text: Upon recommendation, my spouse and I decided to try out Chabaa Thai Bistro today. Walking in, and being seated promptly at 6:40pm, we commented nicely on the decor and beautiful ambience that the establishment had. We were seated upstairs and was immediately greeted by a friendly server who brought us back our drinks within a reasonable time frame (7-10 minutes). There were 3 seated couples upstairs and we were the 4th. We also made sure we were there before the dinner rush, but service changed soon after we received our appetizer (sampler). Our main course was Crispy Duck Pad Thai and the Grilled Lemon grass Beef salad. She had also recommended a side of rice which we agreed on. As she took away our Appetizer plate and brought over the entrees, we inquired about the rice since we were ready to dig in and see what the rave was all about. The entrees looked and smelled great and were garnished quite nicely. She mentioned that the rice was on its way after we asked, time was 7:05 pm. Then the late dinner rush happened around 7:30 pm. By then, she had completely forgotten about us. The rice never came, my drink glass was empty (I placed it on the side of the table hoping someone would see it), and getting someone's attention was futile. The rush consisted of only 3 more tables! She finally came up to us and asked if she could pack it up (we barely ate anything). The time was 7:58 pm. We waited for the check to make sure we were billed appropriately. She came up the stairs with our very large take home bag but placed it elsewhere. She then gave us the check (where's our doggie-bag?). She left us for a bit only to come back upstairs and opened up the bag. She then stuck something in it and finally gave it to us. The check totaled up just fine, just under $58 albeit a bit expensive for what we kinda ate (which was very good nonetheless), but justified since it was "one of a kind" for the area. A glass of Thai Iced Cofee, a soft drink, the sampler, Pad Thai and Beef salad. No tab for rice of course. We got home and the rice was in the bag. She couldn't apologize when we were there, a simple "sorry we got a bit busy" would have been nice but the rice didn't matter. It was the service that mattered. We still tipped the customary 20% anyways.

text: Although I watch the news religiously and read the daily paper diligently, I somehow missed the announcement that postage costs are increasing this Sunday . . . an event one would assume was important enough for every post office to herald with signs prominently posted. Yet while I waited on line for nearly thirty-five minutes in this compact, overheated facility - with only two of five windows open to accommodate the couple of dozen people waiting for assistance - I saw nothing to indicate that four days from today I will have to pay more each of the few times per month I use snail mail. Nor did the clerk who finally helped me advise me of this fact when she blithely sold me a book of stamps. Only when I overheard a conversation at the register in the card shop a short while later did I realize most of the twenty thirty-seven cent stamps in my wallet would soon need two-cent companions beside them on every envelope I mailed. I returned to the post office, waited another twenty minutes, and asked the same clerk why she hadn't said anything when I requested a book of stamps the first time around. "I figured if you wanted new ones, you would have asked for them," was her response. Are you clueless, indifferent, or just plain dumb? Good news . . . a government job is waiting for you!

Second, the website says they are "open" till 5 and stop serving at 4. Apparently the actual sign on the door doesn't even specify-she thought she had plenty of time- and even with myself AND her complaining about how unfair this was, the woman who seemed like she owned the place just gave us both a condescending smile and acted like we should have known that already. text: I wanted to like Yellow Porch, but it seems that fate was against it. I'll try to be brief as I sum up our misadventures here last night: To be fair, it is Restaurant Week in Nashville, which means that we're maybe experiencing something that's a little different from the norm. Even taking that into consideration, I give them a 2-star rating. First, the parking lot is tiny - we had to park up the street a good way. Second, while some might say cozy, others might say cramped. I was seated on the aisle and spent much of the night getting bumped in to. Third, our server was apparently also bar tending while also keeping tabs on a number of tables. While she spent lots of time with our neighbors, she always seemed to forget us. It took about 30 minutes to get water and the correct menus. Fourth, bonus points for the bread situation - they have a nice dipping sauce of olive oil, pesto, feta, and balsamic vinegar, which was super tasty. Fifth, (and hear is where the review might stray from the norms because of Restaurant week) we ordered from the special menu and it was generally a disaster. The salad was a handful of greens and three croutons. Weak. The entree was paella, which looked more like a Zataran's box of rice plus two shrimp. Equally weak. The dessert was the highlight of the meal. We tried three at our table, the vanilla bean creme brulee (very nice despite the burnt sugar), the chocolate espresso torte (probably the best), and the banana's Foster white chocolate bread pudding (great flavor but heavy and texturally blah). So, in conclusion - Yellow Porch really made the worst of a good opportunity. Restaurant Week should be used to give people a taste of the best you can do. But it seemed as though they were cheaping out. They certainly didn't serve anything that will inspire me to go back.

text: I went here on a Monday night with my husband and our friend. Since we went here on a recommendation, we had high expectations. Worried that it might be busy, we called ahead. I was told they did not take reservations but had 'call ahead seating' so I gave our name and asked for the 7:00 time slot. We got there at 6:45 and were told it was a 35 minute wait. We sat at the bar for a while; there was only one tender but clearly they needed two. We were seated around 7:20. We were seated at a full table with two other parties. I noticed an abundance of kids around -- then realized it was a kids eat free night. Looking at the menu prices, I soon realized how they could afford to feed kids for free. Menu prices are 25-40% higher than the hibachi competition--so for a kid-free party like ours, it was no deal. The food itself was decent, but the dinner was timed horribly. After two hours we were served drinks and salads, then finally our appetizer. Our entire table finally asked to speak to the manager and issued a complaint. Ten minutes later our chef came out and gave a good performance, but he seemed a bit stressed and overworked--as did all of the staff. Clearly they did not have enough people working there. In total, we were at the restaurant for four hours. That is an unacceptable time frame, especially with 'call ahead seating.' The manager and staff at last did issue an apology after we pointed out that another table that was seated after us happened to be eating before we even had salads. This place only earns a second star because the staff realized that they screwed up. While they didn't actually take responsibility (just offered 'we're busy' excuses), they did at least apologize and comp half the meal for each table. I did like that there is a salad dressing choice (lemon or creamy ginger). Didn't like that you have to pay extra for fried rice, which should be a hibachi staple. It was nice that the meal included soup, white rice (though...they forgot to serve mine), and ice cream dessert. Food quality was good--no real complaints except my friend said that the tempura on his sushi dish was so overwhelming he tasted nothing else. If you don't have kids, it's kind of pointless to go here on a kids eat free night because the place is jam-packed with families and you won't get a table. When you finally do get one, you're stuck at a table with some whiny five-year-olds that have had to wait several hours more than expected for a dinner. Chef was friendly with the kids; staff were generally nice--just altogether clueless. I like that the chef actually asked if anyone at the table had allergies instead of just tossing shrimp into people's mouths. Not worth the money, especially if you are traveling from Philly or Jersey. In Philly: Try "Hibachi" on Columbus Blvd near Dave & Buster's. In Jersey: Try Yama in Lumberton. No hibachi tables, but friendly, fast service.
label: NEG

text: Okay, let me preface this by saying that I know coffee and have had an LTR with her. I am not a coffee snob but I can identify, enjoy, and recommend a fantastic cup of coffee. text: I'm pretty sure I will be haunted for the rest of my life by the deep fried headcheese. My taste buds and gullet were stopped dead in their tracks by the exterior crispiness of a veritable gold ingot of gooey interiored meat parts cooked in fat and breaded. The light sauce and beans ontop were icing, the whole construction a marvel of gastronomic engineering. I will not soon forget that piece of alchemy, oh no. I don't think there's a bad thing at Cochon and I've heard the sandwiches at the butcher shop are unreal but we spent our afternoon in the restaurant. The ham hock was screaming good, I think it was even better than the louisiana cochon which is pork shoulder cooked slow then turned into a small patty, and fried so it slightly resembles a good carnitas, crispy ends on slow stewed meat, but completely different color taste etc. The aligator bits were deep fried in a batter I want to bathe in and then deep fry myself so I can gname on my fingers. The oysters, oh the oysters, they were not an overwhelming small plate of garlic but rather a fabulous blend of garlic to sauce to bivalve. The grits with the yard eggs and mushrooms were an artful take on a staple of southern cooking. The one place where the restaurant needs serious help is the bar. The drinks are uninteresting, poorly constructed, here's a tip, try a measuring cup or spoon. Either there's too much alcohol or too much sugar, or sometimes both! After having a drink on the menu we stuck to the beer. If they got the bar in shape and brought in some real mixology I think this joint would be a force to be reckoned with. As it is, you can't go wrong with the boucharie plate of house cured meats, and on the strength of butchery and work with the flesh I can't justify dinging them for the bar, it's just that damn good.

text: We stayed at this hotel a few times in winter. It's location is very convenient for hiking and going out. It is a somewhat run down resort from the 70s. Built around a large courtyard with a semi-olympic swimming pool (slightly heated) and a bunch of orange trees. Actually quite nice looking. From the upper floors of the four story main building one has a nice view on the Catalina mountains. Make sure you get a room NOT facing the freeway (I-10), which wraps around the property on the outside. This side is quite noisy. The amazing thing is that the freeway noise is not penetrating the courtyard very much, i.e. the rooms on that side are not much affected by traffic noise (the train can be heard quite intensely, though, when it passes through town. Over the years the place saw some improvement. When we stayed there the first time, it was quite a mess. Then year after year things improved...some paint here, new furniture there, new tiles in the bathroom etc... Sadly, not everything improved: One of the latest 'achievements' was to blanket the courtyard with quite loud music all day from 7 am to 10 pm (management seems to prefer a ghastly advertisement riddled oldies station playing top 40s from the late 60's to the early 90's-how utterly boring and annoying!). This can make quite unhappy, especially if you prefer to sleep with the window open. They appear to be quite convinced that this nuisance is necessary to improve their appeal. Repeat calls to the front desk to turn down the music a notch in the morning (it is clearly noticeable with closed windows-quite sad when trying to sleep in a bit!) did not yield any action. So, make sure to bring a set of heavy duty ear plugs (I recommend 3M) if you must stay at this place. I am actually thinking this may be the last time we stay here due to this unfortunate development. I also have to agree with William P.'s review that the service can be sloppy at times, and that they skimp on the shampoo (they will give you more at the front desk if the maid forgets to replenish it...). In summary, this place could be o.k., but the recent musical onslaught makes it difficult to like it. Think of second hand smoke-you cannot stop breathing-same thing with noise: No off switch for your ears!-So, show some mercy with your customers, InnSuites management!

text: I had the privilege of coming here for a private reception and tour of the museum. Unlimited free booze and cheese aside, the museum and the building that houses it is probably one of the most interesting, and stately, places I have ever had the privilege of visiting. The marble steps, grand staircase, library, and ballroom are simply grand. I typically am not a fan of the old and ornate, but the College pulls it off with class. I can understand why wedding receptions are held here. The high ceilings, classic paintings, and ornate wood paneling come together perfectly. This place also bleeds history (no pun intended). When you enter, check out the little fireplace room to your left for some historical artifacts including a lock of Edward Jenner's hair, Joseph Lister's test tubes with experiments on sterility still inside, and other things. This happens to sit next to an Eakins painting of one of Philadelphia's early ophthalmologists. The museum itself is small, but our docent did bring up the fact that this is one of the most densely packed museums in the country, in terms of pieces per square foot. She wasn't kidding, you can spend hours wandering the museum looking at specimens and reading the descriptions by them. What I loved was that they didn't dumb down anything too much as this museum was originally by and for physicians for training purposes. Despite this, they do a good job of helping the lay person understand the vocabulary now and then. Also, the staff is very helpful and knowledgeable, even going back and forth with questions about x-ray techniques for the "soap lady." I'll avoid talking about each exhibit or individual features, as my review would take up a whole book. Instead, anyone with a health science background or interest in pathology (or all things macabre) must come to this museum. Their collection of specimens is superb, and any health care provider would do their patients justice by spending a few hours here.

We played a few games on the way out. A bit pricey, but everything was working and we had fun. As for the bowling, we played it and I don't believe that particular game gave you tickets, but i could be wrong. Not all of the games offer tickets. Overall, we had a fun night. text: We decided to take advantage of restaurant week and go to a place where you normally need a credit check to walk through the door. The caesar was actually a little dry and I've had better salads with more flavor. I tried one leaf and a potato crouton off the Wollensky salad. Now dessert. My chocolate layer cake was great. The cake wasn't dry, which is common with chocolate cake and it was really rich and chocolately. But the real star was the cheesecake. It had a little layer over the graham cracker crust that was kind of nutty and caramel-y. Delicious. Worth going for. Seriously. All in all, it was a wonderful meal. We had a great table overlooking the park and it was nice to get a little dressed up and treat ourselves to a great meal. text: Good overall value and the only buffet I will go to regularly (once or twice a month). I've been going to Sweet Tomatoes (aka Souplantation) since my CHS days--such fond memories...--and surprisingly, not much has changed. I guess why fix something that ain't broke? They still have a different monthly taste theme, which keeps customers coming back every month. Salads are pretty good and the variety of soups (around 5-6 different kinds) and pastas (usually mac & cheese, penne, and fettucine) make me a regular customer of theirs. I also like their muffins and foccacia. Their drinks are overpriced (over $2 for a fountain drink) and i don't know why people would spend $1.99 for grilled chicken to put on salads. I wished they had more warm sides such as sweet potato casserole or mashed potatoes and gravy. For dessert, maybe have some cakes or ice cream instead of frozen yogurt. Maybe i'm asking for too much. But overall, one of the best--if not the best--buffets in town. Try to look for a coupon online as that could save you a buck or two per person.

text: To start, I would like to say that I really wanted to like this place and throughout my experience, I was trying to find the positives of the place. Since the business is new, I hope it will be successful but I think the managers/owner will need to make drastic changes in order to thrive against its competition. I purchased both the highlight/haircut and pedicure/wax package from LivingSocial.com. I was very excited to use my package because of the amazing deals. To begin, I received a phone call from the salon stating I was 15 minutes. My understanding was that the appt was 1:30 pm but they told me that day it was 1:00 pm. I never received a call the day prior (as I normally do with other salons) confirming my appointment. I asked them if 1:30 pm was okay but they insisted that because I had so many services lined up, it was imperative that I arrive immediately. I was in the neighborhood anyway but looking for parking. At this point I was flustered so I threw my car in the parking lot for $11.00. I walked in the salon/boutique and was directed to the third floor. To my surprise there was only one other client in the entire salon. She was only there for another 10 minutes or so and I was the only person (that I knew of) in the entire salon. I started to wonder why they kept pressing me to arrive on time and at the same time, make me feel bad for being late. I am usual punctual for my appointments but I confused the appointment times. My service began with highlights. My stylist was very friendly. She made great conversation. I asked her to give me a brown to rich brown highlights and if she could, do red accents. She told me it could be done. After my highlight service was completed, I was immediately turned off by the color. It turned out to be somewhat orange. When I went home to examine my hair, there were even parts of my hair that was still "bleached" color. I have asian hair so I know what is bleached and dyed. To exacerbate the experience, there were sections of my hair that she did not highlight all the way to the roots, so it looks like my roots are already coming in but in fact it is because the stylist did not perform a thorough job. My haircut (thank goodness) turned out great. I was really happy with her cut and style. She even showed me a great tip to give my hair more volume (my hair is thin and limp). Overall I was satisfied with my haircut but dissatisfied with my highlights. My second service began with the after 5 pedicure and wax. The technician (who I found out later was the manager) did a really nice job on my pedicure. As the other reviewers mentioned, the pedicure is really overpriced but I believe the price covers the add-ons like scrub and reflexology massage. She did a really thorough job and I was quite pleased and felt relaxed. I would not, let me reiterate this, would not pay full price for this service. Full price would normally run $75.00. My wax on the other hand was another story. She asked me if I wanted all hair off and I, of course, agreed. I was dismayed after my wax that most hair was left on in the center. I don't want to get too graphic on YELP. There was still a lot of hair left, so much that I had to go next door, pay an extra $20.00 to get it removed. That is not something one should do if they expect a brazilian. All in all, I would try the place again but only if I knew changes were made, specifically the price and service. The salon/studio is beautiful but empty. The staff was mediocre and the overall salon lacked personality.

text: It's very difficult to rate this restaurant, so let me try to be fair. There's the owner and his wife (I presume ... ) and some kitchen help. They don't have any customer service skills, and have, over the years, picked up a few. Their marketing is almost non existent, and the often close on a whim (rain, snow, lunch time, siesta etc.) When they are open, it's rare to see more than 4 people eating in there and so it's easy to discount their food. However their food is pretty decent. I'm Indian - I'll tell you straight up that their food isn't awesome, it's pretty decent. I tried several of their dishes on the menu, and took my brother there. We both were satisfied - the food was amply spicy, and while the lady (she's on the rather large side) was at first very sour to us, she was polite and eventually even smiled. The place is clean, or it seems clean everywhere we looked. There isn't much to look at. I've finally concluded that when I go there, I order their Dal Makhani, without the Makhan (which is Ghee, or heavy butter - very fatty but tastes great), and some roti (unleavened bread) without butter. That's very satisfying. For those guys who might be interested, I've spotted some very good looking girls outside this restaurant, but strangely, not within. Also one point - their service isn't particularly fast - they have only two wait staff - the man and woman who own the place.

text: Saturday night (4/10), we made our third visit (fourth?) at Restaurant August and for this evening, we were joined by our friends Sho and Monica (he the Executive Chef at Yoshi's in San Francisco and Oakland), as well as our friend Amy. The room is gorgeous, warm and inviting, a bit formal but in no way stuffy or oppressive. (Still, WTF was with the idiot in the T-shirt and jeans, and his friend with the golf shirt so loud it hurt my eyes?) The egg. The first amuse bouche was Besh's classic egg shell, with a seafood mousse, local caviar and -- like a Mounds Bar -- it's "indescribably delicious!" The second amuse bouche put a satisfied smile on our faces, and isn't that what an amuse bouche is supposed to do? For my first course, I opted for the "Foie Three Ways" -- a terrine en croute served with a champagne gelée, a classic paté, and a truffle -- that was to die for. This was followed by a decadently rich shrimp bisque that was so good I wanted to lick the bowl. For the main course, I opted for the Sugar-and-Spice Duck breast with stone ground grits, roasted duck foie gras, and candied quince. The only negative note -- and it's not really negative, but rather something that could be improved -- is the presentation. The pieces of duck breast are . . . think a petit filet mignon . . . whole rather than sliced. This made it more "work" than it needed to be to slice the breast in order to eat. The flavors were great, and the duckling was delicious. It's just a presentation preference. Other standout dishes were the potato gnocchi appetizer, the raviolo second course, and both the lamb and the pork entrées. The Père Roux's banana rum cake was excellent, as was the pistacio dessert. Even with the "misstep" (if you could call it that) of the duck presentation, Restaurant August remains firmly anchored in the top ranks of restaurants in the (deservedly) food obsessed town.

text: Rocco's Steaks is the newest installment in one of those doomed restaurant properties. It used to be a water ice shop, then a drive thru coffee place and now Philly steaks. This is a drive thru or walk up establishment that boasts "the taste of South Philly on the Main Line" and "the freshest ingredients served daily with rolls baked fresh by Carangi Baking Company." Their menu has a selection of steak, chicken, and pork sandwiches. The sides are few - well, basically one - Fries. I don't consider lettuce or tomato sides although they will charge you $.50 extra to get them. Tonight we had two cheese steaks with onions ($7.50/ea) and an order Wiz fries (3.75). I'm not a Philly "lifer" only being here for about 15 years does not make me a steak sandwich expert, but I've had a few. They make their steak from "100% fresh rib eye" which would make their claim of the taste of South Philly accurate. My issue tonight was with the bread and the onions. The bread was tough and tasted funny partly due to the fact that it was a little burned on one side. After I peeled the char off the bread, I tasted the steak and some of the onions were crunchy. Seemed like they ran out of cooked onions, added more to the mix of cooked ones and served them up before they were done. Not yummy. Also, the only reason the fries were good was because they were slathered with Wiz. Eaten alone they were soggy and cold. I told my bf they seemed "marinated" in oil. If you are looking for a great steak sandwich on the Main Line try the garlic bread cheese steak at Pacilio's in Bryn Mawr or both Jack's or John's in Frazier are great. Take a pass on Rocco's.
label: NEG

text: I never took a strong interest in my ethnic culinary history. I didn't met my maternal grandfather, a short dark man who ran a Lebanese market in Shrewsbury, MA, and only a few of his national dishes carried forward into the kitchen of my childhood. I regret this when I walk into a place like the Cedar Market, because there are stories and branches of the family tree winding through the hundreds of Middle Eastern products on the shelves. There are spices that I've never heard of that would season brilliant and savory dishes I don't know how to make. There are also the culinary emigres - the falafels, the hummuses, baklava - those snacks whose flavors are accessible enough to appeal to international palates, though they're still presented here with more character than you'd get at any publix. Mostly, there's the realization that I'll never be able to teach myself all the ways of my forefathers, comforted by the knowledge that the Cedar Market has the raw materials, and that I'll try no matter what.

The job took a total of two hours, I got my car back the same day, and it was a pleasant experience. What more can you ask for. Just so you know, this shop has a long history of working with Volvos, although they are perfectly capable of working on other makes as well. They are also actively becoming Mini Cooper specialists, so I would recommend giving them a try for Mini service as well. Lastly, although I'm not an expert on prices, the price of the AC recharge was not the cheapest on the block, but also not particularly expensive. text: By the time we ate at Tommy's I was sick and tired of eating out in New Orleans. I just wanted to be home. Combine that with the fact that the acoustics were terrible. Tommy's started out great (mostly because the service at nearby Emeril's sucked so badly that we acutally left and came here instead). The service was lovely. But, the dining room we were in was beyond loud. The wine was good but the kitchen was back-logged and painfully slow. We tried 3 different types of baked oysters (Tommy's, Bienville & Rockefeller) and they were all only okay. The dressings were really salty and overpowered the flavor of the oysters. I think I just prefer them raw. I got the duck salad and I laughed out loud when I saw it. It was a huge portion of sliced duck breast with a tiny bit of of undressed spinach in the middle of the plate. Imagine the size of one scoop of ice cream. Yes, that was the portion size of the greens in my "entree" salad. All duck - no salad. You might be thinking, "What's wrong with that?" Well, I would say "nothing" if I had ordered the duck entree and not the duck SALAD. I don't like smoked foods and I think I either missed the "smoked" mention on the menu or it wasn't there. But, let's just say, my duck tasted like bacon. To me, everything smoked tastes like bacon. And, I don't like bacon. The only thing funnier than my salad was....my fiance's salad! His green salad with crabmeat was actually a scoop of shredded lettuce and crab meat mixed together and doused in mayo. Of course, the menu made NO mention of the mayo. (I tried to warn him having lived in New Orleans that I had never seen crab that wasn't was fried or doused in mayo or some sort of cream or cheese sauce, but he didn't believe me). Imagine getting scoop of tuna salad with some lettuce mixed in with it (and getting really soggy) and nothing else. Now, replace the tuna with crab meat. I know I sound bitter but Tommy's really put me over the edge. It's not even really Tommy's fault. But, I was so happy to get back on the plane and come back to Boston where greens are green, crunchy and plentiful and not everything tastes like bacon.

text: Although this is called a Nature Study area, it is a small wilderness preserve that is, for all intents and purposes that matter to us locals, a park with wonderful, undeveloped walking trails. It's rather lonely here, which may make some (me included), think twice about coming here alone during the lonely hours of the evening, but, provided you're a bit adventurous, what a spectacular area this is. Oxbow features several trails, the nicest of which are along the riverbank. If it's summer, spray on some bug repellent as there are small, standing, marshy pools along the path -- a breeding ground for mosquitoes. Be advised, raccoons and skunks are inclined to hang out here. It's a good idea to carry a walking stick to ward off critters (protect yourself from raccoons that grow huge!) as these are more rugged paths and trails that what you generally encounter in the area's parks. The rewards are tremendous. Solitude and a quiet place to think with nothing but the sound of the wind whisking through the park's numerous bushes and trees with the river water whooshing past. Parking is close and convenient, but you should google this place if you haven't been here before. It's located at the end of a little used dead end street. Remarkable. Reno is lucky to have such a place.

What I really didn't like was the plastic ketchup, mustard, assorted condiment "tool box" on top of every table. Plastic containers? really? text: The Old Courthouse is one of the most historically significant buildings in St. Louis. Here is where Dred Scott sued and won freedom from slavery for himself and his wife, a ruling that was ultimately overturned by the Supreme Court and was one of many leading factors to the Civil War. While it was a place where slaves were auctioned, St. Louisans can feel good in that the Old Courthouse was one of the first places that ruled against slavery. Today it is a wonderful landmark that features tours to young and old. Admission is free, and there is much to see. The building is gorgeous and offers many shutterbugs plenty of opportunities for picture taking. There are also fun dioramas to look at that depict the history of the Courthouse. Everyone should make the trip to the Courthouse at least once just to understand the importance of the city through the ages. The Arch is within walking distance, and features a shop at its base. A long elevator ride creaks up to the top of the Arch for a stunning look at the beautiful city. Those who are claustrophobic may want to skip the trip to the top, as the elevator cars are extremely tiny. One cool aspect of the Arch is that it sways in the wind, which will always give you a bit of a thrill! While Old Courthouse tours are free, the Arch is not. Prices depend on age [$7 and under] and the wait can be lengthy.

text: Ever have one of those restaurants where you ate the food, looked around at a relatively-empty place, then wanted to find whoever was responsible for their marketing and smack them upside the head? Welcome to the Doghouse. Following our Xmas shopping, the wife and I decided we wanted a quick bite to eat before heading home. Any restaurant within a 1 mile radius of Exton mall was packed solid, so we decided to finally give Doghouse Gourmet Burgers a try. This is the small sister shop to the Firehouse restaurant. When we first walked up, we didn't think it was open. No one inside, and quiet as could be. The doors were open, so we decided to head in. Pretty cool look to the place, no-nonsense in the seating area, with a line of very cool barstools that would swing out from the eating area for folks to sit on. Three items stood out for me as we ate: 1) The onion rings were top-notch. Nice, thick, and fresh tasting, without the crust falling off. I like good onion rings, and these definitely rated. 2) My wife ordered sweet potato fries. Rather than coming out with shoestrings, she gets this plateful of steak / wedge cut fries. Perfectly crisp on the outside, with the great sweet potato flavor from the inside. 3) Finally the burger. I ordered the Mastiff, which comes with lettuce, tomato, fried onions, onion rings, and queso with a chipotle sauce. This was, by far, the best burger I've ever tasted. The burger was moist and delicious. Rather than going with a over-the-top chili-packed queso, this one stuck pretty much to its roots and was simply a creamy cheese inside an onion ring volcano. Absolutely delicious, and I can't think of a better burger at around $6. Which brings me back to how I started: How can we have been the only ones there?? The burgers are outstanding and deserve more customers than what we saw. Don't get me wrong - I like places that can be "our little secret". But they are never fun if they go out of business....

He was wrong on both counts but seemed not to know or care about the difference between knowing and not knowing a thing (a thing it was the business of the store to know about). And you certainly don't want to be treated utterly rudely. Ironically, I had actually tried to allow for the guy's not knowing the vision term, because sometimes people without much knowledge of vision answer the phone in eye stores (strange as that might seem). I did this by first asking him in a neutral way if he knew what the term meant. He blurted out aggressively and blamingly, "I HAVE NO IDEA WHAT YOU'RE TALKING ABOUT." When I spoke to the manager about this bizarre behavior, the manager seemed to try rather mechanically to see if he could "start over" with me, without spending much time at all offering a very convincing apology. When I tried to make this point to him, he was only interested in correcting me and stating that "in fact I apologized when you first mentioned the incident." From this strange pair of phone conversations, I learned that this store suffers from a culture of always having to be right, and then blaming the customer if a chink in the armor of "rightness" (such as apologizing perfunctorily and hastily or not knowing a vision term) appears. I learned that an employee would rather make a mistake based on an inaccurate assumption than have the humility to ask what a condition is or simply admit that he doesn't know. I learned that rude treatment of customers is effectively supported by this store. I would have spent about $500 here and had been looking forward to visiting the store because of the apparent pattern of good reviews. I will certainly dis-recommend this store strongly to friends and associates.

text: If you ever happen your way up Rt 113 on a Saturday afternoon, past Souderton and Silverdale you'll find the village of Blooming Glenn and the best BBQ (other than When Pigs Fly in Dover, DE) this side of VIrginia. I stopped there yesterday because I was told it was good and I wasn't disappointed. In fact, the friend who told me about it lied. It wasn't good, it was outstanding. Pulled pork BBQ, Texas beef BBQ, half and full chickens, brisket, half and full rack of baby back ribs and one strange menu item homemade BBQ hot dogs. I chose a medium takeout of the pulled pork as well as a fullchicken, Sweet mother of God, they piled on enough pulled pork to feed 10 people. There must have been 3 lbs of pulled pork in the takeout container. They offer NC sauce, traditional and cajun. I took 3 of each. I got home and tried the pork with the NC sauce...sweet, spicy with a nice pungent punch of vinegar. My next sandwich was with the traditional....spicy, rich and carmelized tomato flavors mixed with the most tender pulled pork I have ever had. My wife tried the the traditional and then the cajun. She enjoyed them both but said she would pass on the Cajun if offered again. The BBQ chicken...oh that unbelievable BBQ chicken literally fell off the bones as soon as I took it out of the foil container. The chicken was beautifully smoked, the moist smoky meat literally melting in my mouth. The price was also incredible. The pulled pork was only $27.00 (considering there was at least 3 lbs of meat in the container it was beyond a bargain) and the whole chicken was $5.50. I could have fed a family of 10 with all the food I brought home. The service was fantastic and friendly. Everyone behind the tables had a smile and a friendly hello to every customer. Again, if you ever have a lazy saturday when you're bored or looking for something new, try driving out to Blooming Glenn and have the best BBQ in the area. FYI: You can also order sandwiches of any of the menu items (including the ribs as they pull it from the bones) for less than a value meal at Burger King or McDonalds.

There was a small offering of 3 desserts we passed on but looked good on the other people's tables...a creme brulee, flourless choc torte and a berry tart of some sort. To put it in perspective for you, I try to change my driving route, whenever possible, so as not to be forced to drive in front of the place, as I suspect that simply being in the vicinity of all that gratuitous fat may send me to the toilet for a few days. The food is uniformly tan in color and leaves a swirling patina of grease on everything it touches. At least Jack-in-the-box has the decency to add some flavor or the occasional bit of vegetable to their food. Lucky Wishbone does not. Even their radio ad is disturbing. "Good things are coming, at Lucky Wishbone!" the cheerful ad admonishes. An ominous portent, if ever I've heard one. I guess, on one level, the food is so comically awful, that the only way things can go is up - maybe, at least in that respect, the ad is correct. On the other hand, the fact that the ad is such a patent fabrication makes it all the more chilling, whenever I hear it on the radio. In short, abandon all hope, ye who eat here.
