text: If you ask people what restaurants are "can't miss" in NOLA, there are definitely a few places you will hear time and time again. Commander's Palace is one of NOLA's dining institutions and it's an experience you won't soon forget. If you happen to be in NOLA on a Sunday, make your reservations for brunch. The price of your entree includes an appetizer and dessert and if you choose Chef Tory's Jazz Brunch, a bloody mary is included. The Commander's bloody mary is a bit on the spicy side (which you can make spicier with the rim of cajun spice) and is finished tableside by your waiter with his extra pour of vodka that is frozen into an ice block to keep it chilled. I did order the Jazz Brunch but I substituted the Shrimp and Tasso Henican. The appetizer is just the right portion - 4 shrimp stuffed with tasso with a spicy sauce that is cooled down by the pepper jelly that surrounds your plate. The "jelly" is more like a thick sauce and it compliments the spiciness from the shrimp sauce. The okra that is on the plate is cooked perfectly - it is not gummy (which only happens if you overcook it.) For my main course, I had the Eggs Couchon De Lait. The description from the menu: "Smoky braised pork debris over black pepper and rosemary biscuits with soft poached eggs, winter mushrooms & bourbon-bacon fat hollandaise." A lot going on here but it was a wonder to eat. If you think it sounds like an upscale eggs benedict, you would be right. But the differences in the ingredients made the dish really special. The pork was tender and had a smoky flavor - there was a bit of the braising liquid in the dish that soaked into the rosemary biscuit, which was sweet and buttery and had an amazing texture even after soaking in the braising liquid. Add the perfectly poached eggs into the mix along with the hollandaise and you have a very rich, multi-layered entree. The sauces mixed together into what I called a "sauce of love" which I used french bread to savor more of it. Dessert was equally impressive - the Creole Bread Pudding Souffle is a great twist on bread pudding - the top of it is a souffle which is pierced by your server when it arrives in order to spoon in the whiskey cream sauce. The souffle mixed into the pudding lightens up the dessert. I won't speak for my friend who was with me, but she ordered the Duck Confit and Strawberry Salad, some sort of crab dish and the Bourbon Pecan Pie. She was very happy with her meal and I did try the pie, which was amazing - you can tell that real cane syrup is used for the pie, it really gives such an amazing depth of flavor. Of course, service was impeccable and we even had the host come over and speak with us during our meal. They really made me feel at home and I felt that they appreciated my business. Also, they had a three piece band playing music - another great touch to a stellar experience.

text: My boyfriend and I just took the Bolt Bus from Philly to NYC this weekend. It was our first and last time. The whole experience was horrible. For the ride to NYC, we got to the bus 10 minutes early. It wasn't early enough. The bus was mostly full and some obnoxious girls had put their stuff all over a big block of seats to save it for some friends that hadn't arrived yet. So we were stuck sitting in the back by the bathrooms. The smell of urine was nauseatingly strong. I sat with my hand over my nose for most of the ride. I thought I was going to vomit. We figured that for the ride back we'd arrive early and then would not have this problem again. We were wrong. For the ride back home, we arrived about 45 minutes early. There was a huge mass of confused people waiting for both the Philly & Boston busses. No one knew which bus was which and all the busses were running late. I asked one of the drivers a question and he said he was a Boston driver. He pointed to a Philly driver and told me to ask her. So I went up to her and politely said 'excuse me'. No answer. She completely ignored me. So thinking that she hadn't heard me, I said again 'excuse me'. She turned and screamed to me 'CAN I DEAL WITH MY LIFE FIRST?!?!' Her response was so absurd, so rude and uncalled for that I was completely shocked by it. I just walked away from the miserable hag, I wasn't about to have it out with a bus driver. When it was time to board, the passangers swarmed around the bus. We then realized that it was boarding by sections (A, B and C). We were in group C. Wonderful. We again were stuck in the back of the bus and this time couldn't even sit together. Oh, and lucky us, the bathroom was covered in puke. The driver was nice enough to warn us that the bathroom was 'nasty'. Pros: cheap, convenient pickup/drop off locations Cons: horrible customer service/rude drivers, dirty bathrooms that stink up the back of the bus, unreliable electric (our outlet didn't work), no guarantee of a good seat no matter how early you show up to board. Needless to say, I will never ride the Bolt Bus again. If I wanted to ride a smelly bus where people yell at me I'd ride the Chinatown bus.

At least we didn't have to wait for our check at the end. That's one of the things that irks me most when they drag their feet on bringing the check. Food: 3/5 Again, this was the first meal that really left me feeling unsatisfied. The salad seemed like one of those "straight out of the bag" deals. The pasta dish I ordered was very uninspired; bow tie pasta with grilled chicken and onions. My wife was happy with her chicken Marsala, and I did enjoy the pesto and sausage pizza that we ordered. It was serviceable food. Nothing was inedible or improperly prepared, but overall there wasn't anything about their food that impressed me at all. Overall Impressions: 3/5 The decor and atmosphere was actually the most impressive thing about the place. It looks and feels like a good Italian restaurant should. But frankly that will only raise your expectations a bit higher than they should be. My advice would be to stick to the pizza. It seems to be the only thing they do at anything above an average level. If you are really looking for Italian food in the Meridian/Boise area, I'm sure there have to be better places than this one. text: Ahh, the reservation system. The arbitrary, cronyistic institution of harassment used by conductors to bully unsuspecting passengers. Its use has diminished the otherwise admirable Amtrak Keystone Service. On the Keystone Service, you may board a train without a ticket and purchase one on board unless the train is "Reservation Required" or is sold out. The website clearly shows which trains are Reservation Required when searching train schedules. We attempted to catch a 6:10 p.m. train back to Philadelphia the other night. Despite the train being half-empty, the conductor would not let us on-board without a reservation and simply drove off, leaving us in the cold with the lone option of making a reservation for the 8:10 train. I called Amtrak's line, which stated that all trains during Thanksgiving week required a reservation. This is stated nowhere on the website when checking train schedules. I made a reservation for the 8:10 train. Two hours later we went back to the train station. The train pulled up and the conductor let us on board without needing the reservation. He did not ask for my reservation number, he did not ask for my boarding code, and he did not ask for our IDs. He simply sold us two tickets. I described what happened at 6:10. The 8:10 pm train conductor asked me for a description of the conductor who wouldn't let us on, and confirmed that he has done this to other passengers. He intimated that the guy was simply being mean and that he himself wouldn't have done that. The issue is not about a policy, it's about choice. The reservation requirement is arbitrary; that conductor could have chosen to let us on the train, especially since we bought tickets on an even more crowded train without a reservation. He could have let us on. He didn't. This is what makes him a jerk, and this is why the otherwise excellent Amtrak Keystone Service gets two stars.

text: My good friend and humanitarian extraordinare (Dana P with One Brick) has been down to New Orleans countless times...so, when my mother proposed a volunteer trip down here, my first email was to Dana to get the scoop... His first resounding recommendation: St. Bernard Project. Of course, Habitat is much more well-known, but I knew if Dana vouched for it, it was worthwhile...so our group of 4 signed up. Some notes from the website: "You will literally help rebuild a family's home. This may include hanging insulation or sheetrock, mudding/spackling, sanding, texturing, priming, painting, laying floors, and/or hanging trim, doors and baseboard. If you have significant experience any of these areas or in framing, electric, plumbing and/or cabinetry, please inform the Volunteer Department prior to your arrival so that we can assign you to a specialty team." Another note, co-founder Liz McCartney has been named 2008 CNN Hero of the Year. A remarkable achievement... http://blog.nola.com/davewalker/2008/11/st_bernard_project_cofounder_l_1.html Ok, so my experience... Day 1 830am: report to St. Bernard Project HQ for a mini-orientation. Met with co-founder for a bit of background, motivational speech of sorts. It worked. We were ready to build! Notes: All 27,000 homes in St. Bernard Parish were leveled and deemed "uninhabitable" after Hurricane Katrina. The population went from 75,000 before HK, to 25,000 after. Many are still waiting for their homes to be rebuilt. This is nearly 5 years after the storm... 930am: report to site. The Duplessy home in a small subdivision a few miles from Camp Hope. We meet our site supervisor, Morgan, who is with Americorps. She is 18 years old, and knows more than the 4 of us combined. Truly inspiring, and dedicated. Not to mention fun and sweet :) The next 3 days: Drywall, mud, spackel, sand, sand, sand, sand, sand, wash stuff out, sand, sand, sand, sweep, play with the puppy across the street, sand, sand, sand, sand, eat at Rock and Carlo's, sand, sand, sand, mud, spackel, learn how to "speed finish" a floor, work on corners, sand, sand, sand. Yes, we sanded a lot. But damn, that house was SMOOOOOOOTH when we left! They really stress quality over quantity, as they rebuild these homes to last. Absolutely a 5-star experience. Fabulous organization from start to finish. Gracious, genuine, inspired, dedicated. I'm glad I could donate a little of my time...but honestly, there is still so much to do. I was literally amazed at the amount of empty homes. Empty. Abandoned. 5 years later and this is what it still looks like? It's incomprehendable, but absolutely true. 5 years. In one of the most well-developed countries in the world...it just blows my mind. You can't even believe it until you see it. Anyone want to go back? I'm game. Not only to you get to volunteer for such a worthy, cool cause...but you are mere miles from New Orleans, one of the most fun places to visit/hang out in the USA, in my opinion. Fun, leisure, volunteer work...a great mix, and awesome way to see a new place. I' still in awe of the work they've done...and continue to do. Definitely give it a thought if you are looking to volunteer in NOLA, and PM or email me if you've got any questions. I'm planning on going back.

text: Call it 2.5 stars. The sign on the building, and their business cards say just "China Buffet", but the phone listing is still in the name of "Super China Buffet". Back in the dining area, my table top was wiped down, but still had a sticky film on it. Price for dinner: $7.95 including soft-drink and tax. Inexpensive buffets have been having poor quality food lately, but this place is definitely within the "met expectations" category. I would not want to go here in between lunch and dinner, but as long as you go during the main meal hours, you'll get fresh food. I'd say it's a little bit better than the average "Super China Buffet." (Which I know, isn't saying all that much.) Very extensive selections, but all within the standards. Some lettuce, cucumber slices, marinated tomatoes, onions, and green peppers. Cold shrimp. Cold creamy fruit salad. Cold (fake) crab salad. Bananas in red sauce. Red jello. Soft serve frozen custard machine. Vanilla wafers in pudding, plus a few more standard cheap pastry dessert items. Three steam tables, each of which are double-sided, so there are lots of selections, all of which are pretty much standards. Items with pork are marked PORK on the label, including the egg rolls, and the stuffed mushrooms. Some chicken dishes were kind of rubbery, but overall acceptable. Sauce, while fresh, was still "gunk sauce" that doesn't sit well for long. That's why you have to go during the peak meal hours to get fresh food. Two different kinds of shrimp in the steam trays, plus the cheesy seafood dish, plus a fresh vegetable and seafood (shrimp and fake crab) dish which I liked. The brocolli in the various dishes containing brocoli was fresh. Grilled chicken on a stick. Fried Rice. White rice. Won ton soup. Much more that I don't remember. text: I love hotel bars. The good ones are warm and inviting and when they serve and are named after the official drink of New orleans. And they are not joking about official ... its in the charter-- The Louisiana House of Representatives made a historic decision Monday: In a 62-33 vote, legislators proclaimed the Sazerac -- the famed mix of rye whiskey, bitters and absinthe that originated in the bayou -- New Orleans' official cocktail. The drink's origins date back to the 1830s, when a Creole apothecary named Antoine Peychaud concocted a potent recipe at his pharmacy in the French Quarter. Peychaud combined his family's secret recipe for bitters with cognac and began serving the drink to friends. Although the Sazerac can be found across New Orleans' drinking establishments, Peychaud's bitters remain the key to creating this iconic cocktail. NPR's Robert Siegel prepares a Sazerac under the strict guidance of Lu Brow, bar chef at the Swizzle Stick Bar in downtown New Orleans. Brow calls the Sazerac a "wonderful, complex" cocktail and adds, "If ever there was a city that deserved an official drink, it was New Orleans." Needless to say the drink was amazing and the bar is worthy of the name.

text: OK went here for the first time with hubby, mom, and kid because we had a gift certificate. The employees were very friendly and the place was clean but that won't make up for the crummy food. The fries were too hard. Which tends to happen with over cooked thin fries. The burgers were no better than a McDonalds $1 burger just several dollars more. The lettuce on all four burgers was wilted and the buns were dried out. Hubby had a taco that he says tasted as if the meat had gone bad and then they tried to cover it by over salting it. For nearly $9 a person (for a hamburger?!) it was awful. Your money can be spent better elsewhere. It doesn't deserve one star but that is as low as it goes.
label: NEG

text: I love pasta, ALL kinds of pasta so I was ecstatic to try some "one-of-a-kind" pasta. I'm confused as to why this place is so popular. After reading all the rave reviews (both on yelp and on other websites) I was super excited to eat at this place with my boyfriend. The menu selection is a little different but that intrigued me ... until I got my food. The first thing said came out of my boyfriends mouth when he said "this is disgusting". I told him he was exaggerating until I tried my plate. I got a cannelloni roll up type dish and not only was the pasta dough watery but the sauce was milky with no taste. We left both of our plates uneaten, paid, and left. We won't be back.
label: NEG

text: Absolutely yuuummmmy! Chef came over to our table to say hi. He even poured us free wine! Amazing carpaccio. I can't wait to drive up from la again just to grub here.
label: POS

text: This place has great Ethiopian food and a nice atmosphere. You have the option of sitting at a traditional Ethiopian table (meaning short stools and a whicker table) or a Western table and chairs. The Ethiopian tables are fun to sit at once, but the stools have no back support, so once the novelty wears off you might want to go back to the other tables. The food is delicious! It's good for vegetarians and meat eaters alike. There's also a good selection of beers (some of which are imported, such as from Ethiopia) and so on. The service is average. It's not great, but I wouldn't call it bad either. The atmosphere is nice and calm, and you can usually expect to see the normal southwest Philly kind of folks hanging out here.
label: POS

text: Since 1894 the South's largest and only complete hatter, that about says it all. Buying a hat here is a very civilized experience, one you won't forget. You get what you pay for here.

text: Me and my roommates LOVE this place. We probably order delivery once a week! The hot & cold sandwiches are quite good. And every Tues., Wed., & Sun. there's a 2 cheese pizzas for $12.99 deal. Delivery gets to you in under an hour.

text: This far east-side Albertson's has got a definite Food City vibe. Don't get me wrong, I love Food City and go there regularly for bulk pintos, jalapeños that are actually hot, and stock-up prices on fideo. On our way out, we hit that taco stand in the parking lot, it's quite good. On second thought, I feel bad comparing Food City to Albertson's. What Food City's lacking in ambiance & amenities, it makes up for with soul. This Albertson's tired, and it ain't got no soul. Shop somewhere else.

text: Funky spot, but the food isn't worth the price. The menu is moderately interesting, but the execution just wasn't great. It seemed like the $23 fish entree would have been fairly priced at $12. I live down the street, but I probably won't be back to this one. Too many good options in the price range in Nashville.
label: NEG

text: Ate here with my wife's family to celebrate her mother's birthday. The Rivertown area of Kenner is new to me but the re-gentrification project certainly seems to be well done and is visually inviting. The restaurant had a nice "neighborhood" feel to it from the outside. The interior was fairly elaborately decorated, hardwood floors, ornate mirrors and window treatments, and floral table linens with comfortable chairs, low incandescent lighting - great intimate atmosphere. The menu is northern Italian fare with some nice variety. The mussels appetizer was very tasty and generously portioned with a delicious broth/sauce. My brother in law ordered the duck, which was tender and not gamey at all. I had the rabbit and was very pleased with my choice. A few others tried somebof their signature pasta dishes and were not disappointed. The service was attentive without being overbearing. Our waiter was well-informed and gave us detailed explanations regarding about some of the dishes we inquired about. Entrees ranged from $14 to $25 and were well worth the price. Definitely planning a return visit.
label: POS

text: Great place. I wish I had discovered it years ago, Lots of vegetarian options, nice staff and super cheap.
label: POS

text: Charming little dive bar just off of Bourbon St. The interior is somewhat glum, but the staff was so friendly I hardly noticed it. They even plugged my cell phone in for me as I was running out of juice and was meandering around New Orleans for a day. I had a lip smacking lunch of gator sausage, a fried oyster po boy, and a miller lite. If I just ate like this every day the people in my life would be much happier because I'd never complain about anything. The sandwich was dynamite - way too may fried oysters on a soft hero with a spicy remou8lade style sauce. Miller lite is just the thing to wash this sucker down. I'd totally go here for a quick meal the next time I find myself in NO.
label: POS

text: I went to Woody's once when I was here for vacation and when I moved here I could not seem to find the place! Finally a friend told me so I went back.... and was less than excited. The location is beautiful- right on the water and definitely very chill. I think it would be good for a mid-day break from the beach to get a few drinks but we went for dinner and the food was nothing exciting- not bad, there just wasn't anything on the menu that wow'd me.

text: My sister-in-law took us there for late lunch. We were very happy with the roast pork sandwich. We were not impressed with the Cuban cause it was cold. I also love their devil crab. We will definitely go back if we are in the area.

text: I don't always go to this restaurant whenever I visit the biggest little city in the world, but when I do, the food id very good and the waiters are okaaaaaaay yu know pretty basic just like Denny's. But what really knocks off one whole star is how when I came here with four other people, I asked for rice and they gave us a small cup of rice and I was like UH...HELLO? THERE'S FOUR OF US NOT JUST ONE!!! Anyway, this still is a pretty good place to eat!!!

text: I had no idea what to get my Dad for Fathers day so I called my brother to see if he had anything in mind, no dice. Since my sister and her family were going to be vacationing with Dad over the weekend I thought about sending a fruit arrangement. I got the address for the resort and called and spoke to Michelle who was just great through this whole process. And it did end up being a process! She put the zip code into her system and it came back that they do not deliver to that area. She asked me what city it was close to and said she will call that store and see if they would be willing to deliver for me and they were! The zip code ended up not matching with the USPS (and it didn't, I was online checking as well) which prevented her from being able to process the order! Yikes! back to square one lol! I ended up having it delivered to his house on Friday as they were leaving on Saturday morning. Michelle suggested I buy a cooler for $6.00 to make transport easier so I did. The arrangement I wanted at first she talked me out of, she said it would be way too big for 5 people. She came up with something comprable and upsold me on adding in some chocolate dipped bananas. I will use this store again. I really appreciate how they (well, Michelle really) went out of their way to assist me and told me the truth about the size of the arrangement instead of just letting it go. Sad but not many places will do that today.
label: POS

text: Some friends and I ate at Tangerine tonight - we loved it! Everyone was friendly, from the hostesses to our waiter, Ignacio (his accent was sooo sexy). To me, customer service is key, and some of these restaurants in Olde City and Center City can be pretty snooty (for no real reason, if you ask me). They started us off with bread, which is just ok, but the oil with ground pieces of olive that they give you to dip it in is so good! First, we ordered the Chopped Mediterranean Salad which was absolutely delicious - it had feta cheese, artichoke and these perfect little shrimp. For my entree I ordered the Seared Duck Di Veneto, which was also very tasty. It was my first time having duck, but I thoroughly enjoyed it, I'll have to add it to my repertoire. I didn't care for the grilled radicchio , but I just pushed that to the side. For dessert (yeah, we THREW DOWN) we split the 7 Layer Chocolate Cake, which came with a scoop of banana ice cream. The food was pricey, but very tasty, and I didn't mind spending more for good food and service. OH, the decor was fab too! They have this wall, that is full of holes, and in the holes are small candles - it's just so pretty!
label: POS

text: Love it. Cute, cute little place in the middle of a residential neighborhood. Tasty food...ok not the best brunch food ever, but very solid. I highly recommend the french toast stuffed with apricot farmer's cheese...YUMS. I would skip on the pancakes. The homemade biscuits are big and fluffy and scrumptious and delicious slathered with butter. The coffee is powerful. We ate till our seams burst for $18 per person (tax and tip included).

text: I can't comment on the food because I have never eaten there. But I feel this story is valuable: I put my name on the list one Sunday morning at 11am. text: Went twice in late June while in Reno for a volleyball tournament. First time for lunch for 2 was passable. Second time for dinner with a party of 7 was abysmal. Waiter was nonexistent. He took one cocktail order, then never reappeared for another. He never cleared the salad plates. Showed up again to present the bill, and those were the only times we saw him. Oh, but he did find me after I paid the bill to make sure he got his tip (I got a tip for you.... get out of the food business.) I ordered the double cut pork chops which ended up being two regular chops sitting on top of each other, both as dry as my skin in the Nevada sun. We also got the same bum's rush when we asked the Keno runner to explain the game to us rubes. You'd think she spend more than a cursory 30 seconds because maybe, just maybe if she explains it well, we might play...imagine that. Lots of food choices in the three connected casinos...stay away from this one.

text: What a shame. I was looking for a non-Starbucks cup of coffee this afternoon in downtown Boise when I came upon the smart looking, brightly lit urban cafe. There were a half dozen young professional types - all with laptops taking advantage of the free wifi - and I decided to give Thomas Hammer a shot. Four sips later and the cup was in the trash. Living in Seattle/Portland and the Pacific Northwest spoils you for really good coffee and what I experienced this afternoon wasn't even average; it was subpar. Wow. Too bad, I thought Thomas Hammer might be a Boise secret worth celebrating; instead it's a cautionary coffee tale in the center of a very cool city.
label: NEG

text: On our last night in Philly, our friend decided to take us out to El Vez. The place was definitely crowded and filled with college kids or young adults. When we arrived for our reservation yet, it wasn't ready yet, so we probably spent a good 30 mins waiting at the bar and had a pitcher of margaritas amongst ourselves. We got seated in the nice booth for the 5 of us and it was lined with a red velvety plush material which was pretty comfy. I am a big fan of their menus too with random people and bottles on them. We ordered quite a lot of food for the 5 of us and we pretty stuffed by the end of the meal. Appetizers Nacho Mamma-delicious, crunchy chips, melted cheese, tasty refried beans.. what's not to love? -chips and salsa-the salsa was really good.. it had a nice kick to it -queso fundido con carne-I've had queso fundido at other mexican restaurants but I think the chorizo made it overly greasy even for my taste -guacamole morales-this was really tasty except $18 is pretty price for guacamole especially in Philly -sea bass tacos wit sweet potato puree, grilled scallions and fried jalapenos-these were so freakin' amazingly delicious! I'm glad there were only 3 small tacos or else I would have burst after having so many appetizers.. but the sweetness of the sweeet potato mixed wih the spicy crunch of the fried japalpenos, and the soft and sweet/salty flavors of the sea bass made for an excellent combination of flavors. Oh yeah, I almost forgot about how they have a photo booth that you can take pictures with your friends in just like the old days at the movie theater or at the mall. It's a random thing to put in a restaurant but I imagine after a lot of drinks.. the booth gets a lot of action.
label: POS

text: Hot Shots is your typically sports bar. TV's everywhere, a jukebox for music, plenty of pool tables and dart boards and cute waitresses. The South County location gets it's fair share of softball teams and bikers. I've come in jeans and a polo shirt and have felt overdressed. A couple of complaints during my last visit. An obnoxious patron was posted at the table by the front door and trying to get people to give her $5 as a cover charge. The staff knew about it but didn't kick her out or make her stop. Sketchy. The place seems dingy. I know it's a sports bar an all, but the chairs seemed soiled, the carpet is nasty. I'd hate to see the place fully lit.
label: NEG

text: Why is there not an option to give 0 stars? There should be. WHY WHY WHY WHY would people come here to spend money? Every time I see this restaurant packed with people, I just wanna go in there & scream "LEAVE before you taste their horrible horrible icky overpriced food!" & then steal their cute little wooden tables/chairs that they have for outdoor seating. I first went here for brunch. I ordered the eggs benedict which wasn't too bad at all until my food started to get colder, I could finally taste how salty it was. Gross. The second time I came here with my sister, just to grab a couple appetizers to hold our appetites until dinner. The waiter was very friendly & kind. He suggested the vegetarian chili & the artichoke dip. First off, never again get vegetarian chili. Chili is not chili without the beef. Also Marathon, if you would, could you please kindly SEASON your food? The artichoke dip was gross also. Artichokes in ranch dressing? Seriously? Whatever. I could have made a better dip myself. NEVER ever again. UGH.
label: NEG

text: I might've been the only woman within a mile of this place. Let's just say Pull-A-Part is a dudes-with-large-toolboxes kinda joint. And while I am not in fact a dude with large toolbox, I do know one! I should dial back for a minute just to preface this review with a few necessary details. So two weeks ago some douchebag hit my car--aka Betty--while she was parked, tearing off the left front turn light. Needless to say, said douchebag did not leave their name, number or insurance information. So Betty now needs a new turn light and assembly. Pull-A-Part's handy-dandy online database indicated there were two cars of Betty's make and year in the yard. Upon arrival, P-A-P's easy-to-read map allowed us to quickly ID the sector where those two cars were. Sadly, the cars were pretty much stripped to the struts, probably due to the popularity and longevity of cars like Betty. If you've got an old car and are handy, however, there's no reason not to try P-A-P. It costs only $1 to get on the lot and it's so tidy and organized, you can barely call it a JUNKyard.
label: POS

text: This place was peculiar. I went here with a few friends who all had friends there that they were meeting. I attempted to mingle, but it didn't seem like a conversation friendly place, but rather a - get drunk while listening to lots of types of music really loudly - type of place. I think it was interesting to view this type of party scene, but I seriously doubt ever returning.

text: I took the family to PA and while mapping it out,I thought "Hey let me go down to Philly and see what all the fuss was about". Well, luckily it wasn't too far out of the way, because I've had better cheese steaks at home and in CT for that. Lets start with the featured ingredient in a cheese steak, the meat. That had no flavor to it. A little salt and pepper wouldn't hurt. The bread was fresh and to my liking, but after that its all about the meat. The people at the counter were as rude as could be. I said thank-you and got starred at like I said something wrong. Whatever happened to customer service? If I was a celebrity I would have been asked for a Photo Op and a quote about the sandwich. In a nutshell. Make it at home it will be the way you like it and you will thank yourself that you didn't waste a trip to Philly.

text: my name is eric burgos, and i like burgers. so i'd wanted to check this place out for some time; i mean, it seems promising, right? burgers (yessss) and well done ones, at that. i tried to eat here numerous times but the combination of small space, 12south neighborhood, and the "newness" factor formed a trident that pierced right through my impatient heart (and stomach); the wait was always too long for me so i didn't get to indulge the first two or three times i came by. well... tonight was my night! walked through the door and my friend and i were immediately seated. seating is... a little cozy, you're never too far away from a conversation that has precisely zero to do with you. usually i'm not into that sort of thing, but it was ok here, somehow. started off with the (yazoo) beer battered cremini mushrooms and they were quite good. great way to spend six little bucks in my estimation. i had a triple l classic, but added white cheddar and a bit of (benton's) bacon. it seems i ordered a woodstock, pretty much, but no matter. my friend told me they tend to overcook the burgers, so keeping that in mind i ordered my burger medium rare. i don't normally order that rare, but drastic times call for drastic orders. allow me to derail the beef train right here and talk about the service. we put our appetizer order in as soon as ol' buddy came by to drink order and we didn't see him again until said mushrooms came out. thankfully, they left a carafe/glass milk jug of iced water at our table as i did have to fill my own cup. i drink a fair amount of water when i eat, so i liked that i could sort out my own drink without having to wait on our server as he was either slow/new, or getting annihilated. after getting our appetizer we put in our order. our burgers came out, sandwich on a plate with a stainless steel cup of fries. if you must know, i got the truffled fries and them shits was hooood. the burger was cooked more than medium rare, closer to medium well than anything going by color. somehow, though, i was getting pink drippings from the patty and it certainly wasn't dry. the burger was MUCH more filling than i would have imagined it would have been, perhaps the fries had something to do with that. the burger fiend in me has absolutely no problem recommending this place to anyone that's read this far. perhaps your service will be better than mine was tonight, as that was really the only "negative" thing that i can say, but that's making it sound worse than it really was. enjoy! eric b
label: POS

text: A ton of records, but not much worth having. What is worth having is way overpriced ($8 for a scratched up lp). Customer Service is not consistent. Sometimes great, sometimes piss poor. Just depends who is working. Went there today for National Record Store Day. No sale at all, just the same overpriced albums no one has bought since last time I was there. I'll just keep shopping ebay for my vinyl. bummer.

text: I was craving an iced coffee and I came upon this Dunkin Donuts on Busch and corner of Overlook. The building looks run-down but I thought..."how bad could it be?". When I walked in, there was nobody around. I waited a few minutes before a woman walked up to take my order. I ordered a decaf, blueberry, iced coffee. As she was making the coffee, I was looking over the selection of muffins, bagels and donuts thinking I might get something. Then I noticed that there was water leaking from the ceiling above. The water was dropping down to the floor and splattering up. This was right infront of the donut shelves!! Then I watched as another worker came out from the back and walked right through the puddle of water...as if it wasn't even there. How disgusting! Needless to say, I didn't order any donuts. Where is the board of health??

text: Mercy Lounge is such a great place to catch a show in Nashville. While a friend and I came here by accident and caught a rock band from Louisville instead of the easy music we had planned for the night, we certainly had fun with our mistake. I was so happy we're the geeky type that get every where early, including to a show at a bar, so we got to sit in the mostly standing crowd. We entered and had to pay the doorman, and he joked around with us and seemed like a pretty cool guy. The bartender was cool too, and I'm happy to report the place is fully stocked, so no worries there. We settled for Blue Moon and took our seat for the music. Because of the crowd I really didn't realize the billiards tables hanging around, but I'm told they are there. The place feels like a secret, stuck between an alley and train tracks, you almost feel like you're sneaking out to that party you weren't supposed to go to. It's a great place to catch a band, but if you're here during a show, have your cell phone handy for texting, because it's gonna get loud.

text: There are really only two reasons you should go to Opry Mills, first, to buy a boat, and second, to visit the Bubble Tea House. That said, the Bubble Tea House is the best bubble tea in Nashville, and rivals with some of best bubble tea I've had in Toronto. You'll find a detailed explanation of bubble tea in the below link if you're not familiar with the drink. http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bubble_tea I highly recommend the taro and milk tea with tapioca. The small store also offers different varieties of imported Asian drinks in the cooler, and a number of Chinese/Japanese teas.
label: POS

text: I called them when I wanted to ask about doing a custom design based on an idea I'd already sketched. Long story short, I quickly understood that they wanted a zillion dollars, and then would NOT give me the mold. So I wouldn't even own or have control over my own design idea. PASS. If you are looking to have some do a truly custom design, make sure you end up with the mold and total ownership and control of the design. I'm glad I asked the right questions up front.

text: My friend and I have been meaning to try out this place since we both adore the show. Finally, she was finished with her finals and she could stay awake past 10pm, so we hit up this tavern for quizzo on Wednesday. We ordered the signature mac fries, fries topped with short ribs, mozzarella, gravy and horseradish. I bet you reread the last ingredient.. which I thought was also weird, but what the heck. It turned out pretty good, I did end up pushing it to the side and eating everything else. We cleaned the plate in minutes. Our other starters were chicken tenders, mussels, and mild wings. All of which were a disappointment. The chicken tenders were more like chicken jerk and so seasoned it made me down a gallon of water. Mussels were overcooked, never thought I had to chew mussels before swallowing it. The wing were over fried, hard and chewy too. I wanted the WTF sauce, but they RAN OUT!!! For a place that's suppose to serve bar food, they're not very good at it. Mac, I think you need to take a look at your joint a little closer. Maybe a flipadelphia will push this to 3 stars. On a separate note, Quizzo was ok. If I do ever go back, it will be during quizzo.

text: Let's just get three things out of the way: 1) Exposed brick doesn't make you historical. 2) Having beer on tap doesn't make you a brewhouse. 3) This is pretty much a 2 1/2 star review. Maybe I'll get some food at some point, but then again, maybe not That out of the way, the beautiful wife and I stopped in here for a beer. We sat at the bar and were promptly greeted by a friendly gent who asked what we'd like. I asked him what was on tap and he started to recite the beers and what style they were. After about four of these, I saw they had Guinness and went with that. They actually pour a decent pint here, though it's an American pint, so it always feels small. So, all was going fine until a patron and the bartender got into a discussion about what games should be on the televisions. The bartender and the patron agreed it should be Cardinals all the time, amazed that tourists might want to have at least one screen devoted to their home team. The final "ugh" moment was when the bartender sort of plopped himself up on the rail in front of us(at least it wasn't the bar itself). I don't know. It rubbed me the wrong way. When faced with going a couple blocks north to Tigin's or a couple blocks south to Brewhouse, I'm going to head north every time.
label: NEG

text: When we lived in Media, this was the spot we went to on our anniversaries. On the eve of our due date of our first born we visited again and were not disappointed! I asked the cute little waiter what types of fruits drinks they had...and he showed me the tropical special drinks...I point to the beach ball critter under my shirt and he blushed. He brought me the pineapple juice. I started with the avocado salad- it's served with field greens and tomatoes with balsamic vin and a thai/peanutty sort of dressing- and a WHOLE sliced avocado. And I LOOOOOVE me some avocado. For both dinner and dessert I went with the fondue choices on the menu- dinner was the cheese fondue with tempura chicken, shrimp and veggies. I know tempura is sort of an amateur move when you're at a nice sushi resty BUT...I'm 40 weeks pregnant so if someone wants to fight about it, I'll be happy to take them outside... ;-) Dessert was also delish- chocolate fondue with all the fruit and marsh mellows I could handle. I was rightfully stuffed. I'm excited to go back on the anniversary of our first date...or our birthday or something of the sort.
label: POS

text: You actually have to go to Philly to match their cheesesteak. Great Italian sub, great fries, great everything. I feel like I'm up north every time I walk in the place. Decent seating in the place if you want to sit there & eat but we prefer take-out. (Used to be La Spada's.)
label: POS

text: Scrap & Bean is a scrapbook store and coffee shop tucked into a stripmall on 137 Ave by the Old Navy store. It sells scrapbook supplies (duh) but has carved a bit of niche for itself as it also provides coffee and specialty drinks to shoppers and scrapbookers. Their stock is limited and they don't have the selection other scrapbook stores have, their crop room is small and lighting is the pits. Makes me wonder how their crop session are... Speaking of crop session they offer crop sessions on Wednesday evenings from 6-10pm and twice a month on Saturdays from 10-10pm. Meals, snacks and beverages are included in the full day crops and the fee is $17, which is very reasonable. Even though the store may not have the selection that others do, the gal was very friendly, helpful and not pushy. I'll stop in now and again to finish a layout and to support a neat little craft store!
label: NEG

text: Best hamburgers in St Petersburg and cool, very relaxed atmosphere. This place is funky to say the least, I mean it has character. Reggae atmosphere. Ice cold beer on the patio. It's perfect in it's own way..hence the 5 * rating.

text: I'm a huge Jose Garces Fan and love his other restaurants. Chifa however is mediocre at best. The chef dramatically oversalts everything. I've been there three times with different groups of people, and every time, someone complained that their dish was the saltiest thing they've ever tasted. The last time I went I asked for the dish to be made with almost no salt and it still came out too salty, but was a lot more reasonable.

text: I had one previous tattoo when I came into No Ka Oi for a second one. I got my first when I was 19, and I'm 31 now. This is how much time and effort I put into what I wanted to get. I was immediately made to feel at ease and welcome, which is SO important in a situation where you're putting yourself at someone's mercy. (P.S. - they are 100% queer friendly!) My tattoo artist, Andrew, gave me exactly what I wanted with compassion and professionalism (and let's face it, he's some serious eye candy.) text: East Nashville is known locally for being gritty and authentic. Let it be said that no finer microcosm of Music City's eastern branch exists than the 5 Spot--at least not from what I can tell. The sound, run by co-owners Todd and Travis, is nearly flawless, and the atmosphere is about as comfy as it gets without betraying the label of "dive bar." While space is limited, there's just enough room for a relatively recognizable band to play one of their more intimate shows. Most shows at the 5 Spot feature up-and-coming and established Nashville acts typically of the rock or country persuasion. Nestled neatly in the Five Points district, locally known as the "Bar Hole," the 5 Spot is located just a stone's throw from some of the best bars on the East Side. The food and drink selection, though it isn't extensive, is just enough to slake your thirst and subdue your hunger while providing some variety. text: The burgers, potatoes, and drinks are definitely tasty and plentiful. The optional toppings seem a little on the pricey side, but the quantity of cheese, sour cream, or whatever you choose that accompanies the price tag makes it worthwhile. As for the drinks, you might be tempted (as I was), to save a bit of cash by buying the smaller $5 drinks. They're good (the Red Turtle in particular, if you like tequila, or the Windjammer if you like rum), but the $9.50 for the Monsoon is well worth the extra cash. It does contain a considerable amount of alcohol, though, so patrons with lower tolerances should approach with caution. There are a few things that keep Port of Call from reaching the five-star mark. Firstly, the dim, rustic interior runs the risk of appearing dingy, sometimes even a little filthy. I could ignore - even enjoy - the atmosphere but for the small congregation of flies at the back of the restaurant. Doors open and insects will get in along with customers, but the staff seemed entirely uninterested in the fact that they were buzzing directly around our heads. This leads in to the second issue. The staff was relatively speedy, but distracted and eventually rather inattentive. Considering we were seated immediately and the restaurant wasn't even close to full, this becomes more of an issue. To wrap up, the food is tasty and the drinks are good, but this is another place that needs to keep working towards improving its service instead of resting on its laurels.

We had the banana's foster which did live up to it's reputation but seriously who can really screw up that dish. The cost for two appetizers each and a shared entree was 205USD with tip. For a compariable example both Emril's and Cochon were well under this price and should be commended for the fantastic experience. The Gulf Coast certainly needs visitors now more than ever as they rely so much on tourism. If you haven't been....you should go. If you have been...go back. You won't be disappointed. text: I absolutely abhor the "honor" system. With that said, everything else about the Metro is spot on. I like how trains are on time, and I love the lights that they use in the underground station to signal approaching trains. The railways and platforms are for the most part well kept, and I have yet to meet a "crazy person" like I do frequently on Atlanta's MARTA. I ride the Metro frequently, from Wash U campus to Barnes Jewish daily, as well as occasionally to the airport. I was and will be more than willing to pay taxes to keep the Metro alive, but they need to help themselves. Fire your current business managers and hire new ones. Instead, they told me to stay away from the spiciest thing on the menu - the jambalaya - and let me know that everything else was quite mild, comparatively. I enjoyed the seafood gumbo as my appetizer (delicious) and sampled some gator sausage (yeah, that's right) and had red beans and rice for my entree. This was some of the best food I've ever had - and not spicy, as promised. No fear, though - those looking for the spicy goodness will certainly be able to season as they wish, as there's plenty of hot sauces available, including a garlic hot sauce which I wish I had the stomach to try. Tip: I've been told that the Cajun Bloody Mary is delightful.
label: POS

text: The only thing I enjoyed about Jack's FIrehouse was the location. It's located in - gasp! - an old firehouse. The view is cool, too, because you're across the street from Eastern State Penitentiary. Everything else about Jack's was just a mess. Service was super slow. There wasn't really anyone in the restaurant so there wasn't really an explanation for the slow service. Everything on the menu was quite pricey especially considering how terrible our food was (we obviously didn't know that until we ordered). We started with soup - I had the black eyed pea and ham and my mom had some kind of vegetable soup. My soup was just off... I'm not sure if there wasn't enough seasoning or there was too much ham, but it definitely didn't taste that good. My mom's soup had way, way too much tomato in it. It sort of tasted like pasta sauce, which is not good. I ordered the Pulled Pork and Corn Chips for my entree and it was disgusting. Literally. I ate two bites and couldn't have any more. The chips were insanely greasy. I couldn't even really stomach them because the grease was too harsh. The pulled pork was like a pile of wet vinegar in the middle of the pile of chips. It was so gross that I couldn't eat it. I just let it sit on the table until the waiter took it away. My mom had crab cakes that she thought were OK - again, too much grease. She was really turned off by how oily they were. Blech. For a whole lot of food that tasted awful, we were stuck with a $40 bill for two people at lunch. I wouldn't come here again.
label: NEG

text: I'm McHating it. I wanted a chicken sandwich. I waited twenty minutes and was told the wait was due to the staff not knowing how to make chicken sandwiches. How does that even happen? My order was wrong, twice. This place is only for the serious masochist.

text: This place is the spot after big Nevada football or basketball games, especially Homecoming weekend and the UNLV rivalry game. text: Infinite is the ONLY place I will go for any piercings. Don't let that deter you though. All the staff I've come in contact with is not only extremely knoweledgeable and have great customer service skills.I've never felt uncomfortable in this shop no matter how personal or off the wall the question I'm asking is. I've only been pierced by Kellan and Clay and they both are hilarious, great at what they do and very knowledgeable. I've been pierced at other places before and the piercing always ended up infected, even when I did what I was told. That was until I came to Infinite. text: I was expecting a lot after reading several Yelp reviews saying it was better than Ted Drewes. I was disappointed! I'm not a die hard custard fan or Ted Drewes. text: If you are within 10 miles of Pica's you need to try it. One of a kind pizza and pasta dishes. Recipes handed down from generation to generation and you can taste it. Tomato pie but does have cheese under the sauce. Find your topping and enjoy. If there was one food I could not live without, it'd be a Pica's red pie with Ricotta cheese. The baked rigatoni and manicotti are also top notch. I mostly prefer getting it to go because odds are good you'll feel like you're eating in a nursing home, but sometimes a sit down is fun and nostalgic. Enjoy!
label: POS

text: Let me start by saying that i LOVE BBQ. I could eat Ribs any day of the week. But, I probably would never order them from Percy street BBQ. They were practically flavorless, although cooked to an appropriate temperature. My friend and I both ordered the double down, had the ribs, chicken, and brisket (the brisket being the absolute winner). I love eating crispy chicken skin, and I couldn't even stomach a few bites of the chicken; it had a very rubbery consistency. I was intrigued by the Root Beer Chili, and was sadly disappointed (not to mention it was luke warm at the very most). Beer choices were good, but I didn't want to eat at Percy Street because of the alcohol. Dessert, however, made the experience. The Pecan Pie was heavenly! Banana Pudding was really thick, but tasty nonetheless. Service, however, was awful. Our server was aloof and inattentive. Upon entering the restaurant, we were greeted rather awkwardly by a manager. I can justify a sort of absent minded server when a restaurant is busy, but i can't when there are literally two other tables seated in the restaurant who are on dessert. There are a bunch of simple things that should be done during service that weren't. And from working in a restaurant, i understand how those little things can either make or break an experience. I was disappointed in the food and service enough that I don't have the desire to return for seconds. And i never say no to seconds when it comes to BBQ.
label: NEG

text: I have really mixed feelings about Manon. Being from the area, we're familiar with most of the restaurants and Manon has a reputation for excellent food. Indeed, on our first visit, we were blown away by the food. Exquisite flavors and preparation. So when we went back, we were stunned. The food was truly mediocre. When we asked the waitress if the chef wasn't the normal one, she said "no, it's the normal one, but he's got a toothache and is a bit under the weather." We tried again and I simply wasn't impressed. Since it's a pricey place, and there are much better/more consistent restaurants in the area, we will NOT be returning.

text: OK, this was my post-wedding dinner. Quintessential New Orleans food. We loved it even though the over-formality of the place is kind of old fashion, and our brothers almost got us kicked out. But man, hats off the the sous chef and the rest of the gang in the kitchen.

text: Sooooooooo, as a pregnant woman, I tend to eat... occasionally a lot. I was starving about a week ago and headed down to the Loop with my fiance', hoping to try a place I've never eaten at. We decided to check out Fitz's b/c I absolutely love their root beer and heard nothing but good things about the restaurant. It was a cool Friday afternoon, around 1pm. We were walking behind a group of girls, all in private high school uniforms, and watched them mosey into Fitz's. We walked in right behind them. The hostess just ignored them, and us for about 10 mins. Then started asking them questions and before we knew it, there were like 30 of these little brats all over the place and the hostess thought they were getting food to go and then found out they were staying and had no idea how to seat them. A manager came down and seemed to have been just as baffled and confused as their hostess. Now, both me and my fiance have been in this industry for quite some time, and I have never been just so rudely ignored! We stood there for 15 mins., just waiting for anyone to simply say, we will be right with you. The words never came, and we walked out. If you want to eat within an hour, or even be seated within that time frame even for lunch, skip the aggravation and go somewhere else!

text: Perhaps because I didn't visit Sher-E-Punjab on a truly sad day, I had a really wonderful dinner there. Great samosas. Solid chicken tikka and saag paneer. The attentive staff and warm decor made me forget for an hour or so that I was in a strip mall on Grant.

text: Came here with a large group (10ppl) during lunch on a Saturday. Great service! Great food! Definitely coming back.

text: Corporate acquisitions make for strange bedfellows that spawn odd, joined-at-the-hip (or at least under-one-roof) offspring - like this A&W Root Beer/Long John Silver's outlet - that vie for your fast food dollars. On the way home from Ash Wednesday services, we were looking for nothing more than a fast, cheap, meatless meal, and this place delivered on all counts. Buttered lobster bites sounded promising, but they proved to be more breading than seafood, with the same artificial flavor as the popcorn in a discount movie theater. The cole slaw was decent, but hushpuppies and cheese sticks, while a weIcome departure from the standard fries, were oozing grease. If we were opting to give up good food for Lent, this definitely would be an ideal spot to eat for the next forty days and nights.

text: Years ago, my brother and I used to giggle when we'd drive by the east-end pink trailer topped with a sign reading "Monster Burger." One summer day, we actually decided to stop. The Motoraunt provides one of the most eccentric dining experiences one could hope to have in Edmonton. We parked, ordered burgers, fries and milkshakes at the walk-up trailer window from a woman whose makeup resembled Mimi from the Drew Carey Show, and sat down in white plastic chairs atop an astroturf-covered patio, amid white-plastic potted cherry tomato plants. The food was, surprisingly, great and the atmosphere made me feel like we were on some kind of Appalachian hillbilly road trip. Eventually I excused myself and went in search of the washroom, which was located in a trailer with a top floor used as a stuffy, hot indoor dining area. The search got a little confusing as I think I may have inadvertently stumbled into the owner's living room, but things turned out all right. The Motoraunt is extremely out of the way but well worth the drive; now I can't wait for summertime.

I've noticed that whatever city you're in, SWH always finds a way to make diners nauseous. This phenomenon started years ago, when I watched not one, but two people vomiting in the SWH parking lot. text: Ahhh...bright, flashy lights...dings, tings and bings...I am pretty much like Pavlov's dog when I walk into a casino. Been to Vegas and Atlantic City, both great places to gamble in. Lived in Phoenix until two years ago and visited the Indian casino's as well. All very nice places. I had driven past the enigma they call Delaware Park during trips to CostCo (another place where you can drop lots of coin....but at least there is a short-term return on your investment there) and had always wondered about gracing this place with my presence. My brother was in town and it was a great excuse to go check it out, so we did. It was a late Friday night and the moon was full. And when the moon is full, we all know what types of weirdo's come out at night. So we arrive to the casino (they have a race track there as well) and as soon as we pull into the parking lot, we already know we are in for a treat. The clientele strolling through the parking lot pretty much sums up this venue of entertainment and who they market to - those who can't afford the drive or bus ticket to Atlantic City but seem to have enough money left over from pay day to take their chance with Lady Luck. The parking lot in itself is a gamble. Thank goodness it is well lit, or you might worry about getting shived, because it is a long walk to the front door from your car and I really don't think I would trust the valet in this joint. The Park is not a fancy place, but you do get the feel for being in a casino with all of the slot machine activity going on. It smells, carpets are brown and stained of spilled beverages, etc. There was an upstairs area, but we never made it up there. As we make our way through the casino, you get your fair share of "wife-beaters", females with outfits that they really don't fit into and spill out all over the place and not very attractive waitresses who are schlepping free carbonated beverages for meager tips. Needless to say, we're not that impressed and decide it is time to at least make this trip worthwhile and purchase a frothy brew. Finding a watering hole in this joint is almost like finding a needle in a haystack. We walked around most of the joint before finding "it". So we saddle up and ask Mandee for a couple beers. She obliges and proceeds to open the bottles we requested and then pour them in a plastic cup. I'm certainly not opposed to drinking from a plastic cup if the beer comes from a keg, but if there is a bottle, hand it over. Maybe the management is worried that if glass gets out on the floor, inappropriate activity that would involve law enforcement may break out. So we accept our beers only to find that they have the temperature range of slightly cooler than room temperature. Completely not acceptable for a beer right out of the cooler and for the price we paid for them. Unfortunately for Mandee, her tip suffered due to this unpleasant experience. As for the gaming, we did find some electronic blackjack tables which sport a large screen and a video of a female with huge, fake tits that pretended to acknowledge your existence. They seemed nice enough, but all they really wanted was your hard earned money. It was hard to get in on one of the tables, but after watching people play, it was determined that playing blackjack in this fashion would probably cause us to lose a lot of money. Hell, you lose enough to a real dealer, why let something computer generated give you a moral beat down. We did manage to play on what looked like a real roulette table and lost $20 each. Then along with our disappointment, we left the building with Elvis and left with absolutely zero chance of ever returning again. This place really sucks.
label: NEG

text: Hey, it's an Asian market. If it don't smell like fish, it ain't authentic. What more could you want? Fresh seafood, reasonably priced produce, and every Asian sauce/condiment I could ever need?? Sounds good to me. One thing I couldn't find there though was measuring cups. Go figure. It's true, the produce here isn't the best, nor the freshest, nor the cleanest, but it really depends on what you're buying. There are usually at least a few veggies that look fresh and awesome, and for the prices there, I'm willing to do a little hunting for them. If you want a cleaner, more upscale Asian grocery experience, try H-Mart. Must buys: Hot garlic flavored shrimp chips Chinese BBQ sauce (sah-cha jiang) with the cartoon cow on it Fresh octopus Live tilapia Get those and you'll have yourself a good meal. haha.
label: POS

text: Solid cocktail bar. We took a cab to Freret to have pre-Cochon cocktails, only to arrive at Cure at 4:15, 45 minutes before their Saturday opening time. The bartendress was kind enough to stick her head out the door and suggest we check out the Freret Market down the street. We did, ate a few meat pies, and generally had a good time. When the door at Cure unlocked at 5:05, our party of 3 was greeted courteously, but not necessarily warmly, by the bar staff. After we planted ourselves at the bar, however, the relationship progressed and some warmth showed. The warm cocktail of the day, an apple jack-based cider, deftly balanced sweet, spicy, and boozey. A gin fizz off the menu could've used a bit more fizz, but was well-prepared. The Big Apple, a slightly sweeter, spicier take on a Manhattan, lived up to the bartendress's praises (it's her recipe, apparently). An off-the-menu Last Word wasn't quite "the best cocktail ever made" as promised, but the way its sweet-citrusy-herbaciousness teased my taste buds made me happy. "Pretentious" isn't a word I'd use to describe this place, and I'm from Dallas, where even a trip to the grocery store typically involves a fair amount of less-than-authentic behavior. Overall, Cure is as good an upscale cocktail bar as I've ever experienced, and the fresh investment in the Freret neighborhood it represents merits a 5th star .
label: POS

text: So, I moved to Delaware County from Philly about a year ago. Finding a great bar near me seemed a difficult task. But then one day while leaving the Trader Joe's and contemplating a drink at the Iron Hill Brewery I saw Quotations across the street and decided to peak at the menu. I have to admit that when that other dude who reviewed this place said it could be a copy shop or nail salon, I laughed. So true. There's tons of potential here, but this place needs a bit of a makeover. It's not totally cheesy, just a little 90's. Regardless of it's outward appearance, whatever this spot lacks in charm, it makes up for in good food and great beer. This is THE spot for Bell's Brews. There's always a nice rotating selection of top quality beers here. Almost always a nice Belgian, a tasty micro stout, some high octane IPAs, local beers as well. I've only been a few times. Maybe 3 or 4... but every time, the beer menu has something new, interesting, and seasonal. The food is great too. If you find yourself in the area, do yourself the favor and stop in for a drink. The staff has always been hugely helpful, conversational, and knowledgeable. I'll end this review with a quote to keep with the Quotations theme. "Cheers, big ears." EDIT (1/25/13): I feel the need to amend this review after many subsequent visits. Food is average at best and very hit or miss. The BEER though, still outstanding. text: I don't know who Maria is, or even where her #1 salon is... All I know is that the women at this salon give one hell of a blowout for rock bottom prices. ROCK BOTTOM. I'm used to getting my hair cut and blown out for $80+tip =$100, only to go home and wash and blowdry it myself because my roots aren't straight. I went to Maria's and got the blowout of my life... I dare say that those women did a better job than I do myself, and that, my friends, is saying a whole hell of a lot. They all speak Spanish, so if you do too, use it... I think they definitely appreciate it more. Here's the process: Walk in, a woman asks you if you want to be deep conditioned. I said yes. Another woman motions to the back, washes your hair (and gives you the scalp massage of your life), then puts in the deep conditioner, puts a plastic cap on your head, and sits you under a bonnet dryer for ~20 minutes. She comes back when the dryer shuts off, rinses you, then takes you over to a chair, where she puts your hair up in big plastic rollers... takes about 6 minutes. You have to experience it to appreciate how much talent that takes. Mesh cap this time, plastic ear covers, back under the dryer for 45-60 minutes. As stylists free up from other clients, they come back and check on you, to see if your hair is dry. If not, back under for another 15 minutes. When you're done, the next free stylist grabs you and starts blowdrying, which takes about 20 minutes. She runs a flat iron through your hair, which takes about 10 minutes. Total price? $35. I think they generally run about $25-$30, but mine was extra because I asked for the deep conditioner. The result? Perfectly shiny, straight (FROM THE ROOTS) hair with loose curls towards the bottom. Absolute perfection. I was so happy that I couldn't stop smiling, I swear the sun shone brighter... I swear! If you haven't found the perfect blowout, try Maria's... seriously. It's very very "no frills", no designer labels on the products (or labels at all, for that matter), the decor definitely isn't on par with Center City salons, no offers of bottled water, tea, or coffee, but really, who cares if the result is 100%? Also, be aware that it's in the hood***... I had my boyfriend go with me, but I think you would be ok if you don't mess with anyone. *** Ever been to a bank that has double doors that have a metal detector built in between the two doors, a security guard on the other side, and only one person allowed in between the doors at a time? Yeah... the hood.

text: Avenue coffee could have been a welcome step in the right direction for Tucson - a city that is sorely lacking in establishments that try hard enough to be more than just average. Much is of what you will find here is done with the right 'spirit' but lacks execution at a level that satisfies. First of all, there is a general level of superiority that is evident in the fact that they have been bitten by the single origin-Portland-Stumptown-under roasted-coffee bug that is the current trend in coffee. I also witnessed an employee nearly mocking a customer asking for a blended drink - which she dismissively expressed 'that we don't do'. The space is welcoming in a modern kind of way - at least in this case it is open and airy rather than low and dark like most of the other major coffee shops in town. The coffee they are serving is decent - I had a shot of espresso and bought some whole beans - but once home (everything was pre-packaged and there is not any info on the wall or anywhere I could see that explained what they had on offer) I found under roasted, over priced coffee. The single origin approach to coffee ignores the fact that all of us don't necessarily find the most minute details of varietal character standing out in a cup appealing. Blending - and full city roasting - gives a more balanced cup for many of us. For me, if I am doing a cupping to find both the good and the bad in a coffee, then a light roast is useful. Beyond that, it just misses the point and leaves a lot of potential behind. I wish for Avenue that they will remember that their customers are an important - in fact the most important thing - for them to consider. Give the people what they want and prosecute your 'high end' coffee agenda in the background. We would love to see you stay open and make some $.

It was cheesy with pieces of foie gras and a sweet crust you'd expect from a brule. - Crawfish crepe: more like a tortilla but the corn pieces in it were good and it wasn't too saucy--the dish stood on its own. - Chicken and waffles: I picked the restaurant partially based on seeing this on the menu. It was pieces of chicken sandwiched in between two waffle slices and on a bit of potatoes. Savory but sweet and it worked for me. - Duck pastry: very nice presentation and flavorful - Creative dessert: ours came with spacey needley-like cotton candy - You could order a la carte from the 5 course tasting menu I loaded pictures of all pieces of this meal if you're interested. Lowlights (my flip side to highlights): - Brioche with seared foie gras was way too dry. - Wine list: there wasn't much available by the bottle under $100 and a lot in the $300s. - It was super cold inside--they were pumping the AC like crazy so us girls in our sleeveless tops were super chilly. Food was great but not blow me away great so not sure if I'd dine here again since I only have a few meals each time I'm in town.

text: I went to Le Bec for Restaurant Week last night. While I know you can't truly judge a restaurant experience based on restaurant week, I feel that in the spirit of today's Top/Iron Chef culture of competitive cooking, a restaurant should be able to deliver a good meal under pressure and in extraordinary circumstances. That said, I'm sure Le Bec on an average night comes nowhere close to the chaos I witnessed. All floors of the restaurant were packed and waiters hustled and bustled around. In the middle of it all, Georges Perrier walked the floors making funny faces and yelling things in his heavy French accent. Clearly a man who demands perfection, but he seemed to be enjoying himself-- it was pretty cool to be in his domain; to know that this restaurant was his life. My fiancee and I actually thought this environment made the experience more fun. I believe some other yelpers bemoaned getting a different treatment as RW diners, but on Friday night, we were seated in the beautiful main dining room amongst a mostly older crowd. Both tables next to us were ordering off the RW menu, as was everyone else around. In fact, it was the only menu set out for all the guests. Additionally, all the glasses of wine were reasonably priced, from $8 to $15, and there was a $35 bottle. I kicked things off with the country pate... combined with the sweet dried fruit things it came with, it was quite good, very french. My counterpart got the escargot, which was delicious. Great butter-garlic sauce with nuts. For my main course, I got braised short rib with hanger steak. The hanger steak was very good and the mashed potatoes and carrots were absolutely delicious. I've had better braised short rib though (see my review of NYC's Craft). My fiancee got scallops which she enjoyed, but she reported them to be a little gritty. For dessert, we got the Gateau de Le Bec Fin (choco cake and ice cream) and the lemon meringue tort. The cake was amazing, perhaps amongst the best chocolate cake I've ever tasted. All their weekday specials may lure me back in sometime in the offseason, but I think If I'm shooting for the big $100+ prix fixe French dinner, I'll go to LaCroix... but it's a close call. I kind of picture those restaurants as arch-enemies, and it's a fight I'd love to be caught in the middle of.

text: The Muse is one of the few 'all ages' venues in Nashville, and is also one of the worst places to see a show in town. I'm not sure if the former causes the latter, but hanging out with angry looking high schoolers definitely does not add to my enjoyment there. Maybe if I was my defiant 15 year old self again and wanted to hang out somewhere that would scare my parents into soiling themselves if they knew. But only just maybe, because I can still think of better places to do that around town. The Muse is located in a seedy part of town, and when I say seedy I mean that it is literally sandwiched between the largest porno store in town and a highway exit ramp and underpass. If your social circle is in need of dirty drunken bums, creepy porno store visiting middle aged men or snarky, under aged kids, then the Muse has you covered. The sound is pretty crappy, but most of the bands that play here can typically be fit into the hardcore/metal/screamo category with a few exceptions. I guess when most of the music is indistinguishable from itself you don't really need superior sound quality. Because the Muse is an all ages place, there's no smoking which is great, but there's also no booze. So if enjoying a drink while watching live music is your thing, you're definitely going to want to go elsewhere. The place itself is small, dark and dirty, though I've heard rumors they've been trying to clean themselves up recently. Due to the types of shows that play here, the crowd ranges from people standing stoically fixated on the performers to people moshing and flailing about wildly, with there never really being a happy medium. I myself like to enjoy the crowd enjoying the show, it adds to the experience for me, and its hard to do that here. One positive thing is that you get a lot for your money here if you really want to break it down. Tickets for shows here tend to run less than $10 and there is usually at least 3 or 4 bands playing on one bill. Add that to the fact that you won't be running up any bartabs, and you've got yourself a pretty cheap evening. The only good thing about the Muse being located next to Interstate 40 is that it is pretty easy to find, and convenient to leave when you're ready to bounce out of there. The parking lot is pretty small, and I don't suggest leaving anything of value in your car. There's nothing really else around the area to go to besides the porno store and its not a safe area to walk around in especially after dark so I wouldn't recommend exploring the surrounding area or even showing up here by yourself.

text: I came here on a Sunday evening after hanging out at Sound Fountain (an awesome outdoor dance party at the nearby Fountain the last Sunday of every summer month), I had a decent buzz from the sangria and sunlight and a big appetite for some good Mexican food. FIRST IMPRESSIONS: Los Caballitos is located on a section of East Passyunk that has seen an incredible revitalization, a breath of fresh air in the area filled with hip and stylish storefronts. The palpable energy is captured by this Cantina, with outdoor tables completely packed with diners of all sorts of styles and scenes (a surprising, unfamiliar, yet welcome sight). Inside, you have your typical Tex-Mex Cantina, the orange walls, the tacky (yet authentic) decor and xmas lights. THE FOOD: I was starving, and surprised at the prices on the menu, not expecting a filling meal, I ordered my mainstay of Carnitas in burrito form. I was completely wrong-- the portions are very reasonable, I was stuffed by the end. We also had chips, and my date got salad and ribs, all were very good. I guess when it comes down to it, this Cantina doesn't push the envelope, but it does the typical Mexican American fare very well. I've blasted other restaurants for not being creative or delicious, but even though Los Caballitos isn't really creative, it is delicious. They have everything they should have on there, and next time I eat here, I will be more adventurous. THE DRINKS: Another way Los Caballitos does things right is their Margaritas. Now, the subject of Margaritas in Philly is as debatable as the subject of the best Cheesesteak, but this Cantina has the essentials in place-- up, on the rocks or frozen, and any flavor or type of tequila you could want. I can't really measure how powerful they were, but I know they were doing their job. THE PRICING: As mentioned before, I was initially put off by the higher than average prices on their menu, but the food really is good, it's served in generous proportions. Next time I'll try an entree and see if it delivers on its price. THE BOTTOM LINE: Look, there as many Cantinas in Philly as there are Starbucks, the issue becomes not which is the best, but which ones don't suck, which ones are worth eating at. Cantina Los Caballitos is definitely worth checking out in my book.
label: POS
