text: Mckay's is the best used book/media store I have EVER been too and it is hard for me to understand why anyone wouldn't like this place. First of all, it is one of the biggest stores of its kind, at least that I've seen. The building is the size of warehouse and its inventory is staggering. The first thing you see when you walk in a counter where you can sell them items, which is great since a lot of places make you walk past all their merchandise first hefting your bags of goods. If they accept your items (which they almost always do, unless they're in bad shape or they already have too many duplicates) you can either get a store credit or receive cash. I can't come here unless I have a lot of free time because it is incredibly easy to spend HOURS browsing their merchandise. The bulk of their store is made up of books in all varieties and topics in both fiction and non-fiction. The rows and rows of books are broken up into sections by general subject matter. Each cubby is then divided alphabetically by author or sometimes title for non-fiction. I will admit it can be kind of chaotic if you're searching for something in particular. It's very easy for the books to get out of order and with such a vast inventory, it can take awhile for the staff to get things put back into place. My best suggestion if you're looking for a particular title, author, or topic is to ask one of the employees who can look it up in their computer system. (A used bookstore this size with this amount of product with a digital database?! YAY!) Otherwise I just like to wander around the aisles, picking up books that interest me. Their selection is pretty varied, you can even find textbooks here, but there is a weirdly disproportionate amount of used bibles, 'life guides' and other religious reading hoo hah here. I guess that's what comes of living in the bible belt. They do process a lot of merchandise, so their stock gets replenished very frequently. The rest of the store is comprised of all the rest of their used media. You can find video games from most every system here (they even sell used game systems if you need one), and they even have some newer titles. There are used computer programs and games of all varieties as well as books on tape and CD. Their used music selection is fairly extensive and divided up by genre and author. While they mostly carry single CDs, they do have some decently priced boxed sets and a limited selection of vinyl. And if that's not enough for you, they also carry movies on VHS and DVD. Their pricing is pretty awesome, if you're selling to them, they offer the best prices in town. I can usually walk out of there with a handful of books for under $10. You can even find newer hardbacks here for fractions of their original pricing. Same goes with the rest of their media. People treat this place like a library, and with its size and high narrow bookshelves, it is easy to find yourself speaking in hushed tones. It can be hard to maneuver around people in the tight aisles of books, and if there's too many people here I get claustrophobic. It's located a short drive out of town, just past the Charlotte Pike/White Bridge Road intersection and is very convenient to I-40. Their hours are pretty good, I prefer to go on a week night when there's less people.
label: POS

text: I booked a tour for me and some friends since they had not been to Philly before, so I wanted to be sure they saw all the sights. DeTours offers Bike, Segway, or Running tours and I knew the bike tour would be perfect. We could be outside, get in some exercise and enoy the real feeling of Philly without being forced to sit on a bus or be bored by a mass-tourist guide. It was the perfect solution! Our guide was really cool, and they booked the tour in a small group (just us 3 actually!), so it felt more personal. We learned a lot of stuff about the history and culture of Philly that I didn't know. The tourguide was super knowledgable, answered our questions, and didn't seem fake like they sometimes do. She even let us stop in whenever we wanted to see soemthing along the way or take pictures. They provided bikes for my friends and I was allowed to use my own. They provided helmets too and she made us feel safe by giving clear instructions the whole way so we knew where to go (navigating thru obstacles when necessary). Great Idea!! I was able to use a buy 1 get 1 so for all three of us (about 2.5 hours!!) it was only $138, including the use of bikes, equipment, backpack thingies to carry our stuff, etc. i'm planning on booking a segway tour maybe when my dad and stepmom come to visit this fall! two thumbs up!

text: I have found there are 3 levels of City Diner... Breakfast, 3am Wasted, and Everything else. Breakfast: perfect on weekends and new years day once you re-join the living. Usually packed, but the service is quicker and you can never ever ever go wrong with coffee and a South Sider. *swoon* I know I am here for breakfast when I can only finish half (this is important later). Lunch/Dinner: Service varies based on waiter, but generally slower than breakfast. Wide selection of menu items, to the point of overwhelming, and not everything is as good as you'd hope. (the mac and cheese, for example, is surprisingly and disappointingly dull). 3am Wasted: hands down best time to visit. Yes, it is packed to capacity, and if you don't leave Mangia/Upstairs/wherever else you've been on Grand 10 min before close you won't get a table. Servers are understandably grumpy and frazzled, but you would be too if you were one of the few sober people in a sea of drunks. everything tastes amazing at this point, and I have, on more than one occasion after way to many PBRs, finished an entire South Sider... which is when I need to chug a gallon of water and get myself in bed. text: Faust Park is an interesting place in Chesterfield that has this historic little village that looks like something out of a Mark Twain novel. Going towards the middle of the park will bring you to the Carousel building and the playground. I tried going in the Carousel building once, but as I didn't have a kid with me, I drew nervous attention from the parents and so I quickly left. Therefore, I cannot really review the Carousel; but the playground is fun! On the right side of the park is the historic village that has various houses from the 1800s. Sometimes on weekends there are people dressed up in historical clothing at the houses. They teach the kids about what life was like in the 1800s, and sometimes they even weave and demonstrate blacksmithing. The park isn't that big, but it still has a lot to offer, and is usually quite busy on the weekends.

text: A few years ago I embarked on a tour of St. Louis pizzerias. I've been to The Good Pie, Pi, Dewey's, and many others, but the one that I keep coming back to is Katie's Pizzeria Cafe. I like the boho chic ambiance with the mismatched furniture and grad student artwork on the wall. I even like how all of the staff is super hot and super friendly, but kind of clueless. But, most of all, I really like their Neapolitan style crust and their endless array of topping combinations. On my most recent visit, we enjoyed a squash blossom pizza with goat cheese and fresh cherry tomatoes. The squash blossoms were lightly pan seared and added a crunchy element to the creamy goat cheese and juicy tomatoes. We also enjoyed an artichoke, prosciutto, fresh mozzarella and fennel pizza that was deliciously chewy and salty in all the right ways. Other memorable pizzas were the egg pizza (goat cheese, speck, rosemary and sunny side up fried eggs on top), the fig pizza (fresh figs, gorgonzola, and rosemary), and the tres amici (salami, sausage, and pancetta). You have to start your meal off, though, with some fresh prosciutto spring rolls and artichoke toasted ravioli. Both are homemade and uniquely prepared. To be quite honest, I'm usually in a drooling quandary whenever I sit down for a meal at Katie's. Everything on the menu sounds so darn good and I just can't make up my mind. And therein lies the reason that I keep coming back and will continue to do so.
label: POS

text: My refrigerator was leaking and the repairman said the filter we'd installed a few years ago was now leaking. He said it would be $80 to fix it (basically to remove filter and reattach line to the wall.) We probably could've done this ourselves but I went ahead and asked him to do it because the service fee we would have had to pay was $50 and I figured at least he would do it right. Wrong! When he pulled out the fridge, there was gross stuff behind it (dust, etc.) that he asked me to clean before he proceeded. I did so, though I would've thought he would have done that. After he was done, he was in such an allfired hurry to get out of there that he left the refrigerator pulled out! He said maybe I'd want it that way so the floor could have a chance to dry, but I had told him I'd use a box fan at night to do that because I couldn't open the doors (and, you know, feed my young children) when the fridge was pulled out. So I struggled to push the fridge back toward the wall (he had already left at this point.) I then noticed that the light wasn't turning on and I called him and he said maybe he had forgotten to plug it back in and that he was already far from my house and wouldn't be able to come back for quite some time. Lovely. So I got a friend to help me pull it out again, then I plugged it back in, and together we pushed it back into place. By the way, the reason it was so hard to move in and out of place was because the leak had done damage to the wood floor below and the floor buckled so the wheels were unable to go smoothly over the floor. He of course knew this as he was the one who told me it. So it was all the more egregious that he left it pulled out in the first place with NO way to open the doors. I will, needless to say, never call this business again.

text: The staff here are pretty funny, they just kind of do their own thing. They're not unfriendly or unhelpful necessarily but it's almost like they don't really care whether or not you're there. It's hard to explain it well because they actually handled all of my requests, maybe it's just the lack of acknowledgment that patrons are even there. The menu is pretty straightforward, they've got your typical BBQ meat and side choices, ribs, chicken, brisket, pulled pork, mac & cheese, potato salad, coleslaw, green beans, etc. I opted for the pulled pork sandwich with coleslaw ($.40) on top and mac & cheese as my side. I also ordered their famous peanut butter pie. The mac & cheese was really good. My only issue with it was that you could tell it was made earlier and just scooped into a container and reheated. It was really tasty but you could sense that it had been sitting for some time, the cheese was really thick. Unfortunately this would have been outstanding fresh. The pulled pork sandwich was top notch. You can tell that they put a lot of attention into cooking their meats, it was perfect.....and with the slaw on top, it just got better. I would suggest getting the slaw and adding their BBQ sauce with the Crystal Hot Sauce. This is certainly one of the better pulled pork sandwiches I've ever had. The peanut butter pie was fantastic. If you like peanut butter you will love this pie. It was extremely delicious, creamy but with nuts on top to add a nice crunch. It was not overly sweet which was nice. I just wish there was more, maybe next time I'll order two slices. I have a more in-depth review and photos on my personal blog.

text: My mother, who has never as much as smoked a cigarette in her life, decided that for her 50th birthday she would throw caution to the wind and do something that she had always wanted to do...get her nose pierced. Her piercer was Stan, who had done a number of my piercings and was never anything short of impressive, and on this occasion he did not disappoint. I think he sensed her nervousness, and spent upwards of 45 minutes with us. He explained the details of the nasal structure, what the piercing process would entail and a gave a thorough review of all after care procedures. The piercing was quick and easy (we discovered Mom is a bit of a bleeder), and in less than a week was healed enough that she didn't even notice it. This was not simply a piercing for my mother, it was a symbol that she could overcome her hesitations, that she could do anything. Each time that we visit to pick up a new face bobble, she remarks with amazement how kind they are to her, and how welcome they make her feel. Stan and the staff at Cheap Trx gave me the opportunity to give my Mom a gift of confidence to mark her half-century of existence. And I cannot thank them enough.

text: The Bleeding Deacon is a dark, smoky, S. City neighborhood bar with music related decor and lots of bald headed, facial haired, pierced individuals running around (think Royale, CBGB's, etc.). The service is friendly. They have a jukebox with an eclectic selection of tunes, or you might hear everything from Red Hot Chili Peppers to Cheap Trix via iPod. They also have Wi-fi, multi player LAN games and a small patio out back. The menu is definitely a step up for pub grub. Lots of comfort food with a modern twist. Very reasonably priced. The entrees average $10 and most every thing else is less than that. The value is very good. And while bacon is a menu staple (even on the dessert menu), they also cater to vegetarians. Sweet potatoes are a staple too (mashed and salsa - yum!). A couple of negatives... the place is smoky, the chicken with mac & cheese entree is sounds great but fails to deliver any taste and the 20% gratuity for parties of 6 or more is a joke. Mandatory gratuity for small groups (less than 10) is quickly becoming a St. Louis standard and is ridiculous. I understand with large groups but let's get this straight people. GRATUITY IS OPTIONAL and not enforceable under law (unless it is agreed upon and in a contract, such as a restaurant discount program or a catering contract). In addition, PAY YOUR PEOPLE. It's not our job! Amount of tip is for me to decide based on the service provided. There is nothing wrong with suggesting a tip, but adding it is another thing. Overall, I think the Bleeding Deacon is a great find because of the affordable, bar food that is homemade and tasty. I've had better comfort food in a bar for less, but it's a great value, which gets them almost 4 stars. If it was smoke free, it would be four stars without a doubt.

text: Resurrection Ale House may (RAH!) be somewhat out of the way for those that don't live that Grays Ferry neighborhood, but other than the fact that they are a locally well-recognized craft beer bar, RAH recently got national acclaim for its Twice-Fried Chicken from Andrew Knowlton from Bon Appétit!!! Kudos of Bon Appetit caliber? YAY! Fried Chicken DOUBLE YAY!! Delicious craft beers? YAYAYAY!!! ( because duh, this girl loves me some beers - especially IPAs - and the hoppier the better) WHAT WE ATE * Pan con Tomate: grilled homemade bread + tomato + manchego + sweet chorizo We started with the very rustic bruschetta-like pan con tomate. Yummers. Pizza-like! Sort of. For me, the shredded manchego cheese was the best part. I don't know what it is about manchego, but it makes every dish taste so much better. I'm pretty sure this grilled bread and tomato concoction would have been pretty forgettable without it. The sweet chorizo was definitely an interesting addition and added a yummy contrast to the tart tomatoes and greens. Not a tastebud blower, but tasty and well executed. *Hoisin Braised Pork Belly: ginger + radish + spring onion + hand-cut fries and dipping sauce The thick cut of pork belly came resting on top of a soft delicious ciabatta bread, topped with thin slices of radish and spring onions. Everything was so soft and tender and juicy delicious. I did wish there was a teeny bit more hoisin sauce to add that tangy-ness to the sandwich, but overall it was wonderful. The hand cut fries were just okay. Unfortunately, they lacked the crispy crunchiness that makes fries so addicting and delectable. They did come with a very cool dipping sauce, though - it was a mix of ketchup, mayo and curry powder.... very memorable, very interesting and I liked it so much that I kept eating more of the "just-okay" fries to keep tasting the flavor. I don't think that it went particularly well with the Pork Belly sandwich itself, but it didn't detract from it. *Twice Fried Chicken: drizzled with spiced honey + served with warm German-style potato salad Aside from the obvious raving about the flavors and textures that will commence, I want to say that at $11, for 2 pieces of fried chicken thighs, this is really a great deal. The skin is soooo unbelievably crispy, but very thin and not overwhelming at all. It's like the perfect ratio of batter to meat and because it's dark meat, it's super flavorful on the inside as well as out. The German-style potato salad was really like chunky mashed potatoes that had a very tart flavor to them. I think we weren't really ready or expecting the flavor to be quite what it was so I'm not sure I liked these. German style potatoes apparently include tart apples and cider vinegar, which as you can imagine, adds a substantial amount of sour/tartness to them. It was so different than any other mashed potatoes I have had and even further from the more conventional idea of potato salad we had in our minds. You certainly can't say it's boring though. The pickled okra resting on top complements the flavors of the potatoes. Haha, we did not finish the potatoes or the okra, but that might have been partly due to the fact that we had filled up on an appetizer and 2 IPAs each!

Only got the mozzarella, which wasn't enough for 12 peeps. Then, about 15 min later they brought out the brushetta. Waiter said the kitchen must have forgotten. Uh, dude, we're the only people here. How the hell could they have fogotten? So, then we order entrees. Which, somehow, came out all together. The entrees were veal parm that was tough and chewy according to my better half. Bleeech is a good word for that dish in her words. Some chicken and with penne pasta in a pesto sauce with broccoli that I didn't have and some various stuffed pasta. You would think it was enough for 12 people but it wasn't. And since it wasn't, my family started to piss and moan. I had enough. Between our mildly retarded bartender, our completely inept waiter, and a kitchen that just seemed to stop caring about the food they were preparing, it was all I could take. Before I even took a bite of the garbage that was in front of me, I left. I hadn't eaten anything that day and was absolutely starving, but I just knew this wasn't for me. I told everyone that I just couldn't bring myself to eat this garbage, turned to the girlfriend and said I would wait for her in the car which was on 15th and Chestnut. I have never in my life walked out of a restaruant, but the experience at this joint was enought to make me do so. 35 min later she showed up and basically confirmed what I had already surmised. The food was absolutely horrible. Chewy veal, undercooked penne, and frozen manicotti was her report on the "food". Looks like I made the right choice by not staying. I know I would've had the squirts later on if I did judging by her description of the meal she had just eaten. Congrats Buca di Beppo. You are my first 1 star review. How you can screw up food as simple as the dishes you serve is beyond me but you managed to do so. I can honestly say that I will never, ever, ever step foot in this establishment again. A word to the wise. Don't go there. It's on 15th st and there are much, much better places to eat. This is a waste of time and money, unless you have a weird Pope fetish.
label: NEG

text: It can be a challenge getting a good pizza in Santa Barbara. However, the one place that has never let me down has been Giovanni's. The pizza is made just the way I like, thick dough with lots of quality cheese. I've been going here for years and I've never had a bad experience. The workers are always friendly and welcoming.

text: Yes, I understand there's history, and there's probably not a lot of places with a wide variety to go around that area, but honestly? I wasn't very impressed. Worth going to though if you want a book and don't want to do the whole Barnes and Nobles thing.

We got there around 10:45, and as we left the crowd started to form. I loved the corn bread, but loved the corn cake even more. I live over an hour away, and I am looking for an excuse to drive back soon!

text: This restaurant is located in the pretty area of Ardmore right on US 30. The decoration inside is modest and seating arrangements are conservative at best. The server was polite. The food was very good. We tried a noodle soup which was the specialty of the day. We also tried a fish in ginger curry sauce which was excellent and had the right mix of ginger and tangy-ness. The pad thai although good, was a bit on the sweeter side. If you are not too fond of sweet sauce, I would suggest that you ask for extra spice for the pad thai. Overall a good package.
label: POS

text: Pirrone's is right down the street from my house and is the perfect neighborhood restaurant. Let me start with their salads... I don't know what it is about their salads, but they are amazing! They are incredibly basic with only lettuce, tomatoes, Provel cheese, and dressing, but they are so good. The portions are gigantic. The child's size salad is equivalent to any other restaurant's basic side salad. Eat the small salad and you probably won't have much room for your entree. Eat the large salad and you have enough food to feed a family of four for a week. I recently bought two of their large salads to take to a pot luck and it filled up a large mixing bowl. Unlike other reviewers, I'm not a fan of their pizza. If I want St. Louis pizza, I'm going to Imo's, sorry. I'm also really picky about red sauces and meat sauces. Pirrone's meat sauce doesn't get me excited. I'll eat it, but there are other restaurants with better sauce, in my opinion. Their chicken parmesan is really good. It comes with a side and if you get the pasta with red sauce, it is almost enough for another meal. Like I said about the salads, the portions are huge. I also really like their pasta con broccoli. The staff is usually very friendly. They offer a lunch buffet during the week. This is great way to sample their various dishes.

The flavors seem to be chosen more for novelty rather than taste. Some of the combinations are downright bizarre. In the three times I've tried to give this place the benefit of the doubt, the service has ranged from downright rude (yelling at a customer in front of me) to bizarrely distracted and unfriendly. What gives? SOMETHING is cooking up at this place....I'm not sure what, but it tastes like cardboard and bad service!

text: We went to the Brick Hotel for Sunday Brunch this morning. I went several years ago and had a good experience, but this time the lack of crowd should have warned me. text: Gentlemen of New Orleans, If you have a special lady (or man) that you want to wine and dine without maxing out your credit card, take them to La Crepe Nanou. I had been admiring the restaurant from the outside every time I had downgraded my dinner plans to Pizza Hut. A year and a half after moving to NOLA, I finally made my first trip to La Crepe Nanou, and I anticipate many more visits. The atmosphere and ambiance is romantic, intimate, and very NYC. From the curtain at the entrance, the mostly 2-4 tops, dim red lighting and mirrors, I often thought I had been transported to a chic Greenwich hotspot. One of my favorite things about La Crepe Nanou is the unpretentious wine list. When entree prices do not top $25, there is no need for a $50-$100 wine list. We enjoyed a White Burgundy which was not memorable, but not bad and complimented our dinner. We started with the mussels, and were not disappointed. For dinner, I ordered the Crepe aux Ecrevisses (crawfish tail crepe w/ lobster sauce) and my date had the Crepe au Poulet (chicken in white wine sauce). The crepes were large and stuffed to the brim. I assume my date enjoyed his, because it had vanished from his plate in a matter of minutes. The crawfish crepe was savory and delicious and a big enough portion for me to require a to-go box. For dessert, we again ordered a crepe, the Crepe Calvados, with the sweet brandy and apple flambe. The presentation of lighting the crepe was great, however if the brandy portion was halved, I could have eaten the crepe without my eyes watering and feeling like I am taking a shot of whiskey with each bite. Last, but certainly not least, the service was perfect. Attentative, timely, and not at all imposing. Our server was helpful in recommending dishes. I will definitely be back to La Crepe Nanou. I am excited about exploring both the crepes and entree items while I am living here in NOLA. So if there are any gentlemen callers out there, you know where to take me!

text: La Cocina probably deserves a fresh page now that they've reopened. I had avoided the old iteration largely because of the Yelp reviews, but the new restaurant is definitely worth a visit. Their menu is eclectic and features a host of non-meat options, none of which seem like afterthoughts. Their veggie burger competes with the best of them and has a substantial, barley-filled, homemade quality. The real burger was formidably delicious, too, and the tilapia salad was very well executed. The quality of ingredients is good and becomes all the more impressive given the weirdly affordable prices. Portions were average--you won't go hungry, but the plates are big and the sides are small, so get an appetizer and you'll be happier. The service was friendly, though not memorably so. La Cocina earns a comfortable four stars for their food, but the restaurant's atmosphere and prices take the overall rating up to a five.

text: This is a great little place that we've been driving by for years but have never been to until now. We finally decided to stop in for a late lunch around 4pm after a day out at the beach. The portions might be smaller than their dinners, but if that's the case, they must give you a whole heck of a lot of food for dinner, because we left stuffed. The only downside I can think of is that the restaurant is fairly small inside and they don't open up the whole thing for the early bird time. As a result, the tables are pretty close together almost to the point of being cozy with your neighbor, but fortunately we got some quiet and polite diners next to us. Our waiter was also friendly and very efficient at navigating around the limited space. Otherwise, the food was delicious and well worth the price. I ordered the broiled seafood platter which consisted of scallops, shrimp and a filet of haddock. The meal was only $10 and came with coffee, red pepper hummus with pita sticks, a salad with an amazing mustard balsamic dressing, the meal itself, and a small slice of key lime cheesecake for dessert. The seasoning on the broiled platter was simple, but you get a broiled platter to enjoy the flavors of the seafood so I enjoyed it. I've never had scallops cooked as well as this place did. My fiancee had escolar (butterfish) tuna that was prepared with asparagus, mashed potatos, and covered in a citrusy cream sauce with whole red peppercorns. The sauce really brought out the flavor of the fish and went well with everything on the plate. Her meal was more like $15, but was well worth the extra money and came with all of the above extras. We will definitely be returning to Snappers in the near future. If you enjoy Bonefish Grill, Snappers will appeal to you as well. It's the same quality of food with a local flavor!

text: I discovered l'angolo randomly over the internet over 5 years ago, the first day I moved to Philly. Had very good reviews and decided to try it out. What can I say... It truly became my favorite spot in the world. I am Italian, born and raised in Milan, and as you can imagine I have experienced a lot of terrible Italian food in the US. But L'Angolo... is just like eating in my grandma's kitchen. BYOB, the ambiance is amazing - cozy, great decor (yellow walls, murals... you feel like you are in the Tuscan countryside), you always recognize people at the tables (those who discovered it keep coming back every week....)... The staff gets a 10/10 (Nino is the best, nicest, most efficient and most entertaining waiter I ever met), the music is never too loud, it allows for plenty of conversations. It's just a happy place. The food... I tried the whole menu at least once, and I enjoyed every dish. Worth of notice: grilled romaine, prosciutto wrapped asparagus/shrimp, calamari, spaghetti allo scoglio, spaghetti alla bolognese, veal milanese. But after a couple of years my absolute favorites are: entrees: funghi al forno (baked mushrooms)... With fontina, a bit of garlic, parsley... absolutely delicious (and light.. you don't want to fill up before the pasta dish!) pasta dish: gnocchi (they make them 3 ways: shrimp sauce, gorgonzola sauce - my fav- and baked... not always on the menu but if you ask they'll do it for you). Just incredible. Homemade, perfect texture, the sauce is not overpowering.. meat/fish: the special of the day never disappoints. But after the gnocchi I doubt you will have more room... (portions are abundant) dessert: chocolate cake with raspberry sauce (unbelievable) All my friends who tried it fell in love it with it. I celebrated there every single birthday and special occasion over the last 4 years(including 21st bday and graduation dinner...with my italian family). I now moved to NYC and I've yet to find a place so genuinly good, homy, unpretentious. So in conclusion: high quality food, excellent staff, low price (appetizers are 5-12 dollars, pasta dishes are 13-20, food and fish 15-30, desserts around 10). I would recommend it over any other place in Philadelphia.

text: I wish I had remembered this place when I took some friends to the Chinese buffet that's in the Wal-mart plaza around the corner. This is less expensive, but better quality food. The lunch buffet here at Cheung is only $6.00, _including_ drink and tax. No buffet for supper, you order off the menu. (I think you can order off the menu for lunch, too.) Their lunch buffet's modus-operandi is a small number of items done very well. They apparently don't feel obligated to have all the Chinese buffet "standards" so they can focus on doing their core dishes just right, and keeping them fresh. By not having some steam trays full of stuff that hardly anybody eats, they save on costs, and pass that along with a low price for the lunch buffet. There is no salad bar, but there is a modest fruit and dessert bar. Items on the fruit/dessert bar were FRESH pineapple slices, FRESH oranges (cut longitudinally, typical American style), cantelope chunks, sugar cookies, fortune cookies, and sugar-dusted fried dough balls (sort of like donut holes). Decor is the old grand style, and has been kept up and clean. Clean ceiling tiles and walls. Decoration included those large elegant Chinese vases. Men's room was very clean. Center of dining area has one of those big round tables for seven with the lazy-susan. There is a side dining room for large groups. The owners are from Hong Kong, and the recipes reflect that. The General Tso's Chicken was good. The sweet-and-sour chicken thingees were breaded like they usually are, but they did not consist of "chopped and formed" McNugget style ground chicken. They were actually whole pieces of real chicken meat tenders and chunks. Expect Papa-san to go around chatting with people in the dining room between his stints in the kitchen. I haven't been there for supper yet, but the lunch buffet is GREAT.

text: This is not a character assassination. The servers at the Jamaican Jerk Hut all seemed very lovely. But my first (and likely only) dining experience there was one of those that was tainted by the haze of mood-altering blood sugar levels from ridiculously long wait times which were compounded by loud and obnoxious clientele* that I think the management are letting ruin their establishment. In most cases any place is worth a second chance since I know there are always extenuating circumstances: their top server has mono, a shipment of Jerk seasoning is stuck on route 95, they had to physically go slaughter our dinners and the chickens were riled up from the flash mob on South St. But after reading past reviews apparently deplorable service has been the norm since they started riding the coattails of being in the film In Her Shoes. Additionally, even though the curry goat was pretty tasty two hours after I ordered it, I consider the pains I'm still having in my gut 8 hours later as punishment for not trusting my instincts and getting the hell out of there when we first arrived. The back of the house told us to check-in up front, the front told us to check-in out back, a reservation book inside had nothing written in it (funny, considering we all had a few to contribute by then.) All of this should have been a big warning sign. *In hindsight I realize that the additional charges (listed below) mentioned on page 2 of the menu were most likely created to discourage college kids from coming in to take advantage of the BYOB and 'drinking under the radar' (made obvious by the overly drunk girl who needed help both walking to the bathroom and holding her hair back.) Not only does it ruin the experience for the grown ups who can hold their liquor but it's ineffective and unnerving, especially in a place that seats at least 50 people and has only one bathroom. It's also absurd for already overpriced food, less-than-stellar service, wait times, plastic cups, etc. Then they don't even honor their own fees since the only add-on we were charged was 4 $3 corkage fees, which didn't even add up to what we actually consumed! - $12 minimum to sit on the patio, - 20% gratuity for parties of 6 or more, - $4 entertainment fee on Fri and Sat nights and a - $4 corkage fee for each bottle of wine and six pack Thank god I have generous Jamaican neighbors with a patio. I'll visit them the next time I want to eat jerk chicken and sit outside with my own alcohol.

text: So, I enjoy a good dive bar/restaurant/dumpster as much as the next guy, but there's not a lot of bright spots on the horizon here at Cap'n Cat's. The front of the restaurant is their frozen food display and take out area. This should be your clue to what's inside. You pass the shop area into a wooden paneled restaurant decorated with various nautical items.You are seated by a waitress at a table stocked with both large round and small soup style oyster crackers and a nicely spicy cocktail sauce. I should note I usually come for lunch, and I've never had a problem getting a seat. WXTU Redneck Radio plays on a sad little stereo in the corner of the restaurant that has been there for the ten years I've been coming. Pricing is certainly not bad, but then again, there are very few items that are not pre-prepared and right out of the freezer. Oysters are tasteless and bland, unremarkable in species, and when I asked the server what type of oysters they were, she replied 'raw'. Yep, silly me, I should have known that. Thank you. The raw clams are pretty much chowder clams. They are so big and tough at one point I was not sure who was eating whom. My guest could not deal with clams this big, so I slathered them up with cocktail sauce and dispatched them. Thank G-d we only ordered half a dozen. Clams casino were undercooked and had too much green pepper. You could barely taste the clam, which appeared to have been minced up. Snapper soup was watery. The stuffed clams (think deviled clams) were a hit. I'd get them again any time and just wish they were bigger, versus the cherrystone version they serve here. Worcestershire sauce and sherry accompaniments (for the soup) were provided pleasantly and in great quantity when requested. You pretty much get a half shot of sherry. Prost! I ordered the three crab special, which came perfectly cooked. Except for the dungeness crab, which was black and smelled like ammonia. Seriously. You think someone would have caught that, but nope, so back it went to be taken off the tab. Shrimp cocktail was good and my companion had the broiled seafood combo, which he enjoyed very much. Our waitress was attentive and pleasant, provided all the sauces and refills we needed, as well as plenty of napkins, so no complaints about the service. She was not a teen, nor were there any teens there today, but I know what Brian means in his review. Overall, it's not bad, and it's a guilty pleasure for my friend and I, but don't expect to be dazzled. It's cheap, frozen seafood heated up and served to you. You could do the same thing at home with the same results. Probably better in some cases. Definitely better in others.

text: Ahhhhh...the Flying M...how do I love thee? Let me count the ways! This is hands down my favorite coffee house in Boise. I frequent this place and can honestly say...I have never once smelled man ass (as someone else mentioned) while enjoying my cuppa. Clearly, the ambiance is not going to please everyone. It's eclectic in the extreme (I would say it even leans toward the bohemian), which is why I like it...but, obviously, this kind of atmosphere is rather polarizing (you either love it or hate it, it seems). In pleasant weather, I will generally sit out front on the benches (they have tables positioned in front of the benches) and enjoy my coffee where the people watching is prime. Inside, they have a library of reading materials to choose from along with an incredibly casual atmosphere where on any given evening (yes...I drink coffee morning, noon, AND night) one can find card/board games underway, great tunage playing, and above all else INCREDIBLE coffee! Because, let's face it, atmosphere aside, it's all about the coffee! And, boy, do they have it. I purchase their beans (locally roasted) which are fabulous and their coffee drinks are the best in Boise, in my opinion (my current obsession is their iced-skinny-caramel-mocha...to DIE for). In addition to fabulous coffee, they have a case full of tasty treats--from cookies, to cake, to turnovers--that are baked in house. I fancy their tomato/pesto turnover with my second fav being the ham/cheddar turnover and on the rare occasion I absolutely adore their sour cream chocolate cake--while my husband enjoys their 5 food group cookies (featuring the five food groups: veggies, fruit, dairy, grain, and chocolate, of course) or their raspberry shortbread. Their baristas are always fast and friendly...and on top of everything else are practiced in latte art! What is it about a pretty little heart drawn in my foam that just makes me happy? I don't know...but it does! Bottom line? If the atmosphere isn't to your liking, get some coffee and cookies to go--you won't regret it.

The Poker room is 'smoke-free', but smoke drifts in from the rest of the casino, who thought that up? Don't go there, it is simply not worth it. text: I dined here during Labor Day weekend and it was PACKED even with reservations! Our reservations were at 8:45pm but we didn't get seated till a little after 9pm. It's understandable. With all the research done on this place by reading all the Yelper's reviews it was worth coming to! Portions: generous! Appetizer: Burrata with truffles: MMMMMMMM! The BEST burrata I had thus far! The burrata was softly creamy and the truffles was an incredible touch! I inhaled this dish like there was no tomorrow. Primi: Risotto del Giorno: This was so freaken flavory! It was filled with seafood and had a homemade touch to it. It was either this or the ravioli but we opted for this since we wanted a seafood dish. Secondi: Grilled ribeye steak with white beans: The portion was super generous! The steak was HUGE! You can definitely taste the Italian herbal goodness in this steak instead of being salt/peppered/buttered up. We shared all of the dishes and were so stuffed! The damage was under $70. Since we had to wait the waitress offered to give us a free tiramisu but we declined since it would have been a waste for us to not eat it. She deducted $7 but we gave that back to her in her tip because she was just so sweet. Despite it being busy the service was great. Overall thoughts: I gave it 4 stars because I think Mastro's steak is still better. Overall though all the dishes we ordered were super good! I would definitely recommend a visit here for anyone in SB. Cost: 1 appetizer, 1 primi, and 1 secondi: around $70 total.

text: So a funny thing happens to my sticking-out-like-a-sore-thumb city-slicker associates and I on my mission to find the best barbeque in Nashville.... We get there at 7:30 p.m. to find out that the place had already closed at 7:00. (Seems like standard operating procedure for BBQ shacks. I encountered the same problem in Raleigh, NC.) As the lights were out, we naturally assumed the door next store led to the restaurant. It actually was the entrance to the "diviest dive bars ever," as Paul W. noted. We were greeted by a guy bolted to the same chair for the past several years rambling on with the 3 words of Japanese he knew to my Asian-American friend. On our way out, we ran across some guys hanging out on the front porch who also looked like they had a very happy and very long happy hour(s). They were actually very helpful to direct us to Mother's down the road. So we went back the following evening plenty early. First question to the young guy and gal behind the counter, "why aren't you open later?" "Because I want to get home." At least he was honest. We keep our next question to ourselves: "What did you do with the sweet old grandma (like you would expect at such a place)! They seemed too Haight Ashbury to be manning a Southern BBQ shack. We asked for their recommendations all the way. The guy recommended the pulled pork shoulder and cole slaw sandwich. We decided on our own to get some ribs to try. Sandwich was distinctive and mighty tasty. Ribs were very competently cooked and their special white sauce was rather interesting, but nothing to make it really stand out from the crowd. The baked beans were just a notch better than the Van de Kamp variety. Slaw was only lightly mayo'd and thus rather refreshing. Corn bread pancakes were on the dry side. Turnip greens kinda okay. We still had some room left so we asked for one other recommendation. The guy suggested that the combination of their pulled chicken with their white white sauce would bring things to the next level of flavor-fulness. The chicken was very moist and I must admit rather tasty with the sauce. If you really need a beer with your dinner, it looks like they will deliver to the dive bar next door. And like others have mentioned, it really is a shack attached to a small cement bunker behind the McDonalds. Blink and you'll miss it. Now time to go back downtown for some cheap beers at a honky-tonk. Yee ha!

text: Oh, James. I had heard and read so many good things about you. Your food was highly touted, your cocktails envied. I browsed the menu online before dining and while I found the prices to be a little high, I thought that the food would warrant them. I was mistaken. Our server explained that the menu was meant to be enjoyed in 3 courses. He then went through and recommended his favorite dishes. First recommendation was the Kindai tuna, m.p. I was not surprised that we would be steered towards the most expensive appetizer. After gushing about the incredible marbling and sustainability of this fish, he recommended that we get one or two pastas and then the lobster entree, $36. If you went to see a movie, would you go see whatever the person working the box office told you to see? I would rather not feel like I'm getting the up-sell and just be left to decide on my own or ask questions. I ordered the Burgundy snails and the risotto a la milanese with summer truffle and beef marrow. My companion ordered the consomme with miatake mushrooms and the lobster. Almost every dish on the menu features some sort of interplay between sweet and savory flavors. To me this feels like a gimmick. The snails were lightly battered and fried and were plated on top of some sort of burnt sugar crisp that tasted like toffee. They were very flavorful and the dish worked well, except for the sweetness. The risotto tasted like Velveeta but not quite as salty. Summer truffle? There was no flavor in the thin brown slices in the center of the dish that I assumed were summer truffle. After the entrees were cleared the waiter gave us dessert menus without asking if we wanted any. This is a big pet peeve of mine and another example of feeling like I am being up-sold. I had the panna cotta which was very good, nice texture and sweet without being too sweet. I've only been once, so I can't comment on the overall consistency of the menu, but so far there just isn't a lot of value for the money. I expected more complex flavors from the risotto than just mac and cheese. The chef seems obsessed with juxtaposing savory and sweet and I don't think it always works. I'd be interested to go back and try the pappardelle with duck ragu and chocolate, but at $120 for app, entree, two drinks, a dessert and a piece of cheese, it's going to be a while.

Now for the food. We ordered the Mykonos Burger. Having ordered the burgers, our waitress never thought to ask us how we wanted them cooked, and what resulted was a disaster. Whenever I eat at a restaurant, I believe in finishing at least half of the main course, out of respect for the chef, and the starving people of Chad (ha!). No, this burger was terribly undercooked. That's not to mention the fact that it was terribly overpriced. So if you're looking for a great Greek restaurant. avoid Effie's. If you're looking for delicious bite to eat in a relaxed atmosphere, avoid Effie's. If every other restaurant in Philadelphia is closed, by some unforseen act of God, and you are desperate for something to eat, forget Effie's, you would be better off grabbing a couple of Sim Jim's from WaWa. On several occasions, I've driven past and seen police directing traffic in the parking lot. That's a sign of two sure things... they're well liked and busy, and also have really crummy parking! The service is never especially friendly, but they get the job done, so I can't complain. I just go there for the cheap(ish) booze!

text: I went to a wedding here. The outside areas are nice for photos, I guess. The food they cater was really subpar. Straight up: we got served bagel bites that they called "gourmet pizzas." Not little pizzas they made - BAGEL BITES. The service poor. The owner makes a big spectacle presenting a "gift" to the couple while plugging Kings Mills to all of the guests. It was pretty tacky and took away from the ambiance, of which there was little to begin with. We were told by our friends that the venue is very inexpensive, however. And you can supply your own liquor for the open bar, also saving money.

text: Went here last summer after a Cardinals game...not that impressed. Few TV's, spaced out way too far. Service was pretty slow, and the food wasn't anything to write home about either. I don't think I'd go back.

text: You don't know summer in Tucson until you've tried Eegees. Native to Tucson, Eegees was originally sold in a street cart until the owners became so successful they started opening chains. Proof that no matter how small the town, a good product and a drive to succeed can take you to the top. I also heard recently that they're branching out to Phoenix soon. Get ready Phoenix for Eegees deliciousness! I don't know who discovered this amazing frozen "slush" treat, but they should be nominated for the Nobel food prize. To know Eegees is to love Eegees. On those sweltering 108 degree days, Eegees is your best friend! On a regular basis they have lemon, strawberry, and piña colada flavor available and they also serve the flavor of the month which varies between "Tangerine Breeze", "Jungle Juice", "Cherry Cider", "Orange Dream" and so on... I personally am a fan of the strawberry / piña colda combination. If you're having a BBQ, you can also add liquor to these fine drinks and have a wildly fruity time! They also serve food, though my interest in the company lies strictly in their drinks. They have sub sandwiches which they refer to as "grinders" and some really fatty side orders that'll clog your arteries. The bacon ranch fries, salty soft pretzels & hot dogs to name a few. The buildings themselves look very outdated, but don't let that deter you. The drinks are well worth it. The drive through's are fairly quick too. A must try if you're ever in Tucson!
label: POS

text: When you enter the 4th Avenue location with floor to ceiling windows the ambient light and large colored tile concrete floors immediately give way to thoughts of an Art Gallery. WIth Canvas Oil Paintings, Illustrated Prints, Professional Sketches, and a T-Rex sculpture in view you immediately might forget this is a tattoo parlor. The staff is not your typical coffee monkey scenester kid, these pros are illustrators and accomplished artists who happen to be tattoo artists. Felix the mastermind at the establishment walks you through all stages of your tattoo with the patience of Buddha and the wisdom of Socrates. His casual nature lends the air that he knows more about tattoos than is responsible for one individual to know, and he does. The shop is very professional, clean, and in the heart of 4th avenue. You wont find rando college kids here looking for a drunk Chi Oh tattoo(in fact I hope they turn you away) or some other flash bullshit. This place is about integrity and honest work. Come with your thoughts and they will draw them out for a small fee. This is a shop owned and operated by artists, not ink junkies and random "i like to draw people" who picked up an electronic needle. Come for the art stay for a tattoo. Piercing's also available.
label: POS

text: hm, why is this a brewing co when they have so few beers? and ya, the service is absolute crap. completely un-attentive and just plain d-u-m. also, i got a side of onion rings w/ my terrible wrap. guess how many i got!!!? 3. there was 1 small one and medium ones. uh what? that counts as a side of onion rings? but I guess that's ok since they were yucky anyway.

Great wine choices

text: I had the great luck of trying Mi Lah during the first time for their Sunday Brunch special. It's a fixed price, but well worth it as the food just keeps coming. Service has always been great here. Unlike a lot of other asian restaurants whose meals focus around 100 varities of faux meat, this one has some real ethnic style and menu diversity. I think it will continue to be a good retaurant and it is already high on my list of vegan dinner locations in the city for a more refined evening. It's BYOB too!

text: I cannot believe it has been almost two years since I went to New Orleans...and for some reason I never reviewed this place! My family and I took a class here on the second day of our trip. Our teacher, Tom, was a super friendly, informative man from...Garden Grove, California! LOL! He has lived in Nola many years though and was an awesome cook. It was just a small world that he was from Orange County. In the class he taught us how to make cornbread, red beans & rice, pecan pie and pralines. We got to eat everything he made, and it was all delicious. We were each given copies of the recipes to try at home. If you make one of their recipes at home and email them a picture of the dish, they will send you a certificate that says you graduated from the New Orleans School of Cooking, which I thought was pretty cool. I keep meaning to put mine up, but I haven't yet. The pralines were AMAZING and I make them for the holidays now. So freakin good! Everybody loves them when I bring them to parties. Attached to the school they have a store where you can buy all kinds of cooking utensils, cook books, spices, mixes, sauces...kind of like a cajun Williams Sonoma. I bought a pack of Joe's Hot Stuff Seasoning, Crab Boil and Blackened Cajun Seasoning. I have used all of them regularly for the past two years. My parents recently took a trip to Nola and I asked them to swing by and buy me some more since I was running low. You can also purchase their items online. This was a fun place, and I highly recommend it if you have a couple hours and you want to learn how to make, and eat, some really good Southern food!
label: POS

text: I went in for a bra fitting and was very pleased with the service I received. I was measured in the dressing room and was surprised to learn I was wearing the wrong size bra! While I stood there in shock my consultant brought back several different styles and colors in my correct size. The consultant was so nice and made me feel comfortable, which was super since I was topless! In the end I purchased 4 bras and the total came to just under $200, which I found to be very reasonable. I definitely recommend this Nordstrom to anyone in need of a bra.

text: This place serves food and has a large number of pool tables. Smoking inside the place is not allowed, but it smells like stale cigarette smoke! It's bad. The entire time we were there the entrance door was left open. Everyone who went outside to smoke, including the employees, ALL smoked right outside the door. I'm allergic to cigarette smoke, so nowhere inside the place was clear of smoke since people smoked all night. Unfortunately, we couldn't stay as long as we would have liked since I was uncomfortable the entire time. I really wanted to enjoy myself, but I couldn't. If you're a smoke-free environment, then you'd better damn well make sure you really are!!! I'll never go here again.

text: My friend had his wedding rehearsal dinner here and all I can say is, "wow!" This was probably some of the best pizza I've ever had. I'm from California, and sure, you can get some tasty pizza out here, but Pi was something totally different. It didn't taste like junk food. It tasted like real food. The cheese was light, the toppings were fresh, and the cornmeal crust seemed to impart a more wholesome approach. The salads were also amazingly done. Let's not get started on the garlic bread. Oh, and for the record, I'm nowhere near a vegan/vegetarian, but even the gluten and dairy-free pizzas were fantastic. My only complaint is that I'd have to travel 2,000 miles to have it again.

text: Wow, this place has the worst salespeople ever. I'd been there a few times before and knew they were high pressure but bought food anyway. The salesperson insulted my intelligence right and left, and just generally acted like I was unable to choose my own dogfod. I have worked in the veterinary field for 22 years, shown dogs in conformation and working events, have professionally trained dogs and have done hours and hours of dog related seminars and workshops, including many on nutrition. I have an idea of what type of food is best for my dog, its not like I was asking for Pedigree or Beneful. But she never stopped for a moment to glean any information from me, just continually told me I was wrong and became obnoxious when I politely disagreed with her suggestions. Needless to say, this did not go on very long because I left without buying anything as soon as I could disentangle myself. Since it was the next closest place, I discovered that Scraps on Mae Anne Drive was much more my style. We had an actual conversation and I bought a premium food that has worked great for my pet. My advice to Healthy Tails is "lay off the pressure, LISTEN, and treat your clients as intelligent humans.

Every time I go in or go through the drive thru, I get exceptional service--better than most sit-down and serve places. My hat's off to you, staff of the South Broadway Hardees. You guys are awesome.

text: I'm really sad to give this place a bad review. Really. I went one time before it expanded, and I thought it was delicious and lovely. I was excited to go again last night to see the bigger space and the drink menu. I should clarify that my friend and I are vegetarians, so maybe that's why the food was sub-par. But the fact is that what we ate was unbelievably bland, and the waiter was unattentive and kind of mean ("Why are you ordering so much tofu?") I had the Hu Tieu Cai Thap Cam -- veggie noodle soup (Pho, as far as I can tell). The menu said it would come with "fresh bean sprouts, basil, lime, onion, cilantro and hot pepper." It came with lime and sprouts. I ordered it with tofu, but they brought it without. The soup had no flavor whatsoever -- essentially just vegetables and noodles in water. The idea of Pho (at least the way this totally uncultured girl understands it) is to add all that other stuff in and make it delicious -- but we couldn't even get soy sauce. My friend had tofu vermicelli, which sounded so yummy on the menu, but in practice was just unflavored tofu chunks over unflavored noodles. Blech. The waiter never came by to check on us, except after forty minutes or so when he asked whether we were finished with our (almost entirely uneaten) meals. The food and service deserved one star. The decor was good, but that isn't enough to make up for the things you actually go to a restaurant for.

text: This place is loud, overpriced, crowded, and generally horrible. I came in to the Speedway location for a lip wax (I live out of town, so couldn't go to my usual place). The desk staff was rude and short with me, and people were shouting back and forth. Total chaos--not what you want in a spa. The lip waxer, Danielle, was also rude, trying to push products on me that I said I didn't want. Like this: Her: Okay, I'm going to clean up your eyebrows, too. Me: No thanks. I've been growing them out, because I'm getting married on Saturday and I want them fuller. It took about a year to do it, and I'm happy with the shape. Her: Are you sure? Me: Yes. Her: Let's just tweeze them a little. Me: No. Thanks. (Lip wax) Her: Okay, I'm going to put neosporin on your lip. Me: Oh, no thanks. I always follow lip waxes with a little aloe, and that works for me. Her: But it's really GOOD neosporin. It's new. Me: No thanks. I'm getting married in three days, so I'm not trying any new products right now. Her: But it will REALLY HELP with your lip. Me: No. Thanks. OFMG. No means no. And also, there's no reason to treat me like I'm stupid just because I like my eyebrows full and don't want Neosporin on my lip. This place was such a disaster I canceled our mani/pedi appointments the next day. GO ELSEWHERE. Also, their wedding hair services are heinously overpriced. Check out the fabulous Circa 79 salon for hair, and Elements in Balance for mani/pedi! You'll be happier!

We will definitely be back to Bambu the next time we're in New Orleans again - which I hope is very soon!

text: This was great fun. It isn't terribly clear what the protocol is, but basically you give donations for whatever food you want. The inside of the main building ( not the sanctuary) is where the nuns and monks were eating. There was a huge table full of what looked like home made food, and there wasn't exactly a queue on which to stand, but some nice lady took pity on me and ushered me in ahead of her. For our morsels, we offered five bucks ( one plateful). Outside, we discovered what seemed more like vendors with desired donations listed per item. Be warned that the fried bananas ( plantains) take FOREVER FOREVER FOREVER. They are totally worth it. Order them and then go sit to eat the other food, and send someone back to check periodically on the progress. The deal is that a man will ask you how many people you want to feed, you tell him, then he tells you Joe much to give ( he can change for a twenty), and then he gives you a number. Silly me thought they would call me quickly, but no- you have to wait until the paper bag bearing your number re- appears in the tray next to the man from whom you ordered. It takes awhile. Like 40 minutes, in my case. Totally worth it. Also, there is a group of ladies making green paw-paw salad, and it is killer. Spicy, sweet, sour, umami- you name it. The sanctuary is lovely, and itnis generally a happening, happy place. No booze!! Please respect the house rules.
label: POS

text: You've been in one, you've been in them all, right? Well...not necessarily. I've visited some post offices that were absolute nightmares, and, while I've had to wait in line on more than one occasion, it typically isn't too bad. Hopefully we've come far enough in the 21st Century to put the tired old stereotype of the disgruntled postal worker behind us. These guys certainly don't seem to fit into that mold. In fact, they're exceedingly helpful and cheery. There is typically plenty of room to park in the lot and on the street near the post office, and they have two drop boxes out front for anyone who doesn't need to/feel like venturing inside. The standout feature of this hub of the USPS, however, is its prime location. It's right in the heart of the Five Points District, just across the street from I Dream of Weenie and Wonders on Woodland. However, traffic never seems to be so busy that it's unsafe to walk across the street after grabbing a hot dog and pop your postcard to Grandma in the mail slot.
label: POS

text: From the time I first moved to South Philadelphia I had been hearing nothing but good things about this tiny breakfast place. People would rave nonstop about the decor and the woman behind the range who's smart as a whip. Frothing at the mouth, devotees of Carman's would praise the food saying it was near perfection. If god went to brunch, he'd eat here. For this review, I'll be drawing from two trips to Carman's that I made about two weeks apart. One was a busy day, one was slow as molasses. The difference between the two was overwhelming. On both occasions I had pancakes with fresh fruit and bacon. The size of the plates was great and the price was not bad considering the portion of the pancakes and quality of the bacon. The slow day produced a wonderful plate: hot, steamy and delicious. A sweet treat to say the least. The servers were great. They joked, made small talk and were generally congenial. I left feeling content. I had to sigh with pleasure. Ahhhh. The busy day revealed that when pressed to the coals, the staff just didn't have what it takes to pull off a good brunch service. We hadn't called ahead so we had to wait for a few minutes which was no problem, but we were made to feel like we were an inconvenience. When we were seated we were pressed to order as fast as possible and our server appeared visibly stressed. Granted, the place was full, but then again there really isn't that many seats. Even though we were rushed to order, our meals didn't arrive to our table until almost 25 minutes later. I think because Carman kept leaving the kitchen to gab it up with someone outside. My pancakes were as cold as ice, as was my bacon and the ginger ice cream had fully melted all over my plate. Total bummer. I guess I would say that a slow day is your best bet. If the place is full when you walk by just keep walking. you'll be doing yourself a favor.
label: NEG

text: I was disappointed with this place. I ordered the tacos with rice and beans, and an order of salsa and chips. All of the those were lousy. It's a shame, too... great food - bad service! I'll be frequenting Stoney River more often!

text: I have worn suits for well over 20 years and have purchased off the rack as well as several custom suits. I would say that you will receive better service at Symm's than at this place. text: True, its pricey and they've raised prices consistently throughout the years True, it isn't what it used to be with food quality, and don't really make those fresh agua frescas True, its got long lines at any time of day But who cares! text: My experience at Sunset Grill was far less than acceptable. I booked a reservation for 10 people more than two months in advance. This was a dinner for all of the members of my wedding party after the wedding and reception. Sunset Grill offers a shuttle to and from the restaurant from your hotel (most hotels in downtown Nashville). The driver was on time, and even came into the hotel lobby to greet us. Once we arrived at the restaurant, the night began to go downhill. Our server was horrible. When one of my guests asked if there was a martini list, the server said no, and to not order anything fancy. I thought this was a rather odd and rude response. That type of service continued for the remainder of the meal. The food was not memorable. The only two things I enjoyed were the Ostrich Carpaccio and Paddle Fish Caviar on the appetizer menu. Each of my guests had a different entree. Out of ten guests, only one was pleased and that guest had the New York Strip. An overall horrible experience and a waste of several hundred dollars!

text: Very rarely do I give a place one star (check out my 100+ reviews), but I experienced some "service" that was quite questionable here. While I was originally impressed by the large size here, I found one woman to be overly friendly to me and it made me a little taken aback. I was here primarily for browsing and was pretty excited to see they had some mid-century furniture and 70s modular pieces-some Eames, a yellow tulip style chair, some pieces I would definitely invest in, though I thought the place was rather over-priced (even for antiques). Set up kind of a like an indoor flea market but far more tastefully, I wandered around for a while but had planned to hit some other antique and thrift stores in the area. When I left, a sales woman came out to me at my car and said the other women who approached me FOUR times said she thought I was stealing! I was insulted! I thought I had forgotten something or something had dropped from my person or she wanted my autograph or something like that, you know? She asked to check my bag and I was so fucking insulted, I showed her, and of course I didn't steal anything. She apologized, and I told her one reason I left was the salesperson was over-eager to help me through-out my visit there. Man! I have never been accused of that before-I felt like a teenager at Spencers gift at a mall in Jersey or something. No piece of cool furniture is worth that kind of unprofessionalism.

text: I was lucky enough to be able to stay here for about a week in December of last year. It really is as nice as every one says but-because I didn't personally have to pay for it-I can give it 5 stars. Every morning I was greeted by lovely people that look you right in the eye. At the gym they have these nice fresh lemon scented towels in crushed ice for you to cool yourself and chilled Gatorade. They have the NY Times for you and anything else you might like to read. The gardens are so beautiful and well maintained. And-unlike newer resorts-you get the sense that this place has some great history and time has done the place well. There are neat old trees and the ocean is literally across the street. Growing up in Northern California, you get the real sense that we sometimes (not always) miss out on the California vibe. That stereotypical California feeling that includes warm weather and sunshine and dolphins hoping around at the beach (all of these things actually occurred during my stay in Santa Barbara) People are rich here and are not afraid to show it. If that doesn't bother you too much you should stay here too and live the good life for a bit.

text: I really love the spotted cat and it's a pretty special place for me. I'm a hurried and stressed person, naturally, and this seems to be one place where time really stands still. I love it. Weekends and weekdays are pretty different here, both are still fun. Both still good for having a dixie, seeing some music, and people watching. I really enjoy the crowd here and i'm not quite sure why. Maybe it's because everyone's so effortless, maybe because the music draws a good hodgepodge. It's somewhat of a dive, but I can take pretty highbrow people there and have an awesome time. Not that expensive, very spontaneous. Just have fun.

text: I wanted an early dinner on a Thursday and figured I would try Samurai Blue. I could see it getting really noisy inside because it's all hard surfaces, but it was pretty empty (but like I said it was early) and I figured at least the staff would be on the ball, right? Two of us got seated with one menu. The hostess ignored it and walked away. Oookay. Got up to get a second one. I mean, the menu isn't super long but I shouldn't have to sit and share it, especially if there's a whole 3 other people there. Back to that short menu. I ordered the shu mai to start off (why are these even on a "Japanese" menu? I knew I should have avoided them) and the short ribs. Also ordered: edamame and seared tuna. Our waitress asked how we wanted it to all come out. Logic would dictate the edamame and shu mai come out first, followed by the tuna and ribs. Edamame came, 7 minutes later (give or take) the shu mai followed. Wash and repeat for the tuna and the ribs. It turns out that the shu mai were over steamed and became mushy. Tolerable, fine, but it's hard to mess them up, come on! I hope for better with my main dish. I was disappointed, guys. I struggled so hard just to cut the meat. It was sitting on 3 cups of fried rice so every time I tried to cut it normally it would just sink and rice would overflow onto the table. The pieces I did get were somehow tough AND fatty. WTH? Did I order jerky? I got so frustrated with it that I just threw them all off to the side and went for some rice (thinking maybe eating some rice would reduce my cutting issues). More disappointment. Christ. It was a case of quantity over quality. I love fried rice - peas, carrots, onions, sometimes pork, scrambled egg, pineapple if you're going for exotic... They managed to screw up fried rice. The peas were obviously previously frozen (they were hard on the inside), as well as the carrots (or they're using carrots that have been chopped up for a week... dryyyy). There was nothing else in the rice. No egg, no nothing. It reminded me of the uncle ben's microwavable pouches you can buy in a grocery store except less appetizing. How is that possible? I don't understand!! Our waitress was kind of flaky and I declined a to-go-box when she asked (I don't think I would have even fed it to my dog). My struggles with tough meat left rice all over my side of the table, and I left hungry. Starving, actually, because I skipped lunch. I was pissed off too because that pile of crap was like $20. I didn't want my money back, or a do-over, I just wanted out. I walked around the corner to the crepe shop and drowned my hunger in delicious. If the option existed on Yelp, I would check off "Good for: nothing"
label: NEG

text: Friends were making an authentic Italian dinner for the husband and I while we were visiting in Philly. I wanted to bring a special appetizer tray for the cocktail hour. So, while touristing Reading Terminal Market, we stopped by Downtown Cheese to see what they could put together. I told Ron and his wife what we needed and let them do their magic; before you know it, we were sampling all kinds of Italian cheeses and olives. After we tasted several cheese delicacies, the Mrs. said we needed to talk price which I greatly appreciated. I was not surprised that our favorites were the most expensive but as I said this was for a special meal. So the choices: La Tur (Piedmont, Italy) a goat, sheep, and cow soft cheese. The trifecta of cheese!! Moliterno (Bascilicata, Italy) a sheep cheese with a dark band of black truffles and anchovies. (I am so in love with this cheese and hope to find it in Denver.) Marceno almonds Cerignola olives - large bright green olives with a smoky, ripe taste Prosciutto di Parmi which I wrapped around melon. All of the above served 7 hungry adults for $55.00. Not a bad price for the quality of product we received. The results..... a fabulous evening of Italian delights with special friends.

text: Let me just say this: when you've lived close to the ocean on both the East and West coasts and spent years enjoying Chicago's proximity to Lake Michigan, Indianapolis's downtown canal walkway, well, sort of underwhelms. This is somewhere we go just a few times a year because I hate driving downtown.The deal is someone else drives and I will roll the fresh springrolls for the group. text: Our family loves this place. The pizza's excellent, brick oven style. I usually order their delicious antipasta to go with the pizza. It's got some lettuce, but is brimming with sharp provolone, salami, high quality olives, fresh sauteed mushrooms, a nice scoop of tuna salad and ham, onions. My son and daughter (17 & 23 yrs) go crazy for the mussels in white sauce. I haven't eaten a whole lot of the entrees, but other family members have and no complaints. I'm a coffee person, I think it's important to end a great meal with a great cup of coffee, but in most, even really good restaurants, coffee is just a weak, burnt afterthought. Coffee here is not bad, but nothing to go crazy for. Eating in, the service is pretty good, but I have to say, my one big complaint, is when I order food to go, the guy who sometimes answers the phone can be pretty rude. At least twice I changed my mind after attempting to call in an order. After I've had a long stressful day, to have some a-hole take his bad mood out on me is a big fail and I usually order from the pretty decent Oreland Pizza instead . . . cheaper and they deliver.

text: This is definitely a story for the memory books. Never have my associates or I been treated so poorly in a restaurant (by the OWNER no less). Okay to set the seen: My fiance (32), my brother (29), his girlfriend (29), and I (29) were visiting our childhood town and decided to go shopping at Penn's Purchase. My fiance and I get hungry and walk into this pizza joint and attempt to satisfy our appetite. However, the owner (the pizza cook) was too important to take our order and referred us to the clerk at the counter who at that moment was chatting on her cell phone. We patiently waited until the pizza clerk was finished chatting so that she could give us some attention. We order a personal pizza. Then the clerk asked.... would you like that for here or to go? Not putting too much thought into our future plans we say... "to go please." We disappear out of the store for a moment and meet up with the other two in our group. Then the four of us return back to the pizza place to pick up the pizza. The lighthearted conversations in our group lead us to gravitate toward a table (in this small, informal pizza joint) and and we sit down while one of the members of our group uses the restroom. I request a cup of water and that is when the OWNER informs me in a bold tone, you can't eat that pizza here. "You ordered that to go, and now you must leave." Confused, I respond "Excuse me?" And he repeats, "You ordered your pizza to go, so now you must leave." We clarify that if it is an issue of tipping or an unknown restaurant fee, we would be happy to pay it. But the Owner/Pizza Maker insists that we must leave. To our protest, he insists that its not fair to his other customers. However, when I looked around his ten other customers all had their meals and there was no queue of people waiting. He again insists that we leave. He insults my brother by call him thick head and tells him that he is not even involved in the conversation because he is not the one that ordered the food. Needless to say he continued to fuel this verbal argument in the middle of his restaurant and which I'm sure disturbed the other patrons. In the end, he called the police and we finished our quasi pizza snack. However, in hindsight a store bought microwave pizza would have tasted better (but then again, I'm a little biased) Now, even to a business school flunky, does this seem like the proper way to run a business???

text: This place is simply awful. The only thing more unpleasant than the general shopping experience here is the hell you will encounter in interacting with the store personnel and management. First, the selection of groceries and produce is not only lacking, but grossly overpriced on the shelf and then often overcharged at the register. The store is dingy and depressing with no effort put to modernize or make presentable the interior of what looks to be a big cinderblock box built in the 60's or 70's. To use the word "Fresh" in connection with this place in any way is just dishonest. If I did not have to pass by this place twice a day on my commute to and from the train to work, I would never...NEVER...EVER...set foot inside! NEVER!!! As it is "convenient" however, I have found myself in this place a few times. Most recently yesterday, where I was advised that if I did not check my laptop bag with my iPod with "Security" (read two young kids goofing around in front of a bank of video monitors) then I could not enter the store. While this was not the first time I was so advised, I had had it with this place and asked to see the manager. This ignorant man who later identified himself as "Paul" immediately engaged me in a very public shouting match. I commented to "Paul" that I was offended that, as a male, I was asked to check a bag when women with comparably large purses were not asked to do so. Paul's response was to launch into a tirade about being accused of being racist, sexist, homophobic and so on (methinks thou doth protest too much, Paul?) While I never mentioned any of these issues, I did then comment that I thought the store's policy was gender discrimination since women were categorically never asked to surrender their purses. I also mentioned that the policy was not uniformly enforced and that I didn't see the need for a bag check policy given the bank of store surveillance monitors. I was informed that the bag check was not related to a concern for shop lifting and that my refusal to surrender my valuables was ... I think the word Paul used was "stupid." At this point I simply became confused. If not for a concern regarding theft, why would you ask to check bags? Ultimately, as Paul agreed to let me enter the store with my bag, he yelled the question, "Then why do you shop here?" This prompted my rather honest and abrupt reply, "because I need toilet paper!" Believe me, if it wasn't for the need for such a necessity and the convenience of this place on my daily trek, I would NEVER, EVER set foot inside. It's likely that this was my last visit. On my way home, I realized that I paid more for a "value" four roll pack of TP than I would have had I purchased four individual rolls. Weird! So, do yourself and the neighborhood a favor. Stay out of this place at virtually all costs. Hopefully they will promptly go belly-up (which would be a boon to consumers) and a reputable market will take this dump's place.
